<section id="H211376072C3B45559A43D23E14F1D584" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>101.</enum><header>Authorization of appropriations</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Funds are hereby authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2024 for procurement for the Army, the Navy and the Marine Corps, the Air Force and the Space Force, and Defense-wide activities, as specified in the funding table in section 4101.</text></section></subtitle> <subtitle id="H58FE6B3A9EF84FAD9F3B1488D6E92BE5"><enum>B</enum><header>Army Programs</header> <section id="HC03EEDBA59BC4955A2EB6B78C28916C3"><enum>111.</enum><header>Limitation on availability of funds pending assessment of Army Trackless Moving Target systems</header> <subsection id="HA043221C28A6476DAAAA3AC67B32CC93"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2024 for the Trackless Moving Target program of the Army, not more than 75 percent may be obligated or expended to procure or further develop the Trackless Moving Target–Infantry variant until the Secretary of the Army—</text> 
<paragraph id="H36CA229DB8A940A3B56295D56AA81CA9"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">acting through the Army Combat Capabilities Development Command, conducts an assessment of the Trackless Moving Target–Infantry variant, which shall include—</text> <subparagraph id="H5647994E9B21490BBC159B26447A5794"><enum>(A)</enum><text>obtaining end-user feedback regarding such variant; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HB462EE419E9A41E689A004B6384CC7E8"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">comparing the performance of such variant against the applicable program requirements set forth in the report of Secretary of the Army titled <quote>Autonomous Robotic Targets for Small Arms Range Training</quote>, as submitted to Congress in March 2023;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H089EC2A386594972AB3BC7F7CEE20EF7"><enum>(2)</enum><text>obtains direct soldier feedback on the current Trackless Moving Target program;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H485DFF634EC5490D827F73F2E8D2A6AE"><enum>(3)</enum><text>certifies to the congressional defense committees that the acquisition strategy of the Army for the Trackless Moving Target–Infantry variant meets the program requirements set forth in the report referred to in paragraph (1)(B); and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H466F6E965BEB49338CFE0C0158F4077F"><enum>(4)</enum><text>submits to the congressional defense committees the report required under subsection (b).</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HC64DC9D69B884EE6AF1C9467C801C3DF"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Report required</header><text>Not later than 30 days after the date of the completion of the assessment and soldier feedback required under paragraphs (1) and (2) of subsection (a), the Secretary of the Army shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report that includes—</text> <paragraph id="H8FBE96490DD54A43A5A4B8EE8EB2613C"><enum>(1)</enum><text>detailed results of the assessment conducted under subsection (a)(1), including a comparison of the Trackless Moving Target–Infantry variant under development by the Army to other operationally deployed, commercially available targets in use by other Armed Forces;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3CC0E713D220428FBE8E6142471BB421"><enum>(2)</enum><text>a summary of the soldier feedback obtained under subsection (a)(2); and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HEEAC5698B9AC40E385D9242A67930594"><enum>(3)</enum><text>a certification that the development of the Trackless Moving Target–Infantry variant is in compliance with the requirements of section 4061 of title 10, United States Code. </text></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="H84765982E9CF4C71B195CD0CE1B3E74A" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>112.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Strategy for Army tactical wheeled vehicle program</header> 
<subsection id="H3F33FD6AA183496EA4322CB101671D96" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Strategy required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In the budget justification materials submitted in support of the budget of the Department of Defense (as submitted with the budget of the President under section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code) for each of fiscal years 2025, 2030, and 2035, the Secretary of the Army shall include a report on the strategy of the Army for tactical wheeled vehicles.</text></subsection> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HDD470F6ED8064327AF167A5ADB18F542"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Requirements for strategy</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Each strategy required by subsection (a) shall—</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H8BBD896CACD64EFCA854CE1B3A7B876D"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">align with the applicable national defense strategy under section 113(g) of title 10, United States Code, and applicable policies; </text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H05C2F3032E994F7E891BBF0F600F7336"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">be designed so that the force of tactical wheeled vehicles provided under the strategy supports the national security strategy of the United States as set forth in the most recent national security strategy report of the President under section 108 of the National Security Act of 1947 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3043">50 U.S.C. 3043</external-xref>); and </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2FAD58E314A349D48A53798BC8E71167"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">define capabilities and capacity requirements across the entire fleet of tactical wheeled vehicles, including—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3FFD41086A7D47AD8399A92D13975790"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">light, medium, and heavy tactical wheeled vehicles; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2E6AD8A423C143B081F4EE71BFBE18F8"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">associated trailer and support equipment.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HD17878DDD8CF48E6B1D16D04DAF5EFEB" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Strategy elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Each strategy required by subsection (a) shall include the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H5445688E9C064083BE1D46715E049FBD" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A detailed program for the construction of light, medium, and heavy tactical wheeled vehicles for the Army over the period of five fiscal years following the date of the strategy.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H0548E407485F4F6B89E9B16FC47A85D0" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of the necessary force structure and capabilities of tactical wheeled vehicles to meet the requirements of the national security strategy described in subsection (b)(2).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HFD0A5A72D3F34FBCB76F0D2B1AEC4710" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The estimated levels of annual funding, by vehicle class, in both graphical and tabular form, necessary to carry out the program described in paragraph (1), together with a discussion of the procurement strategies on which such estimated levels of annual funding are based.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF19D84FA87AE49F587485D0BF69017DC" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The estimated total cost of construction for each vehicle class used to determine the estimated levels of annual funding described in paragraph (3). </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H2EF27F31FFFB4C1BB3D8E54B3A035788" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(d)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Considerations</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In developing each strategy required by subsection (a), the Secretary of the Army shall consider the following objectives and factors: </text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H606954935A0248D0BB6864FCBC472576"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Objectives relating to protection, fleet operations, mission command, mobility, and the industrial base.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCBC29EA5838844729D2A93E9ED7A5F92" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Technological advances that are expected to increase efficiency of and reduce demand for tactical wheeled vehicles. </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7B9080ED472648058DDCC3712CE45804" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Technological advances that allow for the operation of tactical wheeled vehicles in a variety of climate and geographic conditions. </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA16336ABAD254DEF89D69A0FD0701631" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Existing commercial technologies such as vehicle electrification, autonomous capabilities, and predictive maintenance, among others. </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H939672B35BD741CDACD5071A0544AA92" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The capabilities of autonomous equivalents to tactical wheeled vehicles. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H9B2968750CA847418979B3A8BA141E2C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(e)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Briefing requirements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 15 days after each budget submission described in subsection (a), in conjunction with the submission of each strategy required by such subsection, the Secretary of the Army shall provide to the congressional defense committees a briefing that addresses the investment needed for each platform of tactical wheeled vehicle of the Army across the period covered by the most recent future-years defense program submitted to Congress under section 221 of title 10, United States Code (as of the date of the briefing). </text></subsection></section> <section id="H67949AE13A4F488FBDB7AE42FA0837A9" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>113.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Report on acquisition strategies for the logistics augmentation program of the Army</header> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HFEBE5F09462749A5895C80B984A99D9C"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of the Army, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense and the commanders of the geographic combatant commands, shall conduct a review of the proposed recompete of the operational task orders of the geographic combatant commands under the LOGCAP V contract.</text></subsection>

<section id="H8CF96058CFE7410E8B50C4A7BD195DC4"><enum>146.</enum><header>Limitation on actions relating to remote vision systems of KC–46A aircraft</header>

<section id="HBE5866BD5F56473DA4DDF49B207AFDCE"><enum>147.</enum><header> Limitation on retirement of T–1A training aircraft</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">The Secretary of the Air Force may not retire, prepare to retire, or place in storage or on backup aircraft inventory status any T–1A training aircraft until the date on which the Secretary submits to the congressional defense committees—</text> <paragraph id="H84F5E66F03A847F2A76C877F2B62D56D"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a certification indicating that the Secretary has completed the full, fleet-wide implementation of the Undergraduate Pilot Training curriculum (formerly known as the <quote>Undergraduate Pilot Training 2.5</quote> curriculum); and </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H68223571A3254D38B88ED6043A3DE773"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a written assessment of—</text> <subparagraph id="HD549B1BA5F9247FB9BA545909EDAC346"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the effect of the implementation of the Undergraduate Pilot Training curriculum on the availability and training completion rates of undergraduate pilot trainees; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H5B5090D497CE4A968BA3C14D633D11C6"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">how the retirement of T–1A training aircraft may affect programs and initiatives of the Air Force to accelerate the rate at which pilots complete training.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></section> <section id="H387CC72D3EBB41439D0F4E01DB58249A"><enum>148.</enum><header>Plan for long-term Air Force fighter force structure</header> <subsection id="H4F8BE3CDDBAB4C37B59F2FEEB43EE4B5"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Plan required</header><text>The Secretary of the Air Force, in consultation with the Director of the Air National Guard and the Commander of the Air Force Reserve, shall develop a long-term tactical fighter force structure, recapitalization, training, and sustainment plan for the active and reserve components of the Air Force.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H7BCCBD72F62042D6A5F6824B39324D90"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The plan under subsection (a) shall address each of the following:</text> <paragraph id="HBAA5C43249E647DF9BB6DC4F54609E64"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The appropriate mix of tactical fighter aircraft force structure, with accompanying operational risk analyses, required for the Secretary of the Air Force to meet expected steady-state, global force management allocation plans and geographical combatant commander contingency operational plans tasked to the Air Force using active and reserve component units.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0DFC91677650437CA17C293248C7DB0E"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The procurement, divestment, unit activation, deactivation, or re-missioning plans or actions the Secretary plans to implement, fiscal year-by-fiscal year, unit-by-unit, for the next 12 years for each active and reserve component tactical fighter aircraft unit existing as of the date of the enactment of this Act, including the rationale and justification for any such plans or actions.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H03F056CA0E78486F997E75F8011604AE"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The actions the Secretary will take to ensure that required operational readiness rates are maintained during any planned recapitalization, modernization, or change of mission affecting tactical fighter aircraft units.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC1B311C9C0634C37AF6B63DBA83D4C87"><enum>(4)</enum><text>Any plans of the Secretary to augment or supplant existing piloted tactical fighter aircraft capability or capacity with Collaborative Combat Aircraft Increment 1 or Increment 2 capability or capacity.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5DBE4B86AD9746AB8EEB9A9637B0E1DF"><enum>(5)</enum><text>Any plans of the Secretary to augment or supplant existing piloted tactical fighter aircraft training events via acquisition and fielding of common, joint, all-domain, high-fidelity synthetic simulation environments.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H02F9A825BE2045BAA561539F9F50CD92"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than April 1, 2024, the Secretary of the Air Force shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report that includes the plan developed under subsection (a).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H39AD27142F8E468FBFA3F4058244472B"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Form of report</header><text>The report required under subsection (c) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may contain a classified annex.</text></subsection></section></subtitle>

<subparagraph id="H6EC9C7B70CA44FB9A83F14E701A4F77D"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the rationale for the divestment, re-prioritization, or retirement, including a qualitative description of the risk associated with the divestment, re-prioritization, or retirement based on the most recent National Defense Strategy (as of the date of the report);</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H1506D298B75F4C1988A03F2933D4DB11"><enum>(D)</enum><text>any critical dependencies with other program efforts that might affect the timeline for such divestment, reprioritization, or retirement;</text></subparagraph>

<section id="H4402390301E74C1E98ABA671BDBBE4ED"><enum>152.</enum><header>Multiyear procurement authority for domestically processed critical minerals</header> 
<subsection id="HEF380BC684B54B12A0EC49B407241D0D"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Authority for multiyear procurement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Subject to section 3501 of title 10, United States Code, and from amounts made available by discretionary appropriations Acts from the National Defense Stockpile Transaction Fund (as established under section 9(a) of the Strategic and Critical Materials Stock Piling Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/98h">50 U.S.C. 98h(a)</external-xref>)) after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense may enter into one or more multiyear contracts for the procurement of critical minerals that are processed in the United States by domestic sources.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HE3421B6B0F624E21AAF2F2939FAF7F24"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Application of Strategic and Critical Materials Stock Piling Act</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A multiyear contract entered into under this section shall be deemed to be an acquisition under the Strategic and Critical Materials Stock Piling Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/98">50 U.S.C. 98 et seq.</external-xref>).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HE6C05A5ACD0D40D69F7679A2B957196B"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Authority for advance procurement</header><text>The Secretary of Defense may enter into one or more contracts, beginning in fiscal year 2024, for advance procurement associated with the domestically processed critical minerals for which authorization to enter into a multiyear procurement contract is provided under subsection (a).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H4B97D85B555744889FC0254CE41580BB"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Condition for out-year contract payments</header><text>A contract entered into under subsection (a) shall provide that any obligation of the United States to make a payment under the contract for a fiscal year after fiscal year 2024 is subject to the availability of appropriations or funds for that purpose for such later fiscal year.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HC9662D25CC794DC0A980526686ABDDDE"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="HFB00AB8A331249D2AA818D19107F3B4B"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>critical mineral</quote> means a mineral determined to be a strategic and critical material under section 3(a) of the Strategic and Critical Materials Stock Piling Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/98b">50 U.S.C. 98b(a)</external-xref>).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5347A98C9CE9490E9AAC71C0416F927D"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The term <quote>processed</quote> means the processing or recycling of a critical mineral or magnet, including the separation, reduction, metallization, alloying, milling, pressing, strip casting, and sintering of a critical mineral.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE6C7F8709A564A0FBEC1033B8C4A1978"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The term <quote>domestic source</quote> has the meaning given that term in section 702 of the Defense Production Act of 1950 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/4552">50 U.S.C. 4552</external-xref>).</text></paragraph></subsection></section>

<section id="H38582A0C6521440696302BD91D2DF72D" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>221.</enum><header>Support for protection of sensitive research performed on behalf of the Department of Defense</header> 
<subsection id="H34DD6B453B32442A8B511A8D4DBF0952"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense, acting through the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering, may enter into contracts or other agreements with one or more eligible entities to assist institutions of higher education in protecting sensitive research performed on behalf of the Department of Defense.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HDEF338C922E940AF90DBA06B7D67909C"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Activities</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An eligible entity that enters into a contract or other agreement with the Secretary of Defense under subsection (a) shall carry out activities to assist institutions of higher education in protecting sensitive research performed on behalf of the Department of Defense. <paragraph id="H72DB6B7F826B40F895229D3A916629D5"><enum>(1)</enum><text>conducting effective due diligence in vetting visiting scholars;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7171172C1DFD4C44A75070A77808A558"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">assisting institutions in meeting applicable research security requirements, including through the use of common procedures and practices and shared infrastructure, as appropriate;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H83CF8D6D54D24F5BB3490F0E189E53A6"><enum>(3)</enum><text>providing training to employees and offices of the institution that have responsibilities relating to research security; and </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5EB1844F48FB4F32A155AE32CD515830"><enum>(4)</enum><text>providing advice and assistance to institutions in establishing and maintaining research security programs.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H3502F60FDF27416E8FAA26C5D5ED8AAD"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Considerations</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In selecting an entity to receive a contract or other agreement under subsection (a), the Secretary of Defense shall consider the following:</text> <paragraph id="H759805333014461B833E958944F9B205"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Geographic diversity and the extent to which the entity is able to maximize coverage of different regions of the United States.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC203A0C10F174F46989BD2339E50A18F"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any ratings of the entity made by the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency as part of the Agency’s annual security vulnerability assessment ratings.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H86A5A76858C74B19A0AFAD3D02EB25F7"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Whether and to what extent the entity uses best practices for research security as outlined by the National Institute of Standards and Technology.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H11216B4E69854EDD8DE3F2970437E80D"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The entity’s demonstrated excellence in security programs, including receipt of awards for excellence in counterintelligence and outstanding achievement in industrial security.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HA7366B05711D46C0AB4FB011844CEBA5"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Performance metrics</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall establish metrics to measure the performance of each entity with which the Secretary enters into a contract or other agreement under subsection (a).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H01C07B8BBEFB4E76AB9F42B48305F417"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Notification and report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">For any year in which the Secretary of Defense exercises the authority provided under subsection (a), the Secretary shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report that—</text> <paragraph id="HCF15616CC3924961A4CADADF8524E0E0"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">identifies each eligible entity with which the Secretary entered into a contract or other agreement under such subsection; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB11B5BDCAB1A4185BB02365616BA03C9"><enum>(2)</enum><text>evaluates the performance of the entity.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HCECAFD9B8D044B30941EBF8E83411428"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Eligible entity defined</header><text>In this section, the term <quote>eligible entity</quote> means—</text>

<subsection id="H48B5798E6F58442C83EB6E2534EF495F"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Activities</header><text>The Consortium shall—</text> <paragraph id="H3AE0FAE9FFF7434298C4C17D59578668"><enum>(1)</enum><text>facilitate the use of additive manufacturing—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H826F145073434448AB0A958F89E16E55"><enum>(A)</enum><text>to significantly reduce logistic footprints, material costs, and delivery lead-times; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H396405AA3760462D9269E70254FEBF72"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to extended logistical supply chain dependencies that often challenge weapon system readiness for forward deployed warfighters;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H49303009095B48CABF2888DE3C53F2D9"><enum>(2)</enum><text>develop standards and a certification process for the use of additive manufacturing in safety-critical applications, including additive material and part certification requirements for additive manufactured items intended for use in military vehicles;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H1BDD81D2AE564C46BD8ADA256B445C99"><enum>(3)</enum><text>evaluate, adapt, or apply the standards developed in the commercial sector, or new process approaches for additive manufacturing that may be of use to the Department of Defense;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H337D30E7CB87459984C7B9FBE16F88D4"><enum>(4)</enum><text>as directed by an organization of the Department of Defense included in the Consortium, conduct reverse engineering (including testing and certification) for critical parts which may have limited sources of supply;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H67D9B08F08D84CBEA505238DE166DA08"><enum>(5)</enum><text>use data standards, common repositories, and information security to track, store, and secure technical data relating to additive manufacturing and ensure the interoperability of such data; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2F75E280FD8241438568CA2356D0B544"><enum>(6)</enum><text>conduct comparative cost analyses for new and emerging additive manufacturing approaches, including assessments of life-cycle costs for tooling, training, and intellectual property needed to sustain such approaches.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HB723DE2958084AE3B8923B56415C59EB"><enum>224.</enum><header>Next Generation Air Dominance family of systems development program accountability matrices</header> <subsection id="H74643E20F9F142E4A5A6F3775C2CB25D"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Submittal of matrices</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Concurrent with the submission of the budget of the President to Congress pursuant to section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code, for fiscal year 2025—</text>

<paragraph id="H7942A894615647808C545511D05B12C7"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The cost-benefit and technical risk analysis conducted under paragraph (1) shall assess, at a minimum, the cost, risk, modernization, integration activities, and acquisition strategy required for the upgrade and modernization options available for the following major subsystems of F–35 aircraft:</text> <subparagraph id="H375A6A2F9BE64A7D80FB28E878BF02CA"><enum>(A)</enum><text>The aircraft propulsion system and gearbox.</text></subparagraph>

<section id="HEB5563A6C0D644BDA455ABE3B4C1A897"><enum>227.</enum><header>Establishment or expansion of University Affiliated Research Centers for critical materials</header> 
<subsection id="H0B75AE81504C42A18806D239473475B8"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Feasibility and advisability assessment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering, shall—</text> <paragraph id="HE35CA0B76EEF465384F18215558238CB"><enum>(1)</enum><text>assess the feasibility and advisability of establishing a new University Affiliated Research Center (in this section referred to as a <quote>UARC</quote>) or expanding an existing UARC at a specified covered educational institution; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD1954BBAAE2C4C58A3D07394E9544927"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">submit a recommendation regarding the feasibility and advisability of such establishment or expansion to the congressional defense committees.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H21A4C304B0A9472F8B63EB90826D07D3"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Determination</header><text>Not later than 15 days after submitting the assessment required under subsection (a) the Secretary of Defense shall determine whether it is feasible and advisable to establish or expand a UARC and—</text> 
<paragraph id="HDCD3C7D7DC2841BD9DEDD64B31E1750C"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">for a positive determination, submit to the congressional defense committees a plan described in subsection (c); and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7170A94B8FB7441C872BB9F04B500338"><enum>(2)</enum><text>for a negative determination, submit to the congressional defense committees a justification for such determination that includes the data and analysis to support such determination. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA72D2D4992C141D4AE3CCC2E94DEF731"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the Secretary of Defense determines that establishing or expanding a UARC is feasible and advisable under subsection (b), the Secretary shall submit to the congressional defense committees a plan for such establishment or expansion, including an assessment of the institutional capacity of the covered educational institution at which such UARC is to be established or expanded.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HC8C2364BE35F405F886C0F5850188A66"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The plan described in subsection (c) shall include the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H19910023B6F742C383F79D7DA7F00EEA"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of the engineering, applied research, commercialization, or workforce development capabilities relating to critical materials for national security purposes of the United States of the covered educational institution at which the UARC will be established or expanded, including an assessment of the personnel and physical research infrastructure of such institution.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9F57E6F1AB84476C8C8159BDCAEAA8DE"><enum>(2)</enum><text>An assessment of the ability of such institution—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H8EFAD2E90F5E487D99C9C7C319509101"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to participate in engineering, applied research, commercialization, and workforce development activities relating to critical materials for national security purposes of the United States;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H1FA28F84058E45D1B8FFE83DDF58096B"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to effectively compete for engineering, applied research, commercialization, and workforce development contracts and grants relating to critical materials for national security purposes of the United States; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H8A4D678CF8E44EEC9BC30A8025AC8600"><enum>(C)</enum><text>to support the mission of the Under Secretary.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H3956336ABE6B4711BD5D06C699BDD30E"><enum>(3)</enum><text>An assessment of the activities and investments necessary—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H6F76B1EA414E4B17826A81F60C1453DA"><enum>(A)</enum><text>to augment facilities or educational programming at such institution—</text> <clause id="H0140834FCBF740F78263E23F42363A8F"><enum>(i)</enum><text>to support the mission of the Under Secretary;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HBB7944A8B5A0445DB0E0C08659D39AF9"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>to access, secure, and conduct research relating to sensitive or classified information; and</text></clause> <clause id="HA0304B8C2A7D4811BBE74E48AD99036A"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>to respond quickly to emerging engineering, applied research, commercialization, and workforce development needs relating to critical materials;</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HCAC96A6956AE4C93B61158B8D94ADACE"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to increase the participation of such institutions in engineering, applied research, commercialization, and workforce development activities; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H62DFFE9E42F845C794E56D548A3038C4"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to increase the ability of such institutions to effectively compete for engineering, applied research, commercialization, and workforce development contracts and grants.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0E88517D715A498F983F11855E859ABB"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Recommendations identifying actions that may be taken by the Secretary, the Under Secretary, Congress, such institutions, and other organizations to increase the participation of such institutions in engineering, applied research, commercialization, and workforce development activities, contracts, and grants relating to critical materials.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7FB75709DA714B8EB7DEDB0893EF0F91"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any specific goals, incentives, and metrics developed by the Secretary to increase and measure the capacity of such institutions to address the engineering, applied research, commercialization, and workforce development needs of the Department of Defense relating to critical materials.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H67EBB99CAAA746B79A30EEFA360985BA"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Report required</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall—</text> <paragraph id="H9007591A618E40A6B50B278208FA6639"><enum>(1)</enum><text>submit to the congressional defense committees a report that includes the plan developed under this subsection; and</text></paragraph>

<subsection id="H2F6D3B2987964405938B8D0371278282"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The policies required by subsection (a) shall include the following:</text> <paragraph id="H458BA43B61A141DD833F19F8F1E7FFD3"><enum>(1)</enum><text>A standardized process through a Chairman, Joint Chiefs of Staff Manual, to allow Link 16 frequency use within approved special use airspaces for the purpose of testing radio systems and associated software that have not completed electromagnetic compatibility features certification. <subparagraph id="H6DF838D891F54D1793E0204DFA12D844" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text>shall, at a minimum, ensure routine and continued approval for test operations of developmental systems in the Nevada Test and Training Range, Restricted Area 2508, Warning Area 151/470, Warning Area 386, and the Joint Pacific Alaska Range Complex; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H5B222D7506574FE4BFEADBF69128D9B0" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>may incorporate standardized mitigations that enable routine approval including effective radiated power settings and coordination for rapid test termination.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HFC6D5256034145A1B5E89588575C3016"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Processes to streamline approval or denial of temporary frequency assignment for Link 16 operations to not more than 15 days for test, training, and large-scale exercises. <subsection id="H2044F80E6AC446C1A4D91D48FAD989C4"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Information to Congress</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall provide to the congressional defense committees—</text> <paragraph id="HC33A3806F8C9459C840E41E03D5D082D"><enum>(1)</enum><text>a briefing on the policies developed under subsection (a), along with a timeline for implementation of such policies; and</text></paragraph>

<section id="H8043E62205B94987B46A626E15005787"><enum>230.</enum><header>Pilot program to commercialize prototypes of the Department of the Air Force</header> 
<subsection id="HD0F566C9B6B140D193B49A423F8C4683"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Air Force, acting through the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics, shall carry out a pilot program under which the Secretary identifies prototypes under development by the Department of the Air Force that have the potential to be developed into commercial products and provides support to qualified entities to carry out projects to commercialize such prototypes.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H092C63E8892B4CE8802CDB2614D0E18C"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Form of support</header><text>The support provided to a qualified entity under subsection (a) may include the award of—</text>

<paragraph id="H6BF0963810934E98933FD89901C69F78"><enum>(3)</enum><text>such other form of support as the Secretary of the Air Force determines appropriate.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HA38B6DCB14E346B8AAC68C7745F56DAA"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Amount</header><text>The total value of support awarded to a qualified entity under this section may not exceed $10,000,000.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H8C8EB76DF1394DFBA3625ADA66B8435E"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Funding</header><text>The Secretary of the Air Force shall carry out the pilot program under this section using funds designated as budget activity 6 (RDT&amp;E management support) or budget activity 4 (Advanced Component Development and Prototypes) as those budget activity classifications are set forth in volume 2B, chapter 5 of the Department of Defense Financial Management Regulation (DOD 7000.14-R).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H840D2B6873E4476E9B4DFE359F9EB126"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Application</header> <paragraph id="HFC397D73857345FF894E703C0719E921" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>A qualified entity that seeks an award of support under this section shall submit an application to the Secretary of the Air Force at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H22A79E7440B34B06B63ECF0D0F0CD19B" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Contents</header><text>As part of the application required under paragraph (1), a qualified entity shall—</text> <subparagraph id="H89EC43D9DD204BFCBEC8E39D892A84B1" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><text>outline measures the entity will implement to give the Department of Defense purchasing priority when supply chain issues are a factor;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC61799980E8D48C0844980F8AFB0D5EA" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">certify that the entity will, with respect to the export of any such product, comply with—</text> <clause id="HE5D916C1BE604438BD914F151C94B04F"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">International Traffic in Arms Regulations under subchapter M of chapter I of title 22, Code of Federal Regulations (or any successor regulations); and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HA2241C01247E4449AAD2B1F93AD31AF0"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>any other applicable export restrictions; and</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF0A17EA57CB54564A3564AC8E0AC0C7C"><enum>(C)</enum><text>acknowledge that the entity may seek advice and assistance from the Department of the Air Force and the Department of State in the event that the export restrictions applicable to a commercial product developed with support under this section—</text> 
<clause id="H95D1CB3C084145B8A1354A08418BBC6B"><enum>(i)</enum><text>are more restrictive than the export restrictions applicable to the component technologies that comprise the product; and</text></clause> <clause id="H80868239EAA0428098CEE5ABB814AD07"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>are expected to unnecessarily impede the ability to make the product commercially available outside the United States.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HFA5028972E784DA38F930C6D21AE9791"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Briefing</header><text>Not later than December 31, 2024, the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics shall provide to the congressional defense committees a briefing on the implementation of the pilot program under this section and any related policy issues.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HAA1368D6D88844C2862A51F28F1DDEDB"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Notice to Congress</header><text>Not later than 30 days after each instance in which the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics awards support to a qualified entity under this section, the Assistant Secretary shall submit to the congressional defense committees notice of such award.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H96D5C68D98DE4179A85C71FC86EB9F1B"><enum>(h)</enum><header>Termination</header><text>The pilot program under this section shall terminate on the date that is five years after the date of the enactment of this Act.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H9E13D3A010C341DA828D115E2270C648" commented="no"><enum>(i)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text>

<paragraph id="H6A21BFBCD7AD4C25BC750E8EBB3BEDD1"><enum>(1)</enum><text>to solve technical problems and research challenges identified under section 234(e) of the John S. <subsection id="H644093CEF84B423E9E209D407FA79E9C"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Entities specified</header><text>The Secretary of Defense shall seek to carry out the pilot program under subsection (a) in partnership with—</text> <paragraph id="H39D28799EE0F44308119FDF0FA59E5AC"><enum>(1)</enum><text>a federally funded research and development center, university affiliated research center, center of excellence, or similar entity; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H72146ACB55794034ABEF4B525A08A3AA"><enum>(2)</enum><text>one or more private-sector entities with expertise in quantum computing and quantum information science.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HBAAAE3361661453F8C8D6D05C22B3F15"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Activities</header><text>Under the pilot program, the Secretary of Defense, in partnership with the entities specified in subsection (b), may—</text> 
<paragraph id="H4B89A1B999DD4D08808502C2B4CBBB11"><enum>(1)</enum><text>convene a group of experts and organizations to identify and articulate challenges faced by the Department of Defense, including the Armed Forces, that have the potential to be addressed by quantum and quantum-hybrid applications;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H45A7E7C958B144E7B9FF61A06F9ADEB3"><enum>(2)</enum><text>develop and mature demonstrations, proofs of concept, pilot programs, and other measures to address the challenges identified under paragraph (1) using quantum and quantum-hybrid applications;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H81A79E7D030542BBBDD1476C78FA385C"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">develop pathways through which successful demonstrations, proofs of concept, pilot programs, and other measures developed and matured under paragraph (2) may be transitioned to more advanced stages of research and development or into operational use within the Department;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H92AE01D8B8504285B7BE640905564B92"><enum>(4)</enum><text>ensure that any quantum-based or quantum-hybrid application-based solutions identified under the program are capable of development and deployment within the period covered by the most recent future-years defense program submitted to Congress under section 221 of title 10, United States Code (as of the time of the pilot program);</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H956376069F2142A993F37D701B46E3F8"><enum>(4)</enum><text>assess the utility of commercial quantum and quantum-hybrid applications for meeting the near-term needs of warfighters; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA7CE0DC737774C779F20CFF89267799C"><enum>(5)</enum><text>seek to build and strengthen relationships between the Department of Defense, academic institutions, small businesses, and nontraditional defense contractors (as defined in section 3014 of title 10, United States Code) in the technology industry that may have unused or underused solutions to specific operational challenges of the Department relating to quantum and quantum-hybrid applications.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA90976EFDF434D259E9A1C8577AD2CAF"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Briefing and reports</header> 
<paragraph id="H25397198479145D2BD15D94DF0378476"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Interim briefing</header><text>Not later than 30 days before commencing the pilot program under subsection (a), the Secretary of Defense shall provide to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a briefing that—</text> <subparagraph id="H582E27FC495D457498DC4C8033B4860A"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">identifies the entities the Secretary intends to partner with for the purposes of carrying out the pilot program, including—</text>

<paragraph id="HD748D83D7314473BAA66499D56FF1C99"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Annual report</header><text>By December 1 of each year in which the pilot program under subsection (a) is carried out, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a report that includes—</text> <subparagraph id="H983BFDDB6F33407499CEE87558CC3779"><enum>(A)</enum><text>a description of the problem sets and capabilities that were evaluated by organizations of the Department of Defense under the program;</text></subparagraph>

<subparagraph id="HAC4D37D3F8BF479A8623E4887CD79E56"><enum>(D)</enum><text>recommendations regarding how the Department of Defense can better leverage and deploy quantum and quantum-hybrid applications to address near-term military applications and operational needs.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H84715016EF1E4C81BB25EAE583B5FBA4"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Termination</header><text>The authority to carry out the pilot program under subsection (a) shall terminate on September 30, 2026.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H1517B718A9FD4230B13A37E5CD4283B8"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Definition</header><text>In this section, the term <quote>quantum and quantum-hybrid applications</quote> means algorithms and applications which use quantum mechanics through quantum processing units, including—</text> <paragraph id="H9C889AAE82D94D27BBE268B5733B7DCB"><enum>(1)</enum><text>quantum-classical hybrid applications which are applications that use both quantum computing and classical computing hardware systems;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HBA3AF030E87648E3B5F80C699B0F42D7"><enum>(2)</enum><text>annealing and gate systems; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H8E7DBD371AB64329944C1524711D9202"><enum>(3)</enum><text>all qubit modalities (including superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral atom, and photonics).</text></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="H3093AFEA400F4BB9B896DE226CFD1889" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>232.</enum><header>Pilot program to facilitate access to advanced technology developed by small businesses for ground vehicle systems of the Army</header> 
<subsection id="H6408D15FFC5F467BB44A73E1D80C19B4"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Program required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Beginning not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Army shall carry out a pilot program under which the Secretary seeks to facilitate a contract between the Ground Vehicle Systems Center of the Army and a non-profit research institute for the purposes of improving the ability of the Center to access advanced technology developed by a small business concern (as defined under section 3 of the Small Business Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/15/632">15 U.S.C. 632</external-xref>)). Any such contract shall be a commercial solutions opening contract entered into pursuant to section 3458 of title 10, United States Code. </text></subsection> <subsection id="H493A2999142149C2A2ECA4819B5695D3"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Termination</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The authority to carry out the pilot program under this section shall terminate five years after the date of the enactment of this Act.</text></subsection></section>

<quoted-block id="H7445F277EA4A41AB9800AA2A686F95D0" style="USC"> 
<section id="H094B7A698FA948C3BAE878C9BC7C3756"><enum>148.</enum><header>Joint Energetics Transition Office</header></section> 
<subsection id="HE52012950BEF4920A4C8F2A389031F20"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of Defense shall establish a Joint Energetics Transition Office (in this section referred to as the <quote>Office</quote>) within the Department of Defense. The Office shall carry out the activities described in subsection (c) and shall have such other responsibilities relating to energetic materials as the Secretary shall specify.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HBBBB63EA96A240A2ABA999B65495D335"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Leadership and administration</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline"></text> 
<paragraph id="H71D2C3E866AE4C28854883AC7C7A2965"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall designate an individual to serve as the head of the Office. The Under Secretary shall select such individual from among officials of the Department of Defense serving in organizations under the jurisdiction of the Under Secretary at the time of such designation. The head of the Office shall—</text> <subparagraph id="HC0C55F67B9034E74B4DE491DED08B1A8"><enum>(A)</enum><text>report directly to the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF0F378BC97514238B41313B43868AB9F"><enum>(B)</enum><text>coordinate, as appropriate, with the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB79025A2C9DB4C20991889D548C1A1D6"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering shall designate an individual to serve as the deputy head of the Office. The Under Secretary shall select such individual from among officials of the Department of Defense serving in organizations under the jurisdiction of the Under Secretary at the time of such designation. The deputy head of the Office shall report directly to the head of the Office and to the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE860304B4CAB40CE9F8196678C7A68DF"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The head of the Office and deputy head of the Office shall be responsible for the overall management and operation of the Office. The Under Secretaries shall ensure that the head and deputy head of the Office are not assigned outside duties that would diminish their ability to effectively manage and operate the Office.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H24C371D82A1B48678C218C30620CE22A"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Responsibilities</header><text>The Office shall do the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="HF660A4E13F28439784C9EE755FF8D4E9"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Develop and periodically update an energetic materials strategic plan and investment strategy to guide investments in both new and legacy energetic materials and technologies across the entire supply chain for the total life cycle of energetic materials, including raw materials, ingredients, propellants, pyrotechnics, and explosives for munitions, weapons, and propulsion systems. Such strategy and plan shall provide for—</text> <subparagraph id="HE562AA793192445DBAD4D7B31333B8AD"><enum>(A)</enum><text>developing or supporting the development of strategic plans for energetic materials and technologies, including associated performance metrics for the Office, over the periods covered by the future-years defense program required under section 221 of this title and the program objective memorandum process;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H7D769548D89E4309A6CF2633E4069373"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">initiating special studies or analyses—</text> <clause id="H4A452D3EC42C4E4B89181025E9EFB0A5"><enum>(i)</enum><text>to determine targets that would be optimally addressed or defeated by weapons that incorporate novel energetic materials; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HC0C92F8983FB467B91A2FD52B92D1F22"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>to inform the program objective memorandum process; and</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF314C2550E9B4C47B654B11C26AD7815"><enum>(C)</enum><text>identifying any shortfalls in the supply chain for energetic materials and developing plans to alleviate any shortfalls through the expansion of the energetic materials industrial base to include critical contractors, subcontractors, and suppliers.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB12210D8890047179D63BD23562E1FBC"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Coordinate and ensure consistency and congruity among research, development, test, and evaluation efforts in energetic materials across the Department of Defense—</text> <subparagraph id="H4FFC41EBCD9E48D6914FB7D5F8013525"><enum>(A)</enum><text>to identify promising new energetic materials and technologies;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H1E1C31627DF840B1909C6DE394F8F8C3"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to mature, integrate, prototype, test, and demonstrate novel energetic materials and technologies, including new materials and manufacturing technologies;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE90D843E8967440F902A00B9BEABBF8E"><enum>(C)</enum><text>to expedite testing, evaluation, and acquisition of energetic materials and technologies to meet the emergent needs of the Department, including the rapid integration of promising new materials and other promising energetic compounds into weapons platforms;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H90AB9EEF82ED45E48D16089A1E3F0A67"><enum>(D)</enum><text>to identify or establish prototyping demonstration venues to integrate advanced technologies that speed the maturation and deployment of energetic materials; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF624F8A9D5D5422C93B34752EEF81122"><enum>(E)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to support collaboration among industry, academia, and elements of the Department of Defense to transition energetic materials and technologies from the research and development phase to production and operational use within the Department. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1F875620C2894F31842DE78F43B04457"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Oversee a process to expedite—</text> <subparagraph id="H7454C757CEFE48D79E95DAC63405987C"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the validation, verification, and accreditation of modeling and simulation of energetic materials for the development of requirements; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF18A1DFA85504F17AFBE5C918B5E201F"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the qualification process for energetic materials, from discovery through transition to production and integration into weapon systems.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H46BACC7D26DF465AA3396B265DDF9C8A"><enum>(4)</enum><text>Recommend changes to laws, regulations, and policies that present barriers or extend timelines for the expedited process described in paragraph (3).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H6604E24E22C44099943C8020BF75FC6B"><enum>(5)</enum><text>Coordinate with other organizations involved in energetic materials activities within the Department of Defense, including the Armed Forces, and across other departments and agencies of the Federal Government.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HCBB10BCD8AC347609D895D77AB5CA25E"><enum>(6)</enum><text>Pursuant to the authority provided under section 191 of this title, establish and manage a Department of Defense Field Activity dedicated to systems engineering associated with energetic materials. Such Field Activity shall be funded under budget activity 3 (advanced technology development) or budget activity 4 (advanced component development and prototypes) (as such budget activity classifications are set forth in volume 2B, chapter 5 of the Department of Defense Financial Management Regulation (DOD 7000.14-R)) to reduce technical risk, integrate research, development, test, and evaluation, and perform system demonstration programs of the Department of Defense on novel energetic materials for use in weapon systems.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE202AC2145114736BB322668E5018846"><enum>(7)</enum><text>Carry out such other responsibilities relating to energetic materials as the Secretary shall specify.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H8C118B8A5C6849CE824062E29EF874B8"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Additional requirements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall ensure that the Office is budgeted for and funded in a manner sufficient to ensure the Office has the staff and other resources necessary to effectively carry out the responsibilities specified in subsection (c).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H585399F0F1024DB0B1AC883ECE9C6379"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section, the term <quote>energetic materials</quote> means critical chemicals and formulations that—</text> <paragraph id="HE4898C91F3AB44ABB8D6807E4CC625A1"><enum>(1)</enum><text>release large amounts of stored chemical energy; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE82B4CFF084744748199D7BC944F9E02"><enum>(2)</enum><text>are capable of being used as explosives, propellants, pyrotechnics, and reactive materials that—</text> <subparagraph id="H52A1327E40C34AAAA26C1FCD6AF222FF"><enum>(A)</enum><text>create lethal effects in warheads in kinetic weapons components and systems; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFA3698BF9D4F47E8A0C895C6CE217BC9"><enum>(B)</enum><text>increase propellant performance in a weapon propulsion system as related to lethal effects, range, or speed.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subsection> <subsection id="H2E1DF3E31F0947858B87D7188B1F2547"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Status reports</header><text>The Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees—</text> 
<paragraph id="H1708A4E1DEDA41FB81C787C49E18395F"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">not later than 60 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, a report on the status of the establishment of Joint Energetics Transition Office under section 148 of title 10, United States Code, as added by subsection (a);</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2C6FC422BC274EF8B8586CFDB35A204B"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">not later than one year after such date of enactment, a report on the measures taken to provide the Joint Energetics Transition Office with the staff and resources necessary for the Office to carry out the responsibilities specified in subsection (c) of such section 148; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HDDBDC73C8E5448C896CDD12E724DC0FF"><enum>(3)</enum><text>not later than two years after such date of enactment, a report that includes the energetic materials strategic plan and investment strategy required under subsection (c)(1) of such section 148.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HFD140EFDA7E641C182549320018F375C" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Annual reports</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than March 1, 2024, and not later than March 1 of each year thereafter through 2029, the head of the Joint Energetics Transition Office shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report that includes, with respect to the year covered by the report, the following information: </text> 
<paragraph id="H81B3E389DBC74CC09C5F5F1BE3AA3B29"><enum>(1)</enum><text>A description of activities carried out in accordance with the energetic materials strategic plan and investment strategy developed under section 148(c)(1) of title 10, United States Code, as added by subsection (a) of this section, including—</text> <subparagraph id="H896D3D0D60E54D878F1010455C3569F0"><enum>(A)</enum><text>a description of any updates to the performance metrics developed for purposes of such plan and strategy; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC172F07711F14AD19255171CEE168DEE"><enum>(B)</enum><text>an assessment of the performance of the Office against those metrics.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H22CC5EEF6CBD4F3EA7C11869F886648A"><enum>(2)</enum><text>An overview of the research, development, test, and evaluation efforts initiated or completed by the Office.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD698610321B3403B9A2AE5B9FDEF2AC7"><enum>(3)</enum><text>An overview of the efforts of the Office to expedite qualification processes for energetic materials.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDD71DD77294D41B4B4A67B018A4FAE04"><enum>(4)</enum><text>An overview of efforts of the Office to coordinate with other organizations involved in energetic materials activities across the Department of Defense and other departments and agencies of the Federal Government.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="HBDEE359A01044389AFF29645E52CE05F"><enum>242.</enum><header>Consideration of lethality in the analysis of alternatives for munitions</header> 
<subsection id="HD084B79B28574EA3A86AAEAE73C41340"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Analysis of alternatives review</header><text>The Secretary of Defense shall ensure that lethality is considered in any analysis of alternatives conducted prior to issuing a capability development document for purposes of procuring any new munition or modifying an existing munition.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HBCD6DE22E16242ECB653792402038B4A"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Consideration of energetic materials</header><text>In assessing the lethality of a munition for purposes of the analysis of alternatives described under subsection (a), the Secretary of Defense shall include the margin of effectiveness, increased system capacities, and cost implications afforded by the potential use of novel or alternative energetic materials in the munition to achieve increased explosive effects.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF2A95411094D4DDA97548F28C5673BF1"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Energetic materials defined</header><text>In this section, the term <quote>energetic materials</quote> means critical chemicals that—</text> <paragraph id="HBAE66623FFFA4363B05BBC079037CA6F"><enum>(1)</enum><text>release large amounts of energy in a short amount of time; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1F50BD6FEF46448582C8AFF8660DA762"><enum>(2)</enum><text>are capable of being used in explosives that create lethal effects in warheads.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HE9CD9F3BB6624B72BF447819095F1DFD"><enum>243.</enum><header>Pilot program on incorporation of the CL20 compound in certain weapon systems</header> <subsection id="H54C74EC00B394FA292BCAE277EF9F2EA"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Pilot program required</header><text>The Secretary of Defense shall carry out a pilot program under which the Secretary incorporates the CL20 compound as the energetic material for the main fill in the warheads or propellants of three weapon systems under development by the Department of Defense for the purpose of determining cost, schedule, and lethality performance parameters for such systems.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H1F3C74CB7A7D45A5A00F3C47BCE8DC01"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Selection of weapon systems</header><text>Each of the three weapon systems selected under subsection (a) shall be a weapon system that does not, as of the date of the enactment of this Act, already incorporate the CL20 compound as the energetic material for the main fill in the warhead or propellant of the system.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H8EC19D51C2B7467DB2F9EC7EB838627C"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Timeline for integration</header><text>The Secretary of Defense shall ensure that the CL20 energetic compound is integrated into each weapon system selected under subsection (a) by not later than three years after the date of the enactment of this Act.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HEC041FE21216495598B82E6652923588"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Briefing</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall provide to the congressional defense committees a briefing on progress of the Secretary in carrying out the pilot program under this section, including—</text> <paragraph id="H00745B8CE82B40E78D16907F4E4D1FC5"><enum>(1)</enum><text>identification of the weapon systems selected by the Secretary under subsection (a);</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HABDA9253CB3949FC84024DC9B49E2C99"><enum>(2)</enum><text>with respect to each such weapon system, identification of—</text> <subparagraph id="H44A10CB7B6074779A64A81F65B15923F"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a timeline for incorporating the CL20 energetic compound into such weapon system;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HB44C630B781747568FB09A52F3C373C9"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the organization within the Department of Defense responsible for carrying out activities under the pilot program for such weapon system; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H793ACD105FDF4616BD54E639BBC1C826"><enum>(C)</enum><text>any locations at which testing associated with such weapon system under the program is expected to be carried out; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H9395BFFAE1D649B1AF5ED5247E29EBD7"><enum>(3)</enum><text>the baseline cost, schedule, and lethality objectives that will be used to evaluate the performance of weapon systems under the program.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H0BFB86F5765D484A97E31413C4AD04D3"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section, the term <quote>energetic material</quote> means critical chemicals and formulations that—</text> 
<paragraph id="H2F78A6DFECC84331ADCB685F4B6E6CB7"><enum>(1)</enum><text>release large amounts of stored chemical energy; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H4EC52C3F972A4E2B86E9D8B8A882A936"><enum>(2)</enum><text>are capable of being used as explosives, propellants, pyrotechnics, and reactive materials that—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H268B3F24C956401898FB8377CDC808A2"><enum>(A)</enum><text>create lethal effects in warheads in kinetic weapons components and systems; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HAF7B9569FE6C4920AD436F1C3154931E"><enum>(B)</enum><text>increase propellant performance in a weapon propulsion system as related to lethal effects, range, or speed.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="HAEB64626373A49AD919A5EAC9D1A9A34"><enum>244.</enum><header>Limitation on sourcing chemical materials for munitions from certain countries</header> 
<subsection id="H0EF4EA535C4C4451B9F201D1D504ADA0"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Limitation</header><text>The Secretary of Defense may not procure a chemical material for munitions specified in subsection (b) from any country specified in subsection (c).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H708CCCCAF5D04DE394F03CDB1CF3532D"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Chemical materials specified</header><text>The chemical materials for munitions specified in this subsection are the chemicals listed under the heading <quote>Task 1: Domestic Production of Critical Chemicals</quote> in section 3.0E of the document of the Department of Defense titled <quote>Statement of Objectives (SOO) for Critical Chemicals Production</quote> (FOA: FA8650-19-S-5010, Appendix VI, Call: 012) and dated December 5, 2022.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HB2965003BF894FDBA656FDE0A3C482A5"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Countries specified</header><text>The countries specified in this subsection are the following:</text> <paragraph id="HB68A16BFADA64E17BA9F93A2562C923D"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The People’s Republic of China.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD4191198996B466F81C9E3416BDFEF8E"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The Russian Federation.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H3385E8AE48424E87A2708477DA8BB8EA"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Islamic Republic of Iran.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H99EF5F0510AF49F0A4BBDC50D9EAE91F"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Democratic People’s Republic of North Korea.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H9EB1D485A87F40069748C22350AAA8DE"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Effective date</header><text>The requirements of this section shall take effect on a date determined by the Secretary of Defense that is not later than September 30, 2028.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="HE2AAAD19B39E4C6BB9574829DDA85746"><enum>245.</enum><header>Defense industrial base munition surge capacity critical reserve</header> 
<subsection id="H4FEE77CB07704147940CD17201F865CB"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, in coordination with the service acquisition executive of each military department, may establish a reserve of long-lead items and components to accelerate the delivery of munitions described in section 222c(c) of title 10, United States Code.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H3214A85C726D4421BB456C7CF6AEDCFF"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Quantity</header><text>The quantity of long-lead items and components reserved pursuant to subsection (a) should be in amounts commensurate to fulfill the requirements identified as Out-Year Unconstrained Total Munitions Requirement and Out-Year inventory numbers under section 222c(a) of title 10, United States Code.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HCB61ED2B8E6C4A49BF57F995FCD1A5DD"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Authority for advance procurement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment may enter into one or more contracts, beginning in fiscal year 2024, for the advance procurement of long-lead items and components, or economic order quantities of such items and components when cost savings are achievable, associated with munitions identified in subsection (a). Advance procurement authority may include the cost of shipping, storage, tracking, maintenance, and obsolescence management of long-lead items and components while held in the reserve described in subsection (a).</text></subsection> <subsection id="HA752F063431149D08C74153F2E79808B"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Limitations</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">No long-lead item or component may be procured under this section if the anticipated life cycle of such item or component requires disposal due to lack of military utility less than 8 years after such item or component is procured.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H459E9FCB4DDA4DB58BC6207B294A136C"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than February 1, 2025, and annually thereafter until February 1, 2030, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report that describes the use of the authority under this section, including—</text> <paragraph id="HF3496BD485E345C2967D2E9DADB14440"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the type, number, and value of long-lead items and components procured under each contractual action; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2F6C05D00DDF45B28FD38998F0C1C1B4"><enum>(2)</enum><text>information about the location of storage of such items and components.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H9DFE5BA0849142A0B2DE57E9FE738558"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> 
<paragraph id="HDED2E54B2A3349F6A0E45602485CB4FA"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The term <quote>long-lead item or component</quote> means a material, component, or subsystem of a munition that must be procured well in advance of the need for such munition.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA95BEA2D86DC4D6E94F1938710B64396"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The terms <quote>service acquisition executive</quote> and <quote>military department</quote> have the meanings given, respectively, in section 101 of title 10, United States Code. </text></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle>

<subsection id="H1E9619AE70EE4024B1B7EF630A3D5C57"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Requirement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">No Secretary concerned may deploy covered non-tactical vehicles to a military installation until, for each such prospective deployment—</text> <paragraph id="H088F68A6FC42451086C03550219F99C3"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the Secretary concerned—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H9427D9C14AD4464CBE26984AACC78AF4"><enum>(A)</enum><text>ensures there is completed an infrastructure plan for that military installation relating to the prospective deployment; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H5B44B861DE0E4D56B746C12E45CCC46A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>determines such plan is sufficient to ensure the satisfaction of the conditions described in subsection (b); and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H35E05B43BA3E453490B716F072264B06"><enum>(2)</enum><text>in the case of the first prospective deployment to that military installation, a period of 180 days has elapsed since such determination; or</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA84B36A85617400DA127DBE74FB390FD"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">in the case of any subsequent prospective deployment to that military installation, a period of 60 days has elapsed since such determination.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H73764158258C411480D571A03AD0056C"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Conditions described</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The conditions described in this subsection are, with respect to a prospective deployment of covered non-tactical vehicles to a military installation, the following:</text> <paragraph id="H18536BF6EFE8404BBF2A12E209E16398"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Military logistics and operational requirements of that military installation would not be substantially affected as a result of a lack of infrastructure to support the kind and quantity of such vehicles proposed to be deployed.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCC2B7A3C0F634E4C839D5B319D62F79E"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Adequate support facilities for the kind and quantity of such vehicles proposed to be deployed exist at that military installation.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H431C0317FFBC416FA4D73D510A45F202"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section:</text> 
<paragraph id="H633298D4702E45C0B25C490F701165AF"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The term <quote>covered non-tactical vehicle</quote> means a non-tactical vehicle that is an electric vehicle, hydrogen-powered vehicle, or advanced biofuel-powered vehicle, as such terms are defined in section 328 of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/263">Public Law 117–263</external-xref>; 136 Stat. 2519).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H512C7B789C324453BCB0DB3248F9A070"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The term <quote>Secretary concerned</quote> has the meaning given that term in section 101 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph></subsection></section>
