<section id="HA4762FDB37254A15ACD991D0CBF8807F"><enum>716.</enum><header>Establishment of military pharmaceutical and medical device vulnerability working group</header> 
<subsection id="HEE34FEAA0BD3483D91C325A980FE312F"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness, and the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, shall establish a military pharmaceutical and medical device vulnerability working group.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HDF1567FE74394643AC7D3599627BD763"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Membership</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Each member of the working group shall be a member of the Armed Forces or a civilian employee of the Department of Defense.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H7C1CE9FB86694EDEAD42640A06914BA3"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Cochairs</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary shall appoint a chair of the working group. The working group shall elect a cochair from among its members.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H5EB110B2B94B4DD6AAC25165C60B520E"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Duties</header><text>The duties of the working group shall include the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H53F320D3FDD7453F9ED067E591F49FF5"><enum>(1)</enum><text>To provide a forum for members of the working group to discuss issues involving access, threats, and vulnerabilities to pharmaceuticals, therapeutics and medical devices in operational environments of the Department.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HAAC036D0EDBF4BA89D79F6D0CA84ED9B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>To identify current vulnerabilities, including supply chain issues, active pharmaceutical ingredient supplies, device component issues and cyber and electronic threats that may disrupt operations of the Department.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H253FCE16A77340829A973E4D927464F5"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To identify locations where the Secretary can support manufacturing capabilities needed to improve the timely increase of domestic production.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H8C04F5FDE3794D89ABB84E6CA7F82E06"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To review policies of the Department to identify pharmaceutical manufacturing and supply guidance related to—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HD04499A4731A47FBAE78259F507850E1"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">diversification of the supply chain;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HDE0957F568A6454C98FCB740B56FA797"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">transparency from pharmaceutical suppliers and manufacturers;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H934DDCE9BD204C4FAD13619CD687144F"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">prerequisites for a vendor to sell to the Department during a shortage;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HEFC62D9A68F64DACA7C35D8DC402DCCD"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">timely communication regarding a potential shortage or other supply chain disruption; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HEBF219E1D86D4A9B8EDF363C53831DD7"><enum>(E)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the application of rules and processes of the Food and Drug Administration to the Department.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF3B7523E5B2A4B2CB6BE87AD320E38D5"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To include any information in the joint medical estimate of the Department or a similar report that highlights information that would be classified as sensitive or requiring a security classification above unclassified.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HAE51A330CFF846F09BEB5769E85122D0"><enum>(6)</enum><text>To develop a plan for the allocation of scarce pharmaceutical resources within the Department during a supply chain disruption and potential conflicts with competitors highlighted in the national defense strategy.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFE6AE08143644D43A7C3BF9E84ED0C1A"><enum>(7)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To develop a plan for stockpiling essential medications to ensure availability of a 180-day supply during an armed conflict or other supply chain disruption.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC2D29E689A9A40BDB5853E524784FFF4"><enum>(8)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To develop a plan that mitigates vulnerabilities to active pharmaceutical ingredient supply chains and reduces dependence on active pharmaceutical ingredients from foreign sources.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HA6982DAEF908476D9FCA9625BD38114B"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Briefings</header> <paragraph id="H738A35D46F9E4A6AB9CCE1AF0D4E75A9"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Initial briefing</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives an interim briefing on the organization, activities, plans, actions and milestones of the working group.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HFEDBEED174B44A43ACC6F91B15D00AF0"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Annual briefing</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than September 30 of each year, beginning in 2025 and ending in 2028, the Secretary shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives a briefing describing the activities, funding, plans, actions, and milestones of the working group, and other matters determined by the Secretary, during the preceding year.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HF42C52D8B4A7410AA6738AC9003A17CE"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Termination</header><text>The working group shall terminate on September 30, 2028.</text></subsection></section></subtitle>

<section id="H257CE982B2A64F9A9CCB39E79333C121" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>725.</enum><header>Study and report on health conditions of members of the Armed Forces on active duty developed after administration of COVID–19 vaccine</header> 
<subsection id="H45F17E8731EF4ED4ABE41B4EC470718D"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Study</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall conduct a study to assess and evaluate any health conditions arising in members of the Armed Forces on active duty one year after receiving the first dose of a COVID–19 vaccine.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H7952C9ED98684CC3AEA6179F862D3783"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Study parameters</header><text>In conducting the study under subsection (a), the Secretary shall—</text> 
<paragraph id="HE4959984908C453283EE9C23F717E559"><enum>(1)</enum><text>disaggregate data collected by—</text> <subparagraph id="H807CFA66FB5247F1BAECF72CBD698CF2"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">vaccine type and manufacturer;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HA0213987AA0349A0AAD43516444E4441"><enum>(B)</enum><text>age group at the time such first dose was administered;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB501A2A6871F4F9BBE17D854DFE3D565"><enum>(C)</enum><text>any health condition developed after receiving such first dose, regardless of whether the condition is attributable to the receipt of such first dose; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H93FF619A0F1841B58F398154D2B58A52"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">an accounting of adverse events (including hyperimmune response), including further disaggregation by history of infection; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB5DC7675FECF479080ACE51C7607F1B6"><enum>(2)</enum><text>assess the prevalence of each such health condition by each age group specified in paragraph (1)(B) among the unvaccinated population for each of years 2017, 2018, and 2019.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF06BB07CE94E4C09ACC52F43A5436F87"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act and each year thereafter for the subsequent four years, the Secretary shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate a report on the results of each study conducted under subsection (a).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H7D5DE538FC574720889C7F42AB424712"><enum>(d)</enum><header>COVID–19 vaccine defined</header><text>The term <quote>COVID–19 vaccine</quote> means a vaccine licensed under section 351 of the Public Health Service Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/262">42 U.S.C. 262</external-xref>) or authorized for emergency use under section 564 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/21/360bbb-3">21 U.S.C. 360bbb–3</external-xref>) for immunization against the virus responsible for COVID–19.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H22D3694060DD475D829DE9B6C3C45C87"><enum>726.</enum><header>GAO study on health care available to certain individuals supporting the missions of United States Forces Japan and Joint Region Marianas</header> 
<subsection id="HDEA8ACA34232433B8CC24209AE9989BD"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Study required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct a study to determine whether health care services available to covered individuals are sufficient to support the missions and readiness of United States Forces Japan and Joint Region Marianas.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HD3AE040867984FBB822AE9DB366F7499"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The study under this section shall include the following elements:</text> 
<paragraph id="H3FC559B3C2284C23BA451B66B1C4E27F" display-inline="no-display-inline" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The assessment of the Comptroller General of the effects of the changes to the administration and management of the military health system—</text> <subparagraph id="HA2A0A4D8516143789A0D81AE56774A8C"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">under Defense Health Agency Region Indo-Pacific Administrative Instruction 6025.02, signed on December 22, 2022; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HB9065461703F401C91999F4C1692760E"><enum>(B)</enum><text>on health care services available to covered individuals through the direct care component of the TRICARE program.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDDC1F023F8F243BFA70C002E4FB52EA7"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An estimate of—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HE3C6BDEB8FDB4BD2ADA20DD70EBD5C33"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the number of covered individuals who in fiscal years 2020 through 2023 received health care services through the military health system on a space-available basis; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H77B436B5171D47BD89B8690A22A185E7"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the percentage of covered individuals described in subparagraph (A) who had health insurance not provided through the military health system.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB62306B5EABA4166BA22C6776FFDF60C"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A summary of any health-related screenings administered by the Federal Government to a civilian employee before such civilian employee begins an assignment in the area of responsibility of the United States Indo-Pacific Command.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE0A2C398FA5F40D7BDF9D896DA142D2F"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The determination of the Comptroller General whether the Secretary of Defense has conducted or participated in an assessment of health care services—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H6E9054BA20164EBC9D296DD104A868DB"><enum>(A)</enum><text>provided to covered individuals through the military health system; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H379F91B1FEA9423383AB785D2757727F"><enum>(B)</enum><text>otherwise available to covered individuals.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0271DCC4EA044AA5A5BDD0D6229E5D6A"><enum>(5)</enum><text>The evaluation of the Comptroller General of the most recent assessment described in paragraph (4).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC2FA16768C964237A3ECFB0016661415"><enum>(6)</enum><text>Other information the Comptroller General determines appropriate.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H5E31496FED8B4FD5BECC18834CC54C6A"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Briefing; report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Comptroller General shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives—</text> <paragraph id="H491EF7491FDF46C98D1CDA48ED8C9369"><enum>(1)</enum><text>an interim briefing on the study not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H97B78546B5AB42A1BF891E4BD56C10AA"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a final report on the study in a format and on a date agreed to by the Comptroller General and such Committees during such briefing.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HC0EE222390014F48B963431738D2E911"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Covered individual defined</header><text>In this section, the term <quote>covered individual</quote> means an individual who supports the mission of United States Forces Japan or Joint Region Marianas, who is—</text> 
<paragraph id="H4288592FACE1407E8B9EA8AC01F12220"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a United States citizen, national, or lawful permanent resident and—</text> <subparagraph id="H2F5553DB3AAD47949C10F0DF8FEA541B"><enum>(A)</enum><text>a civilian employee of the Federal Government; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H6EB69FA1F02343FFA4A9D2D81A2983B2"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">an employee of a contractor or subcontractor under an agreement between such contractor and the Secretary of Defense; or</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H4FD752E278C646BBB7F7E32E1F5FD984"><enum>(2)</enum><text>a dependent of—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H04AAE72633824D8C89A2FAB2E7C6E600"><enum>(A)</enum><text>a member of the Armed Forces; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HBDE6C5BC12C24D4EBB1D15E1B1F884B5"><enum>(B)</enum><text>an individual described in paragraph (1).</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle></title>

<section id="H51078D2B771C4B429A9B02B71F556216" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>801.</enum><header>Commercial nature determination memo available to contractor</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 3456(b)(2) of title 10, United States Code, is amended—</text> <paragraph id="HBA7B2CC16306411AA3B987A46C03F393"><enum>(1)</enum><text>by striking <quote>for such determination</quote> and inserting <quote>why the product or service was determined to be commercial or noncommercial</quote>; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H107CBD31E7714C3DA7627C66BE8D4EC2"><enum>(2)</enum><text>by adding at the end the following: <quote>Upon the request of the contractor or subcontractor offering the product or service for which such determination is summarized in such memorandum, the contracting officer shall provide to such contractor or subcontractor a copy of such memorandum.</quote>.</text></paragraph></section> <section id="H92209B53BB4848918BA04818F47D0CEB" section-type="subsequent-section" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>802.</enum><header>Modification of truthful cost or pricing data submissions and report</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 3705(b)(2) of title 10, United States Code, is amended—</text> 
<paragraph id="HD4FF0274B5D04164B8988BCF7D4AE7DC"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">in subparagraph (B), by adding at the end the following new sentence: <quote>The Under Secretary shall make appropriate portions of the report available to the leadership of the offerors named in such report.</quote>; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H01A5DD47F9A2423F9E1D534A10AE9D9B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:</text> 
<quoted-block style="USC" id="H850701D6BA7244EE9D69EB46F0CC695F" display-inline="no-display-inline"> 
<subparagraph id="HFDF083036E66491B943D94807CAEA4DE" indent="up2"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall develop a framework for revising what constitutes a denial of uncertified cost or pricing data, including—</text> <clause id="H9E21186473734BFB937E843453ED9E43"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">identifying situations under which such denials occur to exclude situations outside the control of the offeror or Federal Government;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HB2F460ADD8964572843332D96F1189D5"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">identifying whether such denial is from the prime contractor or subcontractor; and</text></clause> <clause id="H0C3CF919EBA0489D8032D75C24FE291D"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">developing an appropriate timeframe for requiring submission of uncertified cost or pricing data before a request for such data is considered a denial, including a standardized determination of a starting point and conclusion for such requests.</text></clause></subparagraph><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph></section> 
<section id="H500D96AC5F2B41528745187C5412F33E"><enum>803.</enum><header>Prohibition on the transfer of certain data on employees of the Department of Defense to third parties</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline"><external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/10/363">Chapter 363</external-xref> of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new section:</text> <quoted-block id="H549F11D1FAFD4865AAC61CE475DC5BB1" style="USC"> <section id="H905306195B8E41F3AE157BEF8B2D8BA3"><enum>4662.</enum><header>Prohibition on the transfer of certain data on employees of the Department of Defense to third parties</header> <subsection id="HE042B268AC2F40E4AF7A73E739026584" commented="no"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Each contract entered into by the Department of Defense on or after the date of the enactment of this section shall include a provision prohibiting the contractor and each subcontractor under such contract from selling, licensing, or otherwise transferring covered individually identifiable Department employee data to any individual or entity other than the Federal Government, except to the extent required to perform such contract or a subcontract under such contract and that would be permissible pursuant to statute or guidance from the Director of the Office of Management and Budget.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H8C7208CEC2FB471EB80A8677B06B6E3C"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Waiver</header><text>The Secretary of Defense may waive the requirements of subsection (a) with respect to a sale, licensing, or other transfer of covered individually identifiable Department employee data if the Secretary determines that such waiver is appropriate.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H115A68BD81F446CB92E9B8D1B8020A6A"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> 
<paragraph id="HB0E28D1C96BC4C36A57791A8FFF42936"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The term <quote>covered individually identifiable Department employee data</quote> means individually identifiable Department employee data obtained by—</text> <subparagraph id="HC28FEB47BAA6480BB1F86739938C274F"><enum>(A)</enum><text>a contractor pursuant to the performance of a contract described in subsection (a) by such contractor; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HEECAD19821D14058BAC2C00A225587DF"><enum>(B)</enum><text>a subcontractor pursuant to the performance of a subcontract under such a contract by such subcontractor.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H26CD5A3D27894849B3AB7ADB678CF80A"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The term <quote>individually identifiable Department employee data</quote> means information related to an employee of the Department of Defense, including a member of the Armed Forces, that—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H5B40E4EF660344A9A7A6C29B0AD09B73"><enum>(A)</enum><text>identifies such employee; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3CD83576C74140A494C65425701481A0"><enum>(B)</enum><text>which may be used to infer, by either direct or indirect means, the identity of such an employee to whom the information applies.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section> 
<section id="H3673A6F54D774C21954E52138B89154D" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>804.</enum><header>Prohibition on contracting with persons that have fossil fuel operations with the Government of the Russian Federation or the Russian energy sector</header> 
<subsection id="H3C769033A37E43138A26E1C630F8233B"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Prohibition</header> 
<paragraph id="H80029435C9A645AF9AC091BAA6428679"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Except as provided under subsections (b), (c), and (d), the Secretary of Defense may not enter into a contract for the procurement of goods or services with any person that is or that has fossil fuel business operations with a person that is not less than 50 percent owned, individually or collectively, by—</text> <subparagraph id="H6CE0A75D5BBC4D10AF7F995BFB41DB97"><enum>(A)</enum><text>an authority of the Government of the Russian Federation; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H6DE1ABDE407E448687B9616BF1909F00" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a fossil fuel company that operates in the Russian Federation, except if the fossil fuel company transports oil or gas—</text> <clause id="HF145BE958F95410BA04021B5DECF45B0"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">through the Russian Federation for sale outside of the Russian Federation; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H1E01860A6C4F41D1AED825B7B4D80153"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">that was extracted from a country other than the Russian Federation with respect to the energy sector of which the President has not imposed sanctions as of the date on which the contract is awarded.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H64E023C711164F86B34657DF0578247A"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Oil and gas origin</header><text>For the purposes of applying the exception under paragraph (1)(B), oil and gas transported by a fossil fuel company shall be deemed to have been extracted from the location of extraction specified in the certificate of origin or other documentation confirming the origin of such oil or gas unless the person with respect to which such exception would apply knew or had reason to know that such location in such documentation was false or incorrect.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H6854AB86829441ABBC288AE104EB11D9"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Exceptions</header> 
<paragraph id="H74C48DCC875F4AB99698C715EE1B56C3"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The prohibition under subsection (a) does not apply to a contract that the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of State jointly determine—</text> <subparagraph id="H66947ACAB30A4631859F7FA57E222B0E"><enum>(A)</enum><text>is necessary—</text> 
<clause id="H21B3AF9C2A1846D3990B7C238521F056"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">for purposes of providing humanitarian assistance to the people of Russia; or</text></clause> <clause id="HFAEC9F21795C4E22B11C0ED524FFBCF8"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">for purposes of providing disaster relief and other urgent life-saving measures;</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H0816416DAB2645FAA0A7C6620D244B18"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">is vital to the military readiness, basing, or operations of the United States or the North Atlantic Treaty Organization;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3C265D8160374E888274AA89F0EEEECF"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">is vital to the national security interests of the United States; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H3D0DA6A3D092411D8F77C4E6BCBB0137"><enum>(D)</enum><text>was a business operation with a fossil fuel company in a country other than the Russian Federation that was entered into prior to the date of the enactment of this section.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC07960E6156943378FD909B873582E8B"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Notification requirement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall notify the appropriate congressional committees of any contract entered into on the basis of an exception provided for under paragraph (1).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3D63210DFC15465C8C196F764CEE3381" commented="no"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Office of foreign assets control licenses</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The prohibition in subsection (a) shall not apply to a person that has a valid license to operate in Russia issued by the Office of Foreign Assets Control of the Department of the Treasury or is otherwise authorized to operate in Russia by the Federal Government notwithstanding the imposition of sanctions.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF4D4FA4DB7A1459A8250928B51E4C47A" commented="no"><enum>(4)</enum><header>American diplomatic mission in Russia</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The prohibition in subsection (a) shall not apply to contracts related to the operation and maintenance of the United States Government’s consular offices and diplomatic posts in Russia.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H54677AB9255D4CACAA96F81859E0F7D8"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Applicability</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">This section shall take effect on the date of the enactment of this Act and apply with respect to any contract entered into on or after such effective date.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H09A319A2FDDA4FF7ADCB4B288F83ACB8"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">This section shall terminate on December 31, 2029.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HFFD7A027E20B44BF8119A3F40121B7E3"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="H1980099E26B24C368B326A7100A72900"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Appropriate congressional committees</header><text>The term <term>appropriate congressional committees</term> means—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HC471AF2BE0A544DA935BE690C0709FF8"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Committee on Oversight and Accountability, the Committee on Armed Services, and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HD165FCC46AB347AD81B3D9BF1CD20DBB" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, the Committee on Armed Services, and the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC0C77A3C6D934383B036102FCC5133BF"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Business operations</header> 
<subparagraph id="HAA500FBAD1FE4BFE933A334E4BE66EF4"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The term <term>business operations</term> means engaging in commerce in any form, including acquiring, developing, maintaining, owning, selling, possessing, leasing, or operating equipment, facilities, personnel, products, services, personal property, real property, or any other apparatus of business or commerce.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H26E59AD483BD443BAFEBAF2B639E6D0D"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Exceptions</header><text>The term <quote>business operations</quote> does not include—</text> 
<clause id="H0C4D166A7D7F43D19DD5284E4BF985C7" commented="no"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">any shipment subject to price caps as specified in the <quote>Statement of the G7 and Australia on a Price Cap for Seaborne Russian-Origin Crude Oil</quote>, issued on December 2, 2022, between member countries of that coalition, or the price caps as specified in the <quote>Statement of the G7 and Australia on price caps for seaborne Russian-origin petroleum products Berlin, Brussels, Canberra, London, Ottawa, Paris, Rome, Tokyo, Washington</quote>, issued on February 4, 2023, between such members, if such shipment complies with the applicable price caps;</text></clause> <clause id="H578F7FB382F24514998FC85310F1343E"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>actions taken for the benefit of the country of Ukraine, as determined by the Secretary of Defense; or</text></clause> 
<clause id="H50B6EF078B1945E7B4544558CFF52787"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">actions taken to support the suspension or termination of business operations for commercial activities during the period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act and ending on the date described in subsection (d), including—</text> <subclause id="H44EE1F2D2D944D34AC7CA37F5BACD536"><enum>(I)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">any action to secure or divest from facilities, property, or equipment;</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="H7CC6A1CAFA8E46AF96370EE2DBA51633"><enum>(II)</enum><text>the provision of products or services provided to reduce or eliminate operations in territory internationally recognized as the Russian Federation or to comply with sanctions relating to the Russian Federation; and</text></subclause> <subclause id="H4A702A9F32174608B09BF78ACFDEC05B"><enum>(III)</enum><text>activities that are incident to liquidating, dissolving, or winding down a subsidiary or legal entity in Russia.</text></subclause></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HEC698EFCBF3E4B5E8A116D02FACB2A61"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Fossil fuel company</header><text>The term <term>fossil fuel company</term> means a person that—</text> <subparagraph id="H1582AA7E2656493E96077F238B46C19B"><enum>(A)</enum><text>carries out oil, gas, or coal exploration, development, or production activities;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC24B23A734564A889DED75E65968BB1B"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">processes or refines oil, gas, or coal; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H8EBD60312F994A2093DA2904B4F65CA9"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">transports, or constructs facilities for the transportation of, Russian oil, gas, or coal.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H7B15555E00404A629364A4148FCB7509"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Person</header><text>The term <term>person</term> means—</text> <subparagraph id="H17C8212BEBC54CB5A08586CDCDCA401C"><enum>(A)</enum><text>a natural person, corporation, company, business association, partnership, society, trust, or any other nongovernmental entity, organization, or group;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H125DE48B00F34CD1A36EF83296C5C763"><enum>(B)</enum><text>any governmental entity or instrumentality of a government, including a multilateral development institution (as defined in section 1701(c)(3) of the International Financial Institutions Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/262r">22 U.S.C. 262r(c)(3)</external-xref>)); and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB9C0AB0043014CB6951F96012C7421BA"><enum>(C)</enum><text>any successor, subunit, parent entity, or subsidiary of, or any entity under common ownership or control with, any entity described in subparagraph (A) or (B).</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="H39937DDC9AFB4DFDB0B8AEAE28B9A665" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>805.</enum><header>Prohibition of the Department of Defense procurement related to entities identified as Chinese military companies operating in the United States</header> 
<subsection id="H017724CE82694A33AC24DC72E42AC3D5"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Prohibition on use or procurement</header> 
<paragraph id="HB14EC4B374204CDDBEC806A29D096ABB"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Except as provided under subsection (d), the Secretary may not—</text> <subparagraph id="H8BF7B1B841AC4424AEA0D61DB91DF960"><enum>(A)</enum><text>enter into, renew, or extend a contract for the procurement of goods, services, or technology with an entity described in paragraph (2); or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H55275A8AD895452D9EF91C41ED5B5A5D"><enum>(B)</enum><text>enter into, renew, or extend a contract for the procurement of goods or services that include goods or services produced or developed by an entity described in paragraph (2).</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H48BB7FDA40A9407A879A7661E05AA741"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Entities described</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An entity described in this paragraph is—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H4B7AB22B3C544997B4A868656698925B"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">an entity that is identified in the annual list published in the Federal Register by the Department of Defense of Chinese military companies operating in the United States pursuant to section 1260H of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/113">10 U.S.C. 113</external-xref> note); or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H8F30F315E36C4BEE852A769501F758EB"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">any entity subject to the control of an entity described in subparagraph (A).</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5D87EAC4D1084CB4900C6FE0E3611E51"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Limitation on applicability</header> 
<subparagraph id="H04FFBAC73CD04576B9008D36F7F10650"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Nothing in paragraph (1) shall prohibit the Secretary from entering into, renewing, or extending a contract for the procurement of goods, services, or technology to provide a service that connects to the facilities of a third party, including backhaul, roaming, or interconnection arrangements.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HA84564F666044EC09E84885C4A156734" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Existing contracts</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in this section shall permit the Secretary to apply the prohibitions in paragraph (1) to existing contracts for goods, services, or technology, including when such contracts are modified, extended, or renewed, entered into prior to the relevant date described in subsection (b).</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H12EAA44926764FC3B2F823EE8F8460E8" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Components</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Paragraph (1) shall not apply with respect to components (as defined in section 105 of title 41, United States Code).</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9CB217A5BD8A4A4CAEEAA738ADB663DB"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Rulemaking</header> <subparagraph id="H0CB19BDE72F44F869F1AD2866AC48645"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Entity prohibition</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement the prohibitions in paragraph (1)(A) for the Department of Defense.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H083B7CCA2768448CB7D3D6BBF53683EE"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Goods and services prohibition</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 545 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to implement the prohibitions in paragraph (1)(B) for the Department of Defense, including—</text> <clause id="HE0CE3E10F9BF40DFA13C063AA5145C02"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">best practices to avoid being subject to the prohibitions described in paragraph (1)(B); and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H6844002A72A641B0838D90B57496AB90"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>technical support to assist affected businesses, institutions, and organizations as is reasonably necessary for those affected entities to comply with this section.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H971D56609F684146B9F73720425AB9C5" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Effective dates</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The prohibition under subsection (a)(1)(A) shall take effect on June 30, 2026, and the prohibition under subsection (a)(1)(B) shall take effect on June 30, 2027.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF07AD3E020CE4A01AECC438C620FF2A1"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Waiver authority</header> 
<paragraph id="H093846BE55914918825C29341A432807"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary may waive the requirements under subsection (a) with respect to an entity that requests such a waiver if the entity seeking the waiver—</text> <subparagraph id="H92369E2510074A1995B0A9FF352D327D"><enum>(A)</enum><text>provides to the Secretary a compelling justification for the additional time to implement the requirements under such subsection, as determined by the Secretary of Defense; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HB96FB629F8A946DF99EBD00B7B6DE167"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">provides to the Secretary a phase-out plan to eliminate goods, services, or technology produced or developed by an entity described in subsection (a)(2) from the systems of the entity.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HCE8DCB4221BC4DFDBB847D39068DA665"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Duration</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A waiver granted under paragraph (1) may remain in effect until the date on which the Secretary determines that commercially viable providers exist outside of the People's Republic of China that can and are willing to provide the Department of Defense with quality goods and services in the quantity demanded.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1E68606793314E259CC6113E3F3F1DED" commented="no"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Delegation</header><text>The Secretary may designate the authority under this section only to—</text> <subparagraph id="H2681D26E260F4F4987C9B88B1C6DE024" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the service acquisition executive of the military department (as such terms are defined in section 101(a) of title 10, United States Code) concerned; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HCA92F758CBDA4D9BB2739AAE4E6F7A3E" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the official responsible for all acquisition functions of such other element or organization of the Department of Defense concerned.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H5E65A11FD4614470AA924975E2FCB3BC" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Exception</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The President shall not be required to apply or maintain the prohibition under subsection (a) for activities subject to the reporting requirements under title V of the National Security Act of 1947 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3091">50 U.S.C. 3091 et seq.</external-xref>), or to any authorized intelligence activities of the United States.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H0E7A286164464166ABD2578CF6628102"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="H774E19F684634965996B1EE6AE88E5BA"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Control</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>control</quote> has the meaning given that term in part 800.208 of title 31, Code of Federal Regulations, or any successor regulations.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCBB84A3A1FB54FAC942B4DC0DFB63476"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Secretary</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>Secretary</quote> means the Secretary of Defense.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HBAA20B2330784FF584FCD7A2680B5A92" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>806.</enum><header>Principal Technology Transition Advisor</header> <subsection id="HB096D77B49834589A463E0F9D4750EBC"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Designation</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, each service acquisition executive of a military department shall designate a Principal Technology Transition Advisor who shall advise each Secretary of a military department on the transition of technologies, including technologies from science and technology programs of the Department, private commercial entities, research institutions, and universities, to fulfill identified and potential warfighter requirements for the military department.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF18B94FCE9BC4B51BAD45ED7C193D376"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Advisor status</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Principal Technology Transition Advisor of a military department designated under subsection (a) shall be a member of the Senior Executive Service or a general officer and directly report to the service acquisition executive of such military department.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H6C28866F062842F9A8EB4ACD0F4D1F12"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Responsibilities</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Principal Technology Transition Advisor of a military department designated under subsection (a) shall do the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H3F8C2ED6A15B45DC89F913A1EF2559F8"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Identify technologies being researched, developed, tested, or evaluated by science and technology programs of the Department, including Defense research facilities (as defined in section 4125(b) of title 10, United States Code), that the military department may use to meet identified and potential warfighter requirements, including technologies for which the Department owns and maintains the intellectual property rights.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HAC6CD407CA4D4BAAB2F3E64C6BF3E25B"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Consult with Department of Defense innovation programs to identify technologies from private commercial entities, research institutions, universities, and other entities that the military department may use to meet identified and potential warfighter requirements.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF0DCD8E0AA2B425CB851A9B6C75BAF4C"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Make recommendations to the service acquisition executive of the military department regarding the acquisition of technologies identified under paragraphs (1) and (2) for acquisition decisions at the service acquisition executive level.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA38C2C19379749DAAB5C2B11E742E623"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Inform program managers (as defined in section 1737 of title 10, United States Code) and other relevant acquisition officials of the military department of relevant technologies identified under paragraphs (1) and (2).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HAE01D486407B4DEA8FD339125C0353A7"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Develop policies and processes for promoting to small business concerns (as defined under section 3 of the Small Business Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/15/632">15 U.S.C. 632</external-xref>)) and nontraditional defense contractors (as defined in section 3014 of title 10, United States Code) opportunities to license intellectual property developed by the Department, including opportunities and methods for small business concerns and nontraditional defense contractors to engage with the Department regarding such licensing.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7EDB5996E6594914A40D9079E7D5FE6E"><enum>(6)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Develop and maintain metrics tracking the outcomes of projects and other activities of the military department for which the military department expended amounts designated as budget activity 3 (Advanced Technology Development), budget activity 4 (Advanced Component Development and Prototypes), and budget activity 5 (System Development and Demonstration), as those budget activity classifications are set forth in volume 2B, chapter 5 of the Department of Defense Financial Management Regulation (DOD 7000.14-R).</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H5623D373934A498DB300CEDC81537E27"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Congressional report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than one year after the designation of the Principal Technology Transition Advisor of a military department under subsection (a), and annually thereafter, the Principal Technology Transition Advisor of such military department shall submit to Congress a report on the following for the one-year period preceding the submission of the report:</text> <paragraph id="H50AB2236F8D044AC97B3FB11A3F17962"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The activities of the Principal Technology Transition Advisor.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2FC5CAE0C1A24439A316D67F96BF3C94"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The outcomes of projects and other activities described in subsection (c)(6), including the metrics described in such subsection.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HA6DEDC4FECC743108F3507D98CD3A6E1"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section—</text> 
<paragraph id="H463DDA7B1AF54F0A815AEE31D10805EF"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the term <quote>Department</quote> means the Department of Defense;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC4D6C5C05EBF4B66900195EBA0491B5A"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the term <quote>Department of Defense innovation programs</quote> means the Defense Innovation Unit of the Department of Defense, AFWERX of the Air Force, and other programs sponsored by the Department of Defense, or any component thereof, with a focus on accelerating the adoption of emerging technologies for mission-relevant applications or innovation; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC9CE01EFBEC44E09890352A19DE82C5F"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the terms <quote>military department</quote> and <quote>service acquisition executive</quote> have the meanings given such terms in section 101(a) of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HE10B0412A1F342CDA7D0C7CB04362F78"><enum>807.</enum><header>Senior contracting official for Strategic Capabilities Office</header> <subsection id="H3CAE5596A45140E9A323B9BA5A9700CC"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Senior contracting official</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The staff of the Director of the Strategic Capabilities Office shall include a senior contracting official (as defined in section 1737 of title 10, United States Code) who shall have the authority to enter into and administer contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, and other transactions in execution of the program activities of the Strategic Capabilities Office.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H9B7FDB62274642EDA8CA17C4249F03B8"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Effective date; Implementation plan</header>

<subparagraph id="H1130CF71DFB94AB7977245A43C5A9C22"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Other matters as appropriate.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HE9C5EBC3186A4D0C933476A2DDF8533C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>808.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Pilot program for the use of innovative intellectual property strategies</header> <subsection id="H43CE92A7BE8943B7A3C34906486F9C38" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Establishment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall establish a pilot program for the use of innovative intellectual property strategies that meet the criteria described in subsection (b) to acquire the necessary technical data rights required for the operation, maintenance, and installation of, and training for, covered programs designated under subsection (c).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HFDABFE118CBC44ED9CE29609611E010C"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Criteria for strategies</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The innovative intellectual property strategies used in a pilot program established under this section may include the following:</text> <paragraph id="H3988466C8B944A94B75759B4877D8F92" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The use of an escrow account to verify and hold intellectual property data.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H29A46AF85327483A965613B7D54E042C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The use of royalties or licenses.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2C738301A2D2430CA72A6F410A19226F"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Other strategies, as determined by the Secretary.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HB39DA28887E04CF3AD48AE4868D232C2"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Designation of covered programs</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than May 1, 2024, and with respect to the pilot program established under this section—</text> <paragraph id="H1F916649EF7F4EE1BF51AAE7FACFD7B8"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the Secretary of each military department shall designate one covered program within the military department under the jurisdiction of such Secretary; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H41EA3C9FA3864556AF6A59ED93891339"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall designate one covered program within the Defense Agencies or Department of Defense Field Activities (as defined, respectively, in section 101 of title 10, United States Code).</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H804D5F883EAD4480818413AC792D0BD8" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(d)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Briefing requirement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, in coordination with the Secretaries of the military departments, shall provide a briefing to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives with a detailed plan to implement the pilot program required under this section.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H0630B0E2D0E7415493D53E2F682E6204" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(e)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Annual report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Beginning on the date on which the first program is designated under subsection (c) and until the termination date in subsection (f), the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, in coordination with the Secretaries of the military departments, shall provide an annual report to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives on—</text> <paragraph id="HD158E9E76BC545A8ACE7E8C56A95661B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the effectiveness of the pilot program in acquiring the necessary technical data rights necessary to support timely, cost-effective maintenance and sustainment of the acquisition programs designated under subsection (c); and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H7D6F13A29E9C414C874C11CF680366D0"><enum>(2)</enum><text>any recommendations for the applicability of lessons learned from the pilot program.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H919F5A17C9894DAAB7EED3665C0A800B" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(f)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Termination</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The authority to carry out the pilot program established under this section shall terminate on December 31, 2028.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H2465F463DC974B62A82B52B1C7B8C1BA" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(g)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section:</text> <paragraph id="H419CB3CA20004BB6AE61E2AC46A7A6DA"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>covered program</term> means an acquisition program under which procurements are conducted using a pathway of the adaptive acquisition framework (as described in Department of Defense Instruction 5000.02, <quote>Operation of the Adaptive Acquisition Framework</quote>).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H7605319B423F4D89A6EA529C1ACE223A"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>technical data rights</term> has the meaning given in section 3771 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H96B8B5B6064A43FFB1E5361E1F184DCC" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>809.</enum><header>Pilot program for anything-as-a-service</header> <subsection id="HA5EE53DCA1CD4F828BDDD36AFF044DAD"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall establish a pilot program to explore the use of consumption-based solutions to address any defense need, hereafter <quote>anything-as-a-service</quote>, that is feasible to provide users on-demand access, quickly add newly released capabilities, and bill based on actual usage at fixed price units.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H6D775F66514B4524B9868E2CC275EB17"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Requirements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A contract or other agreement for anything-as-a-service entered into under the pilot program shall require the outcomes of the capability to be measurable, including the cost and speed of delivery in comparison to using processes other than anything-as-a-service, at the regular intervals that are customary for the type of solution provided.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HD010510586274B71A74B2C380D217789"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Notice</header><text>With respect to each opportunity to participate in the pilot program established under subsection (a), the Secretary shall make publicly available a notice of such opportunity for not less than 60 days.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HFAD4C8AC751943778AD0620CDD6F494D"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Timing</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary shall, to the extent practicable, enter into a contract or other agreement under this section not later than 100 days after the date on which the Secretary, under subsection (c), makes publicly available a notice to participate in the pilot program established under this section.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H3FEC65AB037D4830BEB397009B95B987" commented="no"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Exemptions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A contract or other agreement entered into under this section shall be exempt from the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H395760F3A3E44F68B7233FFFA6B05C58"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The requirements of section 3702 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H3C3ECF8E957E4BA4AEC6A94AEA3B46FF"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">With respect to a modification to add new features or capabilities in an amount less than or equal to 25 percent of the total value of such contract or other agreement, the requirements of full and open competition (as defined in section 2302 of title 10, United States Code).</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H7873055C7F0E4DAB92DC984F2F8C8BFF"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Briefing</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than June 30, 2024, the Secretary of Defense shall provide a briefing to the congressional defense committees on the implementation of the pilot program.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H63D2ABE82602439D81BC7A37FC235A3A" commented="no"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Anything-as-a-service defined</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section, the term <quote>anything-as-a-service</quote> means a model under which a technology-supported capability is provided to the Department of Defense and may utilize any combination of software, hardware or equipment, data, and labor or services that provides a capability that is metered and billed based on actual usage at fixed price units.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="HEA01DFCA7AEF4A3B8394F3619F54A855" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>810.</enum><header>Updated guidance on planning for exportability features for future programs</header> 
<subsection id="HE2EC58168D3A4A85973CFDD692EE4874"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Program guidance on planning for exportability features</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall ensure that the program guidance for major defense acquisition programs (as defined in section 4201 of title 10, United States Code) and for acquisition programs and projects that are carried out using the rapid fielding or rapid prototyping acquisition pathway under section 804 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/114/92">Public Law 114–92</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/3201">10 U.S.C. 3201</external-xref> note prec.) is revised to integrate planning for exportability features under section 4067 of title 10, United States Code, including—</text> <paragraph id="H80B70B61BB3449B8AAC6425F0EFCC11D"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">for major defense acquisition programs, an assessment of such programs to identify potential exportability needs; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB33CE1A92769471282F9772216C4BB0A"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">for technologies under an acquisition program or project carried out using the rapid fielding or rapid prototyping acquisition pathway that are transitioned to a major capability acquisition program, an assessment of potential exportability needs of such technologies not later than one year after the date of such transition.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H394ADF4564B44DF7B57C809D155BAAE1"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Revision of guidance for program protection plans</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than three years after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary shall revise guidance for program protection plans to integrate a requirement to determine exportability for the programs covered by such plans.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H7C7769745C1E4CD0B3C8C4A010C41A93" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>811.</enum><header>Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process</header> 
<subsection id="HFB6B9959BDF047249704080094C86ADF" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than October 1, 2025, the Secretary of Defense, acting through the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, in coordination with the Secretaries of the military departments and the commanders of the combatant commands, and in consultation with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, shall develop and implement a streamlined requirements development process for the Department of Defense, to include revising the Joint Capabilities Integration and Development System, in order to improve alignment between modern warfare concepts, technologies, and system development and reduce the time to deliver needed capabilities to warfighters.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H05F4D895E0F24B479A1DD3B5EF5812B2" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Reform elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The process required by subsection (a) shall—</text> 
<paragraph id="H4B9A60B9AFDC40DD909DD30014FA5C9B" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">streamline requirements documents, reviews, and approval processes, focusing on programs below the major defense acquisition program threshold described in section 4201 of title 10, United States Code;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H17C455A497EE49808647F7480DD58FAC" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">revise requirements management practices using a clean-sheet approach that avoids prescriptive language, is based on mission outcomes and assessed threats, enables a more iterative and collaborative approach with the Armed Forces, maximizes the use of commercial products or commercial services in accordance with section 3453 of title 10, United States Code, and allows for a broader range of new or alternative technological opportunities to be incorporated without the requirement being validated again;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HAC986365378147D1BF59C6062C3CECA2" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">develop a capability needs and requirements framework and pathways that are aligned to the pathways of the adaptive acquisition framework (as described in Department of Defense Instruction 5000.02, <quote>Operation of the Adaptive Acquisition Framework</quote>), and better aligned and integrated with the science and technology development processes of the Department;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB32B0D174B794CD5B4E16C5A0B4E09C4"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">provide continuity to the acquisition and research programs of the military departments by enabling the military departments to develop, with respect to collections of capabilities grouped by function by the Department of Defense, sets of requirements that are designed to remain applicable to programs and systems relating to such capabilities over substantial periods of time;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA53D89834F3A4CD7B90D02F40FEAC66E"><enum>(5)</enum><text>require the military departments to—</text> <subparagraph id="HFF45F27293A6442CA4A147F654D9701F" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text>articulate in a concise model and document with a set of mission impact measures the sets of requirements developed under paragraph (4); and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H104695300DC54DDBBE86859C66DEBAF3" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>seek to continuously improve the capabilities subject to such sets of requirements the acquisition of additional capabilities;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2DF4A08F3BE84E029FF2CE18E9DBA4C4" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(6)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">establish a process to rapidly validate the ability of commercial products and services to meet capability needs or opportunities;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H106FA4C0C2C34C63BA46C64C02D78485" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(7)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">retire and replace the Department of Defense Architecture Framework with a new structure focused on enabling interoperability through application program interfaces, enterprise architectures and platforms, and government and commercial standards; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H12C77F8EC9D144E39358298C2357E9C9" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(8)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">ensure that requirements processes for software, artificial intelligence, data, and related capability areas enable a more rapid, dynamic, and iterative approach than the requirements processes for traditional hardware systems.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H4B71964FB7E1442280C68FB9E008C0E3" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">With respect to the implementation of the process required by subsection (a), the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff shall—</text> <paragraph id="H02A0868B3D944D5BACCAC776E3ECC17C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">collaborate with industry partners, contractors of the Department and nontraditional defense contractors (as defined in section 3014 of title 10, United States Code), and Department of Defense science and technology reinvention laboratories (as designated under section 4121(b) of title 10, United States Code) regarding the development of the streamlined requirements development process under subsection (a) to ensure such process effectively uses the innovation ecosystem (as defined in section 236(g) of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/4001">10 U.S.C. 4001</external-xref> note));</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0F2DB8D31B2C4A648009DEF3708112EA" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">develop a formal career path, training, and structure for requirements managers; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H504E8B9B40D74926936D0B9A24005AF1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">publish new policies, guidance, and templates for the operational, requirements, and acquisition workforces online in digital formats.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HB481BDDE321B4E679CA3C4CF7A791D35" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(d)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Interim report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than October 1, 2024, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the development and implementation of the process required by subsection (a), including—</text> <paragraph id="HF452EAA2824E4BA7BABE5DC1A77D2773" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a description of the efforts to develop and implement the streamlined requirements development process under subsection (a);</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5F8E29EB7A6E4546975D12A90804890E" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the plans of the Department of Defense to implement, communicate, and continuously improve the requirements development process required by subsection (a); and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFF99E16F6CEA4D29B79CDB3E6917C651" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">any additional recommendations for legislation that the Secretary determines appropriate.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HBE93FAD62F0B42F0B013B3E91CD4A436" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(e)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Final report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than October 1, 2025, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report describing activities carried out pursuant to this section.</text></subsection></section> <section id="HC8C3ACCD2696488EBD639374B1B62CFE"><enum>812.</enum><header>Preventing conflicts of interest for entities that provide certain consulting services to the Department of Defense</header> <subsection id="H87B509649F5B448CBFDBC025C4C88F34"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header> <paragraph id="H661B522165154E9D804B415F927C4A45"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Certification</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall amend the Department of Defense Supplement to the Federal Acquisition Regulation to require any entity that provides consulting services and is assigned a North American Industry Classification System code beginning with 5416, after the effective date of such amendment and before entering into a covered contract, to certify that—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H065A5CECF3AD4EDE982AAB73BE7FD7AE"><enum>(A)</enum><text>neither the entity nor any subsidiaries or affiliates of the entity (as that term is defined in section 2.101 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation) hold a contract for consulting services with one or more covered foreign entities; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H72102BBC8E0A4FE58B9649F5F7678F5C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the entity maintains a Conflict of Interest Mitigation plan described under subsection (b) that is auditable by a contract oversight entity.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H94257FDBB432422E82A76D4EDC8D9F3F"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Prohibition</header><text>The Secretary of Defense may not enter into a covered contract with an entity described in paragraph (1) that is unable to make the certification required under such paragraph.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H40D8DEC3639F43AC912D18E76467BA70"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Conflict of interest mitigation plan</header><text>A Conflict of Interest Mitigation plan described under this subsection shall include—</text> 
<paragraph id="H4B7836EA4892439B9653F96D7DCA6E71"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">an identification, where such identification is not otherwise prohibited by law or regulation, of any covered contracts of an entity described in subsection (a) with a covered foreign entity;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HEEE8EBBC29FA45018BF3D837F44C14E5" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><text>a written analysis, including a course of action for avoiding, neutralizing, or mitigating the actual or potential conflict of interest of such a covered contract with the Department of Defense;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HEBD15EEB1F8B42148DA7E929213CD7AB"><enum>(3)</enum><text>a description of the procedures adopted by an entity to ensure that individuals who will be performing a covered contract will not, for the duration of such contract, also provide any consulting services to any covered foreign entity; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H45B48540BE224122804B35E96D6E9FF9"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a description of the procedures by which an entity will submit to the contract oversight entities a notice of an unmitigated conflict of interest with respect to a covered contract within 15 days of determining that such a conflict has arisen.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HE2FBEC0D7A314854A9B05922047E3232"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Alternative identification of covered foreign entities</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If an entity is unable to identify covered foreign entities under subsection (b)(1) due to confidentiality obligations, the entity shall identify any such covered foreign entity as an entity described in subparagraphs (A) through (F) of subsection (f)(4) in the Conflict of Interest Mitigation plan.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H033CC4FBA92D472582BDCFD4CF952A8A" commented="no"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Notification</header><text>Before determining to withhold an award of a covered contract based on a conflict of interest under this section that cannot be avoided or mitigated, the contracting officer for the contract shall notify the offeror of the reasons for such withholding and allow the offeror a reasonable opportunity to respond. If the contracting officer for the contract finds that it is in the best interests of the United States to award the contract notwithstanding such a conflict of interest, a request for waiver shall be submitted in accordance with section 9.503 of title 48, Code of Federal Regulations. The waiver request and decision shall be included in the contract file.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HAC0224DE72E7404194581DAD8223FA0E" commented="no"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Waiver</header> 
<paragraph id="H7119494711CB4256AF8A1EDBF481BEAB" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Authority</header><text>The Secretary of Defense may issue a waiver with respect to the requirements of this section for the award of a covered contract on a case-by-case basis as may be necessary in the interest of national security. The Secretary of Defense may not delegate the authority under this subsection to an official who has not been Presidentially appointed and confirmed by the Senate.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H203A55DDC999403C972513878F342C32" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Waiver notification</header><text>Not later than 30 days after issuing a waiver under this subsection, the Secretary of Defense shall provide a written notification to the Committee on Armed Services of the Senate and the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives regarding the use of such waiver authority. The notification shall include—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HDA7D684520D04B908E7FEF11B5B664D9" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the specific justification for providing the waiver;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB1595498589D428DB5EA9E93195BA293" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>an identification of the covered foreign entity that is the subject of the waiver request;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H9AFEE3BE817B4BB080497B9A742F396D" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the number of bidders for the covered contract for which the waiver was granted;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H85B4219F6FCD498CA20B1776CC6ACF32" commented="no"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the number of bidders for the covered contract that did not request a waiver; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H66436147EC1C47D3932D55BC5B9A6225" commented="no"><enum>(E)</enum><text>the total dollar value of the covered contract.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H2CE24931409444BF84B68B3397598BA8"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> 
<paragraph id="H077EDA6A813A4D59B8BFCD5E981E4602"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The term <term>consulting services</term> has the meaning given the term <term>advisory and assistance services</term> in section 2.101 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation, except that the term does not include the provision of products or services related to—</text> <subparagraph id="H44E8D4CDCABE47D4B11AFF8AB645E2B9"><enum>(A)</enum><text>compliance with legal, audit, accounting, tax, reporting, or other requirements of the laws and standards of countries; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H8A36A61EDA994902AB891D4027FC6E73"><enum>(B)</enum><text>participation in a judicial, legal, or equitable dispute resolution proceeding.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HCBBEEB0DE1064949946A312DE8F16241"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The term <term>contract oversight entity</term> means any of the following:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H3A9A5F5540BF4805B000A1F541AAD22A"><enum>(A)</enum><text>The contracting officer.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H36B881282A734D60A58B792D314BAC49"><enum>(B)</enum><text>The contracting officer representative.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H08AA9B47B36A4B9ABE62DDB781A7235E"><enum>(C)</enum><text>The Defense Contract Management Agency.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HDFF5C0F414354A45B40DE76C56385015"><enum>(D)</enum><text>The Defense Contract Audit Agency.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H8DB54DE97F3047E1887642211B096EA7"><enum>(E)</enum><text>The Office of Inspector General of the Department of Defense or any subcomponent of such office.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H87E5129A087F4D4AB671D590AD142A7D"><enum>(F)</enum><text>The Government Accountability Office.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H7E13F8C9AF0B4195930ACAB0950BE59C"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The term <term>covered contract</term> means a contract of the Department of Defense for consulting services.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H833A129BF6244309ABA98721433353FE"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The term <term>covered foreign entity</term> means any of the following:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H4963053E74214D648FF7D21DFA3EE0E5"><enum>(A)</enum><text>The Government of the People’s Republic of China, the Chinese Communist Party, the People’s Liberation Army, the Ministry of State Security, or other security service or intelligence agency of the People’s Republic of China.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H4D7505C486AC46D69AA134F3B7A062DB"><enum>(B)</enum><text>The Government of the Russian Federation or any entity sanctioned by the Secretary of the Treasury under Executive Order 13662 titled <quote>Blocking Property of Additional Persons Contributing to the Situation in Ukraine</quote> (79 Fed. Reg. 16169).</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H351C776A815540819BB50A8697907E62"><enum>(C)</enum><text>The government of any country if the Secretary of State determines that such government has repeatedly provided support for acts of international terrorism pursuant to any of the following:</text> <clause id="H39F91DB1A8094C28978753758D5DBAE2"><enum>(i)</enum><text>Section 1754(c)(1)(A) of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/4318">50 U.S.C. 4318(c)(1)(A)</external-xref>).</text></clause> 
<clause id="H1A522B9282E54077995E704CCD93D2D1"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>Section 620A of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2371">22 U.S.C. 2371</external-xref>).</text></clause> <clause id="H62E8EA5F626A4D3F92E67A006CE22AD7"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>Section 40 of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2780">22 U.S.C. 2780</external-xref>).</text></clause>
