<subsection id="HFDA145289D954B83B050D0E3F3DCC2C5"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Implementation guidance</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary, acting through the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, shall ensure that each senior contracting official (as defined in section 1737 of title 10, United States Code) for a contract described in subsection (a) has the discretion to implement the pilot program under this section efficiently and effectively by ensuring the following:</text> <paragraph id="HF280DCA06AED45AB867F2F92B72D5F70"><enum>(1)</enum><text>That the pilot program does not include any preferences for contract type or specific contract requirements.</text></paragraph>

<section id="H4DF319C7E1FC4259A1184576A416684B"><enum>842.</enum><header>Demonstration and prototyping program to advance international product support capabilities in a contested logistics environment</header> 
<subsection id="H895A1ED5F49B4A028C2E3B0ACFA187EB"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Contested logistics demonstration and prototyping program required</header><text>The Secretary of Defense shall establish a contested logistics demonstration and prototyping program to identify, develop, demonstrate, and field capabilities for product support in order to reduce or mitigate the risks associated with operations in a contested logistics environment.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HAB05CDE3A91C4220BC726BD1009D34C3"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>In carrying out the Program, the Secretary shall do the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="HAD8AC12BA36249649C02E320DF521020"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Identify ways to capitalize on the inherent interoperability, commonality, and interchangeability of platforms and information systems operated by the United States and one or more covered nations, including to enable effective maintenance and repair activities in a contested logistics environment.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB933EC284DCB4EB5A5374CD7540B79A3"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Determine, develop, or establish best practices to reduce time needed to return repaired equipment to service, including the use of—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HEAB617201FE14D0F81E60C2B8B06D013"><enum>(A)</enum><text>commercial best practices for rapid supply support; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3B10F69C53864E8EB6D558D615C1C375"><enum>(B)</enum><text>common or shared parts pools.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H74CF98C322794119BE0AF223E5648B18"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Explore opportunities to expand the ability to preposition or store materials needed to enable rapid surge capability or to support operations in a contested logistics environment.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H433FBBA8D36343A48E4C1CA211E685FB"><enum>(4)</enum><text>Identify, develop, demonstrate, and field effective and efficient means of conducting repairs of equipment away from permanent repair facilities.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HEA8C8728B7934B08AE664605F6533021"><enum>(5)</enum><text>Explore flexible approaches to contracting and use of partnership agreements to enable use or development of the capabilities of covered product support providers to effectively, efficiently, and timely satisfy the product support requirements of a combat commander and any applicable covered nation in a contested logistics environment.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H826632801EFA46EBBF5594A576639583"><enum>(6)</enum><text>Identify the resources, including any additional authorizations, required by the Secretary of Defense to reduce or mitigate the risks associated with operations in a contested logistics environment.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3E7A9B36086248D59BA559CFBB776EEC"><enum>(7)</enum><text>Identify and document impediments to the performance of product support by covered product support providers in a contested logistics environment, including impediments created by statute, regulation, policy, agency guidance, or limitations on expenditure, transfer, or receipt of funds for product support in contested logistics environments.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H38FDF3B6C0394E2F83AD0CA50D42DBFF"><enum>(8)</enum><text>Identify and document any statutory or regulatory waivers or exemptions that may be applicable or necessary to enable the United States and covered nations to jointly carry out product support activities in contested logistics environments located outside of the United States, including, for each such waiver and exemption—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HEFC7704030714494A6AA00693A560188"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the person responsible for requesting such waiver or exemption;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB250AE0E4FFF4ECA86EBBA8BB9DF3B7C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the criteria for approval of such waiver or exemption; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H0846374554384957A7D4D3CAE6560674"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the person responsible for approving such waiver or exemption.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HDB5FE86843214AEC985647E4313BFB51"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Advance planning and preparation</header><text>The Secretary may establish a product support arrangement, including an agreement for prepositioning or storage of materials, with a covered product support provider to enable a rapid response in a contingency operation (as defined in section 101(a) of title 10, United States Code) to the product support requirements of such contingency operation.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H80773593AC36450AAD02230F8FBF5772"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Authorities</header><text>In carrying out the Program, the Secretary may, in accordance with section 3 of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2753">22 U.S.C. 2753</external-xref>), use the authorities under sections 2342, 2474, 3601, 4021, and 4022 of title 10, United States Code.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HDE61382617B64A0D97B48C39E7CFF035"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than 24 months after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report summarizing Program activities, including—</text> 
<paragraph id="H5EB21AD1ACD440F0860B726FC4843309"><enum>(1)</enum><text>any recommendations to reduce impediments to meeting the requirements of a combatant command or covered nation for product support in a contested logistics environment;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H265A021E8FD14BF28A59F6E05686236B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>a summary of impediments identified under subsection (b)(7) and specific recommendations for necessary changes to statutory, regulatory, policy, agency guidance, or current limitations on expenditure, transfer, or receipt of funds to carry out the product support activities under this pilot indefinitely;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE5BD9D4EBA584A8394D2178F5BC9E077"><enum>(3)</enum><text>a summary of waivers or exemptions identified under subsection (b)(8), along with any recommendations for changes to the processes for obtaining such waivers or exemptions; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDC2DAD8F475E4806BA5760093DBEE7CD"><enum>(4)</enum><text>recommendations for improving the Program, including whether to extend or make the Program permanent.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H5AE6B6ADF2C046CEA858F68C7F8B7F14"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Development and promulgation of Department of Defense guidance</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall issue guidance implementing the Program.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H64B4952A1EB74F8FA31BCF54A4CF07CF"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text>The authority under this section shall terminate on the date that is three years after the date of the enactment of this Act.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H269F62E2E9E64CB0B05D8B53AFA43EB4"><enum>(h)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="HA2061FC3417B4C3DA52E126A1719D069"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Contested logistics environment</header><text>The term <quote>contested logistics environment</quote> has the meaning given such term in section 2926 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA3AC86BECADF444FA500D0A5260F6A76"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Covered nations</header><text>The term <quote>covered nation</quote> means—</text> <subparagraph id="H78BC3C188CE140C4A575BCCE1FA5DF33"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Australia;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF055C69B057A4BCF8A71BF8262FF1925"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Canada;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HC426FEC25E744FF38055E73137094B15"><enum>(C)</enum><text>New Zealand;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H5CFC55946A3240E8A9449CCCAC367E0E"><enum>(D)</enum><text>the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H6AB8820BE4384AA083A6BB165B0F047E"><enum>(E)</enum><text>other nations as designated as a covered nation for the purposes of this Program by the Secretary.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H80FB8DFF70E84D20881D85EFF354F7C6"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Covered product support provider</header><text>The term <quote>covered product support provider</quote> means—</text> <subparagraph id="H3B596DC8B7F642CE8C8A4F687C5DC039"><enum>(A)</enum><text>a product support provider that includes an entity within the government of a covered nation;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H27AE488A48FF45AE8D0F631D73FE2D6A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>a private sector product support provider; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H6781A8EEB8C84F78A97CFCC7F27BE6CC"><enum>(C)</enum><text>a product support integrator domiciled in the United States or a covered nation.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1F9FAB70C5BB418CA4F14085D934609E"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Product support; product support integrator; product support provider</header><text>The terms <quote>product support</quote>, <quote>product support integrator</quote>, and <quote>product support provider</quote> have the meanings given, respectively, in section 4324 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5BF6872432A840DABD28171508466C86"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Product support arrangement</header> <subparagraph id="H6E001A54C6E2418E9F59673681C49F78"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The term <quote>product support arrangement</quote> means a contract, task order, or any other type of agreement or arrangement, between the United States and a covered product support provider, for the performance of the functions described in subparagraph (B) with respect to—</text>

<clause id="HCB49C89A483947198C89625341B1E79A"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>Sustainment support.</text></clause> <clause id="H6356CC0B872948D39C683FCB86B95DBA"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>Contractor logistics support.</text></clause>

<subsection id="H059C400963EC4DEE8B7E0DB8F35C06D9"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The commander of a combatant command, upon providing a written determination to a senior contracting official (as defined in section 1737 of title 10, United States Code), may request use of the special authorities described in subsection (b)—</text> <paragraph id="H65746BCA4A0F402794F7DBFEDBC861AF"><enum>(1)</enum><text>in support of a contingency operation (as defined in section 101(a) of title 10, United States Code);</text></paragraph>

<paragraph id="H156994374EF94819948454896C38CF4A"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">for purposes of protecting the national security interests of the United States during directed operations that are below the threshold of traditional armed conflict.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H711D9557901D454DB923B8FB930BC741"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Special authorities described</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The special authorities for contracting that may be used by the senior contracting official to rapidly respond to time-sensitive or unplanned emergency situations are as follows:</text>

<subsection id="HD48F5AD2D41145DE9BB92720F2DA4634"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Industry day</header> 
<paragraph id="HAEE89603E734429189494BD1883BDDBD"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than March 1, 2024, and not less frequently than annually thereafter, the Secretary of Defense shall conduct an event to be known as the <quote>industry day</quote>—</text> <subparagraph id="H51D4038547C74C35B40BE3EE05230B3E"><enum>(A)</enum><text>to raise awareness and understanding among officials of foreign governments, covered embassy personnel, and representatives of the defense industrial base with respect to the role of the Department of Defense in implementing the foreign military sales process and the Department of Defense security cooperation process; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4CBEC6F7BAC84E1EA47BB0FE3D6AE789"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to raise awareness—</text> <clause id="HCE9AE0B28F254F6E82C806EA5C0C6DD6"><enum>(i)</enum><text>within the private sector of the United States with respect to—</text> 
<subclause id="H4884ABD9F07142069937834F17A5721F"><enum>(I)</enum><text>foreign demand for United States weapon systems; and</text></subclause> <subclause id="H034B134E45104CC9B34474EB61CDD7AD"><enum>(II)</enum><text>potential foreign industry partnering opportunities; and</text></subclause></clause> 
<clause id="H30F5902DCE164CC2AEEF11B304537F2F"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>among officials of foreign governments and covered embassy personnel with respect to potential United States materiel solutions for capability needs.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HD56914749998431CB984C2EFED2AE019"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Format</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In conducting each industry day under paragraph (1), the Secretary of Defense, to the extent practicable, shall seek to maximize participation by representatives of the defense industrial base and government officials while minimizing cost, by—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H3580814094CD47578AC64EBC653F9483" commented="no"><enum>(A) </enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">ensuring that information provided at the industry day is unclassified;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H51B850611ED24C38AB01F31A3A566CC7"><enum>(B)</enum><text>making the industry day publicly accessible through teleconference or other virtual means; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4A5C8B6D7F034BFEBF4502E3FC7ECE51"><enum>(C)</enum><text>posting any supporting materials on a publicly accessible internet website.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2545731A93424093AB18ABEF30A2C4CE"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Covered embassy personnel</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this subsection, the term <quote>covered embassy personnel</quote> means personnel at United States diplomatic and consular posts and personnel of foreign missions located in the United States.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H99A8498013494A6785AE80165C435C81"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Senior-level industry advisory group</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with representatives of the defense industrial base, shall establish or designate senior-level individuals working in the defense industrial base to serve on an advisory group for the purpose of focusing on the role of the Department of Defense in the foreign military sales process and the Department of Defense security cooperation process. Such advisory group shall terminate on the date specified in subsection (f).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H23FA60E5AB0341DBB236BFD4638C29D5"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Department of Defense points of contact for foreign military sales</header> <paragraph id="HBD6C24E0EFE44454B2413E09AF187556"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment and the Secretary of each military department shall each designate an individual to serve as a single point of contact—</text>

<section id="H2B7DDD2F0F134C51BA51C54C75985A58" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>874.</enum><header>Pilot program to incentivize progress payments</header> 
<subsection id="HC516475E57324BEB94279A80D975662B" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Pilot program</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall establish and implement a pilot program to incentivize contractor performance by paying covered contractors a progress payment rate that is up to 10 percent higher than the customary progress payment rate on a contract-by-contract basis.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HEE2F86B234544A1C94D0D162892C4B62" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Incentive criteria</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Under Secretary shall develop and establish clear and measurable criteria for the payment to contractors of higher progress payments as described in subsection (a), including criteria for qualifying for such payments and the amount of such payments.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H7DA40ACAA27C423581E07DB0DBE1680D"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Applicability</header><text>The Under Secretary shall apply the criteria established under subsection (b) and any associated incentive on a contract-by-contract basis when determining whether to pay a contractor a higher progress payment under the pilot program established under subsection (a) and the amount of such payment.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H9B52281481EE459BBBD2A0FD66651127"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Participation voluntary</header><text>Participation in the pilot program established under subsection (a) shall be on a voluntary basis.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H836C586D2619480AADD98F908A55D22F"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Notice and comment</header><text>The Under Secretary shall issue the regulations implementing the pilot program established under subsection (a) and establishing the criteria required by subsection (b) after notice and an opportunity for public comment of not more than 30 days.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H086A14CA89CE431283C0042029383E4B" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(f)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than September 30, 2024, and annually thereafter, the Under Secretary for Acquisition and Sustainment shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives a report on the implementation and activities of the pilot program established under subsection (a), including a comprehensive list of contractors that received increased progress payments under the pilot program and the contracts with respect to which such increased progress payments were made.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HCFC2AF3CF5164E4A83047FBD4D98C7B6" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(g)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section:</text> <paragraph id="H61E1B3237CCC476D88569E968930D0CF" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Covered contractor</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>covered contractor</quote> means a contractor of the Department of Defense that is eligible for progress payments under section 3804 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H08435D0604644BB5913AA0CA5CA544E1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Customary progress payment rate</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>customary progress payment rate</term> refers to the rate of progress payments provided for under section 3804 of title 10, United States Code, and payable in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Federal Acquisition Regulation and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H31A72AEFEF514D70B7C67A3C606D7740"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Under Secretary</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>Under Secretary</quote> means the Under Secretary for Acquisition and Sustainment.</text></paragraph></subsection>

<section id="HC2C1B2F4868A45CA96FA2AD53A61D7BD" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>903.</enum><header>Establishment of Office of Strategic Capital</header> 
<subsection id="HFA0AB0222F5E42F4B0F078C922ECBD0C"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment of Office</header><text><external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/10/4">Chapter 4</external-xref> of title 10, United States Code, as amended by section 241, is further amended by adding at the end the following new section:</text> <quoted-block style="USC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H5949CC3CF84446F1AF06F6665EBFB0FB"> <section id="H5C14EE5374E64F548DB16AE93A177A32" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>149.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Office of Strategic Capital</header> <subsection id="HE9D5E3963CCA4DF097E7B89D5AEE7485" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Establishment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">There is in the Office of the Secretary of Defense an office to be known as the Office of Strategic Capital (in this section referred to as the <quote>Office</quote>).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF8560C4BB7014892A7976D8B67D5824C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Director</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Office shall be headed by a Director (in this section referred to as the <quote>Director</quote>), who shall be appointed by the Secretary from among employees in Senior Executive Service positions (as defined in section 3132 of title 5), or from outside the civil service who have successfully held equivalent positions.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H39CE0DEBB6954ADC8A5498F219C5EDA4" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Duties</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Office shall—</text> 
<paragraph id="H6F662EF3E74248D4B5CBE1F15C33E9D2" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">develop, integrate, and implement capital investment strategies proven in the commercial sector to shape and scale investment in critical technologies and assets; </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H76500879051D4D94BF37EB89CA835779" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">identify and prioritize promising critical technologies and assets that require capital assistance and have the potential to benefit the Department of Defense; and</text></paragraph>

<subparagraph id="H3457DB3B80694AAE80D7C1116A42126D" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>An eligible entity seeking capital assistance for an eligible investment under this subsection shall submit to the Director an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Director may require.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H62EDD8A8AD994E3EB48CBDE5594425ED" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Selection of investments</header><text>The Director shall establish criteria for selecting among eligible investments for which applications are submitted under subparagraph (A). <clause id="H2979E2288C624EFF9456F89087B61D28" commented="no"><enum>(ii)</enum><header>Administration of loans</header> 
<subclause id="H2F80225F5E5C451BA516D60DA6BE83FC" commented="no"><enum>(I)</enum><header>Interest rate</header> 
<item id="HDC2FE4DD8DAE41A9834B90884AAFECD4" commented="no"><enum>(aa)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Except as provided under item (bb), the interest rate on a loan provided under clause (i) shall be not less than the yield on marketable United States Treasury securities of a similar maturity to the maturity of the loan on the date of execution of the loan agreement.</text></item> <item id="HBCEE96C8CB4C4505B2676AF532483421" commented="no"><enum>(bb)</enum><header>Exception</header><text>The Director may waive the requirement under item (aa) with respect to an investment if the investment is determined by the Secretary of Defense to be vital to the national security of the United States.</text></item>

<paragraph id="HFD2EEAFAEA5F45FDB223B6BD41CFF47C"><enum>(2)</enum><text>shall report directly to the Secretary without intervening authority; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB55801040A3F4B4991823B688DDF0E29"><enum>(3)</enum><text>may communicate views on matters within the responsibility of the Unit directly to the Secretary without obtaining the approval or concurrence of any other official within the Department of Defense.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HFC2703E1DCCA424DA64386C4B2D2E9C0"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Responsibilities</header><text>The Unit shall have the following responsibilities:</text> <paragraph id="H6AB9B6BDF20A43929DAD53A12C78E74D"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Seek out, identify, and support development of and experimentation with commercial technologies that have the potential to be implemented within the Department of Defense.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2CF64E8B2D6645B9895F34CA0B8EFE34"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Accelerate the adoption or integration of commercial technologies within the Department of Defense to transform military capacity and capabilities.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H86AA9A675989448DBDDE194536EAABFD"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Serve as the principal liaison between the Department of Defense and individuals and entities in the national security innovation base, including entrepreneurs, startups, commercial technology companies, and venture capital sources.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H9B2E4F709A9747DCAB532B80B4AD00C5"><enum>(4)</enum><text>Carry out programs, projects, and other activities to strengthen the national security innovation base.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE73449F55BFB4FE18717052FA86D4498"><enum>(5)</enum><text>Coordinate and harmonize the activities of other organizations and elements of the Department of Defense on matters relating to commercial technologies, dual use technologies, and the innovation of such technologies.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB882C17048FF4A7486EC9F520DDAE0DF"><enum>(6)</enum><text>Coordinate and advise efforts among elements of the Department of Defense on matters relating to the development, procurement, and fielding of nontraditional capabilities.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF622FD1289E8404B81EB27AC99ADB9FB"><enum>(7)</enum><text>Coordinate with the Joint Staff and the commanders of the combatant commands to identify operational challenges that have the potential to be addressed through the use of nontraditional capabilities, including dual-use technologies, that are being developed and financed in the commercial sector.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCF75EEB1D6A74DE09E96D9022ED7AC15"><enum>(8)</enum><text>Using funds made available to the Unit—</text> <subparagraph id="H93CDDFFE87674B288DB1A814CE9B6CFF"><enum>(A)</enum><text>select projects to be carried out by one or more of the service-level innovation organizations;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HA35CC1AAA2A348B3B35DDA01E92A71EC"><enum>(B)</enum><text>allocate funds to service-level innovation organizations to carry out such projects; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H4D5DFAD91A794FA1B8BFC655F50D0180"><enum>(C)</enum><text>monitor the execution of such projects by the service-level innovation organizations.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H24546EC74CC540A8BA0CEA6094D09CA5"><enum>(9)</enum><text>Serve as the principal liaison between the Department of Defense, nontraditional defense contractors, investors in nontraditional defense companies, and departments and agencies of the Federal Government pursing nontraditional capabilities similar to those pursued by the Department.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HAC5DDD5A3E6F43EE9FE4914526B1F952"><enum>(10)</enum><text>Lead engagement with industry, academia, and other nongovernment entities to develop—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H992232985C7F434DA7E575BEED4843D7"><enum>(A)</enum><text>domestic capacity with respect to innovative, commercial, and dual-use technologies and the use of nontraditional defense contractors; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H42E8627CDE55463396832DC19A24B468"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the capacity of international allies and partners of the United States with respect to such technologies and the use of such contractors.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCCA423505BBD419797699B1F8ECD66CD"><enum>(11)</enum><text>Carry out such other activities as the Secretary of Defense determines appropriate.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H2E2CE24FEB8E48BB88EB0FD945D26B10"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Support for multi-stakeholder partnerships</header> <paragraph id="H837810BD069A44A78BD02503C6EFB58A"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The Director shall identify and support multi-stakeholder research and innovation partnerships that—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HF6A19E5514684BF894B3D698A8AC9CB5"><enum>(A)</enum><text>have the potential to generate technologies, processes, products, or other solutions that address national defense or security needs; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2B3A1CA82E384146A5C8DACCBDC9E44B"><enum>(B)</enum><text>have as an objective the technology transfer or commercialization of the work product generated by the partnership, which may include work product that incorporates Government-developed intellectual property licensed to the partnership in accordance with paragraph (3).</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB4D515F4F7454FA0905C5FFF122072AA"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Support provided by the Director to a multi-stakeholder research and innovation partnership under this subsection may include—</text> <subparagraph id="HDD263846D46D4B4EB43E4A26610FF5DC"><enum>(A)</enum><text>providing funding or other resources to the partnership;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H19EBE18E78B94E6B8111E4ED1B51BB21"><enum>(B)</enum><text>participating in the partnership;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H66FA8600DC2740E5B6780A23C839287A"><enum>(C)</enum><text>providing technical and technological advice and guidance to the partnership;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HB680F260DCA64CE697542ACA4D8E8004"><enum>(D)</enum><text>suggesting and introducing other participants for inclusion in the partnership;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H7BA8C9FDF13447379B19A2B2207BC4AE"><enum>(E)</enum><text>providing the partnership with insight into desired solutions for defense and security needs; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H15E918C00C0C4E4099316761E25DF80B"><enum>(F)</enum><text>such other forms of support as the Director determines appropriate.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6DF16ED329E041A7BCCD7E5B145915D6"><enum>(3)</enum><text>To the extent the Director determines appropriate, the Director shall seek to actively inform potential participants in multi-stakeholder research and innovation partnerships of the availability of Government-developed intellectual property that may be licensed to the partnership.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HFEB53B690197449985DD9CC9A02A03DB"><enum>(4)</enum><text>On an annual basis, the Director shall submit to the Secretary of Defense and the congressional defense committees a report on the activities, advances, outcomes, and work product of the multi-stakeholder research and innovation partnerships supported under this subsection.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <subsection id="H83FB9CF4EAC246F7AA8635B3C7B9777D" commented="no"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text>

<subparagraph id="H5C6C08E581FC4E2FAB7B8345B8577C74" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Non-profit organizations that provide policy, research, outreach, operations, organizational, management, testing, evaluation, technology transfer, legal, financial, or advocacy expertise.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H59E884A190514FE4AD5400C3705FA5B8" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><text>For-profit commercial enterprises that may be publicly or privately owned, early stage or mature, and incorporated or operating by another ownership structure.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HCF57089DC8CF4652802DC75897A0CEC3" commented="no"><enum>(D)</enum><text>Departments or agencies of the Federal Government with expertise, operations, or resources related to the objectives of the multi-stakeholder research and innovation partnership.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HBC0D18F25E7748029FC5FAEFBA894D10" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The term <quote>nontraditional capability</quote> means a solution to an operational challenge that can significantly leverage commercial innovation or external capital with minimal dependencies on fielded systems.</text></paragraph>

<section id="HF1B03FAFC9DC43098C72E0B0A94BE380"><enum>918.</enum><header>Technology release and foreign disclosure reform initiative</header> 
<subsection id="HA0CC9D6359D54684A84EA700685509B1"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Initiative required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline"></text> <paragraph id="HF3EC1957D4234D5FB1A7D727AC8587B8"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of Defense shall carry out an initiative to reform and improve the policies, processes, and procedures applicable to technology release and foreign disclosure decisions by the Department of Defense.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB7B5D03CCFB24C51A8E4A3035122968D"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Objectives</header><text>The objectives of such initiative shall be—</text> <subparagraph id="HBBB0001049D74D89B4A0FD9EAE659C93"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to develop recommendations for the continuous improvement of such policies, processes, and procedures within the Department and across other departments and agencies of the Federal Government involved in technology release and foreign disclosure decisions;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H9CE5C716D1DF40568EF1A6534709A167"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to increase efficiency and reduce timelines for the processing of such decisions;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HD0213E2EC55C49E4A91AE6E69778F23E"><enum>(C)</enum><text>to standardize, to the extent practicable, processes and information sharing systems applicable to such decisions; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H8A2C584F6FDD4F63BEA595E982C63919"><enum>(D)</enum><text>to provide for the continuous exchange of timely and relevant information among—</text> <clause id="HF10F429A83B84092961BD0059CD99180"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the principal organizations involved in technology release and foreign disclosure decisions;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HB488BD5E40C54C58BF9810253E547A60"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the broader acquisition and program executive officer communities; and</text></clause> <clause id="HF4A3B1432B5E49DBA0AEBBDC853F3A22"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>interagency partners of the Department.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB215F0AD7200422DB4AA392CEC0DB659"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Method of implementation</header><text>For purposes of the initiative required under paragraph (1), the Secretary of Defense may—</text> <subparagraph id="H2C65C95449A74E0E9A25BB19D091733E"><enum>(A)</enum><text>establish a new initiative;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H82F099F1E13F4D1189E833BBEE660EA5"><enum>(B)</enum><text>modify an existing initiative of the Department of Defense; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HA6A057720D25401493E9042CADDB1B01"><enum>(C)</enum><text>carry out the initiative through a combination of the approaches described in subparagraphs (A) and (B).</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HD14988BFCD2B4247857714E7CB41C9F2"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Metrics</header> 
<paragraph id="HFFE52EBA71E2427FB7B8FF0F14F20A59" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>In conjunction with the initiative required under subsection (a), the Under Secretary of Defense for Policy shall develop metrics for the management of the technology release and foreign disclosure process to provide objective and subjective measures of performance and improve senior leader decision-making in the Department of Defense.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H20876A2AB78D4C7BB5661220970C17C7"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The metrics developed under paragraph (1) shall include—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H3CB5F15B5C2E4F00845E702524BAC9C2" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text>methods for tracking individual technology release and foreign disclosure decisions made by the Defense Technology Security Administration;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3E8DAC84A2824D1EBC4F75ECCAC44A93" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>objectives and deadlines related to the completion of such decisions; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H98F915A416C64919B88AD97A274DEE33" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><text>a method of prioritizing among technology release and foreign disclosure requests that takes into account—</text> <clause id="H7B340A4A8A714F678D3ECDA681F37BE2"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the importance of the request to the national security of the United States; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H769597D4C6CF46DB93D4DF2D8614E224"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the risks associated with the release or disclosure.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H56B6A88E426D406BBCA295B438D2442E" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Briefing required</header><text>Not later than June 1, 2024, the Under Secretary of Defense for Policy shall provide to the congressional defense committees a briefing on the metrics developed under paragraph (1).</text></paragraph></subsection>

<section id="H0F090A889CBF48C6ACC213C1FE90E0D4"><enum>921.</enum><header>Next generation business health metrics</header> 
<subsection id="H1F1CA018F4A140CC9315A48507E0BC12"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Metrics required</header><text>The Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretaries of the military departments, shall develop an updated set of business health metrics to inform decision-making by senior leaders of the Department of Defense.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H21929E958C4D4E479FB10ACB281750FE"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>In developing the metrics required by subsection (a), the Secretary of Defense shall—</text> 
<paragraph id="H0F5D743E45454B33BE6EE63AA9EBAB0E"><enum>(1)</enum><text>using the latest literature on performance measurement, determine what additional new metrics should be implemented, or current metrics should be adapted, to reduce output-based measures and emphasize objective, measurable indicators aligned to enduring strategic goals of the Department of Defense;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HAE31EE5AA8064FF4B08FEA0CF2F80809"><enum>(2)</enum><text>assess the current business processes of the Department and provide recommendations to align the metrics with available data sources to determine what gaps might exist in such processes;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H13F53FC73F0544948DD399FA1686FFFD"><enum>(3)</enum><text>ensure that data can be collected automatically and, on a long-term basis, in a manner that provides for longitudinal analysis;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HBE9B209199084D989A1A35F7E78FB3F9"><enum>(4)</enum><text>link the metrics with the Strategic Management Plan and other performance documents guiding the Department;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H57646EF520254EF88571FD4D8C98563C"><enum>(5)</enum><text>identify any shortfalls in resources, data, training, policy, or law that could be an impediment to implementing the metrics;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H34656526179E4FC4BE77EB7150D4A8CE"><enum>(6)</enum><text>revise leading and lagging indicators associated with each such metric to provide a benchmark against which to assess progress;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H31C224BFEF0C4EDBA85069ED277E6356"><enum>(7)</enum><text>improve visualization of and comprehension for the use of the metrics in data-driven decision-making, including adoption of new policies and training as needed;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H4524C45018934225853FD6DA4D33189A"><enum>(8)</enum><text>incorporate the ability to aggregate and disaggregate data to provide the ability to focus on functional, component-level metrics; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H933D0F4C7ED14C7DAD6613CC39A9F471"><enum>(9)</enum><text>increase standardization of the use and collection of business health metrics across the Department.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HC1543CE134474647B9F307C4DC59F3EB"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Additional support</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense may enter into a contract or other agreement with a federally funded research and development center or university-affiliated research center to support the development of the metrics required under subsection (a).</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H2109A0053AD642B880F09246CEE3903C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>922.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Independent assessment of defense business enterprise architecture</header> 
<subsection id="H2FFFAB694E844DB3B3F210B8483D9642" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall seek to enter into a contract or other agreement with a federally funded research and development center or a university affiliated research center to conduct an independent assessment of the defense business enterprise architecture developed under section 2222(e) of title 10, United States Code.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H63655F430B20408699C5A17877F16DE5" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The assessment required by subsection (a) shall include the following elements:</text> 
<paragraph id="H727F2D9C383F4B0EB02722CB0F1B4DBA" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of the effectiveness of the defense business enterprise architecture as of the date of the enactment of this Act in providing an adequate and useful framework for planning, managing, and integrating the business systems of the Department of Defense.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HED1B13E1948444F085CB26FC4C1120F5" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A comparison of the defense business enterprise architecture with similar models in use by other government agencies in the United States, foreign governments, and major commercial entities, including an assessment of any lessons from such models that might be applied to the defense business enterprise architecture.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCB57ABF2674941E6B7A074A7F6FA9042" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of the adequacy of the defense business enterprise architecture in informing business process reengineering and being sufficiently responsive to changes in business processes over time.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB2B68632CD37444E9C723464991E408D" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An identification of any shortfalls or implementation challenges in the utility of the defense business enterprise architecture.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H191CD31A2A2E471F85A0BFDC71BF501B" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Recommendations for replacement of the existing defense business enterprise architecture or for modifications to the existing architecture to make that architecture and the process for updating that architecture more effective and responsive to the business process needs of the Department.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H8C8153110CCD4C4E833FE0415F50F7C1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Interim briefing</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than April 1, 2024, the Secretary of Defense shall provide to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a briefing on the status of the assessment required by subsection (a).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H6D2B789FAD2048C7AEA1B95CE37CA324" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(d)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Final report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than January 30, 2025, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a report on the results of the assessment required by subsection (a). </text></subsection></section> <section id="H2A2088CD028B4DBBBD3C7E50CA467206" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>923.</enum><header>Future force design of the Department of the Air Force</header> <subsection id="HAB0D2E387AC44A46AC62D2B85894B111"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Force design required</header><text>Not later than August 31, 2024, the Secretary of the Air Force shall develop a force design for the Air Force and Space Force projected through 2050.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H8DEDB870DCF94C058B0444A86A0E7A53"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The force design under subsection (a) shall address—</text> <paragraph id="H60B24DC44DAF428BBE16EA8C6517345F"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the concepts, capabilities, and structural elements (including size and form) of the Air Force and Space Force that are necessary to ensure those forces effectively execute their core functions through 2050 in support of the National Defense Strategy and the National Military Strategy;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3131AB33084943BE8A501FFEC6E60CAE"><enum>(2)</enum><text>force structure, including the development of capabilities (including platforms and systems) at the correct level of capacity to address the challenges outlined by the National Defense Strategy and the National Military Strategy;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF94E818997D64A7599B830615E816CD7"><enum>(3)</enum><text>force composition, including recruitment and development of human capital, effective distribution of forces in the total force, and policies to increase career flexibility across the various components of the force;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HFB327125AB924B9D9D91B506F2E20461"><enum>(4)</enum><text>organizational design, including development of potential models to increase agility and operational effectiveness across the Air Force and Space Force; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H781B8AC5DA6A4DCE8BBA1F8410F755D0"><enum>(5)</enum><text>such other matters as the Secretary of the Air Force determines to be relevant.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H9CA9651924E64F19A42CED4D30E23EFE"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Information to congress</header><text>Not later than 60 days after completion of the force design required under subsection (a), the Secretary of the Air Force shall—</text> <paragraph id="H28CA5BCFDA5C4E3AA2D2523CE9DA7401"><enum>(1)</enum><text>submit a summary of the force design to the congressional defense committees; and</text></paragraph>

<section id="H8943607B2B6140CBA13F65E70493A98E"><enum>1012.</enum><header>Drug interdiction and counter-drug activities</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 112(a)(3) of title 32, United States Code, is amended by striking <quote>$5,000</quote> and inserting <quote>$15,000</quote>.</text></section> <section id="HC47D3F2334494D2B8D9F7EFA49930B12"><enum>1013.</enum><header>Disruption of fentanyl trafficking</header> <subsection id="H49FFEB9DF7CD461EB0C93E914CFC5AF4"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Development of strategy to counter fentanyl trafficking</header> <paragraph id="H0F4A160DFC314845867A0508A641F050"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Strategy</header><text>Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the Secretary of State and the Attorney General and in coordination with appropriate Federal, State, Tribal, and local law enforcement agencies, shall develop and submit to the appropriate congressional committees a strategy to address threats to the national security of the United States caused or exacerbated by fentanyl trafficking.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H6D1632653E904318A54A684D029B8D4B"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Contents</header><text>The strategy required by paragraph (1) shall outline how the Secretary of Defense will—</text> <subparagraph id="H3D86742A61174F309A7CDBACE4FD792B"><enum>(A)</enum><text>leverage existing authorities regarding counterdrug and counter-transnational organized crime activities with a counter-fentanyl nexus to detect and monitor activities related to fentanyl trafficking;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H003F1BE203B44FC29BFE784356F90731"><enum>(B)</enum><text>leverage existing authorities, as appropriate, to support operations to counter fentanyl trafficking carried out by Federal, State, Tribal, and local law enforcement agencies, or foreign security forces;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H40CD40DBB93344D79B697770119E4F75"><enum>(C)</enum><text>coordinate efforts of the Department of Defense for the detection and monitoring of aerial, maritime, and surface traffic suspected of carrying fentanyl bound for the United States, including efforts to unify the use of technology, surveillance, and related resources across air and maritime domains to counter fentanyl trafficking, including with respect to data collection, data processing, and integrating sensors across such domains, consistent with paragraphs (6) and (10) of section 284(b) of title 10, United States Code, and section 124 of title 10, United States Code;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFDD4C0E0368C4819B9895E919E43C9BB"><enum>(D)</enum><text>provide Department of Defense-specific capabilities to support activities by the United States Government and foreign security forces to detect and monitor the trafficking of fentanyl and precursor chemicals used in fentanyl production, consistent with relevant existing law;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H6FBBC94244894E88A190432DF7FD7102"><enum>(E)</enum><text>leverage existing counterdrug and counter-transnational organized crime programs of the Department to counter fentanyl trafficking;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H7E3132F3D9114CE1ABD6836A3DAC5C3A"><enum>(F)</enum><text>assess existing training programs of the Department and assess whether opportunities exist for the provision of training for Federal, State, Tribal, and local law enforcement agencies to counter fentanyl trafficking, consistent with section 284(b)(5) of title 10, United States Code;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HD45A728FA5CB4ECC973DF55BE8A80786"><enum>(G)</enum><text>engage with foreign security forces to ensure the counterdrug and counter-transnational organized crime programs of the Department—</text> 
<clause id="H36EDC51A936044C3B6DEAD82E3CA8AF3"><enum>(i)</enum><text>support efforts to counter fentanyl trafficking; and</text></clause> <clause id="H78A91B6F98FB4526899B69EB4E98C56D"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>build capacity to interdict fentanyl in foreign countries, including programs to train security forces in partner countries to counter fentanyl trafficking, including countering illicit flows of fentanyl precursors, consistent with sections 284(c) and 333 of title 10, United States Code;</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HE3A651A744A64AC891B6AC9A3218954E"><enum>(H)</enum><text>increase domain awareness to detect and monitor fentanyl trafficking through the North American Defense Ministerial and the bilateral defense working groups and bilateral military cooperation roundtables with Canada and Mexico;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB13EF0BE968A4F668805246D76BA1D5C"><enum>(I)</enum><text>evaluate existing policies, procedures, processes, resources, and existing joint interagency task forces focused on supporting the countering of fentanyl trafficking by Federal, State, Tribal, and local law enforcement agencies, consistent with existing counterdrug and counter-transnational organized crime authorities;</text></subparagraph>

<section id="H3DF84AC098864DC19109B01C5644FC2D" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1070.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Report on use of tactical fighter aircraft for deployments and homeland defense missions</header>

<section id="HB719F31914554DD58F2889AAB8430561" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1076.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Comprehensive assessment of Marine Corps Force Design 2030</header> 
<subsection id="H56A1DDA8FEF347EAB927A90DD6A66557" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall seek to enter into an agreement with a federally funded research and development center for the conduct of an independent review, assessment, and analysis of the modernization initiatives of the Marine Corps. The agreement shall provide that not later than one year after the date on which the Secretary and the center enter into the agreement, the center shall provide to the Secretary a report on the findings of the review, assessment, and analysis. Upon receipt of the report, the Secretary shall transmit the report to the congressional defense committees.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H62BEC7191C884E0D835A376E4CE0E6F7" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The report required under subsection (a) shall include the following elements:</text> 
<paragraph id="H278B0F0623484BED93254A0473F92B23" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of changes in the National Defense Strategy, Defense Planning Guidance, the Joint Warfighting Concept, and other strategic documents and concepts that informed Force Design modernization requirements.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H67782206B1024954822079E1AB2EA662" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of how the Marine Corps, consistent with authorized end strength, can be structured, organized, trained, equipped, and postured to meet the challenges of future competition, crisis, and conflict to include discussion of multiple structural options as relevant and the tradeoffs between different options.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC80A38D4D5F24AD0A348541599AFE45F" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of the ability of the defense innovation base and defense industrial base to develop and produce the technologies required to implement the Force Design modernization plan published by the Marine Corps on a timeline and at production rates sufficient to sustain military operations.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFD0DA4EFB9004B5B8A62073D6F65AC4F" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of forward infrastructure and the extent to which installations are operationalized to deter, compete, and prevail during conflict in support of the Marine Corps modernization.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H4A44E26A45B14702A816A43124DC01CB" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of whether the Marine Corps is in compliance with the statutory organization and functions prescribed in section 8063 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H484F918C9FDA44369D1816536E0A86E3" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(6)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of the current retention and recruiting environment and the ability of the Marine Corps to sustain manpower requirements necessary for operational requirements levied by title 10, United States Code, in light of the published Force Design plan.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5F534DC83C204DDE8A65F731C34B2EB8" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(7)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The extent to which the modernization initiatives within the Marine Corps are nested within applicable joint warfighting concepts.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFEF17DE5BA82496F81FAF14DC2047745" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(8)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of whether the modernization of the Marine Corps is consistent with the strategy of integrated deterrence.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD0DE025E25C445608F2A84A6901648C8" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(9)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of the ability of the Marine Corps to generate required force elements for the Immediate Ready Force and the Contingency Ready Force, based on current and planned end strength and structure.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H0EE1220CFAA149E78B2CA0A5266C1E73" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(10)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The extent to which the plan for modernized capabilities published by the Marine Corps can be integrated across the Joint Force, including warfighting concepts at the combatant command level.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE7BDAF525F1248809FD9859CF01F086D" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(11)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The extent to which the modernization efforts of the Marine Corps currently meet the requirements of the current plans of the combatant commanders and global force management operations, including a description of any mechanisms that exist to ensure geographic combatant requirements inform Marine Corps modernization efforts.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H316710B9725A4D67A16EF671C076818D" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(12)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The extent to which modeling and simulation, experimentation, wargaming, and other analytic methods support the changes incorporated into the modernization initiatives of the Marine Corps, including the underlying assumptions and outcomes of such analyses.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H033450538C66481B84C27173039E0E98" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(13)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An inventory of extant or planned investments as part of the modernization efforts of the Marine Corps, disaggregated by the following capability areas and including actual or projected dates of Initial Operational Capability and Full Operational Capability:</text> <subparagraph id="HC164CB9F497A4E9FBD3BCD67075F87EB" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Command and Control.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HBCB2E19D614F433F8904E4A4E547D039" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Information.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H906B28DF753C401DB31833CF2290FDE3" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Intelligence.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H8C657096E6874556B399BF46A0BF02FB" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Fires.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HC31FA30EFC61488687D17B0C5E930D0F" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(E)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Movement and Maneuver.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H26B43F49515A4C60836751883E9BE5DD" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(F)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Protection.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HD9CE6B75BCFA44FD8264B323C1E5534A" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(G)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Sustainment.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H894531C97DBA46A4B946A400E0240C02" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(14)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An inventory of divestments of capability or capacity, whether force structure or equipment, starting in fiscal year 2020, including—</text> <subparagraph id="H39CAB9D216F443A29D3C25B18802ACCC" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a timeline of the progress of each divestment;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4CFF375CE12C472A9CB1E971386BD109" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the type of force structure or equipment divested or reduced;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HA693A7980A384FD7803725F5DFD74103" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the percentage of force structure of equipment divested or reduced, including any equipment entered into inventory management or other form of storage;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H11B6E7B129F5461D85D2954AE85B0C4F" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the rationale and context behind such divestment; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H65F3F21321D849E5AA21E57965BA222F" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(E)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">an identification of whether such divestment affects the ability of the Marine Corps to meet the requirements of Global Force Management process and the operational plans.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HAC650DE33D3549E880BCC6B8D1AC4311" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(15)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of how observations regarding the invasion and defense of Ukraine affect the feasibility, advisability, and suitability of the modernization plans published by the Marine Corps.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H2E192B7E4D5E4B70BBCCEF2C2E37F3B1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Classification of report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The report required under subsection (a) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified appendix to the extent required to ensure that the report is accurate and complete. </text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H68C1E3AD8647489A9673D57B451D17EE" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1077.</enum><header> Assessment and recommendations relating to infrastructure, capacity, resources, and personnel on Guam</header> 
<subsection id="H4A601B3C13ED48F3A42217C9EB067A22"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Assessment</header><text>The Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Commander of United States Indo-Pacific Command, shall assess the infrastructure, capacity, resource, and personnel requirements for Guam during fiscal years 2024 through 2029 to meet United States strategic objectives.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H3BB8979854A34E7A94F8BBCA0A27A66D"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The assessment under subsection (a) shall include the following elements:</text> 
<paragraph id="HD131FDC6BE9340C18C21232D67EADCC0"><enum>(1)</enum><text>An appraisal of the potential role Guam could play as a key logistics and operational hub for the United States military in the Indo-Pacific region.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H0ADE9DCAB52247D093202BD4FD6CF3EF"><enum>(2)</enum><text>An assessment of whether current Department of Defense infrastructure, capacity, resources, and personnel in Guam are sufficient to meet the expected demands during relevant operations and contingency scenarios.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD5A21CEE8756400E9D806864F08A27EB"><enum>(3)</enum><text>An assessment of the adequacy of civilian infrastructure in Guam for supporting the requirements of United States Indo-Pacific Command, including—</text> <subparagraph id="HC605BFED9E4F47EBA871798D4C617B34"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the resilience of such infrastructure in the event of a natural disaster; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HD2BF5FB757284BE19EB2CC5216EC0C0A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the vulnerability of such infrastructure to cyber threats.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HEF6EB36DC95B486392EA7D56C611280E"><enum>(4)</enum><text>A plan, including timelines and associated estimated costs, to improve Department of Defense infrastructure, capacity, resources, and personnel in Guam during fiscal years 2024 through 2029 to meet United States Indo-Pacific Command strategic objectives, including the need for Department of Defense civilian recruiting and retention programs, such as cost-of-living adjustments, initiatives for dealing with any shortages of civilian employees, and programs to improve quality-of-life for personnel assigned to Guam.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB0B89BCEE6E04176A3C788B6FFF65719"><enum>(5)</enum><text>An assessment of the implementation of Joint Task Force Micronesia.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H703BFD370C1D47F7A3EB7FA164611361"><enum>(6)</enum><text>Any other matters determined relevant by the Secretary.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HDE40D0DE100443B2AF0B1BEFCEF86E67"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report including the results of the assessment required under subsection (a).</text></subsection></section> <section id="H4A0799BE65814AC7AD183BC70A5A1F7A"><enum>1078.</enum><header>Feasibility study on conversion of Joint Task Force North into Joint Interagency Task Force North</header> <subsection id="HC27D986F6DF644F7AE1F7C15941D1AA9"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the head of any relevant Federal department or agency and acting through the Under Secretary of Defense for Policy, shall submit to the congressional defense committees a feasibility study on converting the Joint Task Force North of the United States Northern Command into a joint interagency task force to be known as the <quote>Joint Interagency Task Force North</quote>.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HCB04747A2E404E20B70C178C2971E946"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The study under (a) shall include the following elements:</text> <paragraph id="HC8B6084A4B2C44278FB9E3EBB0F3BEEA"><enum>(1)</enum><text>A description of the mission of a Joint Interagency Task Force North.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H229A2D000A614F618123B321E3FF3936"><enum>(2)</enum><text>A detailed description of the resources of the Department of Defense, including personnel, facilities, and operating costs, necessary to convert Joint Task Force North into a joint interagency task force.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H325BC1A45E4E4418B900A678690B1AEB"><enum>(3)</enum><text>An identification of—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H76BFFB01DA87468787FC1005171955D9"><enum>(A)</enum><text>each relevant department and agency of the United States Government the participation in a Joint Interagency Task Force North of which is necessary in order to enable a Joint Interagency Task Force North to effectively carry out its mission; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H8ECD8A772B3F497391A80D9EAD3A7088"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the interagency arrangements necessary to ensure effective participation by each such department and agency.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE8944DD217314E98A090E1D69E569A15"><enum>(4)</enum><text>An identification of each international liaison necessary for a Joint Interagency Task Force North to effectively carry out its mission.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9E06CD36CFF34F66B8272E1853428F72"><enum>(5)</enum><text>A description of the bilateral and multilateral agreements with foreign partners and regional and international organizations that would support the implementation of the mission of the Joint Interagency Task Force North.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCAABA9050DBF4D379D80E78BDDD4F1A8"><enum>(6)</enum><text>A description of the relationship between a Joint Interagency Task Force North and Joint Interagency Task Force South of the United States Southern Command.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7E0BB8F45E5A4B578DEF3E705393DAD5"><enum>(7)</enum><text>A description of the likely relationship between a Joint Interagency Task Force North and the relevant security forces of the Government of Mexico and the Government of the Bahamas.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8E0D9AA6678F4919B76EBAA0066B36EC"><enum>(8)</enum><text>A recommendation on whether a Joint Interagency Task Force North should be an enduring entity and a discussion of the circumstances under which the mission of a Joint Interagency Task Force North would transition to one or more entities within the United States Government other than the United States Northern Command.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H414A6FF776CF41F2AF05BCEAB53E78F6"><enum>(9)</enum><text>Any recommendations for additional legal authority needed for the Joint Interagency Task Force North to effectively carry out its mission.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB8E2DD5BE46349A1B349EFFAB626B99E"><enum>(10)</enum><text>Any other matters the Secretary of Defense considers relevant.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HD018F69F6F9B4610B17C0720D693A033"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The study required by subsection (a) shall be submitted in unclassified form but may include a classified annex.</text></subsection></section></subtitle>
