<section id="H8AC496436C5E4CADB32CEB7D14D57555" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1250A.</enum><header>Limitation on withdrawal from the North Atlantic Treaty Organization</header> 
<subsection id="H9210BD4C2C444755852FCEC401DAEAA1"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Opposition of Congress to suspension, termination, denunciation, or withdrawal from North Atlantic Treaty</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The President shall not suspend, terminate, denounce, or withdraw the United States from the North Atlantic Treaty, done at Washington, DC, April 4, 1949, except by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, provided that two-thirds of the Senators present concur, or pursuant to an Act of Congress.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HBF3B4FA945324EB28944CD2C6956D091"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Limitation on the use of funds</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">No funds authorized or appropriated by any Act may be used to support, directly or indirectly, any decision on the part of any United States Government official to suspend, terminate, denounce, or withdraw the United States from the North Atlantic Treaty, done at Washington, DC, April 4, 1949, except by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, provided that two-thirds of the Senators present concur, or pursuant to an Act of Congress.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H61DE7CE8374C428DB6BF8E0CC9FC3CBD"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Notification of treaty action</header> 
<paragraph id="HD9B45111A92F4FBAB7DD8B333770BFE6"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Consultation</header><text>Prior to the notification described in paragraph (2), the President shall consult with the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives in relation to any initiative to suspend, terminate, denounce, or withdraw the United States from the North Atlantic Treaty.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6091D0A9419A413BB338904891381984"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Notification</header><text>The President shall notify the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives in writing of any deliberation or decision to suspend, terminate, denounce, or withdraw the United States from the North Atlantic Treaty, as soon as possible but in no event later than 180 days prior to taking such action.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H2F8EFC2DAA5243D885C305EBE8C856F6"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize, imply, or otherwise indicate that the President may suspend, terminate, denounce, or withdraw from any treaty to which the Senate has provided its advice and consent without the advice and consent of the Senate to such act or pursuant to an Act of Congress.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H076DA16EDCBD497C8006B782B1AF6AD6"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Severability</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If any provision of this section or the application of such provision is held by a Federal court to be unconstitutional, the remainder of this subtitle and the application of such provisions to any other person or circumstance shall not be affected thereby.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H810E643A435349A898EC4046743E1DC4"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this subtitle, the terms <quote>withdrawal</quote>, <quote>denunciation</quote>, <quote>suspension</quote>, and <quote>termination</quote> have the meaning given the terms in the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, concluded at Vienna May 23, 1969.</text></subsection></section> <section id="H95EABF2256EC46BEB58D1A484ACBB771" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1250B.</enum><header>Oversight of programs and operations funded with amounts appropriated by the United States for Ukraine</header> <subsection id="H4C837B42557E4C4DBC71C63A13562889"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Special Inspector General for Operation Atlantic Resolve</header> <paragraph id="H7F81CF9759044DA49E0A1C56A67F40E5"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Subject to the requirements of this section, the President, acting through the Chair of the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency, shall maintain the position of the Lead Inspector General for Operation Atlantic Resolve in accordance with section 419 of title 5, United States Code. </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1C027B495FEC46DEBA19F33E1B3C5F44"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Redesignation</header> 
<subparagraph id="H5EEE6B25A6D2479BAFC65E7B390D66C4"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The title of the position of the Lead Inspector General for Operation Atlantic Resolve is hereby redesignated as the <quote>Special Inspector General for Operation Atlantic Resolve</quote> (in this section referred to as the <quote>Special Inspector General</quote>).</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9FCD8712443345FE98A51874BB9D4370" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><header>References</header><text>Any reference in law, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the Lead Inspector General for Operation Atlantic Resolve shall be deemed to be a reference to the Special Inspector General for Operation Atlantic Resolve.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H33E3FE0837AF48969D781364A863D375"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Briefings</header><text>Upon request by the Chair or Ranking Member of an appropriate committee of Congress, not later than 30 days after receiving the request, the Special Inspector General shall to the extent practicable provide a briefing to such committee on the activities of the Special Inspector General with respect to programs and operations funded with amounts appropriated by the United States for Ukraine.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H8ED4EADDE74D4007824D95F8B450FD27" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Publication of accounting of United States assistance for Ukraine</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 45 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, and every 90 days thereafter, the President shall publish on a publicly available website of the United States Government a comprehensive accounting of unclassified amounts appropriated by the United States for Ukraine.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H8C6831D5D7D34313A02914B100EEF098"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Quarterly reports</header> 
<paragraph id="HDE4E35F7AFD8442FA5E92201DCF81107"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 45 days after the end of each fiscal-year quarter, the Special Inspector General shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report summarizing, with respect to that quarter and, to the extent possible, the period beginning on the date on which such quarter ends and ending on the date on which the report is submitted, the activities of the Special Inspector General with respect to programs and operations funded with amounts appropriated by the United States for Ukraine for—</text> <subparagraph id="H609B17C610B84EA7B30E1855B0EB46A2"><enum>(A)</enum><text>security, economic, and humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and other countries affected by the war;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H532755EC02D44064BD5552145CB4C2DD"><enum>(B)</enum><text>United States European Command operations and related support for the United States military; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HBEE1EC754004421D82E048BD8532C70F"><enum>(C)</enum><text>operations of other relevant United States Government agencies involved in the Ukraine response, as appropriate.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HAF2FDC808B56473A887E47CFBD84A640"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>Each report required by paragraph (1) shall include, for the period covered by the report—</text> <subparagraph id="H2A49EF390E2B473BA1CC35F8E10BA548"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a description of any waste, fraud, or abuse identified by the Inspectors General with respect to programs and operations funded with amounts appropriated by the United States for Ukraine;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H3DB3DE6DA4C644CBB91F157707CD2C77"><enum>(B)</enum><text>a description of the status and results of—</text> <clause id="HA10D7B44B3E44B17B971B73194515B29"><enum>(i)</enum><text>investigations, inspections, and audits; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H058A0D8FCCD442E2985C7BF1B46F40A5"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>referrals to the Department of Justice; and</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H4999677CE1D548E697AA7B968E075169"><enum>(C)</enum><text>a description of the overall plans for review by the Inspectors General of such support of Ukraine, including plans for investigations, inspections, and audits.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2B074526515C4883A05377C90666AB3C"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Availability</header><text>The Special Inspector General shall publish on a publicly available website the unclassified form of each report required by paragraph (1). </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF567B11DD09C4F288B8BF3C87E648DCF"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Form</header><text>Each report required by paragraph (1) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex if the Special Inspector General considers it necessary. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H1C3F9696327A447993DF6C09522D2294"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text>Nothing in this section may be construed to limit the Special Inspector General from exercising all authorities and discharging all responsibilities granted to the Lead Inspector General for Operation Atlantic Resolve in accordance with section 419 of title 5, United States Code, in the exercise of oversight responsibilities for Operation Atlantic Resolve generally and under this section with respect to Ukraine.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H2F15CCE31F2A4D9FB86759AB30CBECFF"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The requirements and authorities of this section with respect to the Special Inspector General shall cease in accordance with the sunset provisions for the Lead Inspector General for Operation Atlantic Resolve pursuant to section 419(f) of title 5, United States Code.</text></subsection>

<section id="H0E08EBA880934F5C9A9C661006D1CF5D"><enum>1258.</enum><header>Report</header> 
<subsection id="H26A17DFE49BB41F7A5D38AC5D73183B8"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Report</header> 
<paragraph id="H70EDD7BAF86040BA9AFD91F1E635F117"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to Congress a report on whether any products sold at commissary or exchange stores in fiscal years 2021 or 2022 were produced by companies described in paragraph (2) that have participated in a boycott action against the State of Israel.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H3B89F4BC4CC54C7D81ED225DBD2564E7"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Companies described</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The companies described in this paragraph are companies that have entered into a contract with the Department of Defense to sell products described in paragraph (1) the total value of which exceeds $10,000,000.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HC5CED0F63B624AF080D1E46B50E96454"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Sense of Congress</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Congress is concerned about the antisemitic efforts of the Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions (BDS) movement against the State of Israel, including its efforts to delegitimize, isolate, and ultimately destroy the Jewish state.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H9E536FBB5C804BB99CE595ED90F107AA"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Definition</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In subsection (a), the term <quote>boycott action against the State of Israel</quote> means engaging in a boycott action targeting the State of Israel, companies or individuals doing business in or with the State of Israel, or companies authorized by, licensed by, or organized under the laws of the State of Israel to do business.</text></subsection></section></subtitle> 
<subtitle id="H72D528EB94684297B9C8F4B4EEC9D21F"><enum>E</enum><header>Matters relating to Syria, Iraq, Iran, and Afghanistan</header> 
<section id="H8D3893E5BD604099B81BC645635C169F" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1261.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Middle East integrated maritime domain awareness and interdiction capability</header> 
<subsection id="H9000F1EC8E604C2F8469FB86511245A2" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense, using existing authorities, shall seek to build upon the incorporation of Israel into the area of responsibility of the United States Central Command to develop a Middle East integrated maritime domain awareness and interdiction capability for the purpose of protecting the people, infrastructure, and territory of such countries from—</text> <paragraph id="H7E9BBA1340CB44CDA28B7E4C87505C13" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">manned and unmanned naval systems, undersea warfare capabilities, and anti-ship missiles of Iran and groups affiliated with Iran; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HBF8B70990E974052A3F142ED50D6B924" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">violent extremist organizations, criminal networks, and piracy activities that threaten lawful commerce in the waterways within the area of responsibility of the United States Naval Forces Central Command.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HF7D192ED2F0D460489B3FAE13F0EAAD6" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Strategy</header> <paragraph id="H172817C8DA674684900FAF08456444A4" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 60 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of State, shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a strategy for the cooperation described in subsection (a).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2B4E118D3AF3405985C6E903BA5A0281" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Matters to be included</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The strategy required by paragraph (1) shall include the following:</text> <subparagraph id="HAC20CFD16E184A6197A1FC6A0672740D" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of the threats posed to ally or partner countries in the Middle East by—</text> 
<clause id="H145C06BD4A024ECFB3EE3220A7E7F080" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">manned and unmanned naval systems, undersea warfare capabilities, and anti-ship missiles of Iran and groups affiliated with Iran; and</text></clause> <clause id="HF655D9B8943F4502BF406C62751D7421" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">violent extremist organizations, criminal networks, and piracy activities that threaten lawful commerce in the waterways within the area of responsibility of the United States Naval Forces Central Command.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HE131BE1F8EAC467EB35064ABFF5F64D0" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of existing multilateral maritime partnerships currently led by the United States Naval Forces Central Command, including the Combined Maritime Forces (including its associated Task Forces 150, 151, 152, and 153), the International Maritime Security Construct, and the Navy's Task Force 59, and a discussion of the role of such partnerships in building an integrated maritime security capability.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H11943C796BAD4932908977F797C2BC4A" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of progress made in advancing the integration of Israel into the existing multilateral maritime partnerships described in subparagraph (B).</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HA6308ECD12554684A74510BCD30856DB" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of efforts among countries in the Middle East to coordinate intelligence, reconnaissance, and surveillance capabilities and indicators and warnings with respect to the threats described in subparagraph (A), and a description of any impediment to optimizing such efforts.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H537A4F94873445BF9177F0A0AFE7477A" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(E)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of the current Department of Defense systems that, in coordination with ally and partner countries in the Middle East—</text> 
<clause id="HFA95AF8042004281A9546E538F7B5253" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">provide awareness of and defend against such threats; and </text></clause> <clause id="H23159F2BBCD043719EF7E6DCCAC15EC6" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">address current capability gaps.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H2AF4CE3CFEEE4C93B6FE4E01BA31F807" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(F)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An explanation of the manner in which an integrated maritime domain awareness and interdiction architecture would improve collective security in the Middle East.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB8E5FE02B3304165A2AD69B084EB5765" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(G)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of existing and planned efforts to engage ally and partner countries in the Middle East in establishing such an architecture.</text></subparagraph>

<subparagraph id="HEC04AA4313C84C41988A883EC8E9F978" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(L)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Recommendations for improvements in the implementation of such strategy based on such metrics.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H80B7855E7D99449D9614BCDBFEFD4595" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(M)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of any capabilities or lessons from the Navy’s Task Force 59 that may be leveraged to support an integrated maritime domain awareness and interdiction capability in the Middle East.</text></subparagraph>

<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H5F9580C07A6340179FBE408EFA8F6AED"><enum>(2)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">ISIS member</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>ISIS member</term> means a person who was part of, or substantially supported, the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE165CDD2595D4948A12C758148A8B2A9"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Senior Coordinator</header><text>The term <term>Senior Coordinator</term> means the coordinator for detained ISIS members and relevant displaced populations in Syria designated under subsection (a) of section 1224 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/116/92">Public Law 116–92</external-xref>; 133 Stat. 1642), as amended by subsection (d). </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H43B7B68FE61149D6A751167C4384CB55"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Sense of Congress</header> 
<paragraph id="HF87275C2EF52430AB795B80B3F363197"><enum></enum><text>It is the sense of Congress that—</text> <subparagraph id="HE40D53EAE59C48ACAA4856C163A432B0"><enum>(A)</enum><text>ISIS detainees held by the Syrian Democratic Forces and ISIS-affiliated individuals located within displaced persons camps in Syria pose a significant and growing humanitarian challenge and security threat to the region;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H29DED00E9CBD422BBB6152232667BFC1"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the vast majority of individuals held in displaced persons camps in Syria are women and children, approximately 50 percent of whom are under the age of 12 at the al-Hol camp, and they face significant threats of violence and radicalization, as well as lacking access to adequate sanitation and health care facilities; </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HAE4954BAB4AC441094ECB9DD83EC9F04"><enum>(C)</enum><text>there is an urgent need to seek a sustainable solution to such camps through repatriation and reintegration of the inhabitants;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H658AE9263CD343A1B084A377C797B57F"><enum>(D)</enum><text>the United States should work closely with international allies and partners to facilitate the repatriation and reintegration efforts required to provide a long-term solution for such camps and prevent the resurgence of ISIS; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H6E83C335E3324354887065B059139538"><enum>(E)</enum><text>if left unaddressed, such camps will continue to be drivers of instability that jeopardize the long-term prospects for peace and stability in the region.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HD550189BA00C48FEAA73D8A97F9D9CA6"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Statement of policy</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">It is the policy of the United States that—</text> <paragraph id="H4364C46C1CAA47CC9D3D0542E872574B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>ISIS-affiliated individuals located within displacement camps in Syria, and other inhabitants of displacement camps in Syria, be repatriated and, where appropriate, prosecuted, or where possible, reintegrated into their country of origin, consistent with all relevant domestic laws and applicable international laws prohibiting refoulement; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H09F0D567674B431980E860D047B5E454"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the camps will be closed as soon as is practicable. </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H165860F178E8453CB94624830B47B128"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Modification of establishment of coordinator for detained ISIS members and relevant displaced populations in Syria</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Section 1224 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/116/92">Public Law 116–92</external-xref>; 133 Stat. 1642) is amended—</text> 
<paragraph id="H74EE88A7F7584D22BD2B7B95E8F4D98A"><enum>(1)</enum><text>by striking subsection (a);</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC5EFC784642545B7A342422B682A891E"><enum>(2)</enum><text>by amending subsection (b) to read as follows:</text>

<paragraph id="H72DAB994A323440997BD77281501DBA5"><enum>(7)</enum><text>by redesignating subsections (c) through (f) as subsections (b) through (e), respectively.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HDEAC4578F27146FC8EFA33720C176B91"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Strategy on ISIS-Related detainee and displacement camps in Syria</header> <paragraph id="HE49B83E7A4FD48E4AB07C88E5E3EAF41"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, the Director of National Intelligence, the Secretary of the Treasury, the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, and the Attorney General, shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress an interagency strategy with respect to ISIS-affiliated individuals and ISIS-related detainee and other displaced persons camps in Syria.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H334B4B35C76E4446AAB6B4991425F5C7"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The strategy required by paragraph (1) shall include—</text> <subparagraph id="H3F1697ABCE154C238DAF8266700A073E"><enum>(A)</enum><text>methods to address—</text> 
<clause id="HB65E1B0CBE9F4B9DA00873569431201B"><enum>(i)</enum><text>disengagement from and prevention of recruitment into violence, violent extremism, and other illicit activity in such camps;</text></clause> <clause id="HB1742EA1C53B4FC3A25F5EE1D675319D"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>efforts to encourage and facilitate repatriation and, as appropriate, investigation and prosecution of foreign nationals from such camps, consistent with all relevant domestic and applicable international laws;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HE89C0DA6754B45CCB567BBD41A7C1F0D"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the return and reintegration of displaced Syrian and Iraqi women and children into their communities of origin; </text></clause> <clause id="H16AC9F7B4EBE41E78F79D3B06CFE4B0C"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>international engagement to develop processes for repatriation and reintegration of foreign nationals from such camps;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H7AAAF39F68A04931A3B6C71809BD3073"><enum>(v)</enum><text>contingency plans for the relocation of detained and displaced persons who are not able to be repatriated from such camps;</text></clause> <clause id="H9C7A370A8BED41008F98264CE627ABF8"><enum>(vi)</enum><text>efforts to improve the humanitarian conditions in such camps, including through the delivery of medicine, psychosocial support, clothing, education, and improved housing; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H4D2D71A31B984DC88512FC0496B9D1C1"><enum>(vii)</enum><text>assessed humanitarian and security needs of all camps and detainment facilities based on prioritization of such camps and facilities most at risk of humanitarian crises, external attacks, or internal violence;</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H6299A004A59D429F8C65305725E071EE"><enum>(B)</enum><text>an assessment of—</text> 
<clause id="HA888E196EEF648CF9C09AD15B96E931C"><enum>(i)</enum><text>rehabilitation centers in northeast Syria, including humanitarian conditions and processes for admittance and efforts to improve both humanitarian conditions and admittance processes for such centers and camps, as well as on the prevention of youth radicalization; and</text></clause> <clause id="HF9FD8FED933F45A7AD82EEB15ABCA636"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>processes for being sent to, and resources directed towards, rehabilitation centers and programs in countries that receive returned ISIS affiliated individuals, with a focus on the prevention of radicalization of minor children; </text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H0AFF3256B8F5417BBB443AF9DBC9E78B"><enum>(C)</enum><text>a plan to improve, in such camps—</text> <clause id="H43B786EFDAC44A7E8C3ED1F024861D82"><enum>(i)</enum><text>security conditions, including by training of personnel and through construction; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H330FB6A701844C95A0DB53A89A829265"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>humanitarian conditions; </text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HFD2B1895D1574B38BEDF074B12A4AC7A"><enum>(D)</enum><text>a framework for measuring progress of humanitarian, security, and repatriation efforts with the goal of closing such camps; and </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4451112D8C83424282024DF6568A95EC"><enum>(E)</enum><text>any other matter the Secretary of State considers appropriate. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE42629ABE2F048C5AE71B224E5CACAD9"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The strategy required by paragraph (1) shall be submitted in unclassified form but may include a classified annex that is transmitted separately.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H4796F84AEDA94119A89E166A1CDEED8C"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Annual interagency report</header> 
<paragraph id="HCF05E25FA91842EEADA3D2411C9A1FC7"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, and not less frequently than annually thereafter through January 31, 2025, the Senior Coordinator, in coordination with the relevant agencies, shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a detailed report that includes the following:</text> <subparagraph id="HF826BE85E3CB4607AF8E17D55C1671B4"><enum>(A)</enum><text>A detailed description of the facilities and camps where detained ISIS members, and families with perceived ISIS affiliation, are being held and housed, including—</text> 
<clause id="H86280C4DE74E482186411ADDF5992177"><enum>(i)</enum><text>a description of the security and management of such facilities and camps;</text></clause> <clause id="H15330317DEF941E4A077BFA117AFA240"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>an assessment of resources required for the security of such facilities and camps; </text></clause> 
<clause id="H13F833F306BA4BE1BD08358BAD76CE77"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>an assessment of the adherence by the operators of such facilities and camps to international humanitarian law standards; and</text></clause> <clause id="H228F79FD845243EFAC0E2A06C022CBA8"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>an assessment of children held within such facilities and camps that may be used as part of smuggling operations to evade security at the facilities and camps. </text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H3AC0B50820A54B96A9DB79DBAD394535"><enum>(B)</enum><text>A description of all efforts undertaken by, and the resources needed for, the United States Government to address deficits in the humanitarian environment and security of such facilities and camps. </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HEDB6B23710E548C9A56AB03FF2C93154"><enum>(C)</enum><text>A description of all multilateral and international engagements related to humanitarian access and provision of basic services to, and freedom of movement and security and safe return of, displaced persons at camps or facilities in Iraq, Syria, and any other area affected by ISIS activity, including a description of—</text> 
<clause id="H3D0E0AB29BCC4E17B595AACFF8352FD8"><enum>(i)</enum><text>support for efforts by the Syrian Democratic Forces to facilitate the return and reintegration of displaced people from Iraq and Syria;</text></clause> <clause id="HB9D763FB605B44FE850488BC5467BFE6"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>repatriation efforts with respect to displaced women and children and male children aging into adults while held in these facilities and camps;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HDDC9A450C0934314AACA14E3BDD903DB"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>any current or future potential threat to United States national security interests posed by detained ISIS members or displaced families, including an analysis of the al-Hol camp and annexes; and</text></clause> <clause id="HC5D7F7527D504F2BBCC09CA88C5BC156"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>United States Government plans and strategies to respond to any threat identified under clause (iii).</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H10498D83A6094A1492838F271C9D8F64"><enum>(D)</enum><text>The number of individuals repatriated from the custody of the Syrian Democratic Forces.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE5AB422A48BB4F1B973B38E63A0ABF83"><enum>(E)</enum><text>An analysis of factors on the ground in Syria and Iraq that may result in the unintended release of detained or displaced ISIS members, and an assessment of any measures available to mitigate such releases.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HAC5FD42BCD08470AA4BC3253A1B4088D"><enum>(F)</enum><text>A detailed description of efforts to encourage the final disposition and security of detained or displaced ISIS members with other countries and international organizations.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H03FC4A58761846F7AB18BB6C1D2552F3"><enum>(G)</enum><text>A description of foreign repatriation and rehabilitation programs deemed successful systems to model, and an analysis of the long-term results of such programs. </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H656E654C02AE4E03A53AFF8E6B6B8DA8"><enum>(H)</enum><text>A description of the manner in which the United States Government communicates regarding repatriation and disposition efforts with the families of United States citizens believed to have been victims of a criminal act by a detained or displaced ISIS member, in accordance with section 503(c) of the Victims' Rights and Restitution Act of 1990 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/34/20141">34 U.S.C. 20141(c)</external-xref>) and section 3771 of title 18, United States Code.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H36EFBD8235A94FCBA48CCEF731DAF659"><enum>(I)</enum><text>An analysis of all efforts between the United States and partner countries within the Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS or other countries to share related information that may aid in resolving the final disposition of ISIS members, and any obstacles that may hinder such efforts.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HACACC91614CF43409CD76B843E851373"><enum>(J)</enum><text>Any other matter the Coordinator considers appropriate.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD7E4C3A2CE9D4FDB8E6DEC6C63E14EF6"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The report required by paragraph (1) shall be submitted in unclassified form but may include a classified annex that is transmitted separately. </text></paragraph></subsection>

<section id="HF768832DD3F040739F809716AF8CC65E"><enum>1266.</enum><header>Plan of action to equip and train Iraqi security forces and Kurdish Peshmerga forces</header> 
<subsection id="H47806D3CFDA04770ABD833094481EB58"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than February 1, 2024, the Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the Secretary of State, shall develop a plan of action to equip and train Iraqi security forces and Kurdish Peshmerga forces to defend against attack by missiles, rockets, and unmanned systems. The plan of action shall be based on and informed by the results of the report submitted by the Secretary of Defense pursuant to section 1237 of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/263">Public Law 117–263</external-xref>; 136 Stat. 2839).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H5EA6D93020E64C4EB430CF687A91CFE2"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Matters to be included</header><text>The plan required by subsection (a) shall include the following: </text> 
<paragraph id="HF8D8C403077C41A29C51EAD9D5811FC7"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The provision of available equipment to Iraq and the Iraqi Kurdistan Region to counter the air and missile threats addressed in the report, to include air defense systems, to counter attack by missiles, rockets, and unmanned systems.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB41F202845C240DB8488A277CFAC1BDC"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The provision of appropriate training of Iraqi security forces and Kurdish Peshmerga forces to support fielding and operational employment of the available equipment described in paragraph (1).</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF74D68B2FD934FCFB60800BC6032B116"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Implementation</header> 
<paragraph id="H3475D1D3371245BDA1E17CFE32367BD4"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall begin implementation of the plan required by subsection (a) not later than 90 days after development of the plan required by subsection (a).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H824B16281EEA4F65A653A4A673B3F0FE"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Waiver</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense may delay implementation of the plan required by subsection (a) if such implementation would adversely impact United States stocks and readiness.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H9279F117919742BD8800A2E52FF98548"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Congressional notification</header><text>If the Secretary of Defense exercises the waiver authority under paragraph (2), the Secretary shall—</text> <subparagraph id="H5FAB5754D72B4A5AA5F49E896DAD5900"><enum>(A)</enum><text>notify the congressional defense committees of the exercise of such authority and the reason therefor not later than 10 days prior to the exercise of such authority; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HA6A1F5A97B9B4E59A4396BDA014CC997"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">notify the congressional defense committees of the exercise of such authority every 30 days thereafter until implementation of the plan required by subsection (a) begins.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H25B77A11B646431093A830506742827B"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Congressional briefing</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than July 1, 2024, the Secretary of Defense should provide to the congressional defense committees a briefing on progress of the air defense equipping and training effort against the air and missile threat to Iraq, including in the Iraqi Kurdistan Region.</text></subsection></section>

<subtitle id="H981647E18981428D923D05BBD550422C"><enum>A</enum><header>Matters relating to the Indo-Pacific region</header> 
<section id="H9CC63BCC9E9C4183B2BA6845CD3A5807" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1301.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Sense of Congress on defense alliances and partnerships in the Indo-Pacific region</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">It is the sense of Congress that the Secretary of Defense should continue efforts that strengthen United States defense alliances and partnerships in the Indo-Pacific region so as to further the comparative advantage of the United States in strategic competition with the People’s Republic of China, including by—</text> <paragraph id="HD5D9FE4560BB4A709411AD8029845B09" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">enhancing cooperation with Japan, consistent with the Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security Between the United States of America and Japan, signed at Washington, January 19, 1960, including by developing advanced military capabilities, fostering interoperability across all domains, and improving sharing of information and intelligence;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE9E076783BC3457BA317FA1DEF4932E3" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">reinforcing the United States alliance with the Republic of Korea, including by maintaining the presence of approximately 28,500 members of the United States Armed Forces deployed to the country and affirming the United States commitment to extended deterrence using the full range of United States defense capabilities, and with deeper coordination on nuclear deterrence as highlighted in the Washington Declaration adopted by President Biden and President Yoon Suk Yeol during President Yoon Suk Yeol’s state visit on April 26, 2023, consistent with the Mutual Defense Treaty Between the United States and the Republic of Korea, signed at Washington, October 1, 1953, in support of the shared objective of a peaceful and stable Korean Peninsula;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB21C604DEBB84387935DFFDD452BF838" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">fostering bilateral and multilateral cooperation with Australia, consistent with the Security Treaty Between Australia, New Zealand, and the United States of America, signed at San Francisco, September 1, 1951, and through the partnership among Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States (commonly known as <quote>AUKUS</quote>)—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HC3076CBC899948A99BD936F1DBD9BC6A" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to advance shared security objectives;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3E37A30B9AA542C0AD505E27196103CE" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to accelerate the fielding of advanced military capabilities; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H65AA4AB9164648C28FB56C72C0800286" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to build the capacity of emerging partners;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6F1E0E854396447BAE6635D47B4C86C6" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">advancing United States alliances with the Philippines and Thailand and United States partnerships with other partners in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to enhance maritime domain awareness, promote sovereignty and territorial integrity, leverage technology and promote innovation, and support an open, inclusive, and rules-based regional architecture;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H6DAC66CBE6F44ED395B5E0D1B48E8090" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">broadening United States engagement with India, including through the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue—</text> <subparagraph id="H852275AC74A04262AC2CDA0BF6AFE904" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to advance the shared objective of a free and open Indo-Pacific region through bilateral and multilateral engagements and participation in military exercises, expanded defense trade, and collaboration on humanitarian aid and disaster response; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HEF7A4A72F86047F08F6F2AAC5EE0EE21" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to enable greater cooperation on maritime security;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HD067AB6BA52941A6B5A26020825DE2F5" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(6)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">strengthening the United States partnership with Taiwan, consistent with the Three Communiques, the Taiwan Relations Act (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/96/8">Public Law 96–8</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/3301">22 U.S.C. 3301 et seq.</external-xref>), and the Six Assurances, with the goal of improving Taiwan's defensive capabilities and promoting peaceful cross-strait relations;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H4BD666CD34944FB3B60CC76B47526CA7" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(7)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">reinforcing the status of the Republic of Singapore as a Major Security Cooperation Partner of the United States and continuing to strengthen defense and security cooperation between the military forces of the Republic of Singapore and the Armed Forces of the United States, including through participation in combined exercises and training;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC205AA4E575B40FA8EBF378C32B4FEDE" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(8)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">engaging with the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Republic of Palau, and other Pacific Island countries with the goal of strengthening regional security and addressing issues of mutual concern, including protecting fisheries from illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H60D83CD259924722B5A88C9BDB03655D" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(9)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">collaborating with Canada, the United Kingdom, France, and other members of the European Union and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization to build connectivity and advance a shared vision for the region that is principled, long-term, and anchored in democratic resilience.</text></paragraph></section> <section id="H8F006F12F30D49FF8C2F867F0C8912EF" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1302.</enum><header>Extension of Pacific Deterrence Initiative and report, briefings, and plan under the Initiative</header> <subsection id="HE5782D7D2FA8498482F791DA7137F861"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Extension of initiative</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Subsection (c) of section 1251 of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/113">10 U.S.C. 113</external-xref> note) is amended—</text> 
<paragraph id="H6FDEC61698CB4AD2AC0EF715502712D7"><enum>(1)</enum><text>by striking <quote>the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023</quote> and inserting <quote>the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024</quote>; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H192BD6ADB7C4412B9ED03269295B29E4"><enum>(2)</enum><text>by striking <quote>fiscal year 2023</quote> and inserting <quote>fiscal year 2024</quote>.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HFBB14919AE1E44BDBA6DE3D5052EF7E8"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Extension of report and briefings</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Subsection (d) of such section is amended—</text> <paragraph id="H3DEEEE098BD8407297425E3F37B68182"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">in paragraph (1)(A), by striking <quote>fiscal years 2024 and 2025</quote> and inserting <quote>fiscal years 2025 and 2026</quote>; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC1E8BE9EF56047F5AD325D464C61A57C"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">in paragraph (2), by striking <quote>fiscal years 2023 and 2024</quote> each place it appears and inserting <quote>fiscal years 2025 and 2026</quote>.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H37E0ADD8328A4E108E745742BD07BD80"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Extension of plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Subsection (e) of such section is amended by striking <quote>fiscal years 2023 and 2024</quote> and inserting <quote>fiscal years 2025 and 2026</quote>.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="HF6640F357EFE47AC8FDB8AD197CA3BED"><enum>1303.</enum><header>Modification of pilot program to develop young civilian defense leaders in the Indo-Pacific region</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 1261 of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/311">10 U.S.C. 311</external-xref> note) is amended—</text> <paragraph id="H59ABAB14DF194D12943C7197627B8DB4"><enum>(1)</enum><text>in subsection (b)—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H7BE0F8826ED44D13906472363DB81961"><enum>(A)</enum><text>in the matter preceding paragraph (1), by striking <quote>a national defense mission</quote> and inserting <quote>a defense-related national security mission</quote>; and </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H53CBB0368BEA448D903BD10DD67EB451"><enum>(B)</enum><text>by inserting <quote>and other appropriate ministries with a defense-related national security mission</quote> after <quote>civilian leaders in foreign partner ministries of defense</quote> each place it appears; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0BD38D2AC2F14059809ABCFC17CEBF06"><enum>(2)</enum><text>in subsection (c), by striking <quote>civilian defense leaders from foreign partner ministries of defense</quote> and inserting <quote>civilian leaders in foreign partner ministries of defense and other appropriate ministries with a defense-related national security mission</quote>. </text></paragraph></section> <section id="H05E1882D382D4FBE9B17C429B7FA5CDB" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1304.</enum><header>Indo-Pacific campaigning initiative</header> <subsection id="H8F4D8A4ACCED4A9383CFCE4DA59B0BFB"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of Defense shall establish, and the Commander of the United States Indo-Pacific Command shall carry out, an Indo-Pacific Campaigning Initiative (in this section referred to as the <quote>Initiative</quote>) for purposes of—</text> 
<paragraph id="H19F9B48EF0914255954321CAF9CD274B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>strengthening United States alliances and partnerships with foreign military partners in the Indo-Pacific region;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H4975B8A2B4BB4ACF9AEFFDD00FE83DAF"><enum>(2)</enum><text>deterring military aggression by potential adversaries against the United States and allies and partners of the United States;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H056B6D513E5D4E70BC069E7F1F667DDD"><enum>(3)</enum><text>dissuading strategic competitors from seeking to achieve their objectives through the conduct of military activities below the threshold of traditional armed conflict;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB5EE1D62E26C45EA969A9C352E606D1D"><enum>(4)</enum><text>improving the understanding of the United States Armed Forces with respect to the operating environment in the Indo-Pacific region;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCA0AC1E2E0344DACAAA9751DF8AA1D57"><enum>(5)</enum><text>shaping the perception of potential adversaries with respect to United States military capabilities and the military capabilities of allies and partners of the United States in the Indo-Pacific region; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6D94F00E7F484A35807D8C00428459FB"><enum>(6)</enum><text>improving the ability of the United States Armed Forces to coordinate and operate with foreign military partners in the Indo-Pacific region.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HC92994D74CF541E8AA5AE0C703B4E98D"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Briefing and report</header> 
<paragraph id="H1FA0771235D546D8940AC40BEBAD7832"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Briefing</header><text>Not later than March 1, 2024, the Secretary shall provide the congressional defense committees with a briefing that describes ongoing and planned campaigning activities in the Indo-Pacific region for fiscal year 2024.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H46C2CDFFF9B44FE1AA8A1271F1767FA7"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than December 1, 2024, the Secretary shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report that—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H573591B929F74C6CB40F8480D9036BB4"><enum>(A)</enum><text>summarizes the campaigning activities conducted in the Indo-Pacific region during fiscal year 2024; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB3E3AD3F9A154304B7FE7730EF221CAA"><enum>(B)</enum><text>includes—</text> 
<clause id="H266135D5016548FCACFC050584C8F0B6"><enum>(i)</enum><text>an assessment of the value each such activity contributes to meeting strategic or operational objectives relative to the commitment of resources of such activity;</text></clause> <clause id="HE4165232A18E408592562493177C22F0"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>lessons learned in carrying out such activities;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HE958F22894EE4682B51CF590DD01AE58"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>any identified resource or authority gap that has negatively impacted the implementation of the Initiative; and</text></clause> <clause id="H52DE2A1B96B64637A59251F4B4E2DEF1"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>proposed plans for additional campaigning activities in the Indo-Pacific region to fulfill the purposes described in subsection (a).</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H4DA9A92D874F4232A332B2106E88395D"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Campaigning defined</header><text>In this section, the term <quote>campaigning</quote>—</text> <paragraph id="H3E7755B6A2994774922DD58FD4711D2B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>means the conduct and sequencing of logically linked military activities to achieve strategy aligned objectives, including modifying the security environment over time to the benefit of the United States and the allies and partners of the United States while limiting, frustrating, and disrupting competitor activities; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HFE16A430D32C401E9EE4B73261A7401B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>includes deliberately planned military activities in the Indo-Pacific region involving bilateral and multilateral engagements with foreign partners, training, exercises, demonstrations, experiments, and other activities to achieve the objectives described in subsection (a).</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H50BB3BE5CB444909B2CD96A6A2846470" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1305.</enum><header>Indo-Pacific Maritime Domain Awareness Initiative</header> <subsection id="HC5BD9ED0B576488AA0155C96AD6919A3"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of State, shall seek to establish an initiative with allies and partners of the United States, including Australia, Japan, and India, to be known as the <quote>Indo-Pacific Maritime Domain Awareness Initiative</quote> (in this section referred to as the <quote>Initiative</quote>), to bolster maritime domain awareness in the Indo-Pacific region.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H3D7B7C2691C24CFCB8B3DA63E3137788"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Use of authorities</header><text>In carrying out the Initiative, the Secretary of Defense may use the authorities provided in <external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/10/16">chapter 16</external-xref> of title 10, United States Code, and other applicable statutory authorities available to the Secretary of Defense.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HBA379D9CE22A472CBE091BD2059EEC8E"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Purposes</header><text>The purposes of the Initiative are as follows:</text> 
<paragraph id="HEB0F110C8B9C4654A8816A9416911D0D"><enum>(1)</enum><text>To enhance the ability of allies and partners of the United States in the Indo-Pacific region to monitor the maritime domain of such region.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC7BD752745BF4332B42FE6EB44F70D76"><enum>(2)</enum><text>To utilize emerging technologies to support maritime domain awareness objectives.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H7E28FED1BC5640EAA01098566846E7DF"><enum>(3)</enum><text>To provide a comprehensive understanding of the maritime domain in the Indo-Pacific region, including by facilitating information sharing among such allies and partners.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H4876B8007E4A4EBB851267431782A014" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1306.</enum><header>Limitation on availability of funds pending feasibility study regarding delivery of harpoon missiles to foreign security partners</header> <subsection id="H1993508E97DA4108A0A9ACE1D3FEA176"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Limitation</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act for fiscal year 2024 and available for the Assistant Secretary of the Navy for Research, Development and Acquisition, not more than 85 percent may be obligated or expended until the date on which the Assistant Secretary of the Navy for Research, Development and Acquisition submits to the congressional defense committees the feasibility study required by subsection (b).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H39E1AB3E15D9432D8A37C296AA44E7D2"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Feasibility study required</header> 
<paragraph id="H1DB8D90DCCA344A3BD305478579401B1"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, acting through the Assistant Secretary of the Navy for Research, Development and Acquisition, shall conduct a study to analyze the feasibility and advisability of accelerating the provision of Harpoon missiles to foreign security partners under existing Foreign Military Sales cases, additional appropriations, and pursuant to the authority provided under section 506 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2318">22 U.S.C. 2318</external-xref>) or section 333 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H637C90E9A0654333AD9946C7149AFFD5"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The study required by paragraph (1) shall, at a minimum, include the following: </text> 
<subparagraph id="HAF3CF04CC7D64654812B7C685FB97B94"><enum>(A)</enum><text>A list of existing Foreign Military Sales cases for Harpoon missiles to foreign security partners.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H7D161B7FFAE7467E9FC68625CED1917F"><enum>(B)</enum><text>The current timeline for the delivery of Harpoon missiles under each of the Foreign Military Sales cases identified under subparagraph (A).</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H56578BB7BA6548C4B14B5D7C5E8A66E9"><enum>(C)</enum><text>A detailed analysis of contracting timelines for Harpoon missiles procured by foreign security partners through the Foreign Military Sales process and recommendations, if any, for accelerating such contracting timelines.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H600D4CA917D64F77A3A2471841478D33"><enum>(D)</enum><text>An analysis of the feasibility and advisability of accelerating the provision of Harpoon missiles to foreign security partners under existing Foreign Military Sales cases, including through—</text> 
<clause id="H658FE0F295CF43C896631084D1D1DBAD"><enum>(i)</enum><text>additional appropriations;</text></clause> <clause id="H12A2716984FD4F90B6910F5F1E21F8D4"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the authority provided under section 506 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2318">22 U.S.C. 2318</external-xref>);</text></clause>

<section id="H3FFEC7E7DA8F4E0ABF7618FC740F1CC7" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1307.</enum><header>Sense of Congress on Taiwan defense relations</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">It is the sense of Congress that—</text> <paragraph id="H24A1FD955223429D8C805B72877FD3F6"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the United States’ one China policy, as guided by the Taiwan Relations Act (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/96/8">Public Law 96–8</external-xref>; 22 U.S.C. et seq.), the Three Communiques between the United States and the People’s Republic of China, and the Six Assurances provided by the United States to Taiwan in July 1982, is the foundation for United States-Taiwan relations;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H43BEF09DF4714CD8BF123AB687460F2C"><enum>(2)</enum><text>as set forth in the Taiwan Relations Act, the United States decision to establish diplomatic relations with the People’s Republic of China rests upon the expectation that the future of Taiwan will be determined by peaceful means, and that any effort to determine the future of Taiwan by other than peaceful means, including boycotts and embargoes, is of grave concern to the United States;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H982DCE5170E74806A52F965748DA85EB"><enum>(3)</enum><text>the increasingly coercive and aggressive behavior of the People’s Republic of China toward Taiwan is contrary to the expectation of the peaceful resolution of the future of Taiwan;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HAF262D4DE61C43BF9870ED2857305C15"><enum>(4)</enum><text>as set forth in the Taiwan Relations Act, the capacity to resist any resort to force or other forms of coercion that would jeopardize the security, or the social or economic system, of the people on Taiwan should be maintained;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H3C11FDD94A7C4127A76D3D91D4184A84"><enum>(5)</enum><text>the United States should continue to support the development of capable, ready, and modern defense forces necessary for Taiwan to maintain sufficient defensive capabilities, including by—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HD68EDEB113EE4D82ADA93DCA29512577"><enum>(A)</enum><text>supporting acquisition by Taiwan of defense articles and services through foreign military sales, direct commercial sales, and industrial cooperation, with an emphasis on capabilities that support an asymmetric strategy;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H69F759F1ADAE4AD3A34BB18327101E20"><enum>(B)</enum><text>ensuring timely review of and response to requests of Taiwan for defense articles and services;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H443D8F13431D40FCA067A18017A18229"><enum>(C)</enum><text>conducting practical training and military exercises with Taiwan that enable Taiwan to maintain sufficient defensive capabilities, as described in the Taiwan Relations Act;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H83A0172740214A90B75FF6A86E0B56DD"><enum>(D)</enum><text>exchanges between defense officials and officers of the United States and Taiwan at the strategic, policy, and functional levels, consistent with the Taiwan Travel Act (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/115/135">Public Law 115–135</external-xref>; 132 Stat. 341), especially for the purposes of—</text> 
<clause id="H1613A368848C462BA660938EF6927BE5"><enum>(i)</enum><text>enhancing cooperation on defense planning;</text></clause> <clause id="H80204D7AC3574C00A36B97E3C13046A8"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>improving the interoperability of the military forces of the United States and Taiwan; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HB37D8E98971D4FA2B603EEF58127556D"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>improving the reserve force of Taiwan;</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H5996242E35FF4FB78ADE97FA22284B80"><enum>(E)</enum><text>cooperating with Taiwan to improve its ability to employ military capabilities in asymmetric ways, as described in the Taiwan Relations Act; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC0124435E2DA4F7AB2044E92FF30C00D"><enum>(F)</enum><text>expanding cooperation in humanitarian assistance and disaster relief; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HCC4725C89DB748F0B506D0A72F07A0F2"><enum>(6)</enum><text>the United States should increase its support to a free and open society in the face of aggressive efforts by the Government of the People’s Republic of China to curtail or influence the free exercise of rights and democratic franchise.</text></paragraph></section>

<section id="H33C492E2AEED48B6BBBC1FA6693C125B" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1310.</enum><header>Prohibition on use of funds to support entertainment projects with ties to the Government of the People's Republic of China</header> 
<subsection id="H28E1BCEFF6F84E4FAFD0BC51658F22DB"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act for the Department of Defense may be used to knowingly provide active and direct support to any film, television, or other entertainment project if the Secretary of Defense has demonstrable evidence that the project has complied, or is likely to comply, with a demand from the Government of the People’s Republic of China or the Chinese Communist Party, or an entity under the direction of the People’s Republic of China or the Chinese Communist Party, to censor the content of the project in a material manner to advance the national interest of the People’s Republic of China.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H07E45F74F0344B048C2AA4C596D5B41C"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Waiver</header><text>The Secretary of Defense may waive the prohibition under subsection (a) if the Secretary submits to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and House of Representatives a written certification that such a waiver is in the national interest of the United States.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="HE64CEB8AC9304D30AD32B224928E3C57" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1311.</enum><header>Determination on involvement of the People’s Republic of China in the Mexican fentanyl trade</header> 
<subsection id="HB8AF0831F2AA4DCCBB280EC9B216EDD9"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Determination</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, in consultation with the Director of National Intelligence, shall determine if information available to the Department of Defense indicates that the Government of the People’s Republic of China assisted in or approved of the transportation of pill presses, fentanyl products, or fentanyl precursors to one or more Mexican drug cartels. </text></subsection> <subsection id="H55267DEEE85B49A18EC79789214C0D28"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Reporting requirement</header><text>If the determination of the Secretary of Defense under subsection (a) is an affirmative determination, the Secretary shall submit the determination to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H8638AD33DB234F03861DE0C26FDD79CF" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1312.</enum><header>Analysis of certain biotechnology entities</header> 
<subsection id="HB03877AFBB8E421AA5103DB42FD3927E"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall conduct an analysis to determine if any biotechnology entity, or any subsidiary, parent, affiliate, or successor of such an entity, should be identified as a Chinese military company or a military-civil fusion contributor and included on the list maintained by the Department of Defense in accordance with section 1260H(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/113">10 U.S.C. 113</external-xref> note).</text></subsection> <subsection id="HCC6D276FE88E4FBEA1DDB0DED766A7B5"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Biotechnology entity defined</header><text>In this section, the term <quote>biotechnology entity</quote> means an entity that makes or offers a technology, good, or service that applies to or is enabled by life sciences innovation or product development for biological materials, including disease detection, genetic analysis, and related services.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H67C2EAC072D94017AAB638A5D3F6E5CD" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1313.</enum><header>Studies on defense budget transparency of the People’s Republic of China and the United States</header> 
<subsection id="H2B6C22BEBF6147A89ED60254ABC41234"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Studies required</header> 
<paragraph id="H5446DF64190049BE9BA4C9FBDE790467"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Study of PRC budget</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a study on the defense budget of the People’s Republic of China.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H3804E1B2DCA8403D8D23B4CAD8D392D5"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Comparative study on budgets</header><text>Not later than 90 days after the date on which the study required by paragraph (1) is submitted, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a comparative study on the defense budgets of the People’s Republic of China and the United States.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H66BD95FA2F5347D2B7B67A279154FE86"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Objective</header><text>The objective of the studies required by paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be to provide the people of the United States with an accurate comparison of the defense spending of the People’s Republic of China and the United States.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HB67CF67E70C848AFAAF22A1FA5A24999"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The studies required by subsection (a) shall include, at a minimum, the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H5415B6BC04934BD0915463825BF1F5EF"><enum>(1)</enum><text>A determination of the amounts invested by the applicable subject country across functional categories for spending, including—</text> <subparagraph id="HD0448B2334CE4384BFF4B48DDB20DB49"><enum>(A)</enum><text>defense-related research and development;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H04879377F260464E9B71E724CA463E1D"><enum>(B)</enum><text>weapons procurement from domestic and foreign sources;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HAADC42D323DE4AAAB54C8B0156FC288B"><enum>(C)</enum><text>operations and maintenance;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HBC3906A7F83F46F29A910EC41B950222"><enum>(D)</enum><text>pay and benefits;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2EBA098EC05840C3B2474B1A7D47EDC5"><enum>(E)</enum><text>military construction;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H5289C13C2B734A94BDE1CC7584FD5093"><enum>(F)</enum><text>military pensions; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H8EC3541E4BE04408973FB2A054911B6D"><enum>(G)</enum><text>any other category the Secretary considers relevant.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF46E20C63A084A2684C9551E9167AFA6"><enum>(2)</enum><text>A consideration of the effects of purchasing power parity and market exchange rates, particularly on non-traded goods.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H3071B5D47A4245C491273F684CA8AD59"><enum>(3)</enum><text>An estimate of the magnitude of omitted spending from official defense budget information and, in the study required by subsection (a)(2), an accounting for such spending.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H76465F5960944111A59800ACD60909DE"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Methodology</header><text>The studies required by subsection (a) shall each employ a robust methodology that—</text> <paragraph id="H66A72E25040542BCB923968F801E1740"><enum>(1)</enum><text>does not depend on the official budget pronouncements of the Government of the People’s Republic of China or the Chinese Communist Party;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HADA4D780FCD94B6D971B4FFBB9A5A9DE"><enum>(2)</enum><text>takes into account the military-civil fusion present in the People’s Republic of China;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5912AA07ECD145729B91C4A177C9AF88"><enum>(3)</enum><text>employs the building-block method of analysis or a similar method of analysis, as appropriate; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA38C6221C9F4444198623B6B4F054150" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(4)</enum><text>excludes spending related to veterans benefits, other than military pensions provided to veterans.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H479E5C2B4A87461AA104D8529F137644"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Considerations</header><text>The studies required by this section may take into consideration the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H25A0AD27344E494390BEB95ACB78A844"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The effects of state-owned enterprises on the defense expenditures of the People’s Republic of China.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDBC8C5D318284DC59EAB39CDACEFE22B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The role of differing acquisition policies and structures with respect to the defense expenditures of each subject country.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE781DB5DD72A47819AF23CF73057ADB2"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Any other matter relevant to evaluating the resources dedicated to the defense spending or the various military-related outlays of the People’s Republic of China.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HD647247E8A3C4EB98B15E4449445D999"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The studies required by this section shall be submitted in unclassified form, without any designation relating to dissemination control, but may include classified annexes.</text></subsection></section>

<paragraph id="H917C4B95D0CA446590CC98301FFF762A"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The report required by paragraph (1) shall be submitted in unclassified form but may contain a classified annex.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF15CB8FFC69449C58FA315A4E6590243"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Public availability</header><text>The Secretary shall make available to the public the unclassified form of the report required by paragraph (1).</text></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle> 
<subtitle id="HC101DDDE5C1E454CAF1F9786D1830B21"><enum>B</enum><header>Matters relating to the AUKUS partnership</header> 
<section commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H6E674A19077B441DB4AED77D1DBE1459" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1321.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In this subtitle: </text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H51A8F1E2FAE741EDA185F400E00B2340"><enum>(1)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Appropriate congressional committees</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Except as otherwise provided, the term <term>appropriate congressional committees</term> means—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H141F342120654089B3C1812D911F3327" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Committee on Foreign Relations and the Committee on Armed Services of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H4AFE1BEBBC7D4BEBBAE22A31F9B4FD16" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Committee on Foreign Affairs and the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H209F19EF83C649118BA680E30EA3F66F"><enum>(2)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">AUKUS partnership</header> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H9CA3E8D380CC4AB3B752C832E17F1E2A"><enum>(A)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>AUKUS partnership</term> means the enhanced trilateral security partnership between Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States announced in September 2021. </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H8EE9B2E14A034D6FAB707A72391C7CC2"><enum>(B)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Pillars</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The AUKUS partnership includes the following two pillars:</text> 
<clause id="H07FC8F9842A6437D92CC5964441C3D9D" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Pillar One is focused on developing a pathway for Australia to acquire conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarines.</text></clause> <clause id="H4F1634C2D2234A569AAE4C3645020C7C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Pillar Two is focused on enhancing trilateral collaboration on advanced defense capabilities, including hypersonic and counter hypersonic capabilities, quantum technologies, undersea technologies, and artificial intelligence. </text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H1931E8AB586E48BBA2B756E1FF94B949"><enum>(3)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">International Traffic in Arms Regulations</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>International Traffic in Arms Regulations</term> means subchapter M of chapter I of title 22, Code of Federal Regulations (or successor regulations).</text></paragraph></section> <part id="H0A19B040C286494087E64C362B87F0D6"><enum>1</enum><header>Administrative provisions</header> <section id="H6F0B026DE80C4B7A83A038E48918D78F"><enum>1331.</enum><header>AUKUS partnership oversight and accountability framework</header> <subsection id="H0BDD6708BC4C4725B66C58FBBB6A27C6"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Senior advisor</header> <paragraph id="H19A8C2315C6346CEB16334EEAE7A4A15"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Designation</header> <subparagraph id="HDCB29264AEE64F4E9FED6840A7BCFCF9"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of State shall designate a senior advisor at the Department of State (in this section referred to as the <quote>Senior Advisor</quote>), who shall oversee and coordinate the implementation of the AUKUS partnership.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF9F8B0064F2C4AC98259864E74B03E4E"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Qualification</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Senior Advisor may be an individual serving within the existing leadership of the Department of State but that individual may not hold any other position concurrently while serving as the Senior Advisor.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H80B283A5EFEE46A291BAE6FB51289CA9"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Reporting</header><text>The Senior Advisor shall report directly to the Secretary of State.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HE060A03FEE1540C59AA92C8AB3955349"><enum>(D)</enum><header>Guidance</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of State shall issue guidance to all bureaus of the Department of State specifying the Senior Advisor’s responsibility for coordinating the implementation of all AUKUS partnership-related activities. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFF3A16B1182A4BEFB3A06A4E512BD4F8"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Duties</header><text>The duties of the Senior Advisor shall be to—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H2A7A701596974531930F61B8A1DDF08E"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">coordinate efforts to implement the AUKUS partnership across relevant bureaus, directorates, and offices of the Department of State involved in matters such as arms exports, non-proliferation, deterrence, security assistance, and Indo-Pacific and United Kingdom relations;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB6A5EC44D625444190FC3C6431E28665"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">serve as the lead within the Department of State on matters relating to the AUKUS partnership in the interagency process;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HA92420B4797842348F1BE08E2CD75D66"><enum>(C)</enum><text>lead diplomatic efforts related to the AUKUS partnership with other governments to explain how the partnership will enhance security and stability in the Indo-Pacific region; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H887EEBBE16D6475596BA87556A2846DF"><enum>(D)</enum><text>consult regularly with the appropriate congressional committees and keep such committees fully and currently informed on all aspects of the AUKUS partnership, to include—</text>
