<clause id="H854EF3C7FEA5432488E8634B2C20AFC0"><enum>(i)</enum><text>Australia’s acquisition of conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarines;</text></clause> <clause id="H023A541C25284E60B34117BC0E3D821E"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>jointly developing advanced military capabilities; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HEDA4193435FC43ADA8659E6F0E851E5D"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>any new programs under the AUKUS partnership.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFDF30081BC414C8B9E824D8C4E0AB807"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Personnel to support the Senior Advisor</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of State shall ensure that the Senior Advisor is adequately staffed with respect to the Senior Advisor’s duties described in paragraph (2) through details, or assignment of employees of the Department of State, with expertise consistent with such duties.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF76D9D723CB94F6E9F3ADD604E8E4367"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Task force</header> 
<paragraph id="H945823552A3146DBA79C16BC9E2BB35F"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of State shall establish a task force, to be known as the Task Force on AUKUS (in this section referred to as the <quote>Task Force</quote>), which—</text> <subparagraph id="H0C87D53EEAFA4E1CA9847128C11C8AF3"><enum>(A)</enum><text>shall meet regularly to coordinate internally on issues relating to the implementation of the AUKUS partnership; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF2117A89EEFF4BB1BFB53B8136EDB88D"><enum>(B)</enum><text>shall be led by the Senior Advisor.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H63FC11715A1748AA84E31EF9C6543E66"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Duties</header><text>The duties of the Task Force may include—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H1B765FA3C8434CC689790347AEFAA19A"><enum>(A)</enum><text>ensuring that responsible offices maintain a unified list of all defense-related transactions that have taken place under the AUKUS partnership; </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3CD1CE6371B54E8E9CE94A01D28912E9"><enum>(B)</enum><text>ensuring the establishment of a framework for gathering, maintaining, and exchanging information relating to companies, individuals, or entities that are compromising security of military technology, defense articles, and defense services exchanged under the AUKUS partnership; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HB7579D970E01471FB8E4DFFD5462E780"><enum>(C)</enum><text>establishing an AUKUS industry forum for industry stakeholders, including non-traditional defense contractors (as such term is defined in section 3014 of title 10, United States Code), that will be open for the participation of foreign industry involved in the AUKUS partnership.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2D3243E2E81A41379F92BE88706D0DA0"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Personnel to support the Task Force</header><text>The personnel assigned to support the Senior Advisor under subsection (a)(3) shall also support the Task Force. The Secretary of State may not assign any additional personnel to support the Task Force.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H5725FC15FDC64F868E79F53D6C8C4DB5"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Notification</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, or not later than 90 days after the date on which a senior advisor at the Department of State is designated as the Senior Advisor, whichever occurs earlier, the Secretary of State shall notify the appropriate congressional committees of the number of personnel, relevant expertise of such personnel, and duties of such personnel directly supporting the work of the Senior Advisor and the offices supporting the Task Force.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HA2B9DEE37D624429B942452F9A37DC6D"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report that includes the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="HD34E7F1A5E71497E8FD5E681151EFE47"><enum>(1)</enum><text>A detailed description of the planned work of the Senior Advisor and the Task Force on matters related to the implementation of the AUKUS partnership. </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF4C596DF40504CEEAE202E22030D08EC"><enum>(2)</enum><text>For the preceding two calendar years and the current calendar year—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HE0AA4775B3B4443B97C3EE06C60579B8"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the average and median times for the United States Government to review applications for licenses to export defense articles or defense services to persons, corporations, and the governments (including agencies and subdivisions of such governments, including official missions of such governments) of Australia or the United Kingdom; </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H935C0C8BCFA5455F84BC9AE634DDF133"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the average and median times for the United States Government to review applications from Australia and the United Kingdom for foreign military sales beginning from the date Australia or the United Kingdom submitted a letter of request that resulted in a letter of acceptance; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HB93DEFD3366E442383879BC8B492A4FD"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the number of applications from Australia and the United Kingdom for licenses to export defense articles and defense services that were denied or approved with provisos, listed by year. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB1F05190B73E4A1CA39C10C75B11BBBD"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">For each of the preceding two calendar years, the number of voluntary disclosures resulting in a violation of the International Traffic in Arms Regulations enumerated under section 40 of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2780">22 U.S.C. 2780</external-xref>) or involving proscribed countries listed in section 126.1 of the International Traffic in Arms Regulations, by persons, corporations, and the governments (including agencies and subdivisions of such governments, including official missions of such governments) of Australia or the United Kingdom, including information with respect to—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H5660E6F53A8F495BB03392AA5723EDBC"><enum>(A)</enum><text>any instance of unauthorized access to technical data or defense articles; </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H1C64CB3DDA2B4434B1E71481CB3E46BA"><enum>(B)</enum><text>inadequate physical or cyber security; </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFBA6038C0BB9417AA168261A85C649CB"><enum>(C)</enum><text>retransfers or re-exports without authorization; and </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HCE61E299C9064B289CE1523E9E628E13"><enum>(D)</enum><text>employees of foreign companies that are United States persons that provide defense services without authorization.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H7778765CC3EB48918D3596D5E6462DB6" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Annual report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter, the Senior Advisor shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report that includes—</text> <paragraph id="HA3B6AC6061D843BB86283E0566554E62" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text>a detailed description of any issues that representatives of the United States, the United Kingdom, or Australia have identified that threaten or conflict with the stated goals of the AUKUS partnership and any efforts to resolve these issues;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H9ECC5E6A528D4850BB53BD64697C86ED"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">information on the National Disclosure Policy Committee with respect to adoption of a classification category relating to any anticipatory disclosure policy for Australia and the United Kingdom;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H53F73656CC77456EB50D87D61A751B28" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a detailed description of Department of State investigations into violations under section 38 of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2778">22 U.S.C. 2778</external-xref>) or related provisions that involve AUKUS partners or entities in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8DE599A9CC944FEE9816AE692FD45D31" commented="no"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">details on whether regulatory changes to exemptions authorized under subsection (l) of section 38 of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2778">22 U.S.C. 2778</external-xref>), as added by section 1343 of this Act, are likely or necessary within the next year; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB249FE5E147F4D8AA99E7EAB5A641CF3"><enum>(5)</enum><text>an assessment of the change in the average and median Department of State licensing review times for the current reporting year based on the average and median licensing review times from the prior calendar year, including review times across the interagency for export licenses issued to Australia or the United Kingdom.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H904116A3EB7545BE9C97F89B1E6C68E6"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Sunset</header> 
<paragraph id="HE761241628B54FD1806C00F9EE8A2771"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Subject to paragraph (2), the position of the Senior Advisor and the Task Force shall terminate on the date that is 7 years after the date of the enactment of this Act.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H294EB6103FAE49D0AF60F22A68AF37EA"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Renewal</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of State may renew the position of the Senior Advisor and the Task Force for 1 additional period of 4 years beginning after the date on which the Secretary notifies the appropriate congressional committees of the renewal.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H71C8219363354C80A15AB19416036253" commented="no"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Appropriate congressional committees defined</header><text>In this section, the term <term>appropriate congressional committees</term> means—</text> <paragraph id="H53BBE5BB161A4977B6040350AD61D6C5" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the Committee on Foreign Affairs and Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA2B593486D06483BBC85904AFA93448E" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the Committee on Foreign Relations and Committee on Appropriations of the Senate.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HDF50375269DF4A17AD4EFEBC160094AD" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1332.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Designation of senior official for Department of Defense activities relating to, and implementation plan for, the AUKUS partnership</header> <subsection id="HBA31B58AC2A04341AC6E29858841D0CE" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Designation of senior official</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall designate a senior civilian official of the Department of Defense who shall be responsible for overseeing Department of Defense activities relating to the AUKUS partnership.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H4A6608C23A254A23911482A0EF73264C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Plan</header> 
<paragraph id="HC1FCB44C8C974457B9433F809F019FBD" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Administrator for Nuclear Security and the Secretary of State, shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report containing an implementation plan outlining Department of Defense efforts relating to the AUKUS partnership.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H8C6441989E5B4D37ABA77020CD7A6D3C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The plan required by paragraph (1) shall include the following:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H8E21B2786F50406D9CE7BA32C7B33871" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Timelines and major anticipated milestones for the implementation of the AUKUS partnership.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF0FE9F298279421CB0C20254B771B80D" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An identification of dependencies of such milestones on defense requirements that are—</text> 
<clause id="HF696B362754E4227BDC6A094F655CDF8" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">unrelated to the AUKUS partnership; and </text></clause> <clause id="HF53C9C4AB2AE47B78DDBBE0F6B7EC8B8" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">solely within the decisionmaking responsibility of Australia or the United Kingdom.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H7786F7D5E43E46558A223DCF8F0207C6" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A consideration of the implications of the plan on the industrial base with respect to—</text> <clause id="H4B43C7C34687483C88722527655906D2" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the expansion of existing United States submarine construction capacity to fulfill United States, United Kingdom, and Australia requirements;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H78F0D727DB6F4ACC9C6FC677BD0E44EE" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">acceleration of the restoration of United States capabilities for producing highly enriched uranium to fuel submarine reactors;</text></clause> <clause id="H43945074FE0840FAB6AD279B74ACEFF9" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">stabilization of commodity markets and expanding supplies of high-grade steel, construction materials, and other resources required for improving shipyard condition and expanding throughput capacity; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H31788DD08BF64027A2918F4379314923" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(iv)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">coordination and synchronization of industrial sourcing opportunities among Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H6AC3A15E5ECB41EFB46E0DBEC3855880" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of resourcing and personnel requirements, including—</text> 
<clause id="HF2E505C7848B496BBA923668FBC63477" commented="no"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a detailed assessment of the feasibility of hiring and retaining additional foreign disclosure officers to facilitate more rapid technology transfer to Australia and the United Kingdom; and</text></clause> <clause id="HEAB308D1FD58465DB9E6DCF24291CAC4" commented="no"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">an assessment of any additional requirements for Department of Defense personnel to support the transfer of defense articles to Australia and the United Kingdom.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H1F84244290824B81AFF04833743288D8" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(E)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A plan for improving information sharing, including—</text> <clause id="H0373FE1A2B8040CDA312591FC214E0C8" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">recommendations for modifications to foreign disclosure policies and processes;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HA719667D10824785878F43CCF2AA5928" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the promulgation of written information-sharing guidelines or policies to improve information sharing under the AUKUS partnership;</text></clause> <clause id="H67E92147F9C34A60B972D7F830968E86" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the establishment of an information handling caveat specific to the AUKUS partnership; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H29D8AD479F084BE69001BFC16C6C4C9A" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(iv)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the reduction in use of the Not Releasable to Foreign Nations (NOFORN) information handling caveat.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HD7BC4DB698764DB6966A1B65B58E0E95" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(F)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Processes for the protection of privately held intellectual property, including patents.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFC734150593045CD88D63F0D4793F5CF" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(G)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Recommended updates to other title 10, United States Code, authorities or regulatory, policy, or process frameworks.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H7034B5B52D384760B148279B33D331E6" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Semiannual updates</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 60 days after the date on which the plan required by subsection (b) is submitted, and semiannually thereafter not later than April 1 and October 1 each year through 2029, the senior civilian official designated under subsection (a) shall provide the congressional defense committees and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate with a briefing on the status of all Department activities to implement the AUKUS partnership.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H46F5871EA58343B182FFD32CDA245B3D" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1333.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Reporting related to the AUKUS partnership</header> 
<subsection id="HF4A76D3DC5CD4189A539D977965903FE" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Report on instruments</header> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HC4C5F55814014493869B228529473253"><enum>(1)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 30 days after the signature, conclusion, or other finalization of any non-binding instrument related to the AUKUS partnership, the President shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees the text of such instrument.</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H97228D81DA454B2CAD60F6CAC9AF9BE6"><enum>(2)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Non-duplication of efforts; rule of construction</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To the extent the text of a non-binding instrument is submitted to the appropriate congressional committees pursuant to paragraph (1), such text does not need to be submitted to Congress pursuant to section 112b(a)(1)(A)(ii) of title 1, United States Code, as amended by section 5947 of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/263">Public Law 117–263</external-xref>; 136 Stat. 3476). Paragraph (1) shall not be construed to relieve the executive branch of any other requirement of section 112b of title 1, United States Code, as so amended, or any other provision of law.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H634C97239BCD4454B42E232E6B3750DE" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this subsection:</text> <subparagraph id="HF3C0F3E84C5B4779825F93DE16408B7E" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>text</term>, with respect to a non-binding instrument, includes—</text> 
<clause id="H792BC7D55BC841738231AAB302A4F148" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">any annex, appendix, codicil, side agreement, side letter, or any document of similar purpose or function to the aforementioned, regardless of the title of the document, that is entered into contemporaneously and in conjunction with the non-binding instrument; and</text></clause> <clause id="HF17D81AE0EEA4B64B6EAC9D71D225786" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">any implementing agreement or arrangement, or any document of similar purpose or function to the aforementioned, regardless of the title of the document, that is entered into contemporaneously and in conjunction with the non-binding instrument.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H63878737A57144FEBCD723EB8E04313F" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Contemporaneously and in conjunction with</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">As used in subparagraph (A), the term <term>contemporaneously and in conjunction with</term>—</text> <clause id="H58F61598051F487C8C120720C10CE2AB" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">shall be construed liberally; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HEAD26F294EC14191B14731CA7AC1E358" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">may not be interpreted to require any action to have occurred simultaneously or on the same day.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HF5F9C97EEBB14A22A9ED3BBF65E3F556" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Report on AUKUS partnership</header> <paragraph id="HB7706F52A5C54D38A66824F5FB3EFCC3" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, and biennially thereafter, the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense and other appropriate heads of agencies, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report on the AUKUS partnership.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0266379FD69A4C51A2350590073E88E5" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Each report required under paragraph (1) shall include the following elements:</text> <subparagraph id="HECDE72F5B61E47E9A0BA79871A1516FE" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Strategy</header> <clause id="HC4FF4DA6C00347D0887A82BA1A809614" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An identification of the defensive military capability gaps and capacity shortfalls that the AUKUS partnership seeks to offset.</text></clause> 
<clause id="HDE38A08737164171A7E5AE5BEC7D7B9B" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An explanation of the total cost to the United States associated with Pillar One of the AUKUS partnership.</text></clause> <clause id="HAA4AC38918124BC58C36CA09F4D16DF8" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A detailed explanation of how enhanced access to the industrial base of Australia is contributing to strengthening the United States strategic position in Asia.</text></clause> 
<clause id="HD9ACED0FF6194B069C421092757902A1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(iv)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A detailed explanation of the military and strategic benefit provided by the improved access provided by naval bases of Australia.</text></clause> <clause id="H06392FDB78FF4792BCEDA83CF2605304" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(v)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A detailed assessment of how Australia’s sovereign conventionally armed nuclear attack submarines contribute to United States defense and deterrence objectives in the Indo-Pacific region.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H98E38FBEEB934427AE0A4CD0E9076C1F" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Implement the AUKUS partnership</header> 
<clause id="H99F0F1F7DA424E30A6168A4726E5E392" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Progress made on achieving the Optimal Pathway established for Australia’s development of conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarines, including the following elements:</text> <subclause id="HD8D7FCF3889D413E96D531FFD5F47B02" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(I)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of progress made by Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States to conclude an Article 14 arrangement with the International Atomic Energy Agency.</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="HDEBAFA91273D40C5A6B054826E54ED88" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(II)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of the status of efforts of Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States to build the supporting infrastructure to base conventionally armed, nuclear-powered attack submarines.</text></subclause> <subclause id="H72BAA16368064FB9BC223A42CB1A1F47" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(III)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Updates on the efforts by Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States to train a workforce that can build, sustain, and operate conventionally armed, nuclear-powered attack submarines.</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="HF21F37D089144996B0BE73DEB0F6BE05" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(IV)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of progress in establishing submarine support facilities capable of hosting rotational forces in western Australia by 2027.</text></subclause> <subclause id="H4C19E31AA2924A8AAE0544985C075FA3" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(V)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of progress made in improving United States submarine production capabilities that will enable the United States to meet—</text> 
<item commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2AD5A1CC55194CED800C6935DDF00AA9"><enum>(aa)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">its objectives of providing up to five Virginia Class submarines to Australia by the early to mid-2030’s; and </text></item> <item commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H22928980A9924F9A8E66B1B5C6E4BEFC"><enum>(bb)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">United States submarine production requirements.</text></item></subclause></clause> 
<clause id="H2D4252B8F3B1437AB61D86800C442DD1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Progress made on Pillar Two of the AUKUS partnership, including the following elements:</text> <subclause id="H83B11FE33B6B45E0B40C7E2A0C81BD5A" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(I)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of the efforts of Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States to enhance collaboration across the following eight trilateral lines of effort:</text> 
<item id="HB56246BB066F4B319B159F100E4AD05C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(aa)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Underseas capabilities.</text></item> <item id="H7017BFB5D84E43878FE05F74CBADDD4F" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(bb)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Quantum technologies.</text></item> 
<item id="H7B501129E7834E0DBE5D3A98BC6C7A8F" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(cc)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Artificial intelligence and autonomy.</text></item> <item id="H8DA95690CD78422AAC794606A8DEEAD8" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(dd)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Advanced cyber capabilities.</text></item> 
<item id="H380B7C1855FF4AF9A0479E823510C036" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ee)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Hypersonic and counter-hypersonic capabilities.</text></item> <item id="HE9B796D456DC4CD4943B3B2F598E178C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ff)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Electronic warfare.</text></item> 
<item id="HC24F987517304DB7A024C8DFE1FB2DCB" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(gg)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Innovation.</text></item> <item id="H315D302DB93D456A972E8C3F53CEE91E" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(hh)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Information sharing.</text></item></subclause> 
<subclause id="H0A8941B67A1140F78825BCAA73BCBCAE" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(II)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of any new lines of effort established. </text></subclause></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section></part> <part id="HD78CE9C798C84969915735612035073D"><enum>2</enum><header>Streamlining and protecting transfers of United States military technology from compromise</header> <section id="H4A35173C0A2C478995D25651BB199B63" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1341.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Priority for Australia and the United Kingdom in Foreign Military Sales and Direct Commercial Sales</header> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H38478118AD8F47E08C32E4284E2DAEA6"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The President shall institute policies and procedures for letters of request from Australia and the United Kingdom to transfer defense articles and services under section 21 of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2761">22 U.S.C. 2761</external-xref>) related to AUKUS to receive expedited consideration and processing relative to all other letters of request other than from Taiwan and Ukraine.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H12247E5424444DFEBD2A4A5F989424C1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Technology transfer policy for Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom</header> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H792202CFC6CE488AB090D727A6CF34FA"><enum>(1)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, shall create an anticipatory release policy for the transfer of technologies described in paragraph (2) to Australia, the United Kingdom, and Canada through Foreign Military Sales and Direct Commercial Sales that are not covered by an exemption under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations.</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HC3757278F51847F7B59F63349EA7F1C5"><enum>(2)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Capabilities described</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The capabilities described in this paragraph are— </text> 
<subparagraph id="HAC2EE23ED1D3435FBD40135C6E3504D9" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Pillar One-related technologies associated with submarine and associated combat systems; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HC0F65B01021F4E32A3DCD93879C63AD8" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Pillar Two-related technologies, including hypersonic missiles, cyber capabilities, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, undersea capabilities, and other advanced technologies.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H36359F53EADD4297899114DC80F3A670"><enum>(3)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Expedited decision-making</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Review of a transfer under the policy established under paragraph (1) shall be subject to an expedited decision-making process. </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H4C6F56DF37404BD5B5922076A3FE8722" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Interagency policy and guidance</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense shall jointly review and update interagency policies and implementation guidance related to requests for Foreign Military Sales and Direct Commercial Sales, including by incorporating the anticipatory release provisions of this section.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="HB57CFDCC6F7D4B15AE0805F440D6C443" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1342.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Identification and pre-clearance of platforms, technologies, and equipment for sale to Australia and the United Kingdom through Foreign Military Sales and Direct Commercial Sales</header> 
<subsection id="H2AB60C0050394F41BA27F756C8287ABE"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, and on a biennial basis thereafter for 8 years, the President shall submit to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives a report that includes a list of advanced military platforms, technologies, and equipment that are pre-cleared and prioritized for sale and release to Australia, the United Kingdom and Canada through the Foreign Military Sales and Direct Commercial Sales programs without regard to whether a letter of request or license to purchase such platforms, technologies, or equipment has been received from any of such country.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H973704CAABA44FB68C4E7B990BDB9D3D"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Additional items</header><text>Each list may include items that are not related to the AUKUS partnership but may not include items that are not covered by an exemption under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations except unmanned aerial or hypersonic systems.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H487ED268A7314B88AA715F12F1FCD425" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1343.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Export control exemptions and standards</header> 
<subsection id="H0EACE22DED2E4F77AEDE74C7BDC358D2" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Section 38 of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2778">22 U.S.C. 2778</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H49554422151E4E4D85EC2AD557C6165B"> <subsection id="H9FE22D5BED334D71837BD62945AFA086" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(l)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">AUKUS defense trade cooperation</header> <paragraph id="HDE83891BF01C4CB88A527E411724F872"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Determination and certification</header> <subparagraph id="HBA0F984A4EB94218A29F6B964269C17E"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this subsection, the President shall determine and certify in writing, and include a detailed justification, to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives whether Australia or the United Kingdom has—</text> 
<clause id="H39B940FD2A12461DB1D3F43FBFE7D8AC"><enum>(i)</enum><text>implemented a system of export controls comparable to those of the United States that satisfies the elements of subsection (j)(2)(A)(i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) and subsection (j)(2)(B)(i), (ii) and (v) for United States-origin defense articles and defense services, and for controlling the provision of military training; and</text></clause> <clause id="H922B432699844408A0EA532F6B856BE4"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>implemented a comparable exemption from its export controls for the United States.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H79F87F2372D84FFC908154EF12808779"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Matters to be included</header> 
<clause id="HA8D0FFD26B3941C6895C12A24D78FC55"><enum>(i)</enum><header>Requirements met</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the President makes the determination that Australia or the United Kingdom meets the comparability standards of clauses (i) and (ii) of subparagraph (A), the justification required by such subparagraph shall include an assessment of how the country satisfied the specific elements described in such clauses.</text></clause> <clause id="H09F91136058F46ABA8DC480F7DA8B02D"><enum>(ii)</enum><header>Requirements not met</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the President makes a determination that Australia or the United Kingdom does not meet the comparability standards of clauses (i) and (ii) of subparagraph (A), the justification required by such subparagraph shall include, as applicable—</text> 
<subclause id="HF851350EB08247BB9ED245F9A22DB09A"><enum>(I)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the specific elements of either such clause (i) or (ii) that were determined not to meet the comparability standards;</text></subclause> <subclause id="H068B7BDFB625422383411BC0EDBAA124"><enum>(II)</enum><text>the specific actions the country needs to take in order to meet the comparability standards; and</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="H2A9BCB4936C34BB49AC1B33235BE320C"><enum>(III)</enum><text>the actions the United States is taking, as appropriate, to facilitate that the country is granted an exemption in a timely manner upon meeting the comparability standards.</text></subclause></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2086FFB9EFF3413988E5FAA521A4FAB4"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The determination and certification described in subparagraph (A) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE1049A0E7C9E4C39A3674B498537FE2E"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Exemption</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Upon submittal of a determination and certification to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives that Australia or the United Kingdom has met the comparability standards of clauses (i) and (ii) of paragraph (1)(A), and subject to the limitation in paragraph (4), the President shall immediately exempt from the licensing or other approval requirements of this section exports and transfers (including reexports, transfers, temporary imports, and brokering activities) of defense articles and defense services between the United States and that country or among the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5D90C13D2D7047E0A09D09858E36F251"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Reassessment</header> <subparagraph id="H6718CBE3F4DC4A9CAF2D10DDC1AFBE0B"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>If the President is unable to make a determination that Australia or the United Kingdom has met the comparability standards of clauses (i) and (ii) of paragraph (1)(A) or suspends the exemption pursuant to paragraph (5), the President shall—</text> 
<clause id="HE858F838A0E64BAC95EBE1D714390D71"><enum>(i)</enum><text>not less frequently than once every 120 days reassess whether the country has met those requirements;</text></clause> <clause id="HE98C5AEC8D7F44B9889CA480AE1AA2AE"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>report the results of such reassessment in writing, and include a detailed justification, to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H526662306CB44168B87C5BCA5BFA8258"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>report on steps the country must take to establish the exemption.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3350C6A367FA4244902D7B9DC36050B0"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Positive reassessment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Upon any reassessment under subparagraph (A) in which the President determines that Australia or the United Kingdom has met the comparability standards of clauses (i) and (ii) of paragraph (1)(A), the President shall immediately provide to that country an exemption described in paragraph (2).</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H22CD67EB55954A76815A119DB6143769"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Negative reassessment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the President finds in any reassessment under subparagraph (A) that Australia or the United Kingdom has not met the comparability standards of clauses (i) and (ii) of paragraph (1)(A), the written reassessment shall include, as applicable—</text> <clause id="HE3139E850D1E4BC5A2953D3CAF4F28A1"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the specific elements of either such clauses that were determined not to be comparable;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HEC97551E2A0C4E95A7159B32C4678000"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the specific actions the country needs to take in order to meet the comparability standards; and</text></clause> <clause id="HB4AF98F79B024C6EB4045BC3744A2574"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the actions the United States is taking, as appropriate, to facilitate that the country is granted an exemption in a timely manner upon meeting the comparability standards.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFE41D99A797B4E91BD6CABE9BAAB8D28"><enum>(D)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The reassessment described in subparagraph (A)(ii) shall be submitted in an unclassified form, but may include a classified annex.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H466F2CF0AA9F4477933A70BD56A7253F"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Limitation</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An exemption described in paragraph (2) shall not apply to any activity (including exports, transfers, reexports, retransfers, temporary imports, or brokering) of defense articles and defense services between or among the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia that—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HD22AB27B38A44282B47C3BAD37BEF9FF"><enum>(A)</enum><text>are excluded by those countries;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE573B8D9DC3E4571BE9642F6589741DD"><enum>(B)</enum><text>are referred to in subsection (j)(1)(C)(ii); or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H276D600C73B74DFC9A556B964F7580FF"><enum>(C)</enum><text>involve individuals or entities that are not approved by—</text> <clause id="HCBBCC964BBA246D6981E3CBB7999573C"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the Secretary of State; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HDECE61786EB04475B6E6CA342E023B81"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the Ministry of Defense, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or other similar authority within those countries.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9C39D36EBB714B07AD46A84F8526D901"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Temporary suspension of exemption</header> <subparagraph id="H433C4DA8C5C5448BBDF9D59AF8F0723E"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The President may suspend an exemption described in paragraph (2) with respect to Australia or the United Kingdom if the President determines and certifies in writing, and includes a detailed justification, to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives that—</text> 
<clause id="HE655380D86D14865B056EFB60EB6812A"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the country has ceased to implement a system of export controls comparable to those of the United States that satisfies the elements of subsection (j)(2)(A)(i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) and subsection (j)(2)(B)(i), (ii) and (v) for United States-origin defense articles and defense services, and for controlling the provision of military training; and</text></clause> <clause id="H43F3D0B3ECE944A9ABC92B5EA8907F10"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>due to a substantial change in circumstance, the suspension is necessary to protect the vital national security or foreign policy interests of the United States in relation to the country concerned; or</text></clause> 
<clause id="H04B4A89FD6DC4FBF9C1423E69960F803"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the country concerned has ceased to implement a comparable exemption from its export controls for the United States.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3DE5D8C1C61845D5AC97F4B0E3DFCF46"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Additional matter to be included</header><text>The justification required to be included in the determination and certification described in subparagraph (A) shall also include a description of the specific actions the United States and the country are taking to address the reasons for the suspension.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H13AB13A884184933B1C7A5BD40BFA6B5"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The determination and certification described in subparagraph (A) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE5D062E502014BC0B846E2611DE40705" commented="no"><enum>(D)</enum><header>Report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the President reissues an exemption described in paragraph (2) with respect to Australia or the United Kingdom that the President suspended pursuant to subparagraph (A), the President shall submit to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives a report stating the steps the country took that allowed the exemption to be so reinstated.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA7CFB753A83F498C8D3F32EE3273F087"><enum>(6)</enum><header>Certain requirements not applicable</header> 
<subparagraph id="HB42E7F6E57164A8280B06DE0A1DB7F5D"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of section 3(d) shall not apply to any export or transfer that is the subject of an exemption described in paragraph (2).</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H52AA0580C0574F35B578213FAF9E9E24"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Quarterly reports</header><text>The Secretary of State shall—</text> 
<clause id="H6107374DF905448AAF29C8E5E5B5512B"><enum>(i)</enum><text>require all exports and transfers that would be subject to the requirements of paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of section 3(d) but for the application of subparagraph (A) to be reported to the Secretary; and</text></clause> <clause id="HA41814C32E77433C938E8C10EFBA04A0"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>submit such reports to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives on a quarterly basis.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8C5DA66318D04FEBAA41BEDEC4A66B13"><enum>(7)</enum><header>Sunset</header> 
<subparagraph id="H9FC0C3D5C1284C50AE96E03FC41C2AE7"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Any exemption described in paragraph (2) shall terminate on the date that is 15 years after the date of the enactment of this subsection.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HEB0B34583B60473B94FAFAD89F2B888B"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Renewal</header><text>The Secretary of State may renew such exemption for 5 years upon a certification to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives that such exemption is in the vital national interest of the United States with a detailed justification for such certification.”.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection><after-quoted-block display="yes">.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA344A1A5FB774EF5ADB213448A2DE8A1"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Reports</header> 
<paragraph id="HCD27E967722E4E9AA2631BBF31086B8F"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter until no exemptions described in subsection (l)(2) of section 38 of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2778">22 U.S.C. 2778</external-xref>), as added by subsection (a) of this section, remain in effect, the Secretary of State shall submit to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives a report on the operation of exemptions described in such subsection (l)(2), including whether any changes to such exemptions are likely to be made in the coming year.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H19DCBD3FF2CD436C84EEF134473D524E"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Initial report</header><text>The first report submitted under paragraph (1) shall also include an assessment of key recommendations the United States Government has provided to the Governments of Australia and the United Kingdom to revise laws, regulations, and policies of such countries that are required to implement the AUKUS partnership.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC81B318E324D4D9CAB46166F13DDCC67"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Report on expedited review of export licenses for exports of advanced technologies</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, shall report on the practical application of a possible “fast track” decision-making process for applications, classified or unclassified, to export defense articles and defense services to Australia, the United Kingdom, and Canada.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H536846D7434849B9ACC330D215605F32" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1344.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Expedited review of export licenses for exports of advanced technologies to Australia, the United Kingdom, and Canada</header> <subsection id="H47CBAE54706347D0BAA9DD8EDC2DE989" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, shall initiate a rulemaking to establish an expedited decision-making process, classified or unclassified, for applications to export to Australia, the United Kingdom, and Canada commercial, advanced-technology defense articles and defense services that are not covered by an exemption under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations. </text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H4B90846076514B248BCE767EE98958F4" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Eligibility</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To qualify for the expedited decision-making process described in subsection (a), an application shall be for an export of defense articles or defense services that will take place wholly within or between the physical territory of Australia, Canada, or the United Kingdom and the United States and with governments or corporate entities from such countries.</text></subsection> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H58359F533559453E9C9B7B2A3AEBAB2D"><enum>(c)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Availability of expedited process</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The expedited decision-making process described in subsection (a) shall be available for both classified and unclassified items, and the process must satisfy the following criteria to the extent practicable:</text> 
<paragraph id="HDBD14BF297E34C479D3829DF120C47DE" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any licensing application to export defense articles and services that is related to a government to government agreement must be approved, returned, or denied within 30 days of submission.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H1195B2329CC44BB9A68E9DC858F2AEDB" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">For all other licensing requests, any review shall be completed not later than 45 calendar days after the date of application.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="HF115576035B0499C986276F394F841DC" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1345.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">United States Munitions List</header> 
<subsection id="H393276269AD649A882D80624E656D406" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Exemption for the governments of the United Kingdom and Australia from certification and congressional notification requirements applicable to certain transfers</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Section 38(f)(3) of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2778">22 U.S.C. 2778(f)(3)</external-xref>) is amended by inserting <quote>, the United Kingdom, or Australia</quote> after <quote>Canada</quote>.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HAF58BA7100B349CCAF3C64F1F12A31F1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">United States Munitions List periodic reviews</header> <paragraph id="H32208E202FA24EB2A9CB3315A88BA4F2" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of State, acting through authority delegated by the President to carry out periodic reviews of items on the United States Munitions List under section 38(f) of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2778">22 U.S.C. 2778(f)</external-xref>) and in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of Energy, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, shall carry out such reviews not less frequently than every 3 years.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5D7551FFEFCF430A986DCA36BFD673A1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Scope</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The periodic reviews described in paragraph (1) shall focus on matters including—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H5772C274B5814ECDB6E4ADDB4EF57F2C"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">interagency resources to address current threats faced by the United States; </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H85108BF585A74489B027FE73BCDAC953"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the evolving technological and economic landscape; </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H492E0231618A4034BD7E13ECF93C155C"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the widespread availability of certain technologies and items on the United States Munitions List; and </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H0C30719415CD4FC6831A7741513CFC13"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">risks of misuse of United States-origin defense articles.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC602460233ED43108AA98347DB37553D" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Consultation</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Department of State may consult with the Defense Trade Advisory Group (DTAG) and other interested parties in conducting the periodic review described in paragraph (1).</text></paragraph></subsection></section></part> 
<part id="H8BC265DF58934A918CEF4FF658C3C99A"><enum>3</enum><header>AUKUS Submarine Transfer Authorization Act</header> 
<section id="H6076985E8B5840C7BCF4C2A0C7E401C5" commented="no"><enum>1351.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This part may be cited as the <quote>AUKUS Submarine Transfer Authorization Act</quote>. </text></section> <section id="H75DAD65D70B740C988DDBF4AA857FDE7"><enum>1352.</enum><header>Authorization of sales of Virginia Class submarines to Australia</header> <subsection id="H54084F2DA7084B13AE870CB3E0DE2BB2"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Effective beginning on the date that is one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the President is authorized to transfer up to two Virginia Class submarines from the inventory of the Department of the Navy to the Government of Australia on a sale basis, and transfer not more than one additional Virginia Class submarine to the Government of Australia on a sale basis pursuant to section 21 of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2761">22 U.S.C. 2761</external-xref>) during the 20-year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act, to implement the trilateral security partnership between Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States (in this section referred to as the <quote>AUKUS partnership</quote>).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HFCDE859546314ED9B50F08A5ED7B3175"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Provisions of law superseded</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The transfer of a vessel authorized under subsection (a) shall not be subject to the requirements of—</text> <paragraph id="H2C4DD6FE621D458CB3C44AE12C7D3101"><enum>(1)</enum><text>section 36 of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2776">22 U.S.C. 2776</external-xref>); or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H16BF35ECB5204EAB80944B6CC7604EAE"><enum>(2)</enum><text>section 8677 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HEA6F867D294448BEA55D2D2FD55DEA41"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Costs of transfers</header><text>Any expense incurred by the United States in connection with a transfer of a vessel authorized under subsection (a) shall be charged to the Government of Australia notwithstanding section 516(e) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2321j">22 U.S.C. 2321j(e)</external-xref>).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H5A4B57BAADDB469A871C663309581ECA"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Certifications and other requirements</header> 
<paragraph id="H5AE2DFD0ED65448FB9506C3774237980"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 270 days prior to the transfer of a vessel authorized under subsection (a), the President shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees and leadership a certification that—</text> <subparagraph id="HFFB1F69B079C4168BED492D40E421D5F"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the transfer of such vessels—</text> 
<clause id="H16209AA5BBCB4E9AAAB19DA91B5C3B50"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">will not degrade the United States undersea capabilities;</text></clause> <clause id="HA9FB609019034A40A302F2C4726AAC32" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>is consistent with United States foreign policy and national security interests; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HBFCE6A55D7214CC586379DB161CFED4E"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>is in furtherance of the AUKUS partnership;</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H8A0001D4B9C546FB80A53282C534719A"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the United States is making sufficient submarine production and maintenance investments to meet the combination of United States military requirements and the requirements under subparagraph (A);</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H7B1300BE696C47348D70DEBD1BBBCFD9"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Government of Australia has provided the appropriate funds and support for the additional capacity required to meet the requirements identified in this section; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HCFFE32F998904DBC936D711CB6AE8A74"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Government Australia has the capability to host and fully operate the vessels authorized to be transferred. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HDFA3A26EDCF84FA58E41C664999A110D"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Waiver of chief of naval operations certification</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The requirement for the Chief of Naval Operations to make a certification under section 8678 of title 10, United States Code, shall not apply to the transfer of a vessel authorized under subsection (a).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H276B5F72741C4B0BAB24E79925AB6FC8" commented="no"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Required mutual defense agreement</header> <subparagraph id="H68F7CAA66096498D928F87D301AFB7D2"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The President may not provide for the transfer of a vessel authorized under subsection (a) unless the United States and Australia have entered into a mutual defense agreement that meets the requirements of subparagraph (B) and such agreement is in effect.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC794BA8D19C548A8932E535C222BDED2"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Requirements</header><text>A mutual defense agreement meets the requirements described in this subparagraph if the agreement—</text> <clause id="H506A720E2F3F4EB6B5B1D8C6A5E00591"><enum>(i)</enum><text>provides a clear legal framework for the sole purpose of Australia’s acquisition of conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarines; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H3B1373CB502E42338EA426842833980F"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>meets the highest nonproliferation standards for the exchange of nuclear materials, technology, equipment, and information between the United States and Australia.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H171E09657ED54607BA48A53618503344" commented="no"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Subsequent sales</header><text>A transfer of vessel that is a Virginia class submarine on a sale basis other than a transfer described in subsection (a) may occur only if such transfer is explicitly authorized pursuant to a law enacted after the date of the enactment of this Act. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H85B928CACF324835B4658293692AAD36" commented="no"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Crediting of receipts</header> 
<paragraph id="H567BF8E1933B45B595DB89DC3CC6DAF3"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Notwithstanding any provision of law pertaining to the crediting of amounts received from a sale under the terms of section 21 of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2761">22 U.S.C. 2761</external-xref>), any receipt of the United States as a result of a transfer of a vessel authorized under subsection (a) shall—</text> <subparagraph id="H74B95C3321064EFE928ED3F2AE296D89"><enum>(A)</enum><text>be credited, at the discretion of the President to—</text> 
<clause id="H6776A9D97B3A4F5ABB8533BFDC56A4DF"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the appropriation, fund, or account used in incurring the original obligation; </text></clause> <clause id="H9572A2E7A14B4CFEAA60BC53D75A81BD"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>an appropriate appropriation, fund, or account currently available for the purposes for which the expenditures for the original acquisition of submarines transferred under this section were made; or</text></clause> 
<clause id="H041BB191E0BA4AB8B02FB506D18EE91B"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>any other appropriation, fund, or account available for the improvement of the United States submarine industrial base; and </text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF399668140FB498588AD92FD5B8F068A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>remain available for obligation until expended for the same purpose as the appropriation to which the receipt is credited.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1AE127F198D74DF7A83E6E3D49EEC8DD"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Notifications and Report</header> 
<subparagraph id="H2341022620254EDB90948EA5E04E21A0"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Initial notification</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 30 days before the date of the delivery of the first vessel authorized to be transferred under subsection (a), the President shall notify the appropriate congressional committees and leadership of the following:</text> <clause id="HDF0203A4F9274B21ABB0CA2622A4571A"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Government of Australia has achieved Submarine Rotational Forces-West full operational capability to support 4 rotationally deployed Virginia class submarines and one Astute class submarine, including having demonstrated the domestic capacity to fully perform all the associated activities necessary for the safe hosting and operation of nuclear-powered submarines.</text></clause> 
<clause id="H75CFC821DEBA489781069806A1E6C1D3"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Government of Australia has achieved sovereign-ready initial operational capability to support a Royal Australian Navy Virginia class submarine, including having demonstrated the domestic capacity to fully perform all the associated— </text> <subclause id="HB1CEFEC5C0D6445897044509A275302A"><enum>(I)</enum><text>activities necessary for the safe hosting and operation of nuclear-powered submarines;</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="HEF6A849209A5448D8AA3DB8DF0DD6A52"><enum>(II)</enum><text>crewing;</text></subclause> <subclause id="H82F8D91154A546FE87E71B29DA6FF804"><enum>(III)</enum><text>operations;</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="H98B48D390E3D4E0892F36A3350CD76D2"><enum>(IV)</enum><text>regulatory and emergency procedures, including those specific to nuclear power plants; and</text></subclause> <subclause id="H43995E0E3BCC40CDACCD0768E6C21DD9"><enum>(V)</enum><text>detailed planning for enduring Virginia class submarine ownership, including each significant event leading up to and including nuclear defueling.</text></subclause></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HE70B885AC6DB40F681C2E14AAE66B43F" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Notification</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 30 days after the date of a transfer of any vessel authorized under subsection (a), and upon any transfer or depositing of funds received pursuant to such a transfer, the President shall notify the appropriate congressional committees and leadership of—</text> <clause id="H341C11A57332428DABB40405133763DD"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the amount of funds received pursuant to the transfer; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H1AD7AB37B888428E85CACA28158DD951"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the specific account or fund into which the funds described in clause (i) are deposited.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9B61292639F54707939A4B7E398C6083"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than 30 days after the receipt of funds as described in subparagraph (B), the President shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees and leadership a report on the matters described in clauses (i) and (ii) of subparagraph (A).</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H2CFEC70538A145E1A84337793E98C837" commented="no"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Applicability of existing law to transfer of special nuclear material and utilization facilities for military applications</header> 
<paragraph id="H9BB52799144B447380F1EB119F947035" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>With respect to any special nuclear material for use in utilization facilities or any portion of a vessel transferred under the authority of subsection (a) constituting utilization facilities for military applications under section 91 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/2121">42 U.S.C. 2121</external-xref>), the transfer of such material or such facilities shall only occur in accordance with such section 91.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2AE5E9B1D5D74E2595F73440F02F1046" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Use of funds</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The President may use proceeds from a transfer described in subparagraph (1) for the acquisition of submarine naval nuclear propulsion plants and the nuclear fuel to replace the propulsion plants and fuel transferred to the Government of Australia.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H006FAE605F334A73A667C68C6C99E84F" commented="no"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Repair and refurbishment of AUKUS submarines</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Section 8680 of title 10, United States Code, is amended—</text> <paragraph id="H5491C813A66F4EC3A264ECC366C25F23" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text>by redesignating subsection (c) as subsection (d); and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HEFA73758786345E5AAACE9E5B8AB448F" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><text>by inserting after subsection (b) the following new subsection:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" id="HAD00BAC5D4684FAA86095391B3BBD370" display-inline="no-display-inline"> <subsection id="H06949E06731F47DB9B524BA847CEE030" commented="no"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Repair and refurbishment of certain submarines</header> <paragraph id="HBFD6AB1E6D654381AF2BF72BB7B86017" display-inline="yes-display-inline" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, and subject to paragraph (2), the President shall determine the appropriate public or private shipyard in the United States, Australia, or the United Kingdom to perform any repair or refurbishment of a United States submarine involved in submarine security activities between the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB7E0F2C6061C471CB9D91861DA7FEBE6" indent="up1" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum> 
<subparagraph id="H1F92A97A0ED241C08B6DADDB4898E581" display-inline="yes-display-inline" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text>The President may determine under paragraph (1) that repair or refurbishment described in such paragraph may be performed in Australia or the United Kingdom only if—</text> <clause id="HD749BA6291F94C59A7E9BFA80AD79ACF" indent="up1" commented="no"><enum>(i)</enum><text>such repair or refurbishment will facilitate the development of repair or refurbishment capabilities in the United Kingdom or Australia;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HE897082ED3B6494DA1B0F08DE8BF5146" indent="up1" commented="no"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>such repair or refurbishment will be for a United States submarine that is operating forward outside of the United States; or</text></clause> <clause id="H942131ABEC074375A5CED12C80558085" indent="up1" commented="no"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the Secretary of Defense certifies to Congress that performing such repair or refurbishment at a shipyard in Australia or the United Kingdom is required due to an exigent threat to the national security interests of the United States.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H81DEB056872A4A15AEBC52A4A26B235F" indent="up1" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>In making a determination under subparagraph (A), the President shall consider any effects of such determination on the capacity and capability of shipyards in the United States.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H65BA6BB60A354033B9EF22BC1E7A546A" indent="up1" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Not later than 15 days after the date on which the Secretary of Defense makes a certification under subparagraph (A)(iii), the Secretary shall brief the congressional defense committees on—</text> 
<clause id="H04D75AA945994F9FBB5E9B92FCD87A6B" commented="no"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the threat that requires the use of a shipyard in Australia or the United Kingdom; and</text></clause> <clause id="HF17BAB47251042F48EC43700C186A31D" commented="no"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>opportunities to mitigate the future potential need to leverage foreign shipyards.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H20244AB3D0394711B81D10B2D149BE6E" indent="up1" commented="no"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Repair or refurbishment described in paragraph (1) may be carried out by personnel and contractors of the United States, the United Kingdom, or Australia in accordance with the international arrangements governing the submarine security activities described in such paragraph.</text></paragraph></subsection><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H2664DA728D354669A29624FA87F16826"><enum>(h)</enum><header>Transfer or export of defense services</header> <paragraph id="HF1FCBF7E3AB543FBBBDE14666ED87CF3"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The President may transfer or authorize the export of defense services (as such term is defined in section 47 of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2794">22 U.S.C. 2794</external-xref>)) to the Government of Australia and the Government of the United Kingdom necessary or incidental to support the transfer and operation of vessels authorized under subsection (a).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H658AA0D2E5B2498F93D23FD06B63401C"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Authority to export to Australian and United Kingdom private and public-sector personnel</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The transfer or export of defense services under this subsection may be directly exported to private and public-sector personnel of Australia or to private and public-sector personnel of the United Kingdom to support the development of the Australian submarine industrial base necessary for submarine security activities between members of the AUKUS partnership, including in the case in which such private and public-sector personnel are not officers, employees, or agents of the Government of Australia or the Government of the United Kingdom.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HBB023E3FE8A24F34995E10E9DA1924F4"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Application of requirements for retransfer and reexport</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any person who receives any defense service transferred or exported under paragraph (1) may retransfer or reexport such service to other persons only in accordance with the requirements of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2751">22 U.S.C. 2751 et seq.</external-xref>).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H06B3CC4FC0AE474CB82A0F524D6AAB05"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Security controls</header> 
<subparagraph id="H9009501289FC400ABC41617E2289588C"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Any defense service transferred or exported under paragraph (1) shall be subject to appropriate security controls to ensure that any sensitive information conveyed by such transfer or export is protected from disclosure to persons unauthorized by the United States to receive such information.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H6B7E83809AFA4056B392B8992DC05FDA"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Certification</header><text>Not later than 30 days before the first transfer or export of a defense service under paragraph (1), and annually thereafter, the President shall certify to the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives that the controls described in subparagraph (A) will protect the information described in such subparagraph for the defense services so transferred or exported.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H57163E4CB7994C0C9F3CC6E2C238DCF7"><enum>(i)</enum><header>Report</header> 
<paragraph id="HCB861245B3DA4B689FC7C632820096F3"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act and annually thereafter for 15 years, the President shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees and leadership a report describing—</text> <subparagraph id="H4D046AB3C7014F84933A86C2E11FDBD0"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the status of the transfer of vessels authorized under subsection (a);</text></subparagraph>
