<subparagraph id="H2555603806D249D9A98AA2B258C43769"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the implementation of submarine security cooperation under the AUKUS partnership and challenges towards its implementation;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HC5CC74312D9A4789889A8B005E3E22EC"><enum>(C)</enum><text>expansion of the public and private Virginia class submarine production and repair facilities, to include proposed work conducted in Australia and the United Kingdom to meet the additional work required by commitments under the AUKUS partnership;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HD5B2358AAD044A98886F7D7ABC26D8B8"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">an annual procurement schedule for the total quantity of submarines the Department of Defense plans to procure over the 15 years following the date of the enactment of this Act; and </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H134E408F5D1F45069249BF2E76CCCB24"><enum>(E)</enum><text>a list of transfers or exports of defense services authorized under subsection (h) and the private-sector personnel of Australia or the private-sector personnel of the United Kingdom to whom the defense services were exported.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H9A7F850F96EE44078922C04457575712"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The report required by this subsection shall be submitted in classified form.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H7D7625E156034C979A4A9731ED085F35"><enum>1353.</enum><header>Acceptance of contributions in support of Australia, United Kingdom, and United States submarine security activities</header> <subsection id="H1E5AF8B1850D47A896DA7547EBA056A4"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Acceptance authority</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The President may accept from the Government of Australia contributions of money made by the Government of Australia for use by the Department of Defense in support of non-nuclear related aspects of submarine security activities between Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States (in this section referred to as the ‘AUKUS partnership’).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HB0ECBBFE0A6D4A90913585556F726FA7"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Establishment of Submarine Security Activities Account</header> 
<paragraph id="H21CEC6ED6A40454FB56D25E8A83EB8D3"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>There is established in the Treasury of the United States a special account to be known as the <quote>Submarine Security Activities Account</quote>.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6EEE698574EF41558C2C3F0D87291F4E"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Credit to account</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Contributions of money accepted by the President under subsection (a) shall be credited to the Submarine Security Activities Account.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1FBF12F8926F4AE0AFD5A01120C6B5D5"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Availability</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Amounts credited to the Submarine Security Activities Account shall remain available until expended.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HDAD7AF4A78594CFC80BE89EC5101A73C"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Use of funds</header> <paragraph id="H906800E60876466EA426CABD7D619972"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Subject to paragraphs (2) and (3) of subsection (b), the President may use funds in the Submarine Security Activities Account—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H0DDAE8E189DE481F945D42E396065CE4"><enum>(A)</enum><text>for any purpose authorized by law that the President determines would support the AUKUS submarine security activities;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H635BF3C404244D0CB6611EEFE4E94866"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to carry out a military construction project that is consistent with the purposes for which the contributions were made and is authorized by law;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFB3B64930E834178BC27AE59F8FC350A"><enum>(C)</enum><text>to develop and increase the submarine industrial base workforce by investing in recruiting, training, and retaining key specialized labor at public and private shipyards; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H4D5C9B363901489B98A36217BDFC782D"><enum>(D)</enum><text>to upgrade facilities, equipment, and infrastructure needed to repair and maintain submarines at public and private shipyards. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCD965A180D3D4D9398393EF70682406C"><enum>(2)</enum><header>No further specific authorization in law required</header><text>Funds in the Submarine Security Activities Account may be used as described in this subsection without further specific authorization in law. </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HB855636A762647FF96DC05E356F5CA74"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Plan for use of funds</header><text>Not later than 30 days prior to any use of any funds in the Submarine Security Activities Account, the President shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees and leadership a plan detailing—</text> 
<paragraph id="H80598D65967648BDBC35DA15BA176454"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the amount of funds in the Submarine Security Activities Account; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H253479E59DA14BCBB30A85F7419E3265"><enum>(2)</enum><text>how such funds will be used, including specific amounts and purposes. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HC931EB81786844C5935FCCA520233A9B"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Transfers of funds</header> 
<paragraph id="H6A7B1B0191EF44A786437C809F13CC42"><enum>(1)</enum><header>To Department of Defense</header> 
<subparagraph id="HF94139BA585A406E90FD40A14748B176"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>In carrying out subsection (c), the President may transfer funds available in the Submarine Security Activities Account to appropriations available to the Department of Defense.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H40419EADF5B144069E944C1B7172A2BD"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Authority in addition to other transfer authority</header><text>The authority provided in this paragraph is in addition to any other transfer authority otherwise provided by law and is subject to the same terms and conditions as the authority provided in section 8005 of the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2023 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/328">Public Law 117–328</external-xref>), except for monetary limitations concerning the amount of authority available.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H70A4C197F00B42778DA5B0C1828DA3C1"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Availability</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Funds transferred under the authority provided in this paragraph shall be merged with and available for the same purposes, and for the same time period, as the appropriation to which transferred.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9DEA4274EA7040349F854AF1FA6E24C5"><enum>(D)</enum><header>Limitation on certain transactions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Contributions referred to in subsection (a) may not be obligated for a transaction authorized in subsection (c)(1)(B) until the President submits to the appropriate congressional committees and leadership notice of the transaction, including a detailed cost estimate, and a period of 21 days has elapsed after the date on which the notification is received by the appropriate congressional committees and leadership or, if earlier, a period of 14 days has elapsed after the date on which a copy of the notification is provided in an electronic medium.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC1DC41A8A8E648D5AE3BA431F3D7085A"><enum>(2)</enum><header>To Department of Energy</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In carrying out subsection (c), and in accordance with the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/2011">42 U.S.C. 2011 et seq.</external-xref>), the President may transfer funds available in the Submarine Security Activities Account to appropriations or funds of the Department of Energy available to carry out activities related to AUKUS submarine security activities.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H14F0FB521BBD460497F31D5EA9F541CE"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Transfers back to Submarine Security Activities Account</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Upon a determination by the President that all or part of the funds transferred from the Submarine Security Activities Account under this subsection are not necessary for the purposes for which such funds were transferred, all or such part of such funds shall be transferred back to the Submarine Security Activities Account. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H18682BBBE9D2475C96CFA5F5822973DF"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Investment of money</header> 
<paragraph id="H852D4404AD3542FC92192BD08EBDB5F7"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The President may invest money in the Submarine Security Activities Account in securities of the United States or in securities guaranteed as to principal and interest by the United States.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE3CC94E0198847C592DF54A0C5B08814"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Interest</header><text>Any interest or other income that accrues from investment in securities referred to in paragraph (1) shall be deposited to the credit of the Submarine Security Activities Account.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HDBE7E83EE892445D9541D85811CC7F9F"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Relationship to other laws</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The authority to accept or transfer funds under this section is in addition to any other statutory authority to accept or transfer funds.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H0B92D23BFA584B56BC81C8463393D27E"><enum>(h)</enum><header>Notification and report</header> <paragraph id="H75207B6415E5454BAEA1AAF06BC5BCFD"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Notification</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 60 days prior to the transfer of any funds from the Submarine Security Activities Account, the President shall notify the appropriate congressional committees and leadership of—</text>

<paragraph id="H711ABB50E1C34312BA4C6D71A7552191"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Annual report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than November 30 of each year until one year after the date on which all funds transferred under this section have been fully expended, the President shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees and leadership a report that includes a detailed accounting of—</text> <subparagraph id="H764976CB842E4F4DAFBAC8E8C2C2E372"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the amount of funds transferred under this subsection during the fiscal year preceding the fiscal year in which the report is submitted; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H7A1E24995DC942BEA92B04FCE73A458A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the purposes for which such funds were used.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H2C07D536E52044799BF21FE188B79D11"><enum>(i)</enum><header>Report</header> <paragraph id="H933C0B38DDEC4A808C32E08625E5BDF8"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 30 days after the date on which contributions of money accepted by the President under subsection (a) are credited to the Submarine Security Activities Account under subsection (b), the President shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees and leadership a report on—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HF171705800D44CF0A54671E9F08C6CA7"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the amount of money so transferred;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2B82CE5F2968417781D8DF451FB4F05B"><enum>(B)</enum><text>a description of the intended use of the funds; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H155289F6498348698E3B297500290069"><enum>(C)</enum><text>any other matters related to the administration of the Submarine Security Activities Account as determined necessary by the Secretary.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H324749F9164D402B807FF0B814A5EB9C"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The report required by this subsection shall be submitted in unclassified form but may include a classified annex. </text></paragraph></subsection></section>

<section id="HB92EB6B8ACBF418CBFB8458B8563CE3D" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1414.</enum><header>Critical mineral independence</header> 
<subsection id="H3CBF0378D0C541D2BCFD0D42ECD378DE"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="H9D3D711935824C198D4534E589A52DAE"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Appropriate committees of Congress</header><text>The term <term>appropriate committees of Congress</term> means—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HAC850BEFC05F40FC84890BB838E0BCC5"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the Committee on Armed Services of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF246369FFA2141B2AA73527B5CA2FABF" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD9BEF8AA013B45DE90FD249A367F63DF"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Covered country</header><text>The term <term>covered country</term> means—</text> <subparagraph id="H97FC64029C274B359D53A4CA77F12516"><enum>(A)</enum><text>a covered nation (as defined in section 4872(d) of title 10, United States Code); and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H39DA7F18F54A442087E92D0848CEC43D"><enum>(B)</enum><text>any other country determined by the Secretary of Defense to be a strategic competitor or adversary of the United States for purposes of this section.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HBDC7BDB0B0304F78A6D9CD1631ACDF21"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Critical mineral</header><text>The term <term>critical mineral</term> means a critical mineral (as defined in section 7002(a) of the Energy Act of 2020 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/30/1606">30 U.S.C. 1606(a)</external-xref>)) that the Secretary of Defense determines to be important to the national security of the United States for purposes of this section.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H78FABF916EC74FE495C77A635AA48ED1"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Shortfall material</header><text>The term <term>shortfall material</term> means materials determined to be in shortfall in the most recent report on stockpile requirements submitted to Congress under subsection (a) of section 14 of the Strategic and Critical Materials Stock Piling Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/98h-5">50 U.S.C. 98h–5</external-xref>) and included in the most recent briefing required by subsection (f) of such section.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HF8C1E670FEEC449D8444FA92A04915C5" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Statement of policy</header><text>It is the policy of the United States—</text> 
<paragraph id="H48F60D9FB2144DF28924BCEDE1226D20"><enum>(1)</enum><text>to expand secure sources of supply of critical minerals, including rare earth elements, in the United States and in countries that are allies or partners of the United States to meet the needs of the United States defense sector so that the Department of Defense will achieve critical mineral supply chain independence from covered countries, including the People’s Republic of China, the Russian Federation, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the Democratic People’s Republic of North Korea; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF98F49587C964AC0AA2E072FBF3C69F2"><enum>(2)</enum><text>that the Department of Defense will procure critical minerals and products made using supply chains involving critical minerals that are not mined or processed in or by covered countries.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H04219169153A491489EBD3E46A3EBEC2" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Strategy to achieve critical mineral supply chain independence for the Department of Defense</header> 
<paragraph id="H61A73390DF1E45CBA9D8417F04276CC2"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a strategy to develop supply chains for the Department of Defense that are not dependent on mining or processing of critical minerals in or by covered countries, in order to achieve critical mineral supply chain independence from covered countries for the Department by 2035.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HCB254CB1D91E4BF9872D93CBB7E02A41"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The strategy required by paragraph (1) shall—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HDE6EC8C67CA34048AF9BE8BD03B4C602"><enum>(A)</enum><text>identify and assess significant vulnerabilities in the supply chains of contractors and subcontractors of the Department of Defense involving critical minerals that are mined or processed in or by covered countries;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE0435C561EE84198A259816FD747C51D"><enum>(B)</enum><text>identify and recommend changes to the acquisition laws, regulations, and policies of the Department of Defense to ensure contractors and subcontractors of the Department use supply chains involving critical minerals that are not mined or processed in or by covered countries to the greatest extent practicable;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HAD22EFB7405E4C63B99346A0A0426200"><enum>(C)</enum><text>evaluate the utility and desirability of leveraging the process for acquiring shortfall materials for the National Defense Stockpile under the Strategic and Critical Materials Stock Piling Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/98">50 U.S.C. 98 et seq.</external-xref>) to strengthen mining and processing capacity for critical minerals in the United States and in countries that are allies or partners of the United States;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HA3A95D6F55CE40378B02D82EEC4967DE"><enum>(D)</enum><text>identify areas of potential engagement and partnership with the governments of countries that are allies or partners of the United States to jointly reduce dependence on critical minerals mined or processed in or by covered countries;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H1614652EEF254868825F70E93555F8B1"><enum>(E)</enum><text>identify and recommend other policy changes that may be needed to achieve critical mineral supply chain independence from covered countries for the Department;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H59ED3DCD74A64C35892565EC0FA03D37" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(F)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">identify and recommend measures to streamline authorities and policies with respect to critical minerals and supply chains for critical minerals; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H20498938C3A84056862E8A5EC658D066"><enum>(G)</enum><text>prioritize the recommendations made in the strategy to achieve critical mineral supply chain independence from covered countries for the Department, taking into consideration economic costs and varying degrees of vulnerability posed to the national security of the United States by reliance on different types of critical minerals.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H475A7E6404144CB5943664F826B81B6F"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Form of strategy</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The strategy required by paragraph (1) shall be submitted in classified form but shall include an unclassified summary.</text></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle> 
<subtitle id="HEE7B0843A45D42E582DE81FB009510E7"><enum>C</enum><header>Other Matters</header> 
<section id="HF78F2FE419ED42FCB760C8DE9AAC52E6" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1421.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Modification of leasing authority of Armed Forces Retirement Home</header> 
<subsection id="H2C87D1B717C84D79B503B18CDC5923D6"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Agreements</header><text>Before entering a lease under section 1511(i) of the Armed Forces Retirement Home Act of 1991 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/24/411">24 U.S.C. 411(i)</external-xref>), the Chief Operating Officer of the Armed Forces Retirement Home may enter into an agreement with a potential lessee for such lease providing for a period of exclusivity, access, study, or for similar purposes. The agreement shall provide for the payment (in cash or in kind) by the potential lessee of consideration for the agreement unless the Chief Operating Officer determines that payment of consideration will not promote the purpose and financial stability of the Armed Forces Retirement Home or be in the public interest.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H2E4118E4B9EE44C1B9B36F17E2C68A00" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Approval and notification</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A sublease pursuant to section 1511(i) of the Armed Forces Retirement Home Act of 1991 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/24/411">24 U.S.C. 411(i)</external-xref>) shall not be subject to the approval of the Secretary of Defense or any requirement to notify or submit a report to Congress described in such section if the Chief Operating Officer of the Armed Forces Retirement Home determines that the terms of the sublease conform with the terms of such lease.</text></subsection>

<section id="HAD29ED20EC344EF6B82254AA7723CB81" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1501.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Performance metrics for pilot program on sharing cyber capabilities and related information with foreign operational partners</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline"><external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/10/19">Chapter 19</external-xref> of title 10, United States Code, is amended—</text> <paragraph id="HBFC65EF4CAB945DE81EDDD80A800AEF2"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by redesignating the second section 398 (relating to pilot program for sharing cyber capabilities and related information with foreign operational partners) as section 398a; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H81CF0DFCA8E64291A17A8FF8F11CA998"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">in section 398a, as so redesignated—</text> <subparagraph id="HCBC924D40F6B41729EAACA18E96494D9" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by redesignating subsections (f) and (g) as subsections (g) and (h), respectively; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H5FE5382C3FC041748F2096CC284C4DEE" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by inserting after subsection (e) the following new subsection:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HAC6A385D2B0C4EDB9B0D32499BABBE3F"> <subsection id="H50B45F4A88464E568885940A2750A7A2" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(f)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Performance metrics</header> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="yes-display-inline" id="HF56701140343459D816898397C1FC44A"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall maintain performance metrics to track the results of sharing cyber capabilities and related information with foreign operational partners under a pilot program authorized by subsection (a).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2CDE9D82F3D5469EA30A23B079755DEE" indent="up1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The performance metrics under paragraph (1) shall include the following:</text> <subparagraph id="H1E5D3EF756434A7AA9295B3E4EA67BA0" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Whom the cyber capability was used against.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H10C0FE879A304A0D9A4156EE83D122D4" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The effect of the cyber capability, including whether and how the transfer of the cyber capability improved the operational cyber posture of the United States and achieved operational objectives of the United States, or had no effect.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H41CCB7C956A7429C89129C88C2F63B1C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Such other outcome-based or appropriate performance metrics as the Secretary considers appropriate for evaluating the effectiveness of a pilot program carried out under subsection (a).</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection><after-quoted-block display="yes">.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subparagraph></paragraph></section> 
<section id="HD74451E3F71F4FEF8908E4B61F3A7F86" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1502.</enum><header>Harmonization and clarification of Strategic Cybersecurity Program and related matters</header> 
<subsection id="H337DE11AFD8248E2981B8FA82B8F8821"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Harmonization and clarification</header> 
<paragraph id="H7444685624AC4A9586E0A6633B9BC784"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text><external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/10/19">Chapter 19</external-xref> of title 10, United States Code, is amended by inserting after <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/391a">section 391a</external-xref> the following new section:</text> <quoted-block id="HECB46C157C7D48C3AE8E3881AC89FE72" style="USC"> <section id="HE17903F513B547D5B0032BE689E69FD2"><enum>391b.</enum><header>Strategic cybersecurity program</header> <subsection id="H9A85864DA7C6420BA557AD782A0CE240"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header> <paragraph id="HEE7ED19955004395A3A076C5EDA94493" display-inline="yes-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text>There is a program to be known as the <quote>Strategic Cybersecurity Program</quote> (in this section referred to as the <quote>Program</quote>) to ensure the ability of the Department of Defense to conduct the most critical military missions of the Department.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1FF12DF0325F42CCB033B70F88E3D08E" indent="up1"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The Secretary of Defense shall designate a principal staff assistant from within the Office of the Secretary of Defense whose office shall serve as the office of primary responsibility for the Program, and provide policy, direction, and oversight regarding the execution of the responsibilities of the program manager selected pursuant to subsection (c)(1).</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HB24DB15C0AC14FA1BB0AA40780D3B594"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Membership</header><text>In addition to the office of primary responsibility for the Program under subsection (a)(2) and the program manager selected pursuant to subsection (c)(1), membership in the Program shall include the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H1F354E9F6DB34EA78104A0132A162720"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2C589DE650AE454FAC1D83A5B6DF4EFA"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The Commanders of the United States Cyber Command, United States European Command, United States Indo-Pacific Command, United States Northern Command, United States Strategic Command, United States Space Command, United States Transportation Command.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0FF29F4A94B94793AC831C5A7E6394DF"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H923973E8A63A472ABBA8CE30162EBFB8"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The Under Secretary of Defense for Policy.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HFF04610B70DA4D0D8C3AF9798C475E4F"><enum>(5)</enum><text>The Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB515FB4A01D7455C8CDA5AF41C41DCC3" commented="no"><enum>(6)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCE93BE6EF4E049719AF85ED7F5C6EF0C"><enum>(7)</enum><text>The chief information officers of the military departments.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H73C4C50163F34347A17BE05D3CF0ECD1"><enum>(8)</enum><text>The Principal Cyber Advisor of the Department of Defense.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD7904FBB62C44D78990B97DFE3CACFC6"><enum>(9)</enum><text>The Principal Cyber Advisors of the military departments.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC86BD851F69A41908A2AAFEED91949A0"><enum>(10)</enum><text>Each senior official identified pursuant to subsection (i) of section 1647 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/114/92">Public Law 114–92</external-xref>; 129 Stat. 1118).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H943FD15ECD524507B609C041F11723F2" commented="no"><enum>(11)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Such other officials as may be determined necessary by the Secretary of Defense.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H8D7605542DFF492EB89B14A26CA95370"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Program office</header> <paragraph id="H59C2757121994009A7FBF504EDB42352" display-inline="yes-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text>There is in the Cybersecurity Directorate of the National Security Agency a program office to support the Program by identifying threats to, vulnerabilities in, and remediations for, the missions and mission elements specified in subsection (d)(1). Such program office shall be headed by a program manager selected by the Director of the National Security Agency.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0A2048B72CF14754972EF918AC002282" indent="up1"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense, in exercising authority, direction, and control over the Cybersecurity Directorate of the National Security Agency, shall ensure that the program office under paragraph (1) is responsive to the requirements and direction of the program manager selected pursuant to such paragraph.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF3092521EA544DB89806B640EB95A7E5" indent="up1"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The Secretary may augment the personnel assigned to the program office under paragraph (1) by assigning personnel as appropriate from among members of any covered armed force (including the reserve components thereof), civilian employees of the Department of Defense (including the Defense Intelligence Agency), and personnel of the research laboratories of the Department of Defense, who have particular expertise in the areas of responsibility referred to in subsection (d).</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H971081B1CEA34826BF8180F128BAE419"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Designation of mission elements of program</header> 
<paragraph id="HBA7621EE91604FE0A9CDA993C4FC7E6E" display-inline="yes-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The Under Secretary of Defense for Policy, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, and the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff shall identify and designate for inclusion in the Program all of the systems, critical infrastructure, kill chains, and processes, including systems and components in development, that comprise the following military missions of the Department of Defense:</text> <subparagraph id="H0E4242DD74674371B79E36292B08B216" indent="up1"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Nuclear deterrence and strike.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H35D9591B93C24C1CBF321C452B76C90F" indent="up1"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Select long-range conventional strike missions germane to the warfighting plans of the United States European Command and the United States Indo-Pacific Command.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H50319E2D0B534A49AC84478C3390AC3A" indent="up1"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Offensive cyber operations.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4A72B952EB97451897772E68766B726D" indent="up1"><enum>(D)</enum><text>Homeland missile defense.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H40A39626BCD04ACB8526224978DFD7B0" indent="up1"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff shall coordinate the identification and prioritization of the missions and mission components, and the development and approval of requirements relating to the cybersecurity of the missions and mission components, of the Program.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H232A31951E384159A7777999D1A22D8D"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Additional responsibilities of head of office of primary responsibility</header><text>In addition to providing policy, direction, and oversight as specified in subsection (a)(2), the head of the office of primary responsibility for the Program designated under such subsection shall be responsible—</text> <paragraph id="HD95880B725C94DF387FBF259FBB0834A"><enum>(1)</enum><text>for overseeing and providing direction on any covered statutory requirement that is ongoing, recurrent (including on an annual basis), or unfulfilled, including by—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HD6B3D5000FFA4BA8BC5AE799E97DC8D6"><enum>(A)</enum><text>reviewing any materials required to be submitted to Congress under the covered statutory requirement prior to such submission; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H01011FE7C984427EB465756E5A7BF0A0"><enum>(B)</enum><text>ensuring such submissions occur by the applicable deadline under the covered statutory requirement: and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF6E29576E2834680A755D87AF11E01A0"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">recording and monitoring the remediation of identified vulnerabilities in constituent systems, infrastructure, kill chains, and processes of the missions specified in subsection (d)(1). </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H9A8E905B8BFC4222BA5FFF66B2AB2CD1"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Responsibilities of program manager</header><text>The program manager selected pursuant to subsection (c)(1) shall be responsible for the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="HD46740CF3B8A4A6FB7175F9353DD029E"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Conducting end-to-end vulnerability assessments of the constituent systems, infrastructure, kill chains, and processes of the missions specified in subsection (d)(1).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA31F392D00C24D56B52DE5CAB3C76A59"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Prioritizing and facilitating the remediation of identified vulnerabilities in such constituent systems, infrastructure, kill chains, and processes.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H995880FDA7AF400EAD83E9942053F4A6"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Conducting, prior to the Milestone B approval for any proposed such system or infrastructure germane to the missions of the Program, appropriate reviews of the acquisition and system engineering plans for that proposed system or infrastructure, in accordance with the policy and guidance of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment regarding the components of such reviews and the range of systems and infrastructure to be reviewed.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2FB1ABCE716F4AA8BA1D7006D653C4DB"><enum>(4)</enum><text>Advising the Secretaries of the military departments, the commanders of the combatant commands, and the Joint Staff on the vulnerabilities and cyberattack vectors that pose substantial risk to the missions of the Program and their constituent systems, critical infrastructure, kill chains, or processes.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCA6449741E064FA2B95FD7CF71648097"><enum>(5)</enum><text>Ensuring that the Program builds upon (including through the provision of oversight and direction by the head of the office of primary responsibility for the Program pursuant to subsection (e), as applicable), and does not duplicate, other efforts of the Department of Defense relating to cybersecurity, including the following:</text> <subparagraph id="H2702AC2974F645AC880CD90CBF45DA19"><enum>(A)</enum><text>The evaluation of cyber vulnerabilities of major weapon systems of the Department of Defense required under section 1647 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/114/92">Public Law 114–92</external-xref>; 129 Stat. 1118).</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HA83A4D74E061437A9DF5928AB59A8872"><enum>(B)</enum><text>The evaluation of cyber vulnerabilities of critical infrastructure of the Department of Defense required under section 1650 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/114/328">Public Law 114–328</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/2224">10 U.S.C. 2224</external-xref> note).</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H0408E584B4124EB38FE439CB92C986C8"><enum>(C)</enum><text>The activities of the cyber protection teams of the Department of Defense.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H2A745619803C4309BE41C941BA2344B8"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Responsibilities of secretary of defense</header><text>The Secretary of Defense shall define and issue guidance on the roles and responsibilities for components of the Department of Defense other than those specified in this section with respect to the Program, including—</text> <paragraph id="HC4B80E7454FB4918AD71CD64D962DF8E"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the roles and responsibilities of the acquisition and sustainment organizations of the military departments in supporting and implementing remedial actions;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2C7D217E7CC64A4FA209276E0E49C171"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the alignment of Cyber Protection Teams with the prioritized missions of the Program;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HADB7A73F1E9F4AA9AB0F2CA4C9E5441A"><enum>(3)</enum><text>the role of the Director of Operational Test and Evaluation in conducting periodic assessments, including through cyber red teams, of the cybersecurity of missions in the Program; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H28B05D3B3F2F416181E4B4F02EE29CF4"><enum>(4)</enum><text>the role of the Principal Cyber Adviser in coordinating and monitoring the execution of the Program.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H2D35654CB50D4AA49A7D277587DBAFF1"><enum>(h)</enum><header>Annual reporting</header><text>Not later than December 31 of each year, the head of the office of primary responsibility for the Program, in coordination with the appropriate members of the Program under subsection (b), shall submit to the congressional defense committees an annual report on the efforts carried out pursuant to this section or any covered provision of law, including with respect to such efforts concerning—</text> 
<paragraph id="H181876D263C94F3BB4FFD6FE2EFAD217"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the evaluation of cyber vulnerabilities of each major weapon system of the Department of Defense and related mitigation activities under section 1647 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/114/92">Public Law 114–92</external-xref>; 129 Stat. 1118);</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H0F8E5990885D49FFA2C12B4C42A1C9C8"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the evaluation of cyber vulnerabilities of the critical infrastructure of the Department of Defense under section 1650 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/114/328">Public Law 114–328</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/2224">10 U.S.C. 2224</external-xref> note);</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H440C751FE6AF4000812010AE6C23344A"><enum>(3)</enum><text>operational technology and the mapping of mission-relevant terrain in cyberspace under section 1505 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/81">Public Law 117–81</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/394">10 U.S.C. 394</external-xref> note);</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H29F852B1E0AF4C5FA21D6D597201C845"><enum>(4)</enum><text>the assessments of the vulnerabilities to and mission risks presented by radio-frequency enabled cyber attacks with respect to the operational technology embedded in weapons systems, aircraft, ships, ground vehicles, space systems, sensors, and datalink networks of the Department of Defense under section 1559 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3DD86FD5522E4915827B75E0FD129401"><enum>(5)</enum><text>the work of the Program in general, including information relating to staffing and accomplishments.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H430FA9B6A2E34A27B7FCE159D6536D47"><enum>(i)</enum><header>Annual budget display</header> <paragraph id="HBA7A116B48AE4867AB7E4B149D3CDE95" display-inline="yes-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text>On an annual basis for each fiscal year, concurrently with the submission of the budget of the President for that fiscal year under section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code, the head of the office of primary responsibility for the Program, in coordination with the appropriate members of the Program under subsection (b), shall submit to the congressional defense committees a consolidated budget justification display that covers all programs and activities associated with this section and any covered provision of law, including with respect to the matters listed in subsection (h).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H9E4515856A444C8B8A145E0BCE9A8CBD" indent="up1"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Each display under paragraph (1) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HBCF93C3F5B5245BC949C9F366531C43C" indent="up1"><enum>(3)</enum><text>For the purpose of facilitating the annual budget display requirement under paragraph (1), the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense shall provide to the head of the office of primary responsibility for the Program and the appropriate members of the Program under subsection (b) fiscal guidance on the programming of funds in support of the Program.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H40B1636F29E54576AEC3A62CF46144E1"><enum>(j)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="HCBCDD416450B4BBD8176D7365A2522DB"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The term <quote>covered armed force</quote> means the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, or Space Force.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1F226983B80A44D088CDCEC8CBC56017"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The term <quote>covered statutory requirement</quote> means a requirement under any covered provision of law.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC0CF262161BE45C298C464DCCD37B5D5"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The term <quote>covered provision of law</quote> means the following:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H7B1CFF7223BF4D9EBC5C503E5CDC41F5"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Section 1647 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/114/92">Public Law 114–92</external-xref>; 129 Stat. 1118).</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3409416428954685923DB0E56ED84F9B"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Section 1650 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/114/328">Public Law 114–328</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/2224">10 U.S.C. 2224</external-xref> note).</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HE0B5A16D51BA47C896B4BABBB54222CE"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Section 1505 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/81">Public Law 117–81</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/394">10 U.S.C. 394</external-xref> note).</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H5391477D677647D880E7B4D883C85FB5"><enum>(D)</enum><text>Section 1559 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph>

<section id="H29E15EAF747C424C8C9BCE330E7E9CC2"><enum>1504.</enum><header>Quarterly briefings on joint all domain command and control effort</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 1076 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/116/283">Public Law 116–283</external-xref>; 134 Stat. 3866) is amended—</text> <paragraph id="HA4A61191BD174CB5AE3845A332A8C8E9"><enum>(1)</enum><text>by amending subsection (a) to read as follows:</text>

<subsection id="HCEB080B1CE4E4371A692538D2FA58257"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Quarterly briefings</header> 
<paragraph id="HE7205D7038A34C889135F66856FBA4B4"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>During the period beginning on October 1, 2021, and ending on October 1, 2028, the Deputy Secretary of Defense, the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense, the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense, and a senior military service representative for each of the Armed Forces shall provide to the congressional defense committees quarterly briefings on the progress of the Joint All Domain Command and Control (in this section referred to as <quote>JADC2</quote>) effort of the Department of Defense.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H19607E3CEFF2414F8E45B6941CB92EF0"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Annual participation by certain combatant commands</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">For each fiscal year during the period specified in paragraph (1), a senior representative from each of the United States Indo-Pacific Command, United States Central Command, and United States European Command shall participate in the provision of the first quarterly briefing under such paragraph following the submission of the budget of the President to Congress under section 1105 of title 31, United States Code, for that fiscal year.</text></paragraph></subsection><after-quoted-block>; and</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H4AE1D35040BA40A288596379ED2F5F57"><enum>(2)</enum><text>in subsection (b), by adding at the end the following new paragraphs:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" id="H3B7B9C8709CF4BF788F590452B0746AF" display-inline="no-display-inline"> <paragraph id="H64F10C18067A4A3B81CADA737BC44C21"><enum>(7)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A detailed programmatic table of the funding for the JADC2 efforts of the Office of the Secretary of Defense and the military departments, as set forth in the budget of the President most recently submitted to Congress under section 1105 of title 31, United States Code. The information in such table shall be organized primarily by key programs, projects, and activities (such as data integration layer, joint operating system, global experimentation, and mission command applications).</text></paragraph>

<paragraph id="H5A32544CAE4E427E8EDF0280CED3EC95" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Plans to develop and maintain a sufficient cyber planning capacity in such combatant command.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5CBE7C255FCD4BDC8BF23C682F056A36" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Processes to integrate cyber capabilities into operational support for such combatant command.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H54BD052D17B549109FE4BD507FB14A4B" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A prioritization of cyber risks and vulnerabilities within the geographic area of responsibility of such combatant command.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6FCA199D6C7140ECB75B10E9B221C680" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Specific plans to assist in the defense of friendly foreign countries.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="HC97F1EF8CECA4D54A5EC85B3D21702AD" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1507.</enum><header>Review and plan relating to cyber red teams of Department of Defense</header> 
<subsection id="H45A1FE3CBCB24F5B94D5FF28F26EEF13"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Review relating to prior joint assessment</header> 
<paragraph id="H93346490900D4D1085905A079BFDEA5A"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Review required</header><text>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the officials described in subsection (c) shall review, and assess the status of the implementation of, the recommendations set forth by the Secretary of Defense in response to the joint assessment requirement under section 1660 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/116/92">Public Law 116–92</external-xref>; 133 Stat. 1771). </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HD954861C855A44F4B80F3DE430910C3B" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The review under paragraph (1) shall include, with respect to the recommendations specified in such paragraph—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H67CF959A85B64B76AD7D97906D60C935" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the timelines associated with each such recommendation, regardless of whether the recommendation is fully implemented or yet to be fully implemented; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H5A3BA321D27A478388316DC7F16ECD17" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a description of any impediments to the implementation of such recommendations encountered.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HFD420C9AF12C4E26922540CC884BCF0A" commented="no"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Plan required</header> 
<paragraph id="H060CB406C6BF4857BE138B5EC3805A37" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the officials described in subsection (c) shall submit to the congressional defense committees a plan, developed taking into account the findings of the review under subsection (a), to ensure cyber red teams of the Department of Defense achieve sufficient capacity and capability to provide services and meet current and projected future demands on a Defense-wide basis. Such plan shall include—</text> <subparagraph id="HF95019FA8624450E92608385B65888A6" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a description of the funding necessary for such cyber red teams to achieve such capacity and capability;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HAE9BE81BDCC14BEBB3E4D41E6B67952F" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a description of any other resources, personnel, infrastructure, or authorities for access to information necessary for such cyber red teams to achieve such capacity and capability (including with respect to the emulation of threats from foreign countries with advanced cyber capabilities, automation, artificial intelligence or machine learning, and data collection and correlation); and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HC7EF7F016D6A41E193F309F66E96F238" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">updated joint service standards and metrics to ensure the training, staffing, and equipping of such cyber red teams at levels necessary to achieve such capacity and capability.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H30F0D0D2B28F465F93ED9AFDE6AC17B9"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Implementation</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall prescribe such regulations and issue such guidance as the Secretary determines necessary to implement the plan developed under subsection (a).</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HF31816C2DD724C778C0AB57680F7712D"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Officials described</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The officials described in this subsection are the Principal Cyber Advisor to the Secretary of Defense, the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense, the Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, and the Commander of the United States Cyber Command.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HEA031E796A4540CFB5A4EF10EAB8443C"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Annual reports</header><text>Not later than January 31, 2025, and not less frequently than annually thereafter until January 31, 2031, the Director of Operational Test and Evaluation shall include in each annual report required under section 139(h) of title 10, United States Code, an update on progress made with respect to the implementation of this section, including the following:</text> <paragraph id="H96AA25BE85FB4A129CF33D48B50F571C"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The results of test and evaluation events, including any resource or capability shortfalls limiting the capacity or capability of cyber red teams of the Department of Defense to meet operational requirements.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HDF3352A63F1D41C5AE2A9CC8F79877AA"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The extent to which operations of such cyber red teams have expanded across the competition continuum, including during cooperation and competition phases, to match adversary positioning and cyber activities.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7F4782878E364B2ABBDF256D9CD280EC"><enum>(3)</enum><text>A summary of identified categories of common gaps and shortfalls across cyber red teams of the military departments and Defense Agencies (as such terms are defined in section 101 of title 10, United States Code).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3A2CCF2558774746BF1AE645E563F22D"><enum>(4)</enum><text>Any identified lessons learned that would affect training or operational employment decisions relating to the cyber red teams of the Department of Defense.</text></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle> <subtitle id="H3DB7CA40D2BB43A68AAB02594F14863C"><enum>B</enum><header>Cybersecurity</header> <section id="H3001818F2D134796825AB941D5FA12D0" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1511.</enum><header>Responsibility for cybersecurity and critical infrastructure protection of defense industrial base</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 1724 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (116–283; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/2224">10 U.S.C. 2224</external-xref> note) is amended—</text>

<subparagraph id="HE389A6AED11F45FFAFCFE52328CF3130"><enum>(A)</enum><text>in the matter preceding paragraph (1), by striking <quote>the Principal Cyber Advisor of the Department of Defense</quote> and inserting <quote>the principal staff assistant designated under subsection (b)</quote>; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HCFB21445DAE740D9AA5EAAECFBEEE43F"><enum>(B)</enum><text>in paragraph (1), by striking <quote>Sector Specific Agency</quote> and inserting <quote>Sector Risk Management Agency</quote>; </text></subparagraph></paragraph>
