<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H32206F7CF5A541ADAE0CAA9DD579C708"><enum>(5)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Minimum number of scholarship awards</header> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2B27C847B7B548F5AB89F576B138EA34"><enum>(A)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall award not fewer than 1,000 scholarships under the Program in fiscal year 2026 and in each fiscal year thereafter.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H189F649113324DD1B70C76697B63EB71"><enum>(B)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Waiver</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense may award fewer than the number of scholarships required under subparagraph (A) in a fiscal year if the Secretary determines and notifies the congressional defense committees that fewer scholarships are necessary to address workforce needs.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><after-quoted-block display="yes">.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section> 
<section id="H7E1855E641464D80BF66B0E427372140" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1535.</enum><header>Pilot program and other measures to enhance readiness and effectiveness of Cyber Mission Force</header> 
<subsection id="H2674925828E54BCC932BEAC0A4318E72"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Personnel requirements and training for critical work roles</header><text>Not later than 270 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall—</text> <paragraph id="H84C970D660A34B92BCC14CEC9B63F342" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">direct and oversee the implementation of guidance, to be issued by each Secretary of a military department, that correlates critical work roles to military occupational specialties and periods of obligated service with respect to that military department;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB6540E760F124C048649BB673008E2C7"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">require that, prior to the attachment or assignment of a member of the Armed Forces to a unit of the United States Cyber Command, the Secretary concerned ensure such member is fully trained and in compliance with the required standards for the work role to be assumed by the member within such unit, including with respect to critical work roles within the Cyber Mission Force;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HCA8DF21BBE42466CBA74982243643DB7"><enum>(3)</enum><text>ensure that the period of obligated service for members of the Armed Forces is—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HB2DF734A84D74D0195274FEEAF02E748"><enum>(A)</enum><text>uniform across the military departments with respect to positions of the Cyber Mission Force involving critical work roles;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE4953FEC5A70437EB287F2ECAF63283E"><enum>(B)</enum><text>commensurate with the financial and time investments made by Secretary concerned for the purpose of furnishing training pursuant to paragraph (2); and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H90D6DD9D99AC47109344B516E8E45617"><enum>(C)</enum><text>sufficient to meet the readiness requirements established by the Commander of the United States Cyber Command;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB2E570710BAE46238020566AFAAABABF"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">facilitate consecutive assignments of members of the Armed Forces to the same unit of the United States Cyber Command without inhibiting the advancement or promotion potential of any such member;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HDF9741A2254A499882EB2AB8A87B5E26" commented="no"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">provide to the Secretaries of the military departments direction for the integration of critical work roles into the personnel system of record of the respective military department, to provide for tracking cyber personnel data by work role; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H0BE0DBB03085485A904B35AFD8A83AFE" commented="no"><enum>(6)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">establish within at least one military department the curriculum and capacity necessary to train sufficient numbers of members of the Armed Forces from across the military departments in the performance of critical work roles within the Cyber Mission Force to achieve the readiness requirements established by the Commander of United States Cyber Command.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H47C43CB1C5B4486D84557ECBC8F9B73D" commented="no"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Pilot program on contracting for services relevant to critical work roles</header> 
<paragraph id="H410917B719CA4688A07A627649ED21AC"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Pilot program</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Commander of the United States Cyber Command shall carry out a pilot program under which the Commander shall seek to enter into one or more contracts under which skilled contractor personnel provide services relevant to critical work roles within the Cyber Mission Force, for the purpose of enhancing the readiness and effectiveness of the Cyber Mission Force.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H42F64DEC3932471CBD2D686E0ACC0D4A" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Duration</header><text>The Commander shall carry out the pilot program under paragraph (1) during the three-year period beginning on the date of the commencement of the pilot program and following such period, may—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H88CF3E96EF2D4D0F8E6209299BEF0D2A" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text>continue carrying out such pilot program for such duration as the Commander considers appropriate;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HAD1819210CB045CE8560DBB4650308CC" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>transition such pilot program to a permanent program; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4CF4834C39044C09899890CD7748E461"><enum>(C)</enum><text>terminate such pilot program.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H625A51336A9A48B482563116043BC4A1"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Plan on hiring, training, and retaining civilians to serve in critical work roles</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Commander of the United States Cyber Command shall—</text> 
<paragraph id="H0320AF318A6A47E7BCA2E7F17D1248E9"><enum>(1)</enum><text>develop a plan to hire, train, and retain civilians to serve in critical work roles and other work roles within the Cyber Mission Force, for the purpose of enhancing the readiness and effectiveness of the Cyber Mission Force; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9F77514143B847E7B9DDCBA76D839388"><enum>(2)</enum><text>provide to the congressional defense committees a briefing on such plan.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H1EBAF7ADCB6649D38E437F8A659AFA71"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="HD7163D69D4BF49D69C420BE48C4A5F04"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The term <quote>critical work role</quote> means a work role designated as critical by the Commander of the United States Cyber Command for purposes of this section. </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8EFF1A7EFCF041CDBBF248E051E68018"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The term <quote>Secretary concerned</quote> has the meaning given that term in section 101 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H57ED41AA172A4DAEAFE34C6F0AD565AC" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1536.</enum><header>Authority to conduct pilot program on Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve</header> <subsection id="H5DB6D3E91CDF45CE998ACB5995F978BF"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Authority</header><text>The Secretary of the Army may conduct a pilot program to establish a Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve to provide to the United States Cyber Command manpower to effectively—</text> 
<paragraph id="H680B2A7DBF404102AFB14457687A44DC"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">preempt, defeat, deter, or respond to malicious cyber activity; </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H34A478CDA5B14FFC9513573724FAF818"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">conduct cyberspace operations;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H47EFABADB08A4EC0A5B03BD38E9E04D1"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">secure information and systems of the Department of Defense against malicious cyber activity; and </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7975D707979345A2AAF762C6DA2D7540"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">assist in solving cyber workforce-related challenges. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H82D66D5B408340959D566F075D817B3C"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Conditions prior to conduct of pilot program</header> 
<paragraph id="H459DB994DB0D4F1BB8AB4CEC8CDE9C53"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Implementation plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of the Army may not take any action to commence a pilot program pursuant to the authority under subsection (a) until the Secretary—</text> <subparagraph id="HB1F770ACED1C42A395CE8103CC5D9180"><enum>(A)</enum><text>submits to the congressional defense committees an implementation plan for the pilot program; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H43E4A2160F004B9B8A721D0433DC8E46"><enum>(B)</enum><text>provides to the congressional defense committees a briefing on such implementation plan.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H022FFE67B8F64A1FA2BCF0FCF3C556E4"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Program guidance</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the Secretary of the Army intends to conduct a pilot program pursuant to the authority under subsection (a), prior to commencing such pilot program, the Secretary, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Personnel Management and the Director of the Office of Government Ethics, shall issue guidance for the establishment and implementation of the pilot program.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H45EA915658284137A5A34B351ED03B4D"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Conditions on conduct of pilot program</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any pilot program conducted by the Secretary of the Army pursuant to the authority under subsection (a) shall be subject to the following:</text> <paragraph id="H4F8ED6C194D84DC0AE39FD4E6298B75B"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Hiring authority; status in Reserve</header> <subparagraph id="H685B6CC8D576403FB7F187F7514DB481"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Hiring authority</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In conducting the pilot program, the Secretary of the Army may use any authority otherwise available to the Secretary for the recruitment, employment, and retention of civilian personnel within the Department, including the authority under section 1599f of title 10, United States Code.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HEEAA4C81BA1A47B19878867B6808EE42" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Status in Reserve</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">During the period beginning on the date on which an individual is recruited to serve in the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve and ending on the date on which the individual is appointed to the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve, and during any period elapsing between any such appointments, the individual may not be considered a Federal employee.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H29DF9B94E2EB435C9F8F9237F80B01FF"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Eligibility; Application and Selection</header> <subparagraph id="HE611C7B13C7445708AEA87AB2A968872"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Criteria required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of the Army shall establish criteria for—</text> 
<clause id="H0C86363AF55540B6B9B2B89F336D6064"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">individuals to be eligible to serve in the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve; and</text></clause> <clause id="HBC43EE3537DC451C9EB2087AC20BF959"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the application and selection processes for service in the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HE4416900427F4FA9BC71DBFDB575781A"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Requirements for individuals</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The criteria under subparagraph (A) shall include, with respect to an individual—</text> <clause id="H5CFFACA74A554016BE369EFAF0E7C157"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">if the individual has previously served as a member of the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve, that the previous appointment ended not fewer than 60 days before the individual may be appointed for a subsequent temporary position in the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HC972C33B542746ECA812302819AD0516"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>cybersecurity expertise.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H6D6E947E443A49F7AFBBF306FD40A6AA"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Prescreening</header><text>The Secretary of the Army shall—</text> 
<clause id="H2894E95465924A2CBA4F68690844A150"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">prior to the appointment of an individual to the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve, conduct a prescreening of the individual for any topic or product that would create a conflict of interest; and </text></clause> <clause id="H35BD4087E22142DD9CF9A6A6AA9B2369"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">require each individual so appointed to notify the Secretary if a potential conflict of interest arises during such appointment.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H5665F304C69F402994A136EEACD01F47"><enum>(D)</enum><header>Agreement required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of the Army may only appoint an individual to the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve if the individual enters into an agreement with the Secretary to serve in the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve. Such agreement shall set forth the rights and obligations of the individual and the Army. </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB1745333B7F04708BD92643FE902C0F7"><enum>(E)</enum><header>Exception for continuing military service commitments</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A member of the Selected Reserve under section 10143 of title 10, United States Code, may not serve as a member of the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H667D5E136C4644FFA4FBB5228EDB5371"><enum>(F)</enum><header>Prohibition</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">No individual who is an officer or employee of the United States Government, including any member of the uniformed services, may be recruited or appointed to serve in the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6CB0A028138049A5A4F3C2159A9D1D33"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Security clearances</header> <subparagraph id="HA5A42A2840E741029AD4B3065ED5D7DD"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of the Army shall ensure that each member of the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve is subject to appropriate personnel vetting and adjudication commensurate with the duties of the position, including, with respect to positions for which a security clearance is necessary, a favorable determination of eligibility for access to classified information, consistent with applicable provisions of law and policy.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H324A752CFCD147DAA160E19C785A049C"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Cost of sponsoring clearances</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If a member of the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve requires a security clearance in order to carry out the duties of the member, the Army shall be responsible for the cost of sponsoring the security clearance of the member.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H0F421851373A4F28BE133CFFE77568C3"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Briefings</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than one year after the date on which the guidance under subsection (b)(2) is issued with respect to the pilot program, and annually thereafter until the date on which the pilot program terminates pursuant to paragraph (7), the Secretary of the Army shall provide to the congressional defense committees a briefing on activities carried out under the pilot program, including—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H043B26FBAFCC4267ADD83DAC07CEDFB7"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">participation in the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve, including the number of members of the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve, the diversity of such members, and any barriers to recruitment or retention of such members;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H24084471004E43CBB5C22C57082B101C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>an evaluation of the ethical requirements of the pilot program;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H5C2DCD3A194541F388A7E8C79CDDF2C2"><enum>(C)</enum><text>whether the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve has been effective in providing additional capacity to the Army; and </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HA1C2A6C35B654B948865777651C3BC5F"><enum>(D)</enum><text>an evaluation of the eligibility requirements for the pilot program.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HDDE90957337C43478023DBC243514219"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Final report and briefing required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not earlier than 180 days and not later than 90 days prior to the date on which the pilot program terminates pursuant to paragraph (7), the Secretary of the Army shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report, and provide to the congressional defense committees a briefing, on recommendations relating to the pilot program, including recommendations for—</text> <subparagraph id="H2D6DEDE185DE4756807A5197A8581155"><enum>(A)</enum><text>whether the pilot program should be modified, extended in duration, or established as a permanent program, and if so, an appropriate scope for the program; </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HEBBF1A6342B347988014EA5E785F6419"><enum>(B)</enum><text>how to attract prospective members of the Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve, ensure a diversity of such members, and address any barriers to recruitment or retention of such members; </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HCF18E196F63E4985806B6DFEA932DA3A"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the ethical requirements of the pilot program and the effectiveness of mitigation efforts to address any conflict of interest concerns; and </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFF9DB86036A948C49CD779BECCE6902C"><enum>(D)</enum><text>an evaluation of the eligibility requirements for the pilot program.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H75DEBCB94BDA4F23A960E7667DD4B356"><enum>(6)</enum><header>Evaluation required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than three years after the date on which the pilot program commences, the Comptroller General of the United States shall—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HC859A54DC16D483DA77CCE2B8414803E"><enum>(A)</enum><text>conduct a study evaluating the pilot program; and </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H4DFD3B9969364E6D8C65F6A31FEBA5F0"><enum>(B)</enum><text>submit to the congressional defense committees—</text> 
<clause id="HD34F41BFDF7C42129973BD0579EE01AD"><enum>(i)</enum><text>a report on the results of the study; and </text></clause> <clause id="H39031FF3182245CEA4C8843599E35BB0"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>a recommendation with respect to whether the pilot program should be modified.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF5AEDE2184E64FD39610BF12B876B22A"><enum>(7)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The authority to conduct the pilot program shall terminate on the date that is four years after the date on which the pilot program commences.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HCBB2E62D290E4B7BB86B37E25B8480AE" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1537.</enum><header>Requirements for implementation of user activity monitoring for certain personnel</header> <subsection id="HEA749CA5939D4EA8A3CA97C839F7DBF9"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of Defense shall require each head of a component of the Department of Defense to fully implement each directive, policy, and program requirement for user activity monitoring and least privilege access controls with respect to the personnel of that component, including Federal employees and contractors, granted access to classified information and classified networks, including the following directives (and any successor directives):</text> 
<paragraph id="H92F01F94BF594E40BD702855B5516373"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The Committee on National Security Systems Directive 504, issued on February 4, 2014, relating to the protection of national security systems from insider threats (including any annex to such directive).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5F53EEC9295F45D98F597DF0C489BD81"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Department of Defense Directive 5205.16, issued on September 30, 2014, relating to the insider threat program of the Department of Defense.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H50A7027AD6BB445B9C9BA62B07F21F63"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Additional requirement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall require each head of a component of the Department of Defense to implement, with respect to systems, devices, and personnel of the component, automated controls to detect and prohibit privileged user accounts from performing general user activities not requiring privileged access.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HE0A030ABE44245E9842E8322846CB621"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Periodic testing</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary shall require that, not less frequently than once every two years, each head of a component of the Department of Defense—</text> 
<paragraph id="H2D018436764F411EA9251C87F1CC00C2"><enum>(1)</enum><text>conducts insider threat testing using threat-realistic tactics, techniques, and procedures; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H1D265F130ACE468DB4FE452549E34E1F"><enum>(2)</enum><text>submits to the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense, and the Director of Operational Test and Evaluation of the Department of Defense a report on the findings of the head with respect to the testing conducted pursuant to paragraph (1).</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H3CA200A456704399AAEBB801BEAF2767"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report on the implementation of this section.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H6F02F3157CE14D75A0B6AD10171C35CF"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Appropriate congressional committees defined</header><text>In this section, the term <quote>appropriate congressional committees</quote> means—</text> 
<paragraph id="HA3E78A47516E4946A2A75CB75459088D"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the Committee on Armed Services and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7EBBA24DCFD344CB88D2B5A12F6D535F"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Committee on Armed Services and the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="H8AE5EA53207E410EA45232BBCFE2C737"><enum>1538.</enum><header>Study on occupational resiliency of Cyber Mission Force</header> 
<subsection id="H1738CFD2295A4D258CED395AD6234539"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Study</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Principal Cyber Advisor of the Department of Defense and the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness, in coordination with the principal cyber advisors of the military departments and the Commander of the United States Cyber Command, shall conduct a study on the personnel and resources required to enhance and support the occupational resiliency of the Cyber Mission Force.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H8203E01C09CA4BDB87BAA268927711EA"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The study under subsection (a) shall include the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H34F4C38395294B0F9C50B49B185334E8"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An inventory of the resources and programs available to personnel assigned to the Cyber Mission Force, disaggregated by Armed Force and location.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDA5CEFF7C4774C76BBD9BF5672AA6C4D"><enum>(2)</enum><text>An assessment of the risk to the occupational resiliency of such personnel relative to the respective operational work role within the Cyber Mission Force (as defined by the Commander of the United States Cyber Command) and the number of such personnel available to perform operations in each such category of operational work role.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H7F3EFE44AE804C51A1AE2275A6B6CFDE"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An evaluation of the extent to which personnel assigned to the Cyber Mission Force have been made aware of the resources and programs referred to in paragraph (1), and of measures required to improve such awareness.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6D07140E23E04951BEC159A89F40D60A"><enum>(4)</enum><text>A determination by the Commander of the United States Cyber Command regarding the adequacy and accessibility of such resources and programs for personnel assigned to the Cyber Mission Force.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H27EF28B1E39942709259E9298DB13C67"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Such other matters as may be determined necessary by the Principal Cyber Advisor of the Department of Defense and the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HE8E927D4190B47F78E48183FB6E96E2E"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Submission to Congress</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Upon completing the study under subsection (a), the Principal Cyber Advisor of the Department of Defense and the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report containing the results of such study.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H76560CD5ED3847009F6B49C862F8E50C"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Occupational resiliency defined</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section, the term <quote>occupational resiliency</quote> means, with respect to personnel assigned to the Cyber Mission Force, the ability of such personnel to mitigate the unique psychological factors that contribute to the degradation of mental health and job performance under such assignment.</text></subsection></section></subtitle> <subtitle id="H53F10650367844E0B0DD827B06CA6763"><enum>E</enum><header>Artificial Intelligence</header> <section id="HAC247F47BFA141288D2459D99E076AA9" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1541.</enum><header>Modification to acquisition authority of senior official with principal responsibility for artificial intelligence and machine learning</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 808 of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/116/283">Public Law 116–283</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/4001">10 U.S.C. 4001</external-xref> note) is amended—</text>

<paragraph id="H9B531660DA3B44C38984297581C35FF1" commented="no"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by amending subsection (e)(1) to read as follows:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" id="HF988E4CE81E047058CA668471D96BD51" display-inline="no-display-inline"> <paragraph id="HF4D72C48963848CD8AE7D06BA7260BE0" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header> <subparagraph id="H90D08EFCA03F4B98BADD11950923F0D2" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Plan required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 30 days after the date of the enactment of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, the Secretary of Defense, acting through the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, shall submit to the congressional defense committees a plan for the delegation and exercise of the acquisition authority described in subsection (a).</text></subparagraph>

<section id="H94C8B903993D4DD4963A6125FF12530F" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1543.</enum><header>Prize competition for technology that detects and watermarks use of generative artificial intelligence</header> 
<subsection id="H6BF7D1BF239F4CB4960A75CFC9D62560"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 270 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, under the authority of section 4025 of title 10, United States Code, the Secretary of Defense shall establish a prize competition designed to evaluate technology (including applications, tools, and models) for generative artificial intelligence detection and generative artificial intelligence watermarking, for the purposes of—</text> <paragraph id="HCF5FD022E1EA4BD18092C50FD71083C4"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">facilitating the research, development, testing, evaluation, and competition of such technologies to support the Secretaries of the military departments and the commanders of combatant commands in warfighting requirements; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD1BE5855E2EB4E82AA1B3CCE7ED656B6"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">transitioning such technologies, including technologies developed pursuant to pilot programs, prototype projects, or other research and development programs, from the prototyping phase to production.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H740CE1DDE57B49C892969C6F59FA4336"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Participation</header><text>The participants in the prize competition under subsection (a) may include federally funded research and development centers, entities within the private sector, entities within the defense industrial base, institutions of higher education, Federal departments and agencies, and such other categories of participants as the Secretary of Defense considers appropriate.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H1C95EF7E139044BEBE44521377903839"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Designation</header><text>The prize competition under subsection (a) shall be known as the <quote>Generative AI Detection and Watermark Competition</quote>.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HB854C55258F947CABC724814ABA048C1"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Administration</header><text>The Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering shall administer the prize competition under subsection (a).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H117976CB5F3F40D59053BE040EF2A62E"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Framework</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall provide to the congressional defense committees a briefing on the framework to be used in carrying out the prize competition under subsection (a).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H06304805DCCA44ADABA2811043ABEA11"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Annual briefings</header><text>Not later than October 1 of each year until the date of termination under subsection (g), the Secretary of Defense shall provide to the congressional defense committees a briefing on the results of the prize competition under subsection (a).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H2B2EBC42F3C847DA9DF910BD36EB5245"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Termination</header><text>The authority to carry out the prize competition under subsection (a) shall terminate on December 31, 2025.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H2132EB8BB2A94B73927EE6D68345058A"><enum>(h)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> 
<paragraph id="H8F025FF8441B4453BAAC2FE8C94AF91E"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The term <quote>generative artificial intelligence detection</quote> means, with respect to digital content, the positive identification of the use of generative artificial intelligence in the generation of such content.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H82C0139325C248B3BA79BA96484C27AE"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>generative artificial intelligence watermarking</quote> means, with respect to digital content, embedding within such content data conveying attribution of the generation of such content to generative artificial intelligence.</text></paragraph></subsection></section>

<subsection id="H425CDEF470BB4623A42AA11A570E6CD1" commented="no"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Ethical and responsible artificial intelligence</header> 
<paragraph id="H518CCA9E2A384587A094C05EEAC05713" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Process</header><text>The Secretary of Defense, acting through the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer, shall develop and implement a process—</text> <subparagraph id="H7BAE5680C41544E587974ADCB0E5D87F" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to assess whether a given artificial intelligence technology used by the Department of Defense is in compliance with a test, evaluation, verification, and validation framework that—</text> 
<clause id="H8721F7945BB3453796DC4FA9ADB90C6B"><enum>(i)</enum><text>operationalizes responsible artificial intelligence principles; and</text></clause> <clause id="H4CEBBF59364E4E6FAC4C347B01D72ECD"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>is validated and selected by the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer for purposes of this subsection;</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H6C549A9C4A0F41BF80D95B18DCB9C63C" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to report and remediate any artificial intelligence technology that is determined not to be in compliance with the framework selected pursuant to subparagraph (A); and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H4971D78552DD4FBFBAB0DBA330A07742" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">in a case in which efforts to remediate such technology have been unsuccessful, to discontinue the use of the technology until effective remediation is achievable.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD38A27E4C735422481B1220FC34382CE" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Additional requirements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In developing and implementing the process under paragraph (1), the Secretary of Defense shall—</text> <subparagraph id="H334954796FC046AAA6C8C8D773339C34" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">develop clear criteria against which the compliance of an artificial intelligence technology with the framework selected pursuant to subparagraph (A) of such paragraph may be assessed under such subparagraph, taking into consideration—</text> 
<clause id="H7ABD72CC145744DF902F9CE116F4A355"><enum>(i)</enum><text>similar criteria previously developed by the Secretary; and</text></clause> <clause id="HBFD83515ED7E4032AC81B18B2D87F118"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the identification of potential vulnerabilities in systems and infrastructure of the Armed Forces that could be exploited by adversarial artificial intelligence applications used by the People’s Republic of China, the Russian Federation, or other foreign adversaries;</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HBCFBFC5A16D2422A82DF927C8E802E8B" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">take steps to integrate such process across the elements of the Department of Defense, including the combatant commands; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2DD3B59B9E2A404DAF4FB2BA219DD7BF" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">provide information on such process to members of the Armed Forces and civilian personnel of the Department that are—</text>

<paragraph id="H3A3201372E5D423392A8FCFFDA4F9CF1"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Briefing</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 150 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall provide to the congressional defense committees a briefing on the implementation of this section.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H6F0B3C782AC049DE90E71EE370C26C0D" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1545.</enum><header>Study to analyze vulnerability for artificial intelligence-enabled military applications</header> <subsection id="HF62AE4A9DCCA4F3093DBAB641590559C"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Study</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall complete a study to assess the functionality of artificial intelligence-enabled military applications, research and development needs related to such applications, and vulnerabilities to the privacy, security, and accuracy of such applications.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HE10B029F9891407E94E8AB7CF2D4088E"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The study under subsection (a) shall include the following:</text> <paragraph id="H0BFAC7DA885047FD8506B30B9074D3EE"><enum>(1)</enum><text>An assessment of research and development efforts, including transition pathways, needed to advance explainable and interpretable artificial intelligence-enabled military applications, including the capability to assess the architectures, data models, and algorithms underlying such applications.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2EDD0D511A50417FAF0D3F139D6FD38A"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of any potential risks to the privacy, security, or accuracy of the architectures, data models, or algorithms underlying artificial intelligence-enabled military applications, including the following:</text> <subparagraph id="HF5B2B095954740E38F472224C54FCBEE"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Individual foundational artificial intelligence models, including the adequacy of existing testing, training, and auditing for such models to ensure such models may be properly assessed over time.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HA7A28B01DEBC4C09BE1BB0F05A8357CE"><enum>(B)</enum><text>The interactions of multiple artificial intelligence-enabled military applications and how such interactions may affect the ability to detect and assess new, complex, and emergent behavior among individual agents, as well as the collective effect of such interactions on risks to the privacy, security, and accuracy of such applications over time.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H432F4CA599094F14B3C159C05370EB7C"><enum>(C)</enum><text>The effect of increased agency in artificial intelligence-enabled military applications and how such increased agency may affect the ability to detect and assess new, complex, and emergent behavior, as well risks to the privacy, security, and accuracy of such applications over time.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HBF7C250BBB274054853A7BB422E7D024"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of the survivability and traceability of decision support systems that are integrated with artificial intelligence-enabled military applications and used in a contested environment.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H668F1C09C3CD43F0AB168501C9956D76"><enum>(4)</enum><text>An identification of existing artificial intelligence metrics, developmental, testing and audit capabilities, personnel, and infrastructure of the Department of Defense, including test and evaluation facilities of the Department, needed to enable ongoing assessment under paragraphs (1) through (3).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H239D2A4CE24A4F559564379B5BE59454"><enum>(5)</enum><text>An identification of any research gaps necessary to be filled to sufficiently carry out the assessments and identifications required under paragraphs (1) through (3) that are not currently, or not sufficiently, funded within the Department of Defense.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HE9FD97B0696140F8B0C6EDCF92D2F617"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Interim briefing</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer shall provide to the congressional defense committees a briefing on the interim findings of the study under subsection (a).</text></subsection>

<subsection id="HAEAAFB5A7DE94A72B3D69D2C384632F2"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Foundational artificial intelligence model defined</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section, the term <quote>foundational artificial intelligence model</quote> means an adaptive generative model that is trained on a broad set of unlabeled data sets that may be used for different tasks with minimal fine-tuning.</text></subsection></section></subtitle> <subtitle id="H59069EF5B17D4C5296FD01D380C749B9"><enum>F</enum><header>Reports and Other Matters</header> <section id="H99558CB2522747108EAD646AD82408AD" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1551.</enum><header>Limitation on availability of funds for travel for Office of Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness pending strategy relating to Defense Travel System</header> <subsection id="H40D2C32CFD3E4D0296D874C9717C1FE9"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Strategy</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness shall develop a strategy to modernize or replace the end-to-end travel management system of the Department of Defense known as the <quote>Defense Travel System</quote> (in this section, referred to as the <quote>Defense Travel System</quote>).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF679DAF5CCD144769E009E7B1CD91B54"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The strategy under subsection (a) shall include the following:</text> <paragraph id="H8F1B6BDAFF3F4CC1B1BC691DC767454E" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A business case analysis that evaluates options for modernizing or replacing the Defense Travel System, including—</text>

<section id="HDBDEEFD44E494F9CBDA4C227DFD6075D"><enum>1603.</enum><header>Enhanced authority to increase space launch capacity through space launch support services</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline"><external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/10/135">Chapter 135</external-xref> of title 10, United States Code, is amended by inserting after <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/2276">section 2276</external-xref> the following new section:</text> <quoted-block id="H96E0683A0B3E41359E86BE27F1D9F893" style="USC"> <section id="H7F2C34A9EA274B8B9E4FD5FB8DB7C53A"><enum>2276a.</enum><header>Special authority for provision of space launch support services to increase space launch capacity</header> <subsection id="H4B266D3E165E479ABEE074ED5ACD8FDC"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of a military department may support Federal and commercial space launch capacity on any domestic real property under the control of the Secretary through the provision of space launch support services.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H11825E22131E482AA155EDE32E6CDD01"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Provision of launch equipment and services to commercial entities</header> 
<paragraph id="HF06BE3295C4D47D6B423CAFABE36E69D"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Contract or other transaction authority</header><text>The Secretary of a military department may enter into a contract or other transaction with one or more commercial entities that intend to conduct space launch activities on a military installation under the jurisdiction of the Secretary. Under such a contract or agreement, the Secretary may agree to provide to the commercial entity supplies, services, equipment, and construction needed for commercial space launch.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HBCA4B8C87DB848A6A0378A906F994488"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Costs</header> <subparagraph id="H14145D887808424CA4CEB4EAAE5BD708"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Direct costs</header><text>If the Secretary of a military department enters into a contract or other transaction with a commercial entity under paragraph (1), such contract or transaction shall include a provision that requires the commercial entity to reimburse the Department of Defense for all direct costs to the United States that are associated with any good, service, or equipment provided to the commercial entity under the contract or other transaction.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H7B4B0893D034491BABAF322166580777"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Indirect costs</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the Secretary of a military department enters into a contract or other transaction with a commercial entity under paragraph (1), such contract or transaction may include a provision that requires the commercial entity to reimburse the Department of Defense for such indirect costs as the Secretary considers to be appropriate. In such a case, such contract or other transaction may provide for the reimbursement of such indirect costs through the establishment of a rate, fixed price, or similar mechanism the Secretary concerned determines is reasonable.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6DC7A3F4E39A4CF0A695E581672E0CA3"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Retention of funds collected from commercial users</header><text>Any amount collected from a commercial entity as a reimbursement under paragraph (2) shall be credited to the appropriations account from which the cost for which such reimbursement is provided was derived.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3ED3663AEB1E4ADE9FA058FD1DBE1891"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Regulations</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of each of the military departments shall prescribe regulations to carry out this subsection.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H6053453A9F8047979FB420BDB09C9DC5"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> 
<paragraph id="H12FC95E89DF8429FBC966FA0CEB556F2"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Space launch</header><text>The term <quote>space launch</quote> includes all activities, supplies, equipment, facilities, or services supporting launch preparation, launch, reentry, recovery, and other launch-related activities for both the payload and the space transportation vehicle.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H10BA1D46BCC04FE38FF2772309CDD108"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Commercial entity</header><text>The term <quote>commercial entity</quote> or <quote>commercial</quote> means a non-Federal entity organized under the laws of the United States or of any jurisdiction within the United States.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H5FDB8A5721BB42A2B881D113EEB4DAF6"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Transition limitations and reporting requirements</header><text>For each of fiscal years 2024, 2025, and 2026, the Secretary of a military department shall—</text> <paragraph id="H6F771A21A9BC491F9BAB2648262F2178"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">with respect to any contract or other transaction authority entered into pursuant to subsection (b), limit the amount of the indirect costs that are reimbursable under paragraph (2)(B) of such subsection to not more than 30 percent, not to exceed $5,000,000 annually (based on fiscal year 2024 constant dollars), of the total amount of the direct costs reimbursable under paragraph (2)(A) of such subsection; and</text></paragraph>

<section id="H9E9B55537F1446829541F82A5C9370C2" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1645.</enum><header>Pilot program on development of reentry vehicles and related systems</header> 
<subsection id="H9A9F81DBCA724A7694D17EFB675EA0D6"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of the Air Force may carry out a pilot program, to be known as the <quote>Reentry Vehicle Flight Test Bed Program</quote>, to assess the feasibility of providing regular flight test opportunities that support the development of reentry vehicles to—</text> <paragraph id="HF2E7150A187E48B38BB0DF04AA8B0B70"><enum>(1)</enum><text>facilitate technology upgrades tested in a realistic flight environment;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H10C57AC6036E4F93BEEE0810D65CA432"><enum>(2)</enum><text>provide an enduring, high-cadence test bed to mature technologies for planned reentry vehicles; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H4D2F67019CCE4A92AB307F43C3245A21"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">transition technologies developed under other programs and projects relating to long-range ballistic or hypersonic strike missiles from the research and development or prototyping phases into operational use.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H8C41792232184F099C5E3C204A2ABD05"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Grants, contracts, and other agreements</header> 
<paragraph id="HEE088F6A5A9E4838895F622EA54B8C1F"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Authority</header><text>In carrying out a pilot program under this section, the Secretary may, subject to paragraph (2), award grants and enter into contracts or other agreements with appropriate entities for the conduct of relevant flight tests of reentry vehicles and systems.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H619D3002EDBC425596E7E5FD58C02857"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Grant and contract requirements</header> <subparagraph id="H20056CE4A5B5430CB1217DA9FB61AFDD"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Merit-based grants</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any grant under paragraph (1) shall be awarded through merit-based selection procedures.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H1D7FB501BDAF4765BA338EBA8809D654"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Competitive contract procedures</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any contract or other agreement under paragraph (1) shall be awarded using competitive procedures (as defined in section 3012 of title 10, United States Code). </text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA4E1E0836DAC4092926225E37A8406AD"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Use of funds</header><text>An entity that receives a grant, or enters into a contract or other agreement, as part of a pilot program carried out under this section shall use the grant, or any amount received under the contract or other agreement, to carry out one or more of the following activities:</text> 
<subparagraph id="HE3F24578B3CC4753AF0AB93EEB873608"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Conducting flight tests to develop or validate—</text> <clause id="H6DD4AE037B5246EBA27C68D930B08203"><enum>(i)</enum><text>aeroshell design;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H51A262B4923D4BCB91F6F6DDF2C0C6AE"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>thermal protective systems;</text></clause> <clause id="HE7AAF528007A4CCCA79A6B92DEAED3F1"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>guidance and control systems;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HD4676E192F464EC7B6439CA8FA27CA01"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>sensors;</text></clause> <clause id="HB879EE51B0FE4ACD93355F2F756325DF"><enum>(v)</enum><text>communications;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H1CAF3A7A5A644CCAB1CEF7CA11165C16"><enum>(vi)</enum><text>environmental sensors; or</text></clause> <clause id="H3E23275779DB4BDF96E3DF618638292A"><enum>(vii)</enum><text>other relevant technologies.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H7FBA2FC083B54E90AED42A70CE95E394"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Expanding flight test opportunities through low-cost, high-cadence platforms.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HD429E9C42ED34B4898CC496F17928660"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Coordination</header><text>If the Secretary of the Air Force carries out a pilot program under this section, the Secretary shall ensure that the activities under the pilot program are carried out in coordination with the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of the Navy.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H7DA36D2B66264540A256B1708BB5B82A"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Termination</header><text>The authority to carry out a pilot program under this section shall terminate on December 31, 2029.</text></subsection></section> <section id="H68AC0D41AD0F49C385A71C0537E7C454" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1646.</enum><header>Prohibition on reduction of the intercontinental ballistic missiles of the United States</header> <subsection id="HD3BB704F4A8E4864BBEBDEA22563C32F"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Prohibition</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Except as provided in subsection (b), none of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2024 for the Department of Defense may be obligated or expended for the following, and the Department may not otherwise take any action to do the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H90E3EFE4F1404D27A1BAEF7F6F0787E0"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Reduce, or prepare to reduce, the responsiveness or alert level of the intercontinental ballistic missiles of the United States.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H71772142FB70467A8A0C6561445D6410"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Reduce, or prepare to reduce, the quantity of deployed intercontinental ballistic missiles of the United States to a number less than 400.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H020F4BF82DB74ACFA3C0BB86C52F0F70"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Exception</header><text>The prohibition in subsection (a) shall not apply to any of the following activities:</text> <paragraph id="H8C4F463B3DEA4C32A417E9B3299651D5"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The maintenance or sustainment of intercontinental ballistic missiles.</text></paragraph>

<section id="HE40350ABC5E141668FB742D9FDDA1EAB" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1647.</enum><header> Limitation on availability of funds pending compliance with information requests from the Government Accountability Office</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2024 for Operation and Maintenance, Defense-wide, and available for the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Policy, not more than 35 percent may be obligated or expended until the date on which the Comptroller General of the United States notifies the congressional defense committees that the Secretary of Defense has fully complied with information requests from the Government Accountability Office made in connection with the conduct of the study required by section 1652 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/81">Public Law 117–81</external-xref>; 135 Stat. 2100).</text></section> <section id="HC7B579E3473B4848B05A5FBB4CAB1A5F" section-type="subsequent-section" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>1648.</enum><header>Congressional notification of decision to delay strategic delivery system test event</header> <subsection id="H0584D2E66E26442AA6E0248E0D1370B3"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Notification</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than five days after the Secretary of Defense makes a decision to delay a scheduled test event for a strategic delivery system, the Secretary shall submit to the congressional defense committees written notice of such decision.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H5A37EEE00F2047F98DB3550827CC5748"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Report</header> 
<paragraph id="H1D7781567FB248C89ED1A69BF12D3358"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Except as provided in paragraph (3), not later than 60 days after the submission of a notification required under subsection (a) with respect to a decision to delay a scheduled test event, the Secretary shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the decision.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H4528A6DCCF034ECF801F57BD9C6F56F9"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements required</header><text>A report submitted under paragraph (1) shall include each of the following with respect to the scheduled test event covered by the report:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H67281D08085641EF856169F16928F12F"><enum>(A)</enum><text>A description of the objectives of the test.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H107FA84D42CB4917A12A54ED05BA6C48"><enum>(B)</enum><text>An explanation for the decision to cancel the test.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H14316EBA6EEE4A02BAEA85401E7D9503"><enum>(C)</enum><text>An estimate of expenditures related to the cancelled test.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H41BCD7F71D5B43AC915843867BABEEA9"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of the effect of the test cancellation on—</text> 
<clause id="HA82B8A8A8A204039A7A6A80340EF3F53"><enum>(i)</enum><text>confidence in the reliability of the strategic nuclear weapons delivery system involved; and</text></clause> <clause id="H4A692082EF2D4C8F9B8D8C3B350992C5"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>any research, development, test, and evaluation activities related to the test.</text></clause></subparagraph>

<subparagraph id="H7624960B6AB54E81937FD292400042DA"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Unfavorable weather conditions.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H1DBDFA02F7F94548B853885D0B236557"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Safety concerns.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H702B8D90B89944579971137E91419B40"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Technical issues related to the delivery system or test facility.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9B507C69397E41D19079C42308569D61"><enum>(D)</enum><text>Operational or security concerns at the test facility or on the test range.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="H5EA3393E16D24587BFCE8E9165CBB72A" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>1649.</enum><header>Congressional notification of nuclear cooperation between Russia and China</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">If the Commander of the United States Strategic Command determines, after consultation with the Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency, that militarily significant cooperation between the Russian Federation and the People’s Republic of China related to nuclear or strategic capabilities is likely to occur or has likely occurred, the Commander shall submit to the congressional defense committees a notification of such determination that includes—</text> <paragraph id="HE0E0588B4F4C4A9E8E1AAEA234EFF11C"><enum>(1)</enum><text>a description of the military significant cooperation; and</text></paragraph>

<subsection id="HDF449915B56A434E9E7E59D735788EF8" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(d)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Form</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The plan required by subsection (a) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H35077C96CE4E4B7B94C4237FE57225D8" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(e)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Briefing</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 30 days after the submission of the plan required by subsection (a), the Secretary of the Air Force, the Commander of the United States Strategic Command, and the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Space Policy shall provide for the congressional defense committees a briefing on the actions being pursued to implement the plan.</text></subsection>

<subparagraph id="HD2482D72DD674841BDCF35084C996262"><enum>(B)</enum><text>The appropriate balance of missile detection, tracking, defense, and defeat capabilities in such area of responsibility.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H636F3BB2D64F4810814AB56653CB3B51"><enum>(C)</enum><text>A command and control network for integrating missile detection, tracking, defense, and defeat capabilities across such area of responsibility.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H6982DBACF408437FAE33932FA4D79BCD"><enum>(D)</enum><text>A time-phased scheduling construct for fielding the constituent systems that will comprise the integrated air and missile defense architecture for such area of responsibility.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HD82346037751469FB18E7E05D5FA7F38"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Reporting requirements</header> <paragraph id="H12D7B399C4A447D895EFBA178F7AEE0B"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Report on initial findings</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the findings of the analysis conducted by Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation of the current integrated air and missile defense sensor architecture that informed the submission of the budget of the President (as submitted to Congress pursuant to section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code) for fiscal year 2024, and specific programs of record that can support additional sensor coverage for the State of Hawaii. <section id="HEF0DAF2035014D8087F454B1697966CD"><enum>1671.</enum><header>Independent analysis of space-based missile defense capability</header> 
<subsection id="HFAAA32E0481740B79532F7491CEE2FEA"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, acting through the Director of the Missile Defense Agency, shall seek to enter into an arrangement with an appropriate federally funded research and development center to update the study referred to in subsection (c).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H69D7DBC75FB645BFB9351ACBA62ED1DF"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The updated study under subsection (a) shall include analysis of the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="HB50FC3E0274F46119C02559062229EF6"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The extent to which space-based capabilities would address current and evolving missile threats to the United States and deployed Armed Forces.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2028A867697C4DABBCE789C6107F8460"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The maturity levels of technologies necessary for an operational space-based missile defense capability.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H02CED2B1E0BF43DCA73BC82A6D348315"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Potential options for developing, fielding, operating, and sustaining a space-based missile defense capability, including—</text> <subparagraph id="H61B485B390994B6F8701E9672488E349"><enum>(A)</enum><text>estimated costs; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H6BE561860833490498E2B873A69E3B22"><enum>(B)</enum><text>assessments of the effectiveness of different architectures.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H32FBE3A7CF41449F891F0A7662874A28"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The technical risks, knowledge gaps, or other challenges associated with the development and operation of space-based interceptor capabilities.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H916B8150E9B34962B8067F1285F391DD"><enum>(5)</enum><text>The ability of the Department of Defense to protect and defend on-orbit space-based missile defense capabilities, including any recommendations for resiliency requirements that would be needed to ensure the effectiveness of such capabilities.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HCD2A1D9F1FE64A5FB05FDFED7248D807"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Study specified</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The study referred to in this subsection is the study conducted by the federally funded research and development center known as the <quote>Institute for Defense Analysis</quote> examining the feasibility and advisability of developing a space-based missile defense capability.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H667AFC06A5DF4289A6F9B2248F5B179E"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Report</header> 
<paragraph id="H7BB36C0CDA2C42A596A8A114AB455A55"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 270 days after entering into an arrangement under subsection (a), the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report that includes—</text> <subparagraph id="H5984CA60001946778E57B26B47F447D5"><enum>(A)</enum><text>an unaltered copy of the updated study completed pursuant to the arrangement; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H8ADE2FB5329D4ABF8F2599BD796C37EB"><enum>(B)</enum><text>any views of the Secretary of Defense with respect to such updated study.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HD36FD2B42A07431CBD67FE9A2BB3ABE5"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The report required under paragraph (1) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex.</text></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle>
