<subtitle id="H70E3B3F893074AB5BC04A73B7F5417EB"><enum>B</enum><header>Drone Security</header> 
<section id="H2BA649C6FF3B4104A3A453317F8BCDCC"><enum>1821.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline"> This subtitle may be cited as the <quote>American Security Drone Act of 2023</quote>.</text></section> <section id="H6D3CC50F0D65425592B22C194A201DD7"><enum>1822.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline"> In this subtitle:</text> 
<paragraph id="H7AC95913BB0E4D938926FEA07CFF34EC"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Covered foreign entity</header><text>The term <quote>covered foreign entity</quote> means an entity included on a list developed and maintained by the Federal Acquisition Security Council and published in the System for Award Management (SAM). This list will include entities in the following categories:</text> <subparagraph id="H6F667280EDD24F4487A3106813696450"><enum>(A)</enum><text>An entity included on the Consolidated Screening List.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H14CB3C5BD14E4F2E86E4A463A86F1E06"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Any entity that is subject to extrajudicial direction from a foreign government, as determined by the Secretary of Homeland Security.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HBAF8B4A13006457D82F3FC89B691D7CB"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Any entity the Secretary of Homeland Security, in coordination with the Attorney General, Director of National Intelligence, and the Secretary of Defense, determines poses a national security risk.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H64CB679D6DF045698AD46ABA367A0BBC"><enum>(D)</enum><text>Any entity domiciled in the People’s Republic of China or subject to influence or control by the Government of the People’s Republic of China or the Communist Party of the People’s Republic of China, as determined by the Secretary of Homeland Security.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2F530D20D0BF4AADB74342B522ADA069"><enum>(E)</enum><text>Any subsidiary or affiliate of an entity described in subparagraphs (A) through (D).</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC17EB380ED6F4A0AA230798E07BC29B2"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Covered unmanned aircraft system</header><text>The term <quote>covered unmanned aircraft system</quote> has the meaning given the term <quote>unmanned aircraft system</quote> in section 44801 of title 49, United States Code.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H4B13B95520B1401294B47968746AF4A8"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Intelligence; intelligence community</header><text>The terms <quote>intelligence</quote> and <quote>intelligence community</quote> have the meanings given those terms in section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3003">50 U.S.C. 3003</external-xref>).</text></paragraph></section> 
<section id="H51B6BF8F7E2B4EC28162F0367867C3AC"><enum>1823.</enum><header>Prohibition on procurement of covered unmanned aircraft systems from covered foreign entities</header> 
<subsection id="H50138D6154774EDCB2E0E93CAE79264B"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Except as provided under subsections (b) through (f), the head of an executive agency may not procure any covered unmanned aircraft system that is manufactured or assembled by a covered foreign entity, which includes associated elements related to the collection and transmission of sensitive information (consisting of communication links and the components that control the unmanned aircraft) that enable the operator to operate the aircraft in the National Airspace System. The Federal Acquisition Security Council, in coordination with the Secretary of Transportation, shall develop and update a list of associated elements.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HC3B8A75CDB1E49F5A68085D2C63D8C3D"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Exemption</header><text>The Secretary of Homeland Security, the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of State, and the Attorney General are exempt from the restriction under subsection (a) if the procurement is required in the national interest of the United States and—</text> 
<paragraph id="H3CA467D3087A4A8F8268976C832D0A53"><enum>(1)</enum><text>is for the sole purposes of research, evaluation, training, testing, or analysis for electronic warfare, information warfare operations, cybersecurity, or development of unmanned aircraft system or counter-unmanned aircraft system technology;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5051AE34FA1748D295EE1CC09327D141"><enum>(2)</enum><text>is for the sole purposes of conducting counterterrorism or counterintelligence activities, protective missions, or Federal criminal or national security investigations, including forensic examinations, or for electronic warfare, information warfare operations, cybersecurity, or development of an unmanned aircraft system or counter-unmanned aircraft system technology; or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0B8BDD7FB3E84EE8B16D0BDCE00E985D"><enum>(3)</enum><text>is an unmanned aircraft system that, as procured or as modified after procurement but before operational use, can no longer transfer to, or download data from, a covered foreign entity and otherwise poses no national security cybersecurity risks as determined by the exempting official.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HF46BEB738A7744248614C03C3F2D4AD4"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Department of transportation and federal aviation administration exemption</header><text>The Secretary of Transportation is exempt from the restriction under subsection (a) if the operation or procurement is deemed to support the safe, secure, or efficient operation of the National Airspace System or maintenance of public safety, including activities carried out under the Federal Aviation Administration’s Alliance for System Safety of UAS through Research Excellence (ASSURE) Center of Excellence (COE) and any other activity deemed to support the safe, secure, or efficient operation of the National Airspace System or maintenance of public safety, as determined by the Secretary or the Secretary’s designee.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HD6766007F2524A7D9A7ED0A38008DC77"><enum>(d)</enum><header>National transportation safety board exemption</header><text>The National Transportation Safety Board, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security, is exempt from the restriction under subsection (a) if the operation or procurement is necessary for the sole purpose of conducting safety investigations.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H8F738FDD1552419A9787D90536B200ED"><enum>(e)</enum><header>National oceanic and atmospheric administration exemption</header><text>The Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security, is exempt from the restriction under subsection (a) if the procurement is necessary for the purpose of meeting NOAA’s science or management objectives or operational mission.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H0BC5768B82894869B97A17DA1F3155FB"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Waiver</header><text>The head of an executive agency may waive the prohibition under subsection (a) on a case-by-case basis—</text> <paragraph id="HF092268368894315963746480958C054"><enum>(1)</enum><text>with the approval of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, after consultation with the Federal Acquisition Security Council; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HDFECD88157384D43BF83D2441D88EBA7"><enum>(2)</enum><text>upon notification to—</text> <subparagraph id="H42E4CA282B89471F9EAEA6D539DDF156"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H55C16375F6F4487294DDB2A28536AE0A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Committee on Oversight and Accountability in the House of Representatives; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HEF340707A4C749768324CBBA77B1BCB4"><enum>(C)</enum><text>other appropriate congressional committees of jurisdiction.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="H2BCA891056264E37AC930C2B07E90D84"><enum>1824.</enum><header>Prohibition on operation of covered unmanned aircraft systems from covered foreign entities</header> 
<subsection id="H60592A0745444ADD8FCB1E1B79C5BA22"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Prohibition</header> 
<paragraph id="H8B85E6B6A4474EE9AA38044BB05AAD13"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Beginning on the date that is two years after the date of the enactment of this Act, no Federal department or agency may operate a covered unmanned aircraft system manufactured or assembled by a covered foreign entity.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H8C238FC37EB141178125D78A83512557"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Applicability to contracted services</header><text>The prohibition under paragraph (1) applies to any covered unmanned aircraft systems that are being used by any executive agency through the method of contracting for the services of covered unmanned aircraft systems.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H51171AE0A92A4860BBD7E8F6AE1EDD8E"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Exemption</header><text>The Secretary of Homeland Security, the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of State, and the Attorney General are exempt from the restriction under subsection (a) if the operation is required in the national interest of the United States and—</text> <paragraph id="HED15730D4F424B2EBE1AAF71A5857E61"><enum>(1)</enum><text>is for the sole purposes of research, evaluation, training, testing, or analysis for electronic warfare, information warfare operations, cybersecurity, or development of unmanned aircraft system or counter-unmanned aircraft system technology;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HFE5E9D80B9554B2C8D1CEFD0D0CBEB47"><enum>(2)</enum><text>is for the sole purposes of conducting counterterrorism or counterintelligence activities, protective missions, or Federal criminal or national security investigations, including forensic examinations, or for electronic warfare, information warfare operations, cybersecurity, or development of an unmanned aircraft system or counter-unmanned aircraft system technology; or</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2754F6D5D6A546CA8F18CAECE72EEF36"><enum>(3)</enum><text>is an unmanned aircraft system that, as procured or as modified after procurement but before operational use, can no longer transfer to, or download data from, a covered foreign entity and otherwise poses no national security cybersecurity risks as determined by the exempting official.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HE0B8EDFD187E4C61BE8C0C363C67D702"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Department of transportation and federal aviation administration exemption</header><text>The Secretary of Transportation is exempt from the restriction under subsection (a) if the operation is deemed to support the safe, secure, or efficient operation of the National Airspace System or maintenance of public safety, including activities carried out under the Federal Aviation Administration’s Alliance for System Safety of UAS through Research Excellence (ASSURE) Center of Excellence (COE) and any other activity deemed to support the safe, secure, or efficient operation of the National Airspace System or maintenance of public safety, as determined by the Secretary or the Secretary’s designee.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HFC745FCEF241478DB553397F8F8CFF95"><enum>(d)</enum><header>National transportation safety board exemption</header><text>The National Transportation Safety Board, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security, is exempt from the restriction under subsection (a) if the operation is necessary for the sole purpose of conducting safety investigations.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H16A12CCCD8A246388915F84D02508B61"><enum>(e)</enum><header>National oceanic and atmospheric administration exemption</header><text>The Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security, is exempt from the restriction under subsection (a) if the procurement is necessary for the purpose of meeting NOAA’s science or management objectives or operational mission.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HA8EB1608749A4AAA90FC6E1B5C6CB0C5"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Waiver</header><text>The head of an executive agency may waive the prohibition under subsection (a) on a case-by-case basis—</text> 
<paragraph id="H150F173960B44D309E188D9762EB954B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>with the approval of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, after consultation with the Federal Acquisition Security Council; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC2556A8E93E64C4885302E6D1B6AC666"><enum>(2)</enum><text>upon notification to—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H4EC37A6DB225455C80E6ED5A62B9709E"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H0B8867863B7E494895135862191AEE73"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Committee on Oversight and Accountability in the House of Representatives; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H0D76092821BE457DA0E20416AD3872CE"><enum>(C)</enum><text>other appropriate congressional committees of jurisdiction.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H9B62AE56BBC34DF99EC7A72FAB931534"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Regulations and guidance</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Homeland Security, in consultation with the Attorney General and the Secretary of Transportation, shall prescribe regulations or guidance to implement this section.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="HBA84A055A2E642A38CB11DD77CDF2B9A"><enum>1825.</enum><header>Prohibition on use of Federal funds for procurement and operation of covered unmanned aircraft systems from covered foreign entities</header> 
<subsection id="H6506C2643F62431790DE7B487C565E2A"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Beginning on the date that is two years after the date of the enactment of this Act, except as provided in subsection (b), no Federal funds awarded through a contract, grant, or cooperative agreement, or otherwise made available may be used—</text> <paragraph id="H264CB70F32DD4D2D8828FF43481030EF"><enum>(1)</enum><text>to procure a covered unmanned aircraft system that is manufactured or assembled by a covered foreign entity; or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3D8D31503A7B42F7AA9B4728046E0566"><enum>(2)</enum><text>in connection with the operation of such a drone or unmanned aircraft system.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H3DC245AA8056448E9DD5DA69D88D31D2"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Exemption</header><text>The Secretary of Homeland Security, the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of State, and the Attorney General are exempt from the restriction under subsection (a) if the procurement or operation is required in the national interest of the United States and—</text> 
<paragraph id="H409F96DD68B54F22B3F524EB89E0BFFD"><enum>(1)</enum><text>is for the sole purposes of research, evaluation, training, testing, or analysis for electronic warfare, information warfare operations, cybersecurity, or development of unmanned aircraft system or counter-unmanned aircraft system technology;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFB13EB6ACC2641D2A938E5A45431AD46"><enum>(2)</enum><text>is for the sole purposes of conducting counterterrorism or counterintelligence activities, protective missions, or Federal criminal or national security investigations, including forensic examinations, or for electronic warfare, information warfare operations, cybersecurity, or development of an unmanned aircraft system or counter-unmanned aircraft system technology; or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD8E60E74903F4CD3B14E44D66FB24C5B"><enum>(3)</enum><text>is an unmanned aircraft system that, as procured or as modified after procurement but before operational use, can no longer transfer to, or download data from, a covered foreign entity and otherwise poses no national security cybersecurity risks as determined by the exempting official.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HD21CCF08FC314805A68A35E96E5642F3"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Department of transportation and federal aviation administration exemption</header><text>The Secretary of Transportation is exempt from the restriction under subsection (a) if the operation or procurement is deemed to support the safe, secure, or efficient operation of the National Airspace System or maintenance of public safety, including activities carried out under the Federal Aviation Administration’s Alliance for System Safety of UAS through Research Excellence (ASSURE) Center of Excellence (COE) and any other activity deemed to support the safe, secure, or efficient operation of the National Airspace System or maintenance of public safety, as determined by the Secretary or the Secretary’s designee.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H100F4FC388ED4D79BF94CFDCF35E0EC6"><enum>(d)</enum><header>National oceanic and atmospheric administration exemption</header><text>The Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security, is exempt from the restriction under subsection (a) if the operation or procurement is necessary for the purpose of meeting NOAA’s science or management objectives or operational mission.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H9061FD6C2EBF4395BD1CF1FB64455368"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Waiver</header><text>The head of an executive agency may waive the prohibition under subsection (a) on a case-by-case basis—</text> 
<paragraph id="H4991E478187842F1AF9781AF6484DE27"><enum>(1)</enum><text>with the approval of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, after consultation with the Federal Acquisition Security Council; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDD4183920817442CB659AC6AC0D9B6ED"><enum>(2)</enum><text>upon notification to—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HFB5E0BC90C8E47E4825EA5E4F2103779"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H11A3DEEA2C494E7E8C7093075081CABB"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Committee on Oversight and Accountability in the House of Representatives; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H0EC2D074F6DE45C991FD51B534D4B0A3"><enum>(C)</enum><text>other appropriate congressional committees of jurisdiction.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H5F3C9D0454D841CD813BE80EE3809128"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Regulations</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council shall prescribe regulations or guidance, as necessary, to implement the requirements of this section pertaining to Federal contracts.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H6DAACEF37B9445198740034592B3E76F"><enum>1826.</enum><header>Prohibition on use of Government-issued purchase cards to purchase covered unmanned aircraft systems from covered foreign entities</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline"> Effective immediately, Government-issued Purchase Cards may not be used to procure any covered unmanned aircraft system from a covered foreign entity.</text></section> <section id="H934C3E2A656A489387DCF15C88EB9DE0"><enum>1827.</enum><header>Management of existing inventories of covered unmanned aircraft systems from covered foreign entities</header> <subsection id="HCB3ACCAC41B745F2933593BACE39D04C"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>All executive agencies must account for existing inventories of covered unmanned aircraft systems manufactured or assembled by a covered foreign entity in their personal property accounting systems, within one year of the date of enactment of this Act, regardless of the original procurement cost, or the purpose of procurement due to the special monitoring and accounting measures necessary to track the items’ capabilities.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H9B95B365B68846AE9E78AE78F5A4DCA5"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Classified tracking</header><text>Due to the sensitive nature of missions and operations conducted by the United States Government, inventory data related to covered unmanned aircraft systems manufactured or assembled by a covered foreign entity may be tracked at a classified level, as determined by the Secretary of Homeland Security or the Secretary’s designee.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H8A9893C82C0F49498F552989967C2016"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Exceptions</header><text>The Department of Defense, the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Justice, the Department of Transportation, and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration may exclude from the full inventory process, covered unmanned aircraft systems that are deemed expendable due to mission risk such as recovery issues, or that are one-time-use covered unmanned aircraft due to requirements and low cost.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H0483A8C9B2ED4AEF9C17568652FB7174"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Intelligence community exception</header><text>Nothing in this section shall apply to any element of the intelligence community.</text></subsection></section> <section id="H8EA9B26264274861B65C9779DA925030"><enum>1828.</enum><header>Comptroller General report</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline"> Not later than 275 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to Congress a report on the amount of commercial off-the-shelf drones and covered unmanned aircraft systems procured by Federal departments and agencies from covered foreign entities, except that nothing in this section shall apply to any element of the intelligence community.</text></section> 
<section id="H9B5FB61E344B48E39465D2675F044926"><enum>1829.</enum><header>Government-wide policy for procurement of unmanned aircraft systems</header> 
<subsection id="H964EC5C99D544C298E75EB25E606122E"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, in coordination with the Department of Homeland Security, Department of Transportation, the Department of Justice, and other Departments as determined by the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, and in consultation with the National Institute of Standards and Technology, shall establish a government-wide policy for the procurement of an unmanned aircraft system—</text> <paragraph id="H113B5DC8EA1344C4A7154B5FF5C94D12"><enum>(1)</enum><text>for non-Department of Defense and non-intelligence community operations; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8847121AD4374804B51D86EE53181603"><enum>(2)</enum><text>through grants and cooperative agreements entered into with non-Federal entities.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H142BEE4604AE41638EF9D8D49D880E62"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Information security</header><text>The policy developed under subsection (a) shall include the following specifications, which to the extent practicable, shall be based on industry standards and technical guidance from the National Institute of Standards and Technology, to address the risks associated with processing, storing, and transmitting Federal information in an unmanned aircraft system:</text> 
<paragraph id="H222BF79283534BA6AF533177793D3833"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Protections to ensure controlled access to an unmanned aircraft system.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA8E92BC2D5C54AAEA6C0F6283F8159D7"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Protecting software, firmware, and hardware by ensuring changes to an unmanned aircraft system are properly managed, including by ensuring an unmanned aircraft system can be updated using a secure, controlled, and configurable mechanism.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H24386BF3454B46919BAF9190E13E1B55"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Cryptographically securing sensitive collected, stored, and transmitted data, including proper handling of privacy data and other controlled unclassified information.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HEC8BF8E5EDE24E8EA1139EE60C8B2C12"><enum>(4)</enum><text>Appropriate safeguards necessary to protect sensitive information, including during and after use of an unmanned aircraft system.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H15F936C6285B403291D66F1BC20A01A5"><enum>(5)</enum><text>Appropriate data security to ensure that data is not transmitted to or stored in non-approved locations.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H3357ED496027416FB4372BEB9B4F8BBE"><enum>(6)</enum><text>The ability to opt out of the uploading, downloading, or transmitting of data that is not required by law or regulation and an ability to choose with whom and where information is shared when it is required.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HAFFBF34BDB7248A5B1A985457CBD4F75"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Requirement</header><text>The policy developed under subsection (a) shall reflect an appropriate risk-based approach to information security related to use of an unmanned aircraft system.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H7EF0FE0CE7064FB2B4BE8EBB2C0C3BF4"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Revision of acquisition regulations</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date on which the policy required under subsection (a) is issued—</text> 
<paragraph id="HF4FAD1E7952047A8BAABCBB6572641C5"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council shall revise the Federal Acquisition Regulation, as necessary, to implement the policy; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA17FE6642471445FAFA1C52B0833DF83"><enum>(2)</enum><text>any Federal department or agency or other Federal entity not subject to, or not subject solely to, the Federal Acquisition Regulation shall revise applicable policy, guidance, or regulations, as necessary, to implement the policy.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HAF61E86047604A448FF62856A9D58A51"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Exemption</header><text>In developing the policy required under subsection (a), the Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall—</text> <paragraph id="H1ED8805A57A147929FB0ABDAAB3E80DB"><enum>(1)</enum><text>incorporate policies to implement the exemptions contained in this subtitle; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5E5DE6857DA6410D998D64488DCA3187"><enum>(2)</enum><text>incorporate an exemption to the policy in the case of a head of the procuring department or agency determining, in writing, that no product that complies with the information security requirements described in subsection (b) is capable of fulfilling mission critical performance requirements, and such determination—</text> <subparagraph id="HDE063FA575A04ADAA6068386EE4A12B1"><enum>(A)</enum><text>may not be delegated below the level of the Deputy Secretary, or Administrator, of the procuring department or agency;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H8887D8596EE4488B92CEE6C2E07A8ADC"><enum>(B)</enum><text>shall specify—</text> <clause id="H0C6CCE5D5B0843D08F9B6F66F6A72D59"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the quantity of end items to which the waiver applies and the procurement value of those items; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HBC3825318C0F471F9840491F8701C2A8"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the time period over which the waiver applies, which shall not exceed three years;</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H041225E840584735B13C87A9F9066031"><enum>(C)</enum><text>shall be reported to the Office of Management and Budget following issuance of such a determination; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H1DE98F6739B34D31B22B86310C0657F4"><enum>(D)</enum><text>not later than 30 days after the date on which the determination is made, shall be provided to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H638AD54D27BB4762A21CC4774A6D5C2F" commented="no"><enum>1830.</enum><header>State, local, and territorial law enforcement and emergency service exemption</header> <subsection id="H948204FFFBA24E26AEE652A9A47986DC" commented="no"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text>Nothing in this subtitle shall prevent a State, local, or territorial law enforcement or emergency service agency from procuring or operating a covered unmanned aircraft system purchased with non-Federal dollars.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H0844630B62B448808F409072C8C65A76" commented="no"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Continuity of arrangements</header><text>The Federal Government may continue entering into contracts, grants, and cooperative agreements or other Federal funding instruments with State, local, or territorial law enforcement or emergency service agencies under which a covered unmanned aircraft system will be purchased or operated if the agency has received approval or waiver to purchase or operate a covered unmanned aircraft system pursuant to section 1825.</text></subsection></section> <section id="H67898D69C2714CD29AE8F16900297D6F"><enum>1831.</enum><header>Study</header> <subsection id="H0651A7B3AE5940EAB20C7128866840D0"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Study on the supply chain for unmanned aircraft systems and components</header> <paragraph id="H330B3468875D4A0A9765F2E45D8E86F0"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Report required</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall provide to the appropriate congressional committees a report on the supply chain for covered unmanned aircraft systems, including a discussion of current and projected future demand for covered unmanned aircraft systems.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA2152FF357694ECDAF6735D9495D496A"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The report under paragraph (1) shall include the following:</text> <subparagraph id="HA9BD0B9A39BE4ADC94D23D9FE30D106A"><enum>(A)</enum><text>A description of the current and future global and domestic market for covered unmanned aircraft systems that are not widely commercially available except from a covered foreign entity.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H84797DB0369344A99999253895263F6F"><enum>(B)</enum><text>A description of the sustainability, availability, cost, and quality of secure sources of covered unmanned aircraft systems domestically and from sources in allied and partner countries.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H05279066ECA24AE3A0D031243AFDF8E5"><enum>(C)</enum><text>The plan of the Secretary of Defense to address any gaps or deficiencies identified in subparagraph (B), including through the use of funds available under the Defense Production Act of 1950 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/4501">50 U.S.C. 4501 et seq.</external-xref>) and partnerships with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration and other interested persons.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H064BA80658A54A848AEF906DAC6B5AD3"><enum>(D)</enum><text>Such other information as the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment determines to be appropriate.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7A95B7C009A545B3A5390B29F013C06D"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Appropriate congressional committees defined</header><text>In this section, the term <quote>appropriate congressional committees</quote> means the following:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H3123F9ED96E440C4BA5EC370A8553E3A"><enum>(A)</enum><text>The Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9E7023B15A99450EBB1B0BDE4D515742"><enum>(B)</enum><text>The Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H9D24A7B182BD4E18A6500EEF51A57CD1"><enum>(C)</enum><text>The Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H99FCB487E1D94D8FA7F027A0BEFDE5B5"><enum>(D)</enum><text>The Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HD1B3000DDC9D46D5A8DAFEBB49A98836"><enum>(E)</enum><text>The Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3DD777679E5F4D2397F667F18904F5DB"><enum>(F)</enum><text>The Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H456D5BCBCF584A74AAB2E905033D7AAE"><enum>(G)</enum><text>The Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HE3832056B66243229CD468822DB8E9EC"><enum>1832.</enum><header>Exceptions</header> <subsection id="HCAE45754EA4A4F7390A9C265E86C34B5"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Exception for wildfire management operations and search and rescue operations</header><text>The appropriate Federal agencies, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security, are exempt from the procurement and operation restrictions under sections 1823, 1824, and 1825 to the extent the procurement or operation is necessary for the purpose of supporting the full range of wildfire management operations or search and rescue operations.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF346B3507DF64833BA79C85ABB0B1601"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Exception for intelligence activities</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Sections 1823, 1824, and 1825 shall not apply to any activity subject to the reporting requirements under title V of the National Security Act of 1947 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3091">50 U.S.C. 3091 et seq.</external-xref>), any authorized intelligence activities of the United States, or any activity or procurement that supports an authorized intelligence activity.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H2972C794510E4F5DAC2DFBE929B41E93"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Exception for tribal law enforcement or emergency service agency</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Tribal law enforcement or Tribal emergency service agencies, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security, are exempt from the procurement, operation, and purchase restrictions under sections 1823, 1824, and 1825 to the extent the procurement or operation is necessary for the purpose of supporting the full range of law enforcement operations or search and rescue operations on Indian lands.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H6E654CB7407647BD9BDAD33CA173C03D"><enum>1833.</enum><header>Sunset</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline"> Sections 1823, 1824, and 1825 shall cease to have effect on the date that is five years after the date of the enactment of this Act.</text></section></subtitle> <subtitle id="H1A23CAE7AEF84E5892B86D524B1A8234"><enum>C</enum><header>Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena</header> <section id="H80AE13348155422E8346D50258D46707"><enum>1841.</enum><header>Unidentified anomalous phenomena records collection at the National Archives and Records Administration</header> <subsection id="HB7F4BD81BDE84F77801C0F6972116B3A"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Records collection</header> <paragraph id="H39E481745A1343DA9E3AB4998C59ABED"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Establishment of collection</header> <subparagraph id="H88184A581DEB41E9AF98EB42DD44E7A1" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 60 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Archivist shall commence establishment of a collection of unidentified anomalous phenomena, as such term is defined in section 1673(n)(8) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/81">Public Law 117–81</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3373">50 U.S.C. 3373</external-xref>), records in the National Archives, to be known as the <quote>Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection</quote>.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H10C2D118DCAD458C81E497AE568A0AFB" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Physical integrity</header><text>In carrying out subparagraph (A), the Archivist shall ensure the physical integrity and original provenance (or if indeterminate, the earliest historical owner) of all records in the Collection.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HDA010F72F41445CC9723681EEE7043EC" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Record copies</header><text>The Collection shall consist of record copies of all Government, Government-provided, or Government-funded records relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena, technologies of unknown origin, and non-human intelligence (or equivalent subjects by any other name with the specific and sole exclusion of temporarily non-attributed objects), which shall be transmitted to the National Archives in accordance with section 2107 of title 44, United States Code.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H9930E9359EA54725B03643A21B879879" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(D)</enum><header>Subject guidebook</header><text>The Archivist shall prepare and publish a subject guidebook and index to the Collection.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9495B2419E5B4782872362ED6EA5F23E"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Contents</header><text>The Collection shall include the following:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H0EED6B93315944EA9925606AD0DC075E"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Copies of all unidentified anomalous phenomena records, regardless of age or date of creation—</text> <clause id="HAF4DB590A8F94F3DB9D355DDF01C9F46"><enum>(i)</enum><text>that have been transmitted to the National Archives or disclosed to the public in an unredacted form prior to the date of the enactment of this Act;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HD9C914743E3E4D26A17E5B6D92C1D3A5"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>that are otherwise required to have been transmitted to the National Archives after the date of the enactment of this Act; or </text></clause> <clause id="HFD08C520E13B4A478C2C246FD2BC77CE"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the disclosure of which is postponed under this subtitle.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4374303241C54385A8B79CE54A183ECC"><enum>(B)</enum><text>A central directory comprised of identification aids created for each record transmitted to the Archivist under section 1842(e).</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H069CF8ECE0D5428A8025107BE8BDF1C4"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Disclosure of records</header><text>Copies of all unidentified anomalous phenomena records transmitted to the National Archives for disclosure to the public shall—</text> 
<paragraph id="HAF1A5996ABC14A5C965B26E18867B81D"><enum>(1)</enum><text>be included in the Collection; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE11E06860F594985A401C8F4E337F8AA"><enum>(2)</enum><text>be available to the public—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H0389D443FEFC44F39864B17737B4D6AF"><enum>(A)</enum><text>for inspection and copying at the National Archives within 30 days after their transmission to the National Archives; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9E63242EC26149EBADE12E9EDA29812C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>digitally via the National Archives online database within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed 180 days thereafter.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H53309226B4E84B17927D839B2B597561"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Fees for copying</header> 
<paragraph id="H2D0D7FE8906648EEAA479589AFC764B1"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Archivist shall—</text> <subparagraph id="HAA1EB8E8F29E405E85D7C03677515F4E"><enum>(A)</enum><text>charge fees for copying unidentified anomalous phenomena records; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H9640B38AF02744C3B104DE51231ACC90"><enum>(B)</enum><text>grant waivers of such fees pursuant to the standards established by section 552(a)(4) of title 5, United States Code.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H717880318D6B49FE9B84181CBE4FB32A"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Amount of fees</header><text>The amount of a fee charged by the Archivist pursuant to paragraph (1)(A) for the copying of an unidentified anomalous phenomena record shall be such amount as the Archivist determines appropriate to cover the costs incurred by the National Archives in making and providing such copy, except that in no case may the amount of the fee charged exceed the actual expenses incurred by the National Archives in making and providing such copy.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H8DF4218EE3CC4802A77CE2191E9BCF54"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Additional requirements</header> 
<paragraph id="H3CEF50D50DB14F4E8A7F11B7D3575C28"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Use of funds</header><text>The Collection shall be preserved, protected, archived, digitized, and made available to the public at the National Archives and via the official National Archives online database using appropriations authorized, specified, and restricted for use under the terms of this subtitle.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA5FEC5195516431FAD2AD0C5D703A155"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Security of records</header><text>The National Security Program Office at the National Archives, in consultation with the National Archives Information Security Oversight Office, shall establish a program to ensure the security of the postponed unidentified anomalous phenomena records in the protected, and yet-to-be disclosed or classified portion of the Collection.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H63DA87A8AB7F40C99A9341DB23D9003D"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Oversight</header> 
<paragraph id="HB3ADD795356B4F77A6A14DB0FE689CBA"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Senate</header><text>The Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, the Committee on Armed Services, and the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate shall have continuing legislative oversight jurisdiction in the Senate with respect to the Collection.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H97EE95C0CF2E4E19B6DAC540F928EB6A"><enum>(2)</enum><header>House of Representatives</header><text>The Committee on Oversight and Accountability, the Committee on Armed Services, and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives shall have continuing legislative oversight jurisdiction in the House of Representatives with respect to the Collection.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="HC2FE0E110430469CAF99C32AB7C234A1"><enum>1842.</enum><header>Review, identification, transmission to the National Archives, and public disclosure of unidentified anomalous phenomena records by government offices</header> 
<subsection id="H4BDC9B1B94644371B2AD81965E002822"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Identification, organization, and preparation for transmission</header> 
<paragraph id="H1D247D0AB39F440A9AB793AA4FB921DF"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>As soon as practicable after the date of the enactment of this Act, each head of a Government office shall—</text> <subparagraph id="HE49C831773D4485E8D039377383471B0"><enum>(A)</enum><text>identify and organize records in the possession of the Government office or under the control of the Government office relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H400CE2DD762D4166B31F8ABC415C8184"><enum>(B)</enum><text>prepare such records for transmission to the Archivist for inclusion in the Collection.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H542D468002364B54A247855F6ED43A85"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Prohibitions</header> <subparagraph id="H4710741D82354B8681D20C3371063F81" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Destruction; alteration; mutilation</header><text>No unidentified anomalous phenomena record shall be destroyed, altered, or mutilated in any way.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H23CC9BC439A04E7382E44A68473819C2" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Withholding; redaction; postponement of disclosure; reclassification</header><text>No unidentified anomalous phenomena record made available or disclosed to the public prior to the date of the enactment of this Act may be withheld, redacted, postponed for public disclosure, or reclassified.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H78BFB5100F1A4536B20A012839CC29BE" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Records created by non-Federal persons or entities</header><text>No unidentified anomalous phenomena record created by a person or entity outside the Federal Government (excluding names or identities consistent with the requirements of section 1843) shall be withheld, redacted, postponed for public disclosure, or reclassified.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H6F93B9D83105418C8390DF695BB4F551"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Custody of unidentified anomalous phenomena records pending review</header><text>During the review by the heads of Government offices under subsection (c), each head of a Government office shall retain custody of the unidentified anomalous phenomena records of the office for purposes of preservation, security, and efficiency, unless it is a third agency record described in subsection (c)(2)(C).</text></subsection> <subsection id="HB024EEF9FE9F47BBB5C49072A079A241"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Review by heads of Government offices</header> <paragraph id="HFE69CDFB6A0348FC9D416DFE943AA888"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 300 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, each head of a Government office shall review, identify, and organize each unidentified anomalous phenomena record in the custody or possession of the office for—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HA35012825C8E4BC7AC19840793A3F09D"><enum>(A)</enum><text>disclosure to the public; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HA039F02B02F745E2853402F5256C3523"><enum>(B)</enum><text>transmission to the Archivist.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HAD6A39F3E8944210812349712C6A81BF"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Requirements</header><text>In carrying out paragraph (1), the head of a Government office shall—</text> <subparagraph id="HC219825A35F8498F8A49F47462712872"><enum>(A)</enum><text>determine which of the records of the office are unidentified anomalous phenomena records;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H1DEC821B58DD44A284BBFC537A333620"><enum>(B)</enum><text>determine which of the unidentified anomalous phenomena records of the office have been officially disclosed or made publicly available in a complete and unredacted form;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HDFBFDD87964441E09E51467172C22F77"><enum>(C)</enum> <clause id="HCB30904571AA495686908A01621BA18E" display-inline="yes-display-inline"><enum>(i)</enum><text>determine which of the unidentified anomalous phenomena records of the office, or particular information contained in such a record, was created by a third agency or by another Government office; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HBE74E71DAA92472EB94D3E2D3B9374B0" indent="up1"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>transmit to a third agency or other Government office those records, or particular information contained in those records, or complete and accurate copies thereof;</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H76EA048A3BD64C0085496E13EA495EF3"><enum>(D)</enum> <clause id="HFBEE32B486494E119874E698A3292FB0" display-inline="yes-display-inline"><enum>(i)</enum><text>determine whether the unidentified anomalous phenomena records of the office or particular information in unidentified anomalous phenomena records of the office are covered by the standards for postponement of public disclosure under this subtitle; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H506B30A896434414B879F1448DD63222" indent="up1"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>specify on the identification aid required by subsection (d) the applicable postponement provision contained in section 1841;</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H07D9202373DB42C2921F753F5B8C3FED"><enum>(E)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">organize and make available, upon request, to heads of Government offices other than the Government office with custody, including the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office, all relevant unidentified anomalous records identified under subparagraph (D);</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HCC878E71DD5F46529FBEAC7C4B3B517C"><enum>(F)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">organize and make available to the heads of Government offices other than the Government office with custody, including the All-domain Anomalous Resolution Office, for assistance with any record concerning which the office has any uncertainty as to whether the record is an unidentified anomalous phenomena record governed by this subtitle; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HEBA04A2E403B42F1A4CFE134393F3F50"><enum>(G)</enum><text>give precedence of work to—</text> 
<clause id="H3B015526031F4641AF32464EC66179AE"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the identification, review, and transmission of unidentified anomalous phenomena records not already publicly available or disclosed as of the date of the enactment of this Act;</text></clause> <clause id="H0A75960E85E440A597B0DA99A6CF44FA"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the identification, review, and transmission of all records that most unambiguously and definitively pertain to unidentified anomalous phenomena, technologies of unknown origin, and non-human intelligence;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HAAA166C0D2224751BB4862627E029A6C"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the identification, review, and transmission of unidentified anomalous phenomena records that on the date of the enactment of this Act are the subject of litigation under section 552 of title 5, United States Code; and</text></clause> <clause id="HD672EE75E4EE4854B59A03F24B804116"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>the identification, review, and transmission of unidentified anomalous phenomena records with earliest provenance when not inconsistent with clauses (i) through (iii) and otherwise feasible.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HDE8FF3B9301A49E68EACCA2DFD867E68"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Priority of expedited review for Directors of certain archival depositories</header><text>The Director of each archival depository established under section 2112 of title 44, United States Code, shall have as a priority the expedited review for public disclosure of unidentified anomalous phenomena records in the possession and custody of the depository, and shall make copies of such records available to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H7A3D6EEB4B1647D591F026AB9251DFCE"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Identification aids</header> <paragraph id="H5213886FF1FD4F278C532FFE2B892DFF"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header> <subparagraph id="HE2ECFA4569DE47DBAD008EB054D92BDD" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Preparation and availability</header><text>Not later than 45 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Archivist, in consultation with the heads of such Government offices as the Archivist considers appropriate, shall prepare and make available to all Government offices a standard form of identification, or finding aid, for use with each unidentified anomalous phenomena record subject to review under this subtitle whether in hardcopy (physical), softcopy (electronic), or digitized data format as may be appropriate.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF78656099BC04A8E9795ECBFA8AF3B5F" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Uniform system</header><text>The Archivist shall ensure that the identification aid program is established in such a manner as to result in the creation of a uniform system for cataloging and finding every unidentified anomalous phenomena record subject to review under this subtitle where ever and how ever stored in hardcopy (physical), softcopy (electronic), or digitized data format.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H66A5B4326F324C1DBE171860D79737E3"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Requirements for government offices</header><text>Upon completion of an identification aid using the standard form of identification prepared and made available under subparagraph (A) of paragraph (1) for the program established pursuant to subparagraph (B) of such paragraph, the head of a Government office shall—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H6A50EFF906B941A99E39352AC1107692"><enum>(A)</enum><text>attach a printed copy to each physical unidentified anomalous phenomena record, and an electronic copy to each softcopy or digitized data unidentified anomalous phenomena record, the identification aid describes; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H7EABC764D5C846E092E00F4FA77D627C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>attach a printed copy to each physical unidentified anomalous phenomena record, and an electronic copy to each softcopy or digitized data unidentified anomalous phenomena record the identification aid describes, when transmitted to the Archivist.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H6894F41A42C241A5A49A4D3B57D32E3F"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Records of the national archives that are publicly available</header><text>Unidentified anomalous phenomena records which are in the possession of the National Archives on the date of the enactment of this Act, and which have been publicly available in their entirety without redaction, shall be made available in the Collection without any additional review by another authorized office under this subtitle, and shall not be required to have such an identification aid unless required by the Archivist.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HF66CA5AC35F9451CAE8EEC29B6FAEB28"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Transmission to the National Archives</header><text>Each head of a Government office shall—</text> 
<paragraph id="H59744B7DD8BA4DCFB9CC1A54FB5B9CCA"><enum>(1)</enum><text>transmit to the Archivist, and, as soon as possible, make available to the public, all unidentified anomalous phenomena records of the Government office that can be publicly disclosed, including those that are publicly available on the date of the enactment of this Act, without any redaction, adjustment, or withholding under the standards of this subtitle; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2173981E1786477EAACCBB8711F0E3CA"><enum>(2)</enum><text>transmit to the Archivist upon approval for postponement by the original classification authority upon completion of other action authorized by this subtitle, all unidentified anomalous phenomena records of the Government office the public disclosure of which has been postponed, in whole or in part, under the standards of this subtitle, to become part of the protected, yet-to-be disclosed, or classified portion of the Collection.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H312DA0150E2348E0A3DAE323D9AE4B2B"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Custody of postponed unidentified anomalous phenomena records</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An unidentified anomalous phenomena record the public disclosure of which has been postponed shall, pending transmission to the Archivist, be held for reasons of security and preservation by the originating body until such time as the information security program has been established at the National Archives as required in section 1841(d)(2).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H9AC8F90A455C4D06AF8C52B7AEDDAE45"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Periodic review of postponed unidentified anomalous phenomena records</header> <paragraph id="H219787C15EFE4F11BACA1B660D5DE0D2"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>All postponed or redacted records shall be reviewed periodically by the originating agency and the Archivist.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HEB7CF8D3F6B14C0D9EBD7D91D52E8C3C"><enum>.(2)</enum><header>Requirements</header> 
<subparagraph id="H66AC25E01CFD48F6BCC88F5925CFED96" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Public disclosure</header><text>A periodic review under paragraph (1) shall address the public disclosure of additional unidentified anomalous phenomena records in the Collection under the standards of this subtitle.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H6B78507795B84A60AAC93CB72DBA55B3" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Unclassified written description of reason</header><text>All postponed unidentified anomalous phenomena records determined to require continued postponement shall require an unclassified written description of the reason for such continued postponement relevant to these specific records. Such description shall be provided to the Archivist and published in the Federal Register upon determination.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC1F7EC5EBB524CB9B004920ABEE472A7" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Periodic review; downgrading and desclassification of information</header><text>The Archivist shall establish requirements for periodic review of postponed unidentified anomalous phenomena records that shall serve to downgrade and declassify information.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2D6D4F32287742AB89F01FBD3E145440" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(D)</enum><header>Deadline for full disclosure</header><text>Each unidentified anomalous phenomena record shall be publicly disclosed in full, and available in the Collection, not later than the date that is 25 years after the date of the first creation of the record by the originating body, unless the President certifies that—</text> 
<clause id="HEB0EC10F304A412C9D668A976FD2643D"><enum>(i)</enum><text>continued postponement is made necessary by an identifiable harm to the military defense, intelligence operations, law enforcement, or conduct of foreign relations; and</text></clause> <clause id="H87A2493B6C724520916DB188BCBC5767"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the identifiable harm is of such gravity that it outweighs the public interest in disclosure.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA573832C60B545E0AEDCB16059A97B76"><enum>(h)</enum><header>Requirements for Executive agencies</header> 
<paragraph id="HB3907B1755F94961BF5D606B26F61F55"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The heads of Executive agencies shall—</text> <subparagraph id="HCFB9DAC32D194C98B74B4E7D4F56EA9B"><enum>(A)</enum><text>transmit digital records electronically in accordance with section 2107 of title 44, United States Code;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HB580A88DD4EC4344B42454BA2468DAFD"><enum>(B)</enum><text>charge fees for copying unidentified anomalous phenomena records; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H587F40E06E8749DDADC9D8E86C4B945C"><enum>(C)</enum><text>grant waivers of such fees pursuant to the standards established by section 552(a)(4) of title 5, United States Code.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2018B6D9C5A74084B493C3A14D4948B6"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Amount of fees</header><text>The amount of a fee charged by the head of an Executive agency pursuant to paragraph (1)(B) for the copying of an unidentified anomalous phenomena record shall be such amount as the head determines appropriate to cover the costs incurred by the Executive agency in making and providing such copy, except that in no case may the amount of the fee charged exceed the actual expenses incurred by the Executive agency in making and providing such copy.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HDE98F54BD83F482DB3FE52CDF3B1067D"><enum>1843.</enum><header>Grounds for postponement of public disclosure of unidentified anomalous phenomena records</header> <subsection id="H3CBE5FA820B34D499CB0E4B8548A4BDF"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Postponement determination</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In addition to the relevant authorities in Executive Order 13526, disclosure of unidentified anomalous phenomena records or particular information in unidentified anomalous phenomena records to the public may be postponed subject to the limitations of this subtitle if the original classification authority makes a determination that there is clear and convincing evidence that—</text> 
<paragraph id="H519CC62F06774A279B3DF20D5ABA21F5"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the threat to the military defense, intelligence operations, or conduct of foreign relations of the United States posed by the public disclosure of the unidentified anomalous phenomena record is of such gravity that it outweighs the public interest in disclosure, and such public disclosure would reveal—</text> <subparagraph id="H09F9CD4495B44DC2A14694855CBCE7E5"><enum>(A)</enum><text>an intelligence agent whose identity currently requires protection;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HB8036CB225174FFCBC583F11A7EE2673"><enum>(B)</enum><text>an intelligence source or method which is currently utilized, or reasonably expected to be utilized, by the Federal Government and which has not been officially disclosed, the disclosure of which would interfere with the conduct of intelligence activities; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H55DE26B447B64EF4912ADA7C3E034A80"><enum>(C)</enum><text>any other matter currently relating to the military defense, intelligence operations, or conduct of foreign relations of the United States, the disclosure of which would demonstrably and substantially impair the national security of the United States;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H573486A2C11D435892649CC95AE9B320"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the public disclosure of the unidentified anomalous phenomena record would violate section 552a of title 5, United States Code (referred to as the <quote>Privacy Act of 1974</quote>);</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HD178F68E34EA4367A48A0C7CC7B33883"><enum>(3)</enum><text>the public disclosure of the unidentified anomalous phenomena record could reasonably be expected to constitute an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy, and that invasion of privacy is so substantial that it outweighs the public interest; or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8D7EC64E71634D55815D0D4675F0E329"><enum>(4)</enum><text>the public disclosure of the unidentified anomalous phenomena record would compromise the existence of an understanding of confidentiality currently requiring protection between a Federal Government agent and a cooperating individual or a foreign government, and public disclosure would be so harmful that it outweighs the public interest.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H0436B442E8794F2CB2966C120CDB1665" commented="no"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Withdrawal of records</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Senior Agency Officials designated in accordance with Executive Order 13526 or any successor Orders may withdraw records in the Collection that are determined to be both not related to unidentified anomalous phenomena and properly classified. The Senior Agency Official must notify the congressional leadership and the oversight committees of Congress, as identified in section 1841(e), by not later than 60 days before each record is withdrawn.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HBF5269D506294347B78D8E0EE5D709EA" commented="no"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Congressional notification of postponement of disclosure</header><text>In the event that the disclosure of unidentified anomalous phenomena records or particular information in unidentified anomalous phenomena records to the public is postponed by an Executive agency, the head of the Executive agency shall notify congressional leadership and the oversight committees of Congress, as identified in section 1841(e), within 15 days of such decision with a reason for the postponement of disclosure.</text></subsection></section></subtitle> <subtitle id="H79A87FCB30C446CB951894468F9B7180"><enum>D</enum><header>World Trade Center Health Program</header> <section commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H81C2D6279592493686A2DDD92C809255"><enum>1851.</enum><header>Flexibility and funding for the World Trade Center Health Program</header> <subsection id="HD85DC443E1624F808560A1A68047984B"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Department of Defense, Armed Forces, or other Federal worker responders to the September 11 attacks at the Pentagon and Shanksville, Pennsylvania</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Title XXXIII of the Public Health Service Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/300mm">42 U.S.C. 300mm et seq.</external-xref>) is amended—</text>

<section id="H39E8675F372341B7BF37D059F3FAC6D3" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>2611.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Authority to conduct restoration and modernization projects at the First City Troop Readiness Center in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania</header> 
<subsection id="HEA827A5C8CF7420398E163D962097079"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Subject to the conditions described in subsection (b), the Chief of the National Guard Bureau may only obligate or expend amounts available to the Army National Guard for Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization, or award a contract, to conduct restoration and modernization projects at the First City Troop Readiness Center in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. </text></subsection> <subsection id="H0E6ACCE536764414A330FF5490017C96"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Conditions</header><text>The conditions described in this subsection are the following:</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H71CE1DDC048C491893EF81816D8DC042"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">As of the date on which the Chief awards a contract under subsection (a), any lease held by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania for the First City Troop Readiness Center has a term sufficient to allow a project described in subsection (a) to realize the applicable full lifecycle benefit.</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HE5FC2B81BDFC478A8923A01BB5CDC440"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Federal contribution for such a project does not exceed 50 percent of the total cost of the project.</text></paragraph>

<section id="H0CC3E342A6634457B8F12CC089888CE1" section-type="subsequent-section" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>2805.</enum><header>Authority for certain construction projects in friendly foreign countries</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Subchapter I of <external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/10/169">chapter 169</external-xref> of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new section:</text> <quoted-block style="USC" id="H1C81D439A3924A7D96579750E930AE42" display-inline="no-display-inline"> <section id="H71826DA9B0D34B6F9371D9E83FD2BCEE"><enum>2817.</enum><header>Authority for certain construction projects in friendly foreign countries</header> <subsection id="H18CE51605D21473B947E03080B24E974"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Construction authorized</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Using funds available for operations and maintenance, the Secretary of Defense may carry out a construction project in a friendly foreign country, and perform planning and design to support such a project, that the Secretary determines meets each of the following conditions:</text> 
<paragraph id="H3AB5819773554471BF31CE715788C7E1"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The commander of the geographic combatant command in which the construction project will be carried out identified the construction project as necessary to support vital United States military requirements at an air port of debarkation, sea port of debarkation, or rail or other logistics support location.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H8234C8E6B44D43E7A29D70481753B4E1"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The construction project will not be carried out at a military installation.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF20F16BE903741528757DCB50CD7D1C5"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The funds made available under the authority of this section for the construction project—</text> <subparagraph id="H27010D63601B442EA83E745BC88A19EF"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">will be sufficient to—</text> 
<clause id="HDA2DA0016BFA4893BE5F932A985FD39B" commented="no"><enum>(i)</enum><text>construct a complete and usable facility or make an improvement to a facility; or</text></clause> <clause id="HB2F092B4ED2F44629BDA352CB7FDC7BB"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>complete the repair of an existing facility or improvement to a facility; and</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H2ADE80C2F48C459C800C216A25030191"><enum>(B)</enum><text>will not require additional funds from other Department of Defense accounts.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H544E7B8299734A5D8F66254453764BE0"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The level of construction for the construction project may not exceed the minimum necessary to meet the military requirements identified under paragraph (1).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H4494C16EFA584AD887CF45911FE18BCB"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Deferral of the construction project pending inclusion of the construction project proposal in the national defense authorization Act for a subsequent fiscal year is inconsistent with the military requirements identified under paragraph (1) and other national security or national interests of the United States.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H229046E8356E4661ADAC36F32A427D4F"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Congressional notification</header> <paragraph id="H1145D76BEC8E4CF482C5BBCF15CFC1DE"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Notification required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Upon determining to carry out a construction project under this section that has an estimated cost in excess of the amounts authorized for unspecified minor military construction projects under section 2805(c) of this title, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the specified congressional committees a notification of such determination. </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H38615AD648714E3280E3051604224C52"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The notification required by paragraph (1) shall include the following:</text> <subparagraph id="H2BE21E8E25C746989D1321DA3B8F9E68"><enum>(A)</enum><text>A certification that the conditions specified in subsection (a) are satisfied with regard to the construction project.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H41B956653F77466F981A779BE261C499"><enum>(B)</enum><text>A justification for such project.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE8D6672415C44D85B90C366695757DE7"><enum>(C)</enum><text>An estimate of the cost of such project.</text></subparagraph></paragraph>

<section id="HB7D182E3619C45198B0548910F1F058D" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>2834.</enum><header>Certification of habitability of covered military unaccompanied housing</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 2856b of title 10, United States Code (as added by section 2832) is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:</text> <quoted-block style="USC" id="H81E5ED7A1DF148A4879069A00C732B47" display-inline="no-display-inline"> <subsection id="HD4BBE480CB1C489D9280CF1A518CB3EE"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Certification</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall include, in conjunction with the submission of the budget of the President to Congress pursuant to section 1105 of title 31, a certification from each Secretary of a military department to the congressional defense committees that the cost for all needed repairs and improvements for each occupied covered military unaccompanied housing facility under the jurisdiction of such Secretary does not exceed 20 percent of the replacement cost of such facility, as mandated by Department of Defense Manual 4165.63 titled <quote>DoD Housing Management</quote> and dated October 28, 2010 (or a successor document).</text></subsection><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section> 
<section id="H3E4CB9C00E6D4607A608B17EB847D30A" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>2835.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Pilot program for military construction projects to replace certain covered military unaccompanied housing facilities</header> 
<subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H72F72AC18B664BB5A37D31A121B7DD1D"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Each Secretary of a military department may carry out a pilot program under which each such Secretary administers a military construction project, not otherwise authorized by law, to replace a covered military unaccompanied housing facility—</text> <paragraph id="H2A05A2E125434A9F8CD4990D6A0A89F7"><enum>(1)</enum><text>that such Secretary determines is not in compliance with the uniform standards for covered military unaccompanied housing under section 2856b of title 10, United States Code (as added by section 2832); and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H77AB394BFB9C4F689B8915E94A6353F3"><enum>(2)</enum><text>for which the total cost of a repair project to bring such covered military unaccompanied facility into compliance with such uniform standards exceeds 75 percent of the total cost of such a military construction project.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H8E5EC59F48C149F6BBC44AAB78C1352B" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Facility requirements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A facility constructed pursuant to a military construction project under a pilot program under subsection (a)—</text> 
<paragraph id="H8D9C8433A3454A9D969399CF071D88E1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">with respect to the covered military unaccompanied housing facility such facility replaces—</text> <subparagraph id="H2106FA175D144D4697417F764A90C77E"><enum>(A)</enum><text>may not have a capacity to house more members of the Armed Forces;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HBAE9E9E59E984365BAEDFFA977ED76F6" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">shall be designed and utilized for the same purpose; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H5973F4B892394AA5BF9876E2A9EFB47E" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">shall be located on the same military installation; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H7B5D8337EB7943BEB604CEAF436AA677" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">shall be designed to meet, at a minimum, standards for construction, utilization, and force protection. </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HB196702F7E1A49CBB32209A533A47524"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Nondelegation</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">For the purposes of carrying out a military construction project under a pilot program under subsection (a), the authority of a Secretary of a military department to determine whether a covered military unaccompanied housing facility is in substandard condition may not be delegated.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H1D84FB8D938A4E09840B1A55964AE0D4" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(d)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Source of funds</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A Secretary of a military department may spend amounts available to such Secretary for operation and maintenance or unspecified military construction to carry out this section.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H127F5B5CB23D4609BF6582D135F52DAC" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(e)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Congressional notification</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">With respect to a military construction project proposed to be carried out under a pilot program under subsection (a) with an estimated cost in excess of $10,000,000, the Secretary of the military department concerned shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report that includes—</text> 
<paragraph id="H6877776756A9404FA433B7951DD5D6A7" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a justification for such military construction project;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H575505C09F2C413E8EAA7890A1C326E9"><enum>(2)</enum><text>an estimate of the total cost of such military construction project; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1103972054FB49C0900DF64D5E08171C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a description of the elements of military construction, including the elements specified in section 2802(b) of title 10, United States Code, incorporated into such military construction project.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H0671F88654344F6ABDEC219299D68E4A" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(f)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Sunset</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The authority to carry out a pilot program pursuant to subsection (a) shall terminate on the date that is five years after the date of the enactment of this Act.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HFA8D19A67F874F9FAB07F15DA80712A3" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(g)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section:</text> <paragraph id="HA92F018CF00E42CFA07DF544F5B62EC3" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>appropriate committees of Congress</term> has the meaning given such term in section 2801 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph>
