<section id="H2B2604ABED454A70BDCF8258F25F8D23"><enum>2841.</enum><header>Elimination of flexibilities for construction standards for covered military unaccompanied housing</header> 
<subsection id="H188AA5021EA54208BC185F3C54168FAA"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense and each Secretary of a military department shall modify all directives, instructions, manuals, regulations, policies, and other guidance and issuances of the Department of Defense or appropriate military department to eliminate the grant of any flexibilities to the standards for construction of new covered military unaccompanied housing.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HAF28F474266E49519BF45A068946BFA8"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Matters included</header><text>The requirement under subsection (a) shall include modifications that remove the flexibility provided to the military departments with respect to new construction standards for covered military unaccompanied housing, including modification of the Department of Defense Manual 4165.63 titled <quote>DoD Housing Management</quote> and dated October 28, 2010 (or a successor document).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA1888EE223E0402A9291A0F290E9FF37"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Covered military unaccompanied housing defined</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section, the term <quote>covered military unaccompanied housing</quote> has the meaning given in section 2856 of title 10, United States Code (as amended by section 2831).</text></subsection></section></subtitle> <subtitle id="H43426DB942224EC6BF11D7A2E91DA3AE"><enum>D</enum><header>Real Property and Facilities Administration</header> <section id="HF0FDF38AAF04400EAEF32E1604E103A0"><enum>2851.</enum><header>Guidance on Department of Defense-wide standards for access to military installations</header> <subsection id="H4243C9B931B74F1BA936CC89B7C22D4A"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Interim guidance</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 30 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall issue interim guidance to the appropriate official or officials within the Department of Defense for purposes of establishing final standards of the Department of Defense for determining the fitness of individuals for access to military installations, which shall include modifying volume 3 of the Department of Defense Manual 5200.08 titled <quote>Physical Security Program: Access to DoD Installations</quote> (dated January 2, 2019) or any comparable or successor policy guidance document.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H4E40FBE9E374449A9B1D56050C155F21"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Final guidance</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall issue final guidance relating to the standards described in subsection (a).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H18915C42EFDA4C7D9B78235A3B116516"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Briefing</header><text>Not later than 60 days after issuing the interim guidance required under subsection (a), the Secretary of Defense shall brief the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives on such guidance, which shall include a timeline for the issuance of such final guidance.</text></subsection></section>

<paragraph id="H256E596E90F74BD9A2C299EE36E1B1EA"><enum>(1)</enum><text>have not been privatized or transferred pursuant to a conveyance under section 2688 of title 10, United States Code; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H18C17209E817497C88D32731BEF87B67"><enum>(2)</enum><text>are located on a military installation (as defined in section 2801 of such title).</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HB478B4E5EBDD4C63855D59A154E52865"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Report</header> 
<paragraph id="H0BADCDBE347145EBA8C166ADF1D91CB6"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Beginning on February 1 of the year immediately following the date on which the plan under subsection (a) is submitted, and annually thereafter, the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with each Secretary of a military department, shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a consolidated report on the condition of critical infrastructure systems owned by the Federal Government located at military installations.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDAA3528055EB49E2B74EDC42A30C50D0"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>Each report required by paragraph (1) shall include the following:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H7D5BF12067024E18BB0EF98A09699679"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Installation-level data for each critical infrastructure system described in paragraph (1) that includes the following for each such system:</text> <clause id="H97820EBDF319480E89D72E7261658D8B"><enum>(i)</enum><text>For the five-year period preceding the date of submission of the report, all instances of noncompliance of such system with any applicable Federal or State law or regulation, including information on any prior or current consent order or equivalent compliance agreement with any Federal or State regulatory agency.</text></clause> 
<clause id="H1771D25AD14D4A5B80654117CB5BA7A1"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>The year of original installation of critical infrastructure system components, including treatment facilities, pump stations, and storage tanks.</text></clause> <clause id="HD3F91A34B28346F8B05CCB8625153574"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>The average age of distribution system piping and wiring.</text></clause> 
<clause id="H00A4E21D832E4EEAA71A8BCC4D3E9EF2"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>The rate of system recapitalization, represented as an annual percentage replacement rate of all critical infrastructure system assets.</text></clause> <clause id="HE3DEA52C28CC4009A7B80D5BF6B7C66D"><enum>(v)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">For the one-year period preceding the date of submission of the report, the percentage of key system operational components (including fire hydrants, valves, and backflow preventors) inspected and determined through testing to be fully operational.</text></clause> 
<clause id="HA6C505AA2F1F42E4921B821A7552EF14"><enum>(vi)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">For the one-year period preceding the date of submission of the report, the absolute number, and a normalized measure for comparative purposes, of all unplanned system outages.</text></clause> <clause id="HDFF0CB873AD34EF2A9D72F28FC2B9E55"><enum>(vii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">For the one-year period preceding the date of submission of the report, the absolute duration, and a normalized measure for comparative purposes, of all unplanned system outages.</text></clause> 
<clause id="H48D070E67C75478BB00D40D03C12853E"><enum>(viii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">For the one-year period preceding the date of submission of the report, the absolute number, and a normalized measure for comparative purposes, of all critical infrastructure system main breaks and leaks.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H189D3FD7B86F413EBEC0AF09FB8A4DEF"><enum>(B)</enum><text>A standardized risk assessment for each military installation, identifying the current and projected level of risk related to the following:</text> 
<clause id="HEDC70B2646604948A77BBEC1E30C345E"><enum>(i)</enum><text>The ability to maintain compliance with applicable current and proposed State regulations and standards and applicable regulations and policies of the Department of Defense and the military departments related to each critical infrastructure system described in paragraph (1), and the ability to operate critical infrastructure systems in accordance with accepted industry standards.</text></clause> <clause id="H1452C1F7626E46D09D514B1C8F40B050"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>The ability to maintain a consistent and compliant supply of water for current and projected future installation needs based on current and projected source water availability and quality, including an assessment of source water contamination risks for each critical infrastructure system described in paragraph (1).</text></clause> 
<clause id="H145D3E7071794C06B507966D12ADE2A3"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The ability of each critical infrastructure system described in paragraph (1) to withstand severe weather events, including drought, flooding, and temperature fluctuations.</text></clause> <clause id="H50F33C2FC33C4ADD960578B9F3D8A674"><enum>(iv)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The ability for utility industrial controls systems for each critical infrastructure system described in paragraph (1) to maintain compliance with applicable current and proposed cybersecurity standards and regulations.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA2EE240E636F457EBCD207FE0CAD39F1"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Form</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A report under this subsection shall be submitted in an unclassified form but may contain a classified annex.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H57761C5ED2EE42C5A8D094702FE96459"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Critical infrastructure system defined</header><text>In this section, the term <quote>critical infrastructure system</quote> includes a transportation infrastructure system and a utilities infrastructure system.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="HF07972685806484D9A52E56320D56F13"><enum>2854.</enum><header>Closure and disposal of the Pueblo Chemical Depot, Pueblo County, Colorado</header> 
<subsection id="H7F5EBE53EE04446E96A3A1490FD23D68"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of the Army shall close Pueblo Chemical Depot in Pueblo County, Colorado (in this section referred to as the <quote>Depot</quote>), not later than one year after the completion of the chemical demilitarization mission in such location in accordance with the Chemical Weapons Convention Treaty.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H98C048DC282F4D7F98B3E026F2A1D6CC"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Procedures</header><text>The Secretary of the Army shall carry out the closure and subsequent related property management and disposal of the Depot, including the land, buildings, structures, infrastructure, and associated equipment, installed equipment, material, and personal property that comprise the Chemical Agent-Destruction Pilot Plant, in accordance with the procedures and authorities for the closure, management, and disposal of property under the appropriate base closure laws (as defined in section 101 of title 10, United States Code).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HD7F70565E2614703A6947CA72447021E"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Office of local defense community cooperation activities</header><text>The Office of Local Defense Community Cooperation of the Department of Defense may make grants and supplement other Federal funds pursuant to section 2391 of title 10, United States Code, to support closure and reuse activities of the Depot.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H4FB356831B2342F0B0D74ED81D94755D"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Treatment of existing permits</header><text>Nothing in this section shall be construed to prevent the removal or demolition by the Program Executive Office, Assembled Chemical Weapons Alternatives of the Department of the Army of existing buildings, structures, infrastructure, and associated equipment, installed equipment, material, and personal property of the Chemical Agent-Destruction Pilot Plant at the Depot in accordance with the existing Hazardous Waste Permit Number CO-20-09-02-01 under the Solid Waste Disposal Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/6901">42 U.S.C. 6901 et seq.</external-xref>) (commonly known as the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act of 1976) issued by the State of Colorado, or any associated or follow-on permits under such Act.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H7F108FEE40F148AFBD946415C99720E3" commented="no"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Relation to procedures for use to assist the homeless</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Such land, buildings, structures, infrastructure, and associated equipment, installed equipment, material, and personal property comprising the Chemical Agent-Destruction Pilot Plant at the Depot is—</text> <paragraph id="H5BE9005E057848BA9F60D8117AC1D9EF" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text>hereby deemed unsuitable for use to assist the homeless; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC05249F3155E484CB0C49208E7D6F300" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">not subject to the procedures relating to the use to assist the homeless of buildings and property at military installations under the Defense Base Closure and Realignment Act of 1990 (part A of title XXIX of <external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/101/510">Public Law 101–510</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/2687">10 U.S.C. 2687</external-xref> note).</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H89D84124BDD144A393C0626CEB11EE80"><enum>2855.</enum><header>Limitation on authority to modify or restrict public access to Greenbury Point Conservation Area at Naval Support Activity Annapolis, Maryland</header> <subsection id="H169FF815EE084B258545A3ED4981ABDE"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Except as provided in subsection (b), the Secretary of the Navy may not modify or restrict public access to the Greenbury Point Conservation Area at Naval Support Activity Annapolis, Maryland.</text></subsection>

<subsection id="HFB5A2C58CB1E41728EF8909D74C3BD89"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall—</text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H0657F6BBABBC4A8FBF816A9BBA9CE08E"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">update Department of Defense Instruction 4165.70 (relating to real property management) and Unified Facilities Criteria 2–100–01 (relating to installation master planning) to—</text>

<subparagraph id="H91304947A7674A759306AD65FAA6CA2D" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">define the 17 identified military installation resilience hazards to ensure that the impacts from such hazards are reported consistently across the Department;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H665D50110C2D46D2A97BB968519776CE" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">require each commander of a military installation to address the rationale for determining that any such hazard is not applicable to the military installation concerned;</text></subparagraph>

<section id="H22C2F2FBA2074F34A98DF5510D44A594"><enum>2873.</enum><header>Pilot program to provide air purification technology in covered military housing</header> 
<subsection id="HE6B0C0814673419D8D26286643D3F473"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of Defense may carry out a pilot program to—</text> <paragraph id="H2C89BCA4A5244FF69516297A814C8A27"><enum>(1)</enum><text>provide commercially available off-the-shelf items (as defined in section 104 of title 41, United States Code) for air purification and covered sensors to landlords; and</text></paragraph>

<paragraph id="HCCBE03C2239A4DB8AAEA00F4913025F1"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Considerations</header><text>Each Secretary shall ensure that the military installation selected under this section contains military unaccompanied housing in which the items described in subsection (a) may be used.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HD4D9724B1A454E49AC53925D28FD38C9"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Devices</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An air purification item or a covered sensor provided under this section shall use technology proven to reduce indoor air risks and yield measurable environmental health and public health outcomes.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H33BC7A4C63974A738E4EBC92FC4AB313"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Briefing</header><text>Not later than 365 days after the date on which a pilot program is commenced under this section, the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Secretary of the Air Force shall each provide to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate a briefing on the pilot program established under this section, including a description of the items described in subsection (a) used under such program. <subparagraph id="H2BF6B9293FB140CCA1172697B4EA20AA"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">extending the durability and habitability of covered military housing; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HBEB3B3BDFDAF4FFDB553E7A1882BB6E5"><enum>(B)</enum><text>reducing maintenance frequency; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H70FEE6108F6141158B585D83F25E08DD"><enum>(2)</enum><text>with respect to cost savings identified in paragraph (1), a plan to expand the use of covered sensors and air purification items in newly constructed covered military housing.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H66FF335D26514DD082BDC914178ACD1D"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text>

<section id="H0BCDF465005B4F1CB4D9620ACD5E93AE"><enum>2882.</enum><header>Development and operation of Marine Corps Heritage Center and National Museum of the Marine Corps</header> 
<subsection id="HCC8FC90083F34B569448F46E752D492A"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text><external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/10/861">Chapter 861</external-xref> of title 10, United States Code, is amended by inserting after <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/8617">section 8617</external-xref> the following new section:</text> <quoted-block id="HD1636FA763254F0A8FB1EEFB3610AA19" style="USC"> <section id="H2C0254CF86F447AF83C73DB25F5A69E3"><enum>8618.</enum><header>Marine Corps Heritage Center and National Museum of the Marine Corps at Marine Corps Base, Quantico, Virginia</header> <subsection id="HDAC9795AFEB34C27B667853F21A72D7B"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Joint venture for development and continued maintenance and operation</header><text>The Secretary of the Navy may enter into a joint venture with the Marine Corps Heritage Foundation (in this section referred to as the <quote>Foundation</quote>), a not-for-profit entity, for the design, construction, and maintenance and operation of a multipurpose facility to be used for historical displays for public viewing, curation, and storage of artifacts, research facilities, classrooms, offices, and associated activities consistent with the mission of the Marine Corps University. The facility shall be known as the Marine Corps Heritage Center and the National Museum of the Marine Corps.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HB391F444B99244AEA6977541D74422DB"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Design and construction</header><text>For each phase of development of the facility described in subsection (a), the Secretary may—</text> <paragraph id="H409D49238FFE4AA093A96E82DCDB66C6"><enum>(1)</enum><text>permit the Foundation to contract for the design, construction, or both of such phase of development; or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H16F47D3D1A4A4E6BA4E9DF65DDA189F5"><enum>(2)</enum><text>accept funds from the Foundation for the design, construction, or both of such phase of development.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H7DF7BCC8A64E493CA4136E460244A9E6"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Acceptance authority</header><text>Upon completion of construction of any phase of development of the facility described in subsection (a) by the Foundation to the satisfaction of the Secretary, and the satisfaction of any financial obligations incident thereto by the Foundation, the facility shall become the real property of the Department of the Navy with all right, title, and interest in and to facility being in the United States.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H11D1B812F5D74237B0C7DD91450DD752"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Maintenance, operation, and support</header> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="yes-display-inline" id="H392496F9DDF44E8D9F8B8F4CDFF6840F"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The Secretary may, for the purpose of maintenance and operation of the Marine Corps Heritage Center and the National Museum of the Marine Corps—</text> <subparagraph id="H8EB9FA012BCD462285609181703D8811" indent="up1"><enum>(A)</enum><text>enter into contracts or cooperative agreements, on a sole-source basis, with the Foundation for the procurement of property or services for the direct benefit or use of the Marine Corps Heritage Center and the National Museum of the Marine Corps; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF128760573C348CC84DCBB9BF0CF8D86" indent="up1"><enum>(B)</enum><text>notwithstanding the requirements of subsection (h) of section 2667 of this title and under such terms and conditions as the Secretary considers appropriate for the joint venture authorized by subsection (a), lease in accordance with such section 2667 portions of the facility developed under subsection (a) to the Foundation for use in generating revenue for activities of the facility and for such administrative purposes as may be necessary for support of the facility.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7ED971F5AC1B459DA8E957BCB3522043" indent="up1"><enum>(2)</enum><text>In making a determination of fair market value under section 2667(b)(4) of this title for payment of consideration pursuant to a lease described in paragraph (1)(B), the Secretary may consider the entirety of the educational efforts of the Foundation, support to the Marine Corps Heritage Center history division by the Foundation, or the funding of museum programs and exhibits by the Foundation, or other support related to the Marine Corps Heritage Center and the National Museum of the Marine Corps, in addition to the types of in-kind consideration provided under section 2667(c) of this title.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8AA61EFFA6F94BDDB3CB4A3B83353E30" indent="up1"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The Secretary may authorize the Foundation to use real or personal property within the Marine Corps Heritage Center and National Museum of the Marine Corps to conduct additional revenue-generating activities, as the Secretary considers appropriate considering the work of the Foundation and needs of the Marine Corps Heritage Center and National Museum of the Marine Corps. The Secretary shall only authorize the use of such property for a revenue-generating activity if the Secretary determines the activity will not interfere with military activities and personnel or the activities of the Marine Corps Heritage Center and National Museum of the Marine Corps.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC44F0CD1C8C245F39CA799FD76C7747F" indent="up1"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The Secretary shall retain lease payments received under this section, other than in-kind consideration authorized under paragraph (2) or under section 2667(c) of this title, solely for use in support of the Marine Corps Heritage Center and the National Museum of the Marine Corps, and funds received as lease payments shall remain available until expended.</text></paragraph></subsection>

<section id="H9923C38B91444FB0A840B25387576E2E" section-type="subsequent-section" commented="no"><enum>2887.</enum><header>Guidance on encroachment that affects covered sites</header> 
<subsection id="H4B8BFC62B27A40B3ADAA4BB730A50E91" commented="no"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Guidance required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, each Secretary of a military department shall issue guidance to establish—</text> <paragraph id="H50C2EBA0899444F296FC093BAB423C1F" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text>a process to identify encroachment with respect to a covered site;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE781E909E8B44EE8BC1F07070C2ECBAE" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><text>a method to mitigate such encroachment; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H716CDB33679A4421820B973B9896B7E2" commented="no"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a procedure to certify that such encroachment does not directly result in a national security risk to the covered site.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA267B50D68D8421A94059EE27C87D76A" commented="no"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Considerations</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In developing the guidance required by this section, each Secretary of a military department shall consider the following:</text> <paragraph id="HD16CCBBA362742BBADF30F9978015322" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The process by which a commander or head of a covered site identifies and reports encroachment with respect to such covered site.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H082001DA1FB5462393DE7B60C59B2B6A" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Methods to track data relating to processes, methods, and procedures described in subsection (a).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H14A2C00FA55F404FADDE0C27E90C3CE3" commented="no"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Coordination processes to track and mitigate encroachment—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H175AB9708AA3439FB03C09330300F3BF"><enum>(A)</enum><text>within each military department; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H06D2E5B6D3C740AAA11AE9EA3D4EA48C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>between the military departments and the Assistant Secretaries of Defense for Sustainment and Industrial Base Policy.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H0C01687D2D904AFEB9633B8B02CAC8C4" commented="no"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Foreign investment encroachment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Such guidance shall include a requirement that if a Secretary of a military department determines that encroachment described in subsection (a) involves or may involve foreign investment, such Secretary shall—</text> <paragraph id="H7FF74A13EDD7452F9034BA208E8EE238" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text>report information about encroachment relating to foreign investment to the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Industrial Base Policy; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3018FEC60A764BA7BD3FE27F5C7FEE80" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">coordinate with the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Industrial Base Policy on efforts to mitigate such encroachment or potential encroachment.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H9663EA9F2AB045288526E58E153B491E" commented="no"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date on which the guidance required by subsection (a) is issued, the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Sustainment, in coordination with the Secretaries of the military departments, shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a report on the guidance required by this section, including—</text> 
<paragraph id="H6C681BF991174FE8B396119A5E1ABAF3" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the extent to which such guidance has been implemented within the Department of Defense; </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H932B9AEB0704406E9D482210851036CA" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><text>a description of methods to update any lists of covered sites; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H6DC0A7D87A6B4A78BA2324B4826379B8" commented="no"><enum>(3)</enum><text>an assessment of the procedure described in subsection (a)(3).</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H0617E4C6F9BF4F5AA81C796CF0DC12B5" commented="no"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> 
<paragraph id="H97D3BB437C954C818DC6B815A20F9C1E" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>covered site</quote> means a military installation or another facility or property of the United States Government.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H335B1F79D8AC4DBA88C17FB4FE26A931" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>encroachment</quote> means an activity conducted within close proximity to a covered site that—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HC3F8C12156E04E4DAE5E29B8622DE8BB" display-inline="no-display-inline" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text>may pose a national security risk to a covered site;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HDFE052BE4CA14554996ADB13FB96F3F5" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>may affect the operational mission of a covered site; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HCB2BD1AE1DEF4D5FBB391F04D07A3A75" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">is incompatible with an installation master plan of a covered site.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H21EFB058509A4C3EACCB6D2345F478B1" commented="no"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>military department</quote> has the meaning given such term in section 101 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HEBFE3EF6FA5545DBA65A9954F1A059CF"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The term <quote>military installation</quote> has the meaning given such term in section 2801 of title 10, United States Code.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HBABD848095744CFA95D967A2ECCE2CA0" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>2888.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Extension and modification of annual updates to master plans and investment strategies for Army ammunition plants</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 2834(d) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (division B of <external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/81">Public Law 117–81</external-xref>; 135 Stat. 2201) is amended—</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2F197F975F77480C97DF4B48EB0675B4"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">in the matter preceding paragraph (1), by striking <quote>March 31, 2026</quote> and inserting <quote>March 31, 2030</quote>; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC77B237288F24E74A4F07DC531FD908B" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by adding at the end the following new paragraph:</text> 
<quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H1A3B95F5481D450A8AE21152BF907AE8"> 
<paragraph id="HE7454BBE11134CBD951A650AE171F7FB" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of any changes to a master plan for an ammunition production facility made in response to global events, including pandemics and armed conflicts.</text></paragraph><after-quoted-block display="yes">.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph></section> <section id="HFA57256C5CAE467390FA93928B8CCCB0" section-type="subsequent-section" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>2889.</enum><header>Limitation on use of funds for United States Space Command Headquarters</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2024 for the Department of Defense may be obligated or expended to acquire, construct, plan, or design a new headquarters building for United States Space Command until June 30, 2024, when the Inspector General of the Department of Defense and the Comptroller General of the United States shall complete reviews of the selection announced in July of 2023.</text></section> 
<section id="HA689BFAB3AEA41FFB4D455EBC10EDA11"><enum>2890. </enum><header>Plan for use of excess construction materials on southwest border</header> 
<subsection id="HFAD7A053BD15476A86062AB66F934B18"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 75 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to Congress a plan to use, transfer, or donate to States on the southern border of the United States all covered materials, with prioritization given to the refurbishment and or maintenance of ports of entry along the southwest border and construction projects aimed at stopping illicit human and vehicle traffic along the border of the United States with Mexico.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HCD47D0177B18465AADDB60E99ED989CE"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The plan required by subsection (a) shall include the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H0CC68154233446B0878D9FAD3AFD864D"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A detailed proposal for the disposition of such covered materials, including a timeline for disposition and the authorities under which such disposition shall occur.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H194240162FD8441884EBDCB123473870"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of the condition of such materials being stored, including (if applicable) a description of materials that have depreciated in value, become damaged, or been lost.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H892DC69E9EE74133BDE6C8FC8CC6FA44"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Requirements of requesting States</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any State requesting the covered materials made available under this section must certify, in writing, that the materials it accepts will be exclusively used for the refurbishment or maintenance of ports of entry along the southwest border or construction projects aimed at stopping illicit human and vehicle traffic along the border of the United States with Mexico.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H1919F17F2E0A4D35BA854E1EF0FE423D"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Execution of plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 100 days after the date of submission of the plan required by subsection (a), the Secretary of Defense shall commence execution of such plan until the date on which the Department of Defense is no longer incurring any costs to maintain, store, or protect the covered materials.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H71072CDA98BA4280BAABF9607C312680"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to Congress a report containing the following:</text> <paragraph id="H5D8AC19C4E8F4540A2E436B720146395"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline"> A detailed description of the decision process of the Secretary to forgo the excess property disposal process of the Department of Defense and instead pay to store the covered materials.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HAE477534E952401B952DB0BEE73FA4A6"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A list of entities the Department is paying for use of their privately owned land to store the covered materials, with appropriate action taken to protect personally identifiable information, such as by making the list of entities available in an annex that is labeled as controlled unclassified information.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2E81AB7088314413ADE2F256B0A88690"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An explanation of the process through which the Department contracted with private landowners to store the covered materials, including whether there was a competitive contracting process and whether the landowners have instituted an inventory review system.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF6E6E0BB44E449CE948A6D3E24CD71A3"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of any investigations by the Inspector General of the Department that have been opened related to storing the covered materials.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H419A00C57BF2495399315EC752EF932B"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section, the term <quote>covered material</quote> means all remaining construction materials currently possessed by the United States Government that were purchased under section 2808 and 284 of title 10, United States Code, from fiscal years 2017 through 2021, including bollards and Nucor tubular square structural tubes.</text></subsection></section></subtitle></title></division>

<section id="H63B1A6C0576E418EADA082298D3AE385"><enum>3113.</enum><header>Cybersecurity Risk Inventory, Assessment, and Mitigation Working Group</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Subtitle A of the National Nuclear Security Administration Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/2401">50 U.S.C. 2401 et seq.</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following new section:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" id="H6B3F8A879DBE45D89EFCA5B9AA566D91" display-inline="no-display-inline"> <section id="H3DA8D69708BD46E78131478674772D21"><enum>3222.</enum><header>Cybersecurity Risk Inventory, Assessment, and Mitigation Working Group</header> <subsection id="H0A18EAC24E6644BD826CB244EBA903F0"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">There is in the Administration a working group, to be known as the <quote>Cybersecurity Risk Inventory, Assessment, and Mitigation Working Group</quote> (referred to in this section as the <quote>working group</quote>). </text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H930ACD21F41E464280BADF878BAF0A7B"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Membership</header><text>Members of the working group shall include—</text> <paragraph id="HF1F41F03682D4219A1FF9651FDCCA23C"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the Deputy Administrator for Defense Programs;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H626CBDFE37F74B0EB6270EF5C9424C81"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the Associate Administrator for Information Management and Chief Information Officer; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC6F96115775C437FBD270ADD84888FDF"><enum>(3)</enum><text>such other personnel of the Administration as are determined appropriate for inclusion in the working group by the Chairperson.</text></paragraph></subsection>

<subsection id="H8836BB1112564824B6D5B31D041E59F4"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Inclusion in future-years nuclear security program</header><text>The milestone schedule document required under subsection (a) shall be included in the future-years nuclear security program for fiscal year 2025 and each subsequent fiscal year.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H8FE6BC2CCD2D455F93798024924AF3A5"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Covered construction project</header><text>In this section, the term <quote>covered construction project</quote> means—</text> 
<paragraph id="H4256256865A6429B9D9FCE67770A43E1"><enum>(1)</enum><text>a construction project that is subject to Department of Energy Order 413.3B, or a successor order; or</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2B7C9E2307EB4724813841CAB7A883FA"><enum>(2)</enum><text>a program designated as Enhanced Management A or B under the Program Execution Instruction of the Office of Defense Programs of the National Nuclear Security Administration.</text></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle> 
<subtitle id="HF297B3178C084240AFDDA1415C2D5EB6"><enum>C</enum><header>Other Matters</header> 
<section id="HADD384ECCFA04909B1F5C3D312754D5B" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>3131.</enum><header>U.S. nuclear fuel security initiative</header> 
<subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD1C5879504E64FF3A4E76B9AC0049308"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Short title</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">This section may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Nuclear Fuel Security Act of 2023</short-title></quote>.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H2E6B5412BB034D9C99D6A970FE5C975F"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Sense of Congress</header><text>It is the sense of Congress that—</text> 
<paragraph id="HD876521CE8494626B2D788CB685096B6"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the Department should—</text> <subparagraph id="HC6B84ECB15004FE09B72D9AC28503903"><enum>(A)</enum><text>support increased domestic production of low-enriched uranium; and </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4CC42D05B64841FD8FD92BDD1ECE48C4"><enum>(B)</enum><text>accelerate efforts to establish a domestic high-assay, low-enriched uranium enrichment capability; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HBA4876E4FF3C47D59BAA366AAD44DC3E"><enum>(2)</enum><text>if domestic enrichment of high-assay, low-enriched uranium will not be commercially available at the scale needed in time to meet the needs of the advanced nuclear reactor demonstration projects of the Department, the Secretary shall consider and implement, as necessary—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H40C437B10C044CB79CFE5D0E041C231D"><enum>(A)</enum><text>all viable options to make high-assay, low-enriched uranium produced from inventories owned by the Department available in a manner that is sufficient to maximize the potential for the Department to meet the needs and schedules of advanced nuclear reactor developers, without impacting existing Department missions, until such time that commercial enrichment and deconversion capability for high-assay, low-enriched uranium exists at a scale sufficient to meet future needs; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9E01B3117F364A8E9CBFFDD7AAFBE8BC"><enum>(B)</enum><text>all viable options for partnering with countries that are allies or partners of the United States to meet those needs and schedules until that time.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H81C35E1C8D0445E3880A9FB95BEE915B"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Objectives</header><text>The objectives of this section are—</text> <paragraph id="H63C18DC6D42D4C08ACF3997DA4C12A58"><enum>(1)</enum><text>to support domestic production of low-enriched uranium;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE4AC5101F1EF49BA92794A8313477761"><enum>(2)</enum><text>to expeditiously increase domestic production of high-assay, low-enriched uranium by an annual quantity, and in such form, determined by the Secretary to be sufficient to meet the needs of—</text> <subparagraph id="HFDE657E7B6F14D939568E0CB52023DDA"><enum>(A)</enum><text>advanced nuclear reactor developers; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HCF626454D1BA4469A10C4EAEE6995965"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the consortium;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF50FDDE6A5D74DC18E1B3A16C6AECDCB"><enum>(3)</enum><text>to ensure the availability of domestically produced, converted, enriched, deconverted, and reduced uranium in a quantity determined by the Secretary, in consultation with U.S. nuclear energy companies, to be sufficient to address a reasonably anticipated supply disruption;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H254D5A21919F482CA05C9AF4EDF557E4"><enum>(4)</enum><text>to address gaps and deficiencies in the domestic production, conversion, enrichment, deconversion, and reduction of uranium by partnering with countries that are allies or partners of the United States if domestic options are not practicable;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF8B03F856E8948D89C33503B07199450"><enum>(5)</enum><text>to ensure that, in the event of a supply disruption in the nuclear fuel market, a reserve of nuclear fuels is available to serve as a backup supply to support the nuclear nonproliferation and civil nuclear energy objectives of the Department, including collaborative research and development activities with other Federal agencies;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H37875221AC424AB9BA0D753F159E72BC"><enum>(6)</enum><text>to support enrichment, deconversion, and reduction technology deployed in the United States; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF7E459F857174582A2039B411A6F891B"><enum>(7)</enum><text>to ensure that, until such time that domestic enrichment and deconversion of high-assay, low-enriched uranium is commercially available at the scale needed to meet the needs of advanced nuclear reactor developers, the Secretary considers and implements, as necessary—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H67A0B7590AA845229EA11EDC46780A05"><enum>(A)</enum><text>all viable options to make high-assay, low-enriched uranium produced from inventories owned by the Department available in a manner that is sufficient to maximize the potential for the Department to meet the needs and schedules of advanced nuclear reactor developers; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H6676F702994949EC9072F70096B636CC"><enum>(B)</enum><text>all viable options for partnering with countries that are allies or partners of the United States to meet those needs and schedules. </text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H2FCAE4DC2CC04614BF938105CE6C230B"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="HE796BA19996F41778B85B14F142CDB08"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Advanced nuclear reactor</header><text>The term <term>advanced nuclear reactor</term> has the meaning given the term in section 951(b) of the Energy Policy Act of 2005 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/16271">42 U.S.C. 16271(b)</external-xref>).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF5E2BDEAD3A34EC98D90C971F8040DC7"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Associated entity</header><text>The term <term>associated entity</term> means an entity that—</text> <subparagraph id="H46E1A3D193C941A2A2D81FA54EFB1F64"><enum>(A)</enum><text>is owned, controlled, or dominated by—</text> 
<clause id="HDBAE30936D96487386AF75A610598A8B"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the government of a country that is an ally or partner of the United States; or</text></clause> <clause id="H7850DBBED1ED4A32A9F9189C76D805AA" commented="no"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>an associated individual; or</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HDC023836FA1243ADA6D8AF14FA5C00DC" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text>is organized under the laws of, or otherwise subject to the jurisdiction of, a country that is an ally or partner of the United States, including a corporation that is incorporated in such a country. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7E355E926304434BBDD5E8CC7931D2EC"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Associated individual</header><text>The term <term>associated individual</term> means an alien who is a national of a country that is an ally or partner of the United States.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H140C11D7220045EE9CCA6AFD6CB33168"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Consortium</header><text>The term <term>consortium</term> means the consortium established under section 2001(a)(2)(F) of the Energy Act of 2020 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/16281">42 U.S.C. 16281(a)(2)(F)</external-xref>).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H32437CD12B05466897B8815A8A6D2B96"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Department</header><text>The term <term>Department</term> means the Department of Energy.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H69238D3FD6054941B5A5D1597732AE5A" commented="no"><enum>(6)</enum><header>High-assay, low-enriched uranium; HALEU</header><text>The term <term>high-assay, low-enriched uranium</term> or <term>HALEU</term> means high-assay low-enriched uranium (as defined in section 2001(d) of the Energy Act of 2020 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/16281">42 U.S.C. 16281(d)</external-xref>)). </text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" id="HF5F9C7981E5849A5A0319E2862ED0850"><enum>(7)</enum><header>Low-enriched uranium; LEU</header><text>The term <term>low-enriched uranium</term> or <term>LEU</term> means each of—</text> 
<subparagraph commented="no" id="H6F9669E9C3E646E4BB85FFC3F188EAD1"><enum>(A)</enum><text>low-enriched uranium (as defined in section 3102 of the USEC Privatization Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/2297h">42 U.S.C. 2297h</external-xref>)); and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H900BCE5337CD466EB74106D65DB0231D" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text>low-enriched uranium (as defined in section 3112A(a) of that Act (42 U.S.C. 2297h–10a(a))). </text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H925DF63D1F544B4595E706E22A5FD266"><enum>(8)</enum><header>Programs</header><text>The term <term>Programs</term> means—</text> <subparagraph id="H5112B91B1E224979A8BDDCB6AF5B9777"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the Nuclear Fuel Security Program established under subsection (e)(1);</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HE826875BA3214BD8962D1BC8C6362600"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the American Assured Fuel Supply Program of the Department; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE3370B4DD4B740B595A859A5C37ABA9E"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the HALEU for Advanced Nuclear Reactor Demonstration Projects Program established under subsection (e)(3).</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0AF02F5FF9544B749AA83794C3D5BF9A"><enum>(9)</enum><header>Secretary</header><text>The term <term>Secretary</term> means the Secretary of Energy.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H355DED7FF8F64321995A07B6D0560931" commented="no"><enum>(10)</enum><header>U.S. nuclear energy company</header><text>The term <term>U.S. nuclear energy company</term> means a company that—</text> 
<subparagraph commented="no" id="HA16CAFA61A604364B7D1F516A9BA8D84"><enum>(A)</enum><text>is organized under the laws of, or otherwise subject to the jurisdiction of, the United States; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H29AA2320F1E54032BA09E8C891F3489B" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text>is involved in the nuclear energy industry. </text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H33247C1D72E34FB791FB7916C27E7007"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Establishment and expansion of programs</header><text>The Secretary, consistent with the objectives described in subsection (c), shall—</text> <paragraph id="HA91445D2B4514B1486B95C4FA1F47659"><enum>(1)</enum><text>establish a program, to be known as the <quote>Nuclear Fuel Security Program</quote>, to increase the quantity of HALEU and, if determined to be necessary after completion of a market evaluation, LEU produced by U.S. nuclear energy companies;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB02CABD951774710A978562F50D0277B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>expand the American Assured Fuel Supply Program of the Department to ensure the availability of domestically produced, converted, enriched, deconverted, and reduced uranium in the event of a supply disruption; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H39719E279FF247A5AFB3223C6B13EAA9"><enum>(3)</enum><text>establish a program, to be known as the <quote>HALEU for Advanced Nuclear Reactor Demonstration Projects Program</quote>—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HE15B69CEC3574943B9E34EDF1546B953"><enum>(A)</enum><text>to maximize the potential for the Department to meet the needs and schedules of advanced nuclear reactor developers until such time that commercial enrichment and deconversion capability for HALEU exists in the United States at a scale sufficient to meet future needs; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HC4C057C2A4D24F4AA800AE058C8489DA"><enum>(B)</enum><text>where practicable, to partner with countries that are allies or partners of the United States to meet those needs and schedules until that time.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HABD5BBF6C80A4095B2229E2CAFA8D2A9"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Nuclear Fuel Security Program</header> 
<paragraph id="H7D1BB6C0588F480FAD2DEEB6C68BEFB6"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>In carrying out the Nuclear Fuel Security Program, the Secretary—</text> <subparagraph id="H68BBB70B38564C2BB7AA5CDD2BE787CD"><enum>(A)</enum><text>shall—</text> 
<clause id="H52C498BE3A544F25BCE5FE03366A3960"><enum>(i)</enum><text>if determined to be necessary or appropriate based on the completion of a market evaluation, not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, take actions, including cost-shared financial agreements, milestone-based payments, or other mechanisms, to support commercial availability of LEU and to promote diversity of supply in domestic uranium mining, conversion, enrichment, and deconversion capacity and technologies, including new capacity, among U.S. nuclear energy companies;</text></clause> <clause id="H7789600420404EFC8A4725D25327D2A9"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, enter into 2 or more contracts with members of the consortium to begin acquiring not less than 20 metric tons per year of HALEU by December 31, 2027 (or the earliest operationally feasible date thereafter), from U.S. nuclear energy companies;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H2B497D5E5EEF4D708CFC3ADE3CDA8067"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>utilize only uranium produced, converted, enriched, deconverted, and reduced in—</text> <subclause id="H2A4C1A346A80487A8B9D46B6B21D487B"><enum>(I)</enum><text>the United States; or </text></subclause> 
<subclause id="H987EA884215A45368928AC25CC87EA73"><enum>(II)</enum><text>if domestic options are not practicable, a country that is an ally or partner of the United States; and</text></subclause></clause> <clause id="H1D5840225B9343FAA1970751D6EC4E48"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>to the maximum extent practicable, ensure that the use of domestic uranium utilized as a result of that program does not negatively affect the economic operation of nuclear reactors in the United States; and</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H2179A6CFF920410C8D73ABDAC96345F3"><enum>(B)</enum> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="yes-display-inline" id="HE2EB908D85444B4483419FBF1DA377D6"><enum>(i)</enum><text>may not make commitments under this subsection (including cooperative agreements (used in accordance with section 6305 of title 31, United States Code), purchase agreements, guarantees, leases, service contracts, or any other type of commitment) for the purchase or other acquisition of HALEU or LEU unless—</text> <subclause id="HDF6EFB4AA2184C9CB66479E43330BE6E" indent="up1"><enum>(I)</enum><text>funds are specifically provided for those purposes in advance in appropriations Acts enacted after the date of enactment of this Act; or</text></subclause> 
<subclause indent="up1" id="H3B670C764B264F4E96D9A2F44B544441"><enum>(II)</enum><text>the commitment is funded entirely by funds made available to the Secretary from the account described in subsection (j)(2)(B); and</text></subclause></clause> <clause indent="up1" id="H0E73FEE7A01E425EA18B2A8D3F85D875"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>may make a commitment described in clause (i) only—</text> 
<subclause id="H46AD6DAE09E5400184FF5554EF1A48FD"><enum>(I)</enum><text>if the full extent of the anticipated costs stemming from the commitment is recorded as an obligation at the time that the commitment is made; and</text></subclause> <subclause id="HEAB8DF9F1A9A4866B796AAD1CF965889"><enum>(II)</enum><text>to the extent of that up-front obligation recorded in full at that time.</text></subclause></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H91DC891DAD4046B7B28D3758DF0639D2"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Considerations</header><text>In carrying out paragraph (1)(A)(ii), the Secretary shall consider and, if appropriate, implement—</text> <subparagraph id="H426093DEFC5B4FB8B995175CA7AEAD77"><enum>(A)</enum><text>options to ensure the quickest availability of commercially enriched HALEU, including—</text> 
<clause id="H8FF35E9FF3244A1988B19406CF397FE5"><enum>(i)</enum><text>partnerships between 2 or more commercial enrichers; and</text></clause> <clause id="HD6FD959B2D934ADFA964AF00930B22EC"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>utilization of up to 10-percent enriched uranium as feedstock in demonstration-scale or commercial HALEU enrichment facilities;</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H2D667CDA9F984E0AB79B7919A8F5D4B0"><enum>(B)</enum><text>options to partner with countries that are allies or partners of the United States to provide LEU and HALEU for commercial purposes;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H7A1D8AD5B8EA4CBABCE35F72ACE96156"><enum>(C)</enum><text>options that provide for an array of HALEU—</text> 
<clause id="H927D02952961423F8ECFAB55C7114DBC"><enum>(i)</enum><text>enrichment levels;</text></clause> <clause id="H7747A5AAA53748C9863A16890A8328F2"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>output levels to meet demand; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H1BB278E384494786A759505D37EC24F0"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>fuel forms, including uranium metal and oxide; and</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HEEF19C92FEA3474A80F3BD1DBF771271"><enum>(D)</enum><text>options—</text> 
<clause id="HDF894372E79341B6A1BB838AE0037438"><enum>(i)</enum><text>to replenish, as necessary, Department stockpiles of uranium that were intended to be downblended for other purposes, but were instead used in carrying out activities under the HALEU for Advanced Nuclear Reactor Demonstration Projects Program;</text></clause> <clause id="HF7B102813B074F459D7F10C5DB219C6D"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>to continue supplying HALEU to meet the needs of the recipients of an award made pursuant to the funding opportunity announcement of the Department numbered DE–FOA–0002271 for Pathway 1, Advanced Reactor Demonstrations; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HA3B4EC92073C4C93BAC401050A523312"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>to make HALEU available to other advanced nuclear reactor developers and other end-users.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H1BB340AE30B14473BA20FC53EE2295B5"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Avoidance of market disruptions</header><text>In carrying out the Nuclear Fuel Security Program, the Secretary, to the extent practicable and consistent with the purposes of that program, shall not disrupt or replace market mechanisms by competing with U.S. nuclear energy companies.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H86B8742018D54CA090F38440ECF8C367"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Expansion of the American Assured Fuel Supply Program</header><text>The Secretary, in consultation with U.S. nuclear energy companies, shall—</text> <paragraph id="H9021442AA8B44CECAB296267237B5D45"><enum>(1)</enum><text>expand the American Assured Fuel Supply Program of the Department by merging the operations of the Uranium Reserve Program of the Department with the American Assured Fuel Supply Program; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H370D3BA3E3A046FBAEF7BBD555EE1F1A"><enum>(2)</enum><text>in carrying out the American Assured Fuel Supply Program of the Department, as expanded under paragraph (1)—</text> <subparagraph id="H6B262E55D78C4781A924E7C237B3CDF4"><enum>(A)</enum><text>maintain, replenish, diversify, or increase the quantity of uranium made available by that program in a manner determined by the Secretary to be consistent with the purposes of that program and the objectives described in subsection (c);</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H66ACDBF3EAF24B3DBE7D21381214AA75"><enum>(B)</enum><text>utilize only uranium produced, converted, enriched, deconverted, and reduced in—</text> <clause id="HBC0766AFF366439992EAC7A104F0DC71"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the United States; or</text></clause> 
<clause id="HB15EE633D8F1485AA79DA829F1268D3D"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>if domestic options are not practicable, a country that is an ally or partner of the United States;</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H642510D737B64FF5B5FE331FE328909A"><enum>(C)</enum><text>make uranium available from the American Assured Fuel Supply, subject to terms and conditions determined by the Secretary to be reasonable and appropriate;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H21517A3C9EFE4E18B841AF21FA2FEB23"><enum>(D)</enum><text>refill and expand the supply of uranium in the American Assured Fuel Supply, including by maintaining a limited reserve of uranium to address a potential event in which a domestic or foreign recipient of uranium experiences a supply disruption for which uranium cannot be obtained through normal market mechanisms or under normal market conditions; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HBB59F5F4742446DCA3AFB608196259A8"><enum>(E)</enum><text>take other actions that the Secretary determines to be necessary or appropriate to address the purposes of that program and the objectives described in subsection (c).</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H6B838FFAFED4464199642A1AB2F077E9"><enum>(h)</enum><header>HALEU for Advanced Nuclear Reactor Demonstration Projects Program</header> 
<paragraph id="H1A7CC50A4AF0470184344FA14B6FC772"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Activities</header><text>On enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall immediately accelerate and, as necessary, initiate activities to make available from inventories or stockpiles owned by the Department and made available to the consortium, HALEU for use in advanced nuclear reactors that cannot operate on uranium with lower enrichment levels or on alternate fuels, with priority given to the awards made pursuant to the funding opportunity announcement of the Department numbered DE–FOA–0002271 for Pathway 1, Advanced Reactor Demonstrations, with additional HALEU to be made available to other advanced nuclear reactor developers, as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6DF61CCDB05D48D8A325FD2819428644"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Quantity</header><text>In carrying out activities under this subsection, the Secretary shall consider and implement, as necessary, all viable options to make HALEU available in quantities and forms sufficient to maximize the potential for the Department to meet the needs and schedules of advanced nuclear reactor developers, including by seeking to make available—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H9127219B15F24C0F8AEEF81CA45F1F3F"><enum>(A)</enum><text>by September 30, 2024, not less than 3 metric tons of HALEU;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3009170EA8D844BBB9DF5ED805DA6105"><enum>(B)</enum><text>by December 31, 2025, not less than an additional 8 metric tons of HALEU; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H77A71EAB477C4CB984ED7C6B7AAC4800"><enum>(C)</enum><text>by June 30, 2026, not less than an additional 10 metric tons of HALEU.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H79531970516B4775959679A6A811A62E"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Factors for consideration</header><text>In carrying out activities under this subsection, the Secretary shall take into consideration—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HE52C9AD4CF404437B6B72EE3DC1EE9E8"><enum>(A)</enum><text>options for providing HALEU from a stockpile of uranium owned by the Department, including—</text> <clause id="H1305446602AB4EA0A00828359FC2A16F"><enum>(i)</enum><text>uranium that has been declared excess to national security needs during or prior to fiscal year 2023;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HFF6D91A69AD94C4ABF38180554DEA7D7"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>uranium that—</text> <subclause id="HC2B24081C3E4465DA1408216153A06D1"><enum>(I)</enum><text>directly meets the needs of advanced nuclear reactor developers; but</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="H281BE67CC78B4FD183A5CD8938B185A5"><enum>(II)</enum><text>has been previously used or fabricated for another purpose;</text></subclause></clause> <clause id="HB711F9E14B6E4295A55A7719C9CAF509"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>uranium that can meet the needs of advanced nuclear reactor developers after removing radioactive or other contaminants that resulted from previous use or fabrication of the fuel for research, development, demonstration, or deployment activities of the Department, including activities that reduce the environmental liability of the Department by accelerating the processing of uranium from stockpiles designated as waste;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HDD436BDE2D664C5F909E851D0221B29D"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>uranium from a high-enriched uranium stockpile (excluding stockpiles intended for national security needs), which can be blended with lower assay uranium to become HALEU to meet the needs of advanced nuclear reactor developers; and</text></clause> <clause id="H80A9C83B3A6A4528A798649F5A1E082E"><enum>(v)</enum><text>uranium from stockpiles intended for other purposes (excluding stockpiles intended for national security needs), but for which uranium could be swapped or replaced in time in such a manner that would not negatively impact the missions of the Department;</text></clause></subparagraph>
