<paragraph id="HFA884EB27BC147F5B7B996960C041723"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the Department of Defense of section 2631 of title 10; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB289299600014ED1891C2AE2646E7699"><enum>(2)</enum><text>other Federal departments and agencies of programs the Administrator determines are subject to section 55305 of this title.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H1A1854C44E3046D19DDE408DBA6D2302"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Contents</header><text>Each annual report required under subsection (a) shall include, for each Federal department or agency that administers a program covered by the report—</text> <paragraph id="H8A3DCB6B6BF84B428AC028DE742AF1B2"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the gross tonnage of cargo (equipment, materials, or agricultural products), expressed by type of cargo, transported on United States flag vessels as compared to on foreign vessels; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HFFF3EFB849CF46D4994F6F0E2F2CD74B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the total number of United States flag vessels and total number of foreign vessels contracted by each department or agency.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H0C3DE03744184F4BA0EDC4429BF562A1"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Agency reporting requirements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than January 31 of each year, the head of each Federal department or agency that administers a program covered by a report required under subsection (a) shall submit to the Administrator of the Maritime Administration the information described in subsection (b) for that department or agency.</text></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE4659EAE4DAC4AC691425669DC46C9D1"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Clerical amendment</header><text>The analysis for <external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/46/553">chapter 553</external-xref> of title 46, United States Code, is amended by inserting before the item relating to section 55302 the following new item:</text> <quoted-block id="H5F4D6132497E4DDF89BD37B788E7B309" style="USC"> <toc regeneration="no-regeneration"> <toc-entry level="section">55301. Report on administration of programs by other Federal departments and agencies. </toc-entry></toc><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H4D391D7AC9F54D96B26BECB6CC22CF1A"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Report on survey of United States shipbuilding and repair facilities</header> <paragraph id="HE5021A6EA2414EE0B0030897B5A974B0"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter for each of the subsequent four fiscal years, the Secretary of Transportation, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, the Administrator of the Maritime Administration, and the Commandant of the Coast Guard, shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report that includes a survey of United States shipbuilding and repair facilities.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA2D36C94C900403BA1B56AECB4C765CC"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Contents</header><text>Each report required under paragraph (1) shall include an identification of all requirements for a survey of United States shipbuilding and repair facilities in accordance with sections 50102 and 50103 of title 46, United States Code, and section 502(f) of the Merchant Marine Act of 1936 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/46/53101">46 U.S.C. 53101</external-xref> note).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H961CFBB1FB3F44AEBF241F1BBD6B4AB1"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Public availability</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">At the time the Secretary of Transportation submits to the appropriate congressional committees a report under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall make the report, and all report data, publicly available on an appropriate website.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA637815E93B6456FBA4E744DCB9C399F"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Definition</header><text>In this subsection, the term <term>appropriate congressional committees</term> means—</text> <subparagraph id="HDCACE0CFA6F4442A8B065149C817A699"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFB20F408214444C5A1880B8366D43BAE"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H1D2B0F825A1346FEA6594F0577CD7324"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Report on port preferences for US-flag vessels</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Administrator of the Maritime Administration shall submit to Congress a report on the preference, if any, afforded by each port authority or marine terminal operator, as applicable, to vessels documented under the laws of the United States, including such vessels—</text> 
<paragraph id="HF929DFF374B44898BA2F73D9A10B81A1"><enum>(1)</enum><text>operated by an armed force (as such term is defined in section 101(4) of title 10, United States Code);</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H20155653845749529B481D7E4095C0E1"><enum>(2)</enum><text>participating in the Maritime Security Program or the Emergency Preparedness Program under <external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/46/531">chapter 531</external-xref> of title 46, United States Code, the Cable Security Fleet under chapter 532 of such title, the Tanker Security Fleet under chapter 534 of such title, or the National Defense Reserve Fleet under section 57100 of such title; or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H33D742C1377C47A394BE7F29B33D9F0C"><enum>(3)</enum><text>with a coastwise endorsement under <external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/46/121">chapter 121</external-xref> of title 46, United States Code.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HD6BEC83A4C9342599DE00AAF14306404"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Report on increasing effectiveness of marine highways</header> <paragraph id="H2F10B9B79BD34ECAA602861D3BB6CC4C"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Administrator of the Maritime Administration shall complete and make publicly available on an appropriate website a study that identifies opportunities for, and barriers to, increasing the effectiveness of marine highways designated under section 55601 of title 46, United States Code, in addressing two or more of the components described in clauses (i), (ii), and (iv) of subparagraphs (A) and subparagraph (B) of section 50307(a)(2) of title 46, United States Code.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HDFF91F506253405F8F8FA87112CBF98B"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Pilot program</header><text>Beginning on the date that is 120 days after the date of the completion of the study required under paragraph (1), the Administrator shall carry out a one-year pilot program under which the Administrator shall select one marine highway project and implement the findings of the study with respect to that project.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HEEECFC98192A4FE2B2BC3DA7D8BB0A90"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Final report</header><text>Not later than 90 days after the completion of the pilot program under paragraph (3), the Administrator shall provide to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives, a briefing on the lessons learned from the pilot program, any recommendations based on feedback from maritime stakeholders, States, Indian Tribes, nonprofit organizations, and other stakeholders, and recommendations for establishing future marine highways in the United States.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HD6B0B94E42CC4D9D99F1978175051AE8"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Study on availability of Federal student aid for mariner training</header> 
<paragraph id="HA9D344DF525549CC850FEA40E0DA7553"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct a study of the availability of Federal financial assistance for licensed and unlicensed mariners, as applicable, for mariner training and the effectiveness of coordination with respect to such assistance of—</text> <subparagraph id="H9D99C49F9DB34943B7C4EB6822A028A5"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Federal agencies;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFF019BCE45484061B14C8F991DEA576F"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Federal agencies and States; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9C9B79530AA04B3B8326184E4A8D0D0F"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Federal agencies and Indian Tribes.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H711F37C944BC4156A91CBF6D1268F15B"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Matters evaluated</header><text>The study conducted under paragraph (1) shall include an evaluation of the following:</text> <subparagraph id="H9695E58EC7B849AB93E3618E20A084BF"><enum>(A)</enum><text>The availability of Federal financial assistance for mariner training provided by the Department of Education, the Department of Veterans Affairs, the Department of Labor, the Maritime Administration, or other agencies to the full range of prospective mariners, and an identification of any gaps in financial assistance.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HD822EB9FEE704CD6B86AFE7D82387418"><enum>(B)</enum><text>The extent to which the Maritime Administration has effectively coordinated with the Department of Education, the Department of Veterans Affairs, the Department of Labor, or other relevant Federal agencies to align Federal financial assistance with the education and training needs of mariners.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HA61450D6C0594CD4813C74EB3C52FEC2"><enum>(C)</enum><text>The extent to which the Maritime Administration has effectively communicated with prospective and current mariners about the availability of Federal financial assistance to facilitate their training and education needs.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H320D048912BF4D318316FFC654DC32DA"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Scope</header><text>The study conducted under paragraph (1) shall include an examination of the availability of Federal financial assistance, and the service obligations related to such financial assistance, if applicable, at mariner training institutions within the United States, including for students attending, or participating in—</text> <subparagraph id="H1BA3678225734978AF0E9C950C8AA5A8"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the United States Merchant Marine Academy;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HE7007E16C663488A890D42B3589CA40C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>a State maritime academy;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H91D76ADE2B44473FB9519BB92C21F367"><enum>(C)</enum><text>an institution described in subparagraphs (B) and (C) of section 51706(c)(1) of title 46, United States Code;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H0A931C7BD53E41EFB596359EEE21D143"><enum>(D)</enum><text>an Indian Tribe apprenticeship or other training program; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HFB0EF51A5807403CB0378B75CE133AD9"><enum>(E)</enum><text>an educational program carried out by a Federal agency.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD95D1B0C911C4525AAB27C24B3A0EC42"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than two years after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives a report containing the findings of the Comptroller General with respect to the study conducted under paragraph (1).</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H9C3984E5D1CF46CE91B77634A408E857" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>3522.</enum><header>Reports on availability of used sealift vessels and the scrapping and recycling of imported vessels</header> <subsection id="HCDF6F34955C547A085E5EA7088BCF5FC"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Report on availability of used sealift vessels</header> <paragraph id="HB8895C5850CF4A3ABEEFFC797BB84C7F"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Commander of the United States Transportation Command, in consultation with the Administrator of the Maritime Administration, shall conduct a market analysis to determine the availability of used sealift vessels that—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H9356844F399B42968DDEB9C4363BCAAE"><enum>(A)</enum><text>meet military requirements; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF7DE9213A1494E3CA870FF393A438DEB"><enum>(B)</enum><text>may be purchased using the authority provided under section 2218 of title 10, United States Code, within the period of five years following the date of the enactment of this Act.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA8F0F41E7C374165BE6CD0FA037B226E"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Report</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Commander of the United States Transportation Command shall submit to the congressional defense committees and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate a report on the results of the market analysis conducted under paragraph (1).</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HE8AF8FB0DEB14218B2F51B9F0C262E54"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Study on the scrapping and recycling of imported vessels</header> <paragraph id="H0BFD87465078417C8F6C71FA7C786AD2"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Administrator of the Maritime Administration and the Deputy Under Secretary for International Affairs of the Department of Labor shall jointly conduct a study to review domestic United States ship scrapping capacity and capability.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8D68E78BAC4A478AA8CB29655CF013A4"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The study required under paragraph (1) shall include the following:</text> <subparagraph id="H604A78489D184679A5A63F44EDB3B459"><enum>(A)</enum><text>An assessment of—</text> 
<clause id="HD88B4E9F1EE04B1D821387672641AFAE"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the capabilities of United States shipyards to recycle and dispose of domestic and foreign vessels and their component parts;</text></clause> <clause id="HB9094D22DBFD4E17AB12759C9D15A386"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the capacity of United States shipyards to complete ship recycling and disposal of domestic and foreign vessels and their component parts and related activities; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HBB6D5DAA37F54B43A8E9100A66CFE569"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the infrastructure, regulatory, economic, or other barriers to domestic ship recycling and disposal of vessels of the United States (as defined in section 116 of title 46, United States Code) and foreign vessels and their component parts.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3497EC8DA1204E24AB9529060FCA70BF"><enum>(B)</enum><text>An identification of—</text> 
<clause id="HDE46EF21D710498188B4E49C717E302E"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the estimated number of vessels over 1,000 tons that were recycled or scrapped globally each year for the ten-year period preceding the date of the enactment of this Act;</text></clause> <clause id="HC973F38AAA0D4A62B91A463898BF7643"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the country in which such vessels were scrapped or recycled;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HFAC8042E55DE4DB485A37D69804AE3BF"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the component parts of a vessel that require additional processing after ship recycling;</text></clause> <clause id="H421D84E9C8FB4686918997BF4190F06B"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>best practices and methods used globally, including in the United States, at the time of the study, to recycle or dispose of the components described in clause (iii); and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H52B493F822BD46DE89CFD4D2223FB372"><enum>(v)</enum><text>for the 15 foreign countries with the highest global market share for ship recycling and disposal, and for any countries with documented labor exploitation or environmental concerns (as determined by the Administrator and the Deputy Under Secretary)—</text> <subclause id="HFEC8043BCF0645ABA49B6FEE2312CBD2"><enum>(I)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the practices used at the time of the study for ship recycling and disposal, including for the component parts described in clause (iii); and</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="HBB761CCEC04E4A4A99B063053091F655"><enum>(II)</enum><text>to the extent such information is available, environmental and labor practices used in such recycling and disposal.</text></subclause></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H20E4DD107FD84313965ACDCC1F6D0687"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a report containing the findings of the study required under paragraph (1).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2D06CFE18F7E42DCAE56CDA616D530B0"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Definitions of component parts</header><text>In this subsection, the term <term>component parts</term> means an item or items on a ship that require additional processing after removal from the ship, such as cable insulation, rubber and felt gaskets, electronic equipment, caulking, or paint.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H8F0AA2D43DAD426DAA4369075C02EF5E"><enum>3523.</enum><header>Study on foreign ownership and control of marine terminals</header> <subsection id="H9F2B517A8DCF4FD68C5F57E897472782"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Transportation, in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce, shall seek to enter into an agreement with a federally funded research and development center under which the center shall evaluate how foreign state-owned enterprises with leases, long term concessions, partial ownership, or ownership of marine terminals (including marine terminal operators) at the 15 largest United States container ports affect, or could affect, United States national and economic security.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H0AFC5D41E58F4779887D60BEAB16DD30"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Contents</header><text>An agreement entered into pursuant to subsection (a) shall provide that the center shall—</text> <paragraph id="HC04838E0C3934B33865F0754A7DFE3E6"><enum>(1)</enum><text>consider—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H2F21F1D5032C4E719F1577B33C7D1E53"><enum>(A)</enum><text>foreign ownership or state-owned enterprises with leases, long-term concessions, partial ownership, or ownership of marine terminals (including marine terminal operators) at 15 largest United States container ports over the 30-year period preceding the date of enactment of this Act;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H37F803CBA46C4779B7140069FC2DA858"><enum>(B)</enum><text>instances of ownership in individual marine terminals and cumulative ownership by Chinese or Russian entities, state-owned enterprises, or nationals;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H8CD7719931294AB3BFD79BB4F10480B0"><enum>(C)</enum><text>instances of ownership in individual marine terminals and partial or complete ownership by any foreign entity;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H723831AFEF1F4EC69CFA62472F6069F5"><enum>(D)</enum><text>the amount of Federal funds that have been distributed to ports and marine terminals that are wholly or partially foreign-owned, including Chinese and Russian state-owned enterprises;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF49682CBFB974DF791C1E3371BA31699"><enum>(E)</enum><text>where any stake in foreign ownership, or other vectors of control, exists (including any level of equity stake in joint ventures with United States or foreign marine terminal operators), including Chinese or Russian state-owned enterprises, a detailed description of foreign operational control, including both affirmative and negative control; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H4CC7D63BCCE349C58D7792EEC53983DD"><enum>(F)</enum><text>the degree to which transactions for leases, long-term concessions, partial ownership, or ownership of marine terminals referred to in subparagraph (A) were considered covered transactions by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States and subsequently subject to review during the 30-year period preceding the date of the enactment of this Act; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H84C98D782A444FFAA98F7C217C587FDF"><enum>(2)</enum><text>offer recommendations on—</text> <subparagraph id="H7A5F02CC81D846908CC1291D909CB29B"><enum>(A)</enum><text>policies by ports and marine terminal operators with respect to foreign ownership or control to prevent any degree of threats to United States national security and economic security;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H1EA87EAA9F37483C974ACDB8AECA09EB"><enum>(B)</enum><text>whether foreign ownership, a positional relationship, or state-owned enterprises with leases, long term concessions, partial ownership, or ownership of marine terminals (including marine terminal operators) affords the foreign entity access to operational technology and information unique to the United States and otherwise unavailable; </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE5EBA67669814D3DBB2630A5C5B05543"><enum>(C)</enum><text>whether foreign ownership or state-owned enterprises with leases, long term concessions, partial ownership, or ownership of marine terminals (including marine terminal operators) has or could affect the supply chain and policies related to the prioritization of certain cargoes; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFB013B07064547749EBFF50340722EEB"><enum>(D)</enum><text>legislative or other policy changes needed to secure and advance United States national and economic security of the United States.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H35739A249B4C4E8398178C9E503A2FA5"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than one year after the initiation of an evaluation carried out pursuant to an agreement entered into under subsection (a), the Secretary of Transportation shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a report containing the results of such evaluation.</text></subsection>

<subsection id="H2AD751B0B3DD49F48E270D4A68D6233B"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Section 55305 of title 46, United States Code, is amended—</text> <paragraph id="HF36BB7CC4FC64CB58455ABC3AC2B9C7A"><enum>(1)</enum><text>by striking subsection (a);</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB9F7B5F18D7749CBB243F4ED9911B961"><enum>(2)</enum><text>by redesignating—</text> <subparagraph id="H1D1F47183A5243FC9A87A2CC2BEE6BC8"><enum>(A)</enum><text>subsection (b) as subsection (a); and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H7ABD55950FA54AF68D9D633C045A3C1A"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">subsections (c), (d), and (e), as subsections (d), (e), and (f), respectively;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H38BCCB69D49E4A838F061A53BF7EE07D"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">in subsection (a), as so redesignated, by striking <quote>privately-owned commercial vessels of the United States,</quote> and inserting <quote>privately-owned commercial vessels of the United States, as provided under subsection (b),</quote>; </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF3E7C4341A734FAF9B13FB0159CE66F1"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by inserting after subsection (a), as so redesignated, the following:</text> <quoted-block style="USC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H53BDCE66E42E4231B86E8BDCF832AFC8"> <subsection id="HE02310B04B974A92A52A69D8DE723E60"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Eligible vessels</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To be eligible to carry cargo as provided under subsection (a), a privately-owned commercial vessel shall be documented under the laws of the United States—</text> 
<paragraph id="H10D7390AA8344B8C990D629C0DCB5B5F"><enum>(1)</enum><text>for not less than three years; or</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H12DDD4447EA14928A114F12B027794D4"><enum>(2)</enum><text>after January 1, 2030, for less than three years, if the vessel owner signs an agreement with the Secretary providing that—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H7BB9EFBA97C5455CA530B2B1575362F0"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the vessel shall remain documented under the laws of the United States for not less than three years; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H7855A327FBC34EA69C669F7819DE4BC1"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the vessel owner shall, upon request of the Secretary, agree to enroll the vessel in an emergency preparedness agreement or voluntary agreement authorized under section 708 of the Defense Production Act of 1950 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/4558">50 U.S.C. 4558</external-xref>) and shall ensure the vessel remains so enrolled until the vessel ceases to be documented under the laws of the United States.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA59AFBA7A6F44A16A811DF18D80E7569"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Violation of agreement</header><text>A vessel under an agreement executed pursuant to subsection (b)(2) may be seized by, and forfeited to, the United States if, in violation of that agreement—</text> <paragraph id="H364AE81C938942CC9C8B9B200F771884"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the vessel owner places the vessel under foreign registry; or</text></paragraph>

<subsection id="H8A682B1F4F574F39B5621D3863052143"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Waivers</header> 
<paragraph id="H1777E10796874CDF939688F59712467F" display-inline="yes-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Notwithstanding any other provision of law, when the President, the Secretary of Defense, or the Secretary of Transportation declares the existence of an emergency justifying a temporary waiver of this section or section 55314 of this title, the President, the Secretary of Defense, or the Secretary of Transportation, following a determination by the Maritime Administrator, acting in the Administrator’s capacity as Director, National Shipping Authority, of the non-availability of qualified United States flag capacity at fair and reasonable rates for commercial vessels of the United States to meet the requirements of this section or section 55314 of this title, may waive compliance with such section to the extent, in the manner, and on the terms the Maritime Administrator, acting in such capacity, prescribes, and no other waivers of the requirements of this section or section 55314 of this title shall be authorized.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H46B044462EAA490590FC822D9487A57B" indent="up1"><enum>(2)</enum> <subparagraph id="HE9608FCF527F4EB495D0808C08396A60" display-inline="yes-display-inline"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Subject to subparagraphs (B) and (C), a waiver issued under this subsection shall be for a period of not more than 60 days.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC88828A0DE11475CA95901AF47F8BD99" indent="up1"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Upon termination of the period of a waiver issued under this subsection, the Maritime Administrator may extend the waiver for an additional period of not more than 30 days, if the Maritime Administrator makes the determinations described in paragraph (1).</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HD7B62C092BB34C64B409540EDB4987FE" indent="up1"><enum>(C)</enum><text>The aggregate duration of the period of all waivers and extensions of waivers under this subsection with respect to any one set of events shall not exceed three months in a fiscal year.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA363C46EFD3643C8ABE7E57D412515E6" indent="up1"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The Maritime Administrator shall—</text> <subparagraph id="H31F2CAE06DA8414C94786E1F67B3E009"><enum>(A)</enum><text>for each determination referred to in paragraph (1), identify any actions that could be taken to enable qualified United States flag capacity to meet the requirements of this section or section 55314 at fair and reasonable rates for commercial vessels of the United States;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4E1E0479D9114934BCBEBD29706FB221"><enum>(B)</enum><text>provide notice of each determination referred to in paragraph (1) to the Secretary of Transportation and, as applicable, the President or the Secretary of Defense; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3D15E344D3BC45BEB123DBF77E3BCB22"><enum>(C)</enum><text>publish each determination referred to in paragraph (1)—</text> 
<clause id="H102CBC1E25CF4346A1965891C39A4844"><enum>(i)</enum><text>on the website of the Maritime Administration not later than 24 hours after notice of the determination is provided to the Secretary of Transportation; and</text></clause> <clause id="H6DD742D51B674EDDBA5AD030C5DA0D62"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>in the Federal Register.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HEBE3606C16FF4A22B71C88A304F9C944" indent="up1"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The Maritime Administrator shall notify—</text> <subparagraph id="H7A0A6D5436FB482E84FF163011A0E697"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives of—</text> 
<clause id="HB20A753B1AF1498AA96ED736EF95BCBD"><enum>(i)</enum><text>any request for a waiver (or an extension thereof) made by the Secretary of Transportation of this section or section 55314(a) of this title by not later than 72 hours after receiving such a request; and</text></clause> <clause id="H286D991AC00C41FD8E291A3E13AAB74C"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the issuance of any such waiver (or an extension thereof), and why such waiver or extension was necessary, by not later than 72 hours after such issuance; and</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF4A4DFE7406346EF8821F7FE2330F028"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation and the Committee on Armed Services of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives of—</text> <clause id="H95CDFC4FBFA84203A69C62199EA9720A"><enum>(i)</enum><text>any request for a waiver (or an extension thereof) made by the Secretary of Defense of this section or section 55314(a) of this title by not later than 72 hours after receiving such a request; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HC0C5123177F04987A8C3642431E4DEFB"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the issuance of any such waiver (or an extension thereof), and why such waiver or extension was necessary, by not later than 72 hours after such issuance.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H3F93CD0DE8B94BDD9105F680CF1C1E7F" commented="no"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Small passenger vessels with overnight accommodations</header> <paragraph id="H52495CFCF53F4F39BA76C2364EB29A1F" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Extension authority</header> <subparagraph id="HAF3ED532C7D54259992FDF65B1638133" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Commandant of the Coast Guard shall not enforce the requirements of section 3306(n)(3)(A)(v) of title 46, United States Code, against an operator of an overnight fishing charter before April 1, 2024.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H369FE956159F4A1B85ED963F9B924174" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Plan required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than April 1, 2024, an operator of an overnight fishing charter not in compliance with such section 3306(n)(3)(A)(v) shall submit to the Commandant a plan for complying with such requirements.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HCB2364F545074A90AF9959FD0D0944E4" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Extension</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">On and after April 1, 2024, with respect to an operator of an overnight fishing charter which has submitted a plan for compliance in accordance with subparagraph (B), a captain of the port may extend the period described under subparagraph (A) until a date not later than January 1, 2026.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H15B094EAB77847F492B37D2E140BB712" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Limitation</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Without further Congressional action, a captain of the port may not extend the period of nonenforcement of the requirements of section 3306(n)(3)(A)(v) of title 46, United States Code, with respect to an overnight fishing charter, to a date later than January 1, 2026.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDE24AC9DF543458AAF113223E34DB272" commented="no"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Notice to passengers</header><text>Beginning on the date on which the requirements under section 3306(n)(3)(A)(v) of title 46, United States Code, take effect, the owner or operator of a vessel for which an extension is granted under paragraph (1)(C) shall provide on the website of such owner or operator of the vessel, the vessel, and each ticket for a passenger a prominently displayed notice that the vessel is exempt from meeting the Coast Guard safety compliance standards concerning egress as described in such section.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF5356086D1A940269965D4D1547E2CAC" commented="no"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Overnight fishing charter defined</header><text>In this section, the term <term>overnight fishing charter</term> means a vessel that—</text> <subparagraph id="HBB8269E2ECBC4360BF8A0A32A6DF01EC" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text>is engaged in <term>charter fishing</term> as such term is defined in section 3 of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/16/1802">16 U.S.C. 1802</external-xref>); and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H18244FD045594DFC9A883E1292F92EE7" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>has overnight accommodations for passengers.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H1673A6478D344B4EAB0FB549A56F5EFF"><enum>3532.</enum><header>Recapitalization of National Defense Reserve Fleet</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 3546 of the James M. <section id="H0F9D4757AE244E449EB7485B180A333D" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>3533.</enum><header>United States Merchant Marine Academy and Coast Guard Academy matters; Maritime Administration requirements</header> 
<subsection id="H291D7228BEE84C01A81E5D08F90EE5FB"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Training course on workings of Congress</header> 
<paragraph id="HFE2F4606DEE147C5A651B3555C66AE19"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this section, the Secretary of Transportation, in consultation with the Maritime Administrator, the Superintendent of the United States Merchant Marine Academy, and such other individuals and organizations as the Secretary of Transportation considers appropriate, shall develop a training course on the workings of Congress and offer that training course at least once each year. This course shall be similar in design to the training course required under section 315 of title 14, United States Code, as practicable.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB75E60419FE3419ABC916100D6B5082E"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Course subject matter</header><text>The training course required by paragraph (1) shall provide an overview and introduction to Congress and the Federal legislative process, including—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HA0C8B812BDFF4F9C92A530975F6239B9"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the history and structure of Congress and the committee systems of the Senate and the House of Representatives, including the functions and responsibilities of the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H8F3734FCDF0E4376836E046D905CB202"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the documents produced by Congress, including bills, resolutions, committee reports, and conference reports, and the purposes and functions of those documents;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HA0AC2D8CD5204C60A2FEE773B43ADB61"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the legislative processes and rules of the Senate and the House of Representatives, including similarities and differences between the processes and rules of each chamber, including—</text> <clause id="HBCB1D1B709DD4656AF367678B64D76EA"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the congressional budget process;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HDAA3317EE54B4CC78CA08C91074B8102"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the congressional authorization and appropriations processes;</text></clause> <clause id="H8D804AA7B38D4B3BB62E301881C161DC"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the Senate advice and consent process for Presidential nominees; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HB64F47652B2D4F788B79C5708B0E81F6"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>the Senate advice and consent process for treaty ratification;</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H65EA9517B13E469AAEEEE5D4EC9635BD"><enum>(D)</enum><text>the roles of Members of Congress and congressional staff in the legislative process; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HD376B53935334545AD25DC4DCD47A702"><enum>(E)</enum><text>the concept and underlying purposes of congressional oversight within the governance framework of separation of powers of the United States.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA9EF3A1324D341E8900D9BD3D0097219"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Lecturers and panelists</header> <subparagraph id="H540D13691FE340738CC5A24B1DD63847"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Outside experts</header><text>The Secretary of Transportation shall ensure that not less than 60 percent of the lecturers, panelists, and other individuals providing education and instruction as part of the training course required by this subsection are bipartisan subject matter experts on Congress and the Federal legislative process who are not employed by the executive branch of the Federal Government.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H8319F75E5FF947D9A7DFBD3C8AA8BA5D"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Authority to accept pro bono services</header><text>In satisfying the requirement under subparagraph (A), the Secretary of Transportation shall seek, and may accept, educational and instructional services of lecturers, panelists, and other individuals and organizations provided to the Department of Transportation on a pro bono basis.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H14FBCACA5A8942C7A900590435479F0A"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Completion of required training</header> <subparagraph id="HBE9528BEC8F849969A2E958BAFE2D690"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 60 days after the date on which the Secretary of Transportation completes the development of the training course described in this section, and annually thereafter while serving in applicable positions, the covered individuals described in subparagraph (B) shall complete the training course described in this subsection.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H5FE71D6F11C349C8999A0C8B6DADB53E"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Covered individuals</header><text>The covered individuals in this subsection are the following:</text> <clause id="HCB8FF35A09054629A93228CD2E1BA253"><enum>(i)</enum><text>The Administrator of the Maritime Administration and the Deputy Administrator of the Maritime Administration.</text></clause> 
<clause id="HD7C57B33C756446DA2D1AF0F4142101B"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>Any official of the Maritime Administration whose appointment is subject to the advice and consent of the Senate and Maritime Administration employees that are serving in a Senior Executive Service position (as defined in section 3132(a) of title 5, United States Code).</text></clause> <clause id="H90801593208B422499DE281E04CF656B"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>Any Maritime Administration employees whose duties consist of engagement with congressional, governmental, or public affairs, who are appointed or assigned to a billet in the National Capital Region on the date on which the Secretary of Transportation completes the development of the training course described in this section.</text></clause> 
<clause id="H16D5E984C5E54A1B99BAA0ED3D30D4D1"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>The Superintendent, Deputy Superintendent, Provost, Commandant of Midshipmen, Counsel, and Director of Public Affairs of the United States Merchant Marine Academy.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE18FED5EFE314A8A887B021939E75550"><enum>(C)</enum><header>New officials and employees</header><text>Any Maritime Administration official or employee or United States Merchant Marine Academy official or employee who is a covered individual described in subparagraph (B) who is newly appointed, newly employed in the National Capital Region, or newly employed by the United States Merchant Marine Academy after the date on which the Secretary of Transportation completes the development of the training course described in this subsection, shall complete a training course that meets the requirements of this subsection not later than 60 days after reporting for duty, and annually thereafter, while serving in applicable positions.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H5B4BB45C336F4006A21E89A9B09E13A6"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Government Accountability Office report on Maritime Administration staffing requirements</header> 
<paragraph id="H414AF0A41F12433F836DB0769D278637"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than six months after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives, a report that includes an analysis of the staffing requirements for effectively executing the mission of the Maritime Administration and an identification of any existing gaps that could impede its operations.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H91567E0C3DD94EBC80813FD606C4229B"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Contents</header><text>The report under paragraph (1) shall include—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H5A83D85650CF49E1A1148126FB82C83B"><enum>(A)</enum><text>an evaluation of the personnel requirements for the successful execution of the mission of the Maritime Administration, including such requirements for—</text> <clause id="H565229FDD7574B2284F8482DEA65CB87"><enum>(i)</enum><text>those offices that deal with infrastructure, shipbuilding, or student safety;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HF590E9508E704BE5BE3FBEF86016ECA6"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">those offices that have significant delays in meeting constituent needs, including offices involved in the processing of permits and grants, or which preform a communication or outreach function to the public, constituents, or Congress (including the Office of Public Affairs of the Maritime Administration);</text></clause> <clause id="H5943C591BBA54A9CBE0C2BBA1FBDEAEE"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the United States Merchant Marine Academy; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HA3C1298917F64C0C82860AE05E59B023"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>other activities carried out by the Maritime Administration;</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HFBFD4D2EFD384EFB9E38EE06346906CE"><enum>(B)</enum><text>a thorough analysis of any deficiencies or inadequacies in staffing levels, at the time the report is submitted, that could hinder the efficient functioning of the Maritime Administration; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H1F3E992C7BEE46529611DD73F2122786"><enum>(C)</enum><text>recommendations for integrating the findings of the report into the policies and planning processes of the Maritime Administration, with the aim of addressing the identified gaps and enhancing the overall effectiveness of the Maritime Administration.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H68751682594043E9960EC1BC867BC35E"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Coast Guard Academy improvement briefing</header><text>Not later than 30 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Commandant of the Coast Guard shall provide to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate a briefing on—</text> 
<paragraph id="HB78CDE92D4CB488DA6C2A2848105C383"><enum>(1)</enum><text>a plan, which shall include timelines and cost estimates, to—</text> <subparagraph id="H6AC8524BA00743AF8CF8CB2B8A1B161F"><enum>(A)</enum><text>remediate asbestos, lead, and mold from the Chase Hall of the Coast Guard Academy;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H591EEAB14047498DB6657B8266E4EE4E"><enum>(B)</enum><text>house not more than two students to a room in Chase Hall; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H58279EA22C744A688E6C26F3C84079B4"><enum>(C)</enum><text>upgrade electric outlet availability and storage space in student rooms at Chase Hall; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF6BB3FE865894818A5E42BF8C7DC0E13"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the increased student housing capacity necessary to allow the Coast Guard to put through sufficient officers to eliminate the current portion of the officer shortfall due to space constraints at the Coast Guard Academy, including the Officer Candidate School and direct Commission Officer Program housed at the Academy.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HA777EAB86FD24D3C8161825B5953794B"><enum>3534.</enum><header>Maritime workforce working group</header> <subsection id="H53AB930E9386402A8FFBF08E6E88DF0C"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Maritime Administrator, in consultation with the National Merchant Marine Personnel Advisory Committee, the National Offshore Safety Advisory Committee, the National Towing Safety Advisory Committee, and the Committee on the Marine Transportation System, shall convene a working group to examine and assess the size of the pool of mariners with covered credentials necessary to support the United States flag fleet.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H75CD50A9B7D64CAAADF181004228B08F"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Membership</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Maritime Administrator shall designate individuals to serve as members of the working group convened under subsection (a). The working group shall consist of—</text> <paragraph id="HBE057D143BE24E8BBF88588A25683515"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the Maritime Administrator, who shall serve as chairperson of the working group;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5D35DEACA3BD45E7B1163C77DA00A0B9"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the Superintendent of the United States Merchant Marine Academy;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H8C41C0A4B1CD41B280276C47D64B715D"><enum>(3)</enum><text>the Commandant of the Coast Guard;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD78FCB0CD7D74F08A5E15EB92F709139"><enum>(4)</enum><text>the Commander of the United States Transportation Command; </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5D239987193E4F24B35EC4AE50ADA540"><enum>(5)</enum><text>the Secretary of the Navy; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2096163DAC874AB4B0E78003175EFE3C"><enum>(6)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">at least one representative from each of—</text> <subparagraph id="H95AD5D05857747339089D6CF59894205"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the State maritime academies;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HE54EA8FFE02A4F2CA0FF1FB18E47947F"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the owners and operators of United States-flagged vessels engaged in offshore oil and gas exploration, development, and production;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HAD6B0DA828C9496DB6679C5C6E68C383"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the owners and operators of United States-flagged vessels engaged in inland river transportation;</text></subparagraph>

<subparagraph id="HDBA81B6BA8AA439AA537751A46CA9CDD"><enum>(F)</enum><text>a nonprofit labor organization representing a class of licensed or unlicensed mariners who are employed on vessels operating in the United States flag fleet;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HCF770C7C1245414C827E0FB4B440BDA8"><enum>(G)</enum><text>the owners of vessels operating in the United States flag fleet, or their private contracting parties, that are primarily operating in international transportation;</text></subparagraph>

<subsection id="HBBEDCA9151744B2D938230AF3833B845"><enum>(c)</enum><header>No quorum requirement</header><text>The Maritime Administrator may convene the working group virtually and without all members present.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H35791978938F49D388DDE046C950C979"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Responsibilities</header><text>The working group shall carry out the following responsibilities:</text> 
<paragraph id="H489EF8036519455398C20882B9E78095" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Reviewing the report required by section 3525(b), and the study required by section 3545(a), of the James Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/263">Public Law 117–263</external-xref>), if available.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HD21061C9AE4A4A18A028F7A48797E658"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Identifying the number of mariners with covered credentials in each of the following categories:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H68BEA83DFFED41459A20FE8DFD7C5855"><enum>(A)</enum><text>All such mariners.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H7416C342D5CC40B5B3F0E42C724FAA11"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Such mariners who have a valid Coast Guard merchant mariner credential with the necessary endorsements for service on unlimited tonnage vessels that are subject to the International Convention on Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping for Seafarers, 1978, as amended.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HEE627C7579854904BE234BD121EE78EB"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Such mariners who are participating in a Federal program that supports the United States merchant marine and the United States flag fleet.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H54DBA1E808A24086858C4089ABF1249D"><enum>(D)</enum><text>Such mariners who are available to crew the United States flag fleet and the surge sealift fleet in times of a national emergency.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4DE3BEBB66794D2C9A3C75A743EB11EB"><enum>(E)</enum><text>Such mariners who are full-time.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HFD3328C4CF4E432DA83AF18AA8E54564"><enum>(F)</enum><text>Such mariners who are merchant mariner credentialed officers in the United States Navy Reserve.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC61B8D5991D8460C88533B11C7F3C22E"><enum>(G)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Such licensed and unlicensed mariners—</text> <clause id="H3546BB97AC654752955A629D306698D3"><enum>(i)</enum><text>required to maintain, mobilize, and operate the entire Ready Reserve Force for periods of 30 days, 90 days, 180 days, and one year including separate totals for merchant mariners employed to maintain the Ready Reserve Force in a reduced operating status; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H743E229AA8254C62970DFF6391C57C26"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>required to submit documentation of sea service to the National Maritime Center, including such mariners that have acquired sea service during the prior year and such mariners that have not acquired sea service during the prior year.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H581386DBCBCE495E920A50B3150419AD"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Evaluating potential gaps or surpluses of credentialed merchant mariners, by rating and qualification, required to maintain, mobilize, and operate the Ready Reserve Force for periods of 30 days, 90 days, 180 days, and one year and the potential impacts such mobilization and operation will have on the commercial maritime industry’s capability to operate during such periods. </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H091904405B994DF88F43B13748004501"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Identifying a list of all actively operating documented vessels of at least 500 gross registered tons, as measured under section 14502 of title 46, United States Code, or an alternate tonnage measured under section 14302 of such title as prescribed by the Secretary under section 14104, of such title, with the tonnage of each such vessel. </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5E293B990E434375BB270CD2B98C2DBB"><enum>(5)</enum><text>Assessing the effect on the United States merchant marine and United States Merchant Marine Academy if graduates from State maritime academies and the United States Merchant Marine Academy were assigned to, or required to fulfill, certain maritime positions based on the overall needs of the United States merchant marine.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1D6C45AD25BD4383A579E1EE4B892227"><enum>(6)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Assessing the effectiveness of marketing and outreach efforts, including recruitment and retention strategy and methods of publicizing opportunities, for new mariner accession into the maritime industry. </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC0097B24F3A1446FBEA20C779CFCF27C"><enum>(7)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Assessing the accessibility of Coast Guard Merchant Mariner Licensing and Documentation System data for mariners with covered credentials, the maritime industry, and the Maritime Administration for the purposes of evaluating the pool of mariners with covered credentials.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCC5255621033401AA1929EDB2A4FEEAD"><enum>(8)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Assessing the impediments to the credentialing of United States merchant mariners, including training capacity, credentialing system delays, costs to merchant mariners, statutory or regulatory requirements, and other factors. </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9CFE92EF59584C409AA2571EAF1743A3"><enum>(9)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Making recommendations to—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H1AA2A71308AC4AB680D2BEE5B83BB396"><enum>(A)</enum><text>enhance the availability and quality of interagency data, including data from the United States Transportation Command, the Coast Guard, the Navy, and the Bureau of Transportation Statistics, for use by the Maritime Administration in evaluating the pool of mariners with covered credentials;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9996B60DAE84454881F6F73936FD8413"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">close any gaps identified in the evaluation described in paragraph (3), including specific policy, legislative change proposals, and funding requests; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC23C6372D01C46ACB8231A25510583C4"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">improve United States merchant mariner recruitment and retention.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H58D6F0E064E24B86A0A9867C524DCAE2"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Provision of information</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">All members of the working group convened under subsection (a) shall provide to the Maritime Administrator, in a timely manner and in a suitable format agreed to by members, any information that is needed to carry out the responsibilities under subsection (d). </text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H71B88019CA3048068912B344463BAA1F"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Transportation shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate, the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives, and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a report that contains the findings and conclusions of the working group gathered in the course of performing the responsibilities under subsection (d). Such report shall include each of the following:</text> <paragraph id="H9DB875A48D8944C7B857CE755151B39B"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The number of mariners with covered credentials identified for each category described in subparagraphs (A) through (G) of subsection (d)(2). </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2948D5DD915B43438D7AB18805A6485B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The results of the evaluation under subsection (d)(3).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF3CE0B796A784245933CE9ADAEB12DA3"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The list identified under subsection (d)(4).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H4E91DE1C766B487EAA62131D2D7D44E3"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The results of the assessments conducted under paragraphs (5) and (8) of subsection (d).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA05366BE25D84BC8A14D10A1FC3C1380"><enum>(5)</enum><text>The recommendations made under paragraphs (5) and (9) of subsection (d).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HEE9CE30880AA457389FBEB26655BE69A"><enum>(6)</enum><text>Such other information as the working group determines appropriate.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H3AA65ED94EDC4DB3B4C79973D8C2455F"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Classified annex</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The report required under this section shall be submitted in unclassified form, but shall include a classified annex including the results from subsection (d)(2)(G) and subsection (d)(3). </text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H3E22B3288BDA4F3395901FDC20654EBA"><enum>(h)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section:</text> <paragraph id="H1C02E2286AD94953AD30026AC2B67BBD"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The term <term>covered credential</term> means any credential issued under part E of subtitle II of title 46, United States Code.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H71536229571A47C08DB9A38DFF548A91"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The term <term>documented vessel</term> has the meaning given the term in section 106 of title 46, United States Code.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H4A3500ACA34042D0BC0B11E30B491FB1"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The term <term>Ready Reserve Force</term> has the meaning given the term in <external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/46/571">chapter 571</external-xref> of title 46, United States Code.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H2892C702571946B4A20885DA4210DFD7"><enum>(i)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text>The Maritime Administrator shall disband the working group upon the submission of the report required under subsection (f).</text></subsection> <subsection id="HE7BD00AAAE3A419EA3FBD76E797BD916"><enum>(j)</enum><header>Temporary reduction of lengths of certain periods of service</header><text>For the 3-year period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act—</text> 
<paragraph id="H73628DEC0F1A4D099F3CF78553182670"><enum>(1)</enum><text>section 7307 of title 46, United States Code, shall be applied by substituting <quote>18 months</quote> for <quote>3 years</quote>;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H8AD2CECE9FA14D899F6A83FD2C2053EE"><enum>(2)</enum><text>section 7308 of such title shall be applied by substituting <quote>12 months</quote> for <quote>18 months</quote>; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H183CDB5D8CAA425EAB1949FC4E1ABB12"><enum>(3)</enum><text>section 7309 of such title shall be applied by substituting <quote>6 months</quote> for <quote>12 months</quote>.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H82DBED76C50E48C8B4B6516F6C47805C"><enum>(k)</enum><header>Centers of excellence for domestic maritime workforce training and education</header><text>Section 51706 of title 46, United States Code, is amended—</text> 
<paragraph id="HC8801FC707494CB9A9471F9F78750703"><enum>(1)</enum><text>in subsection (a)—</text> <subparagraph id="HAE95E310C991472985E8B5333FA6384A"><enum>(A)</enum><text>by striking <quote>The Secretary</quote> and inserting the following:</text>

<section id="H983A2AFAC059493297BD191C535DFE86"><enum>3536.</enum><header>Loans for retrofitting to qualify as a vessel of the United States</header> 
<subsection id="H7A19B547E2F84EB1B9E04DBB07FF19E7"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Section 53706(a) of title 46, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" id="H81A1D92BACF844D080232AE9F9BFBF81"> <paragraph id="H509336E75A25446081CF131C076FB005"><enum>(8)</enum><text>Financing (including reimbursement of an obligor for expenditures previously made for) the reconstruction, reconditioning, retrofitting, repair, reconfiguration, or similar work in a shipyard located in the United States.</text></paragraph><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subsection> 
<subsection id="H392A33ECFA03461DAC33C25B1D979F75"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Prohibition on use of appropriated funds</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Amounts appropriated to the Maritime Administration before the date of enactment of this Act shall not be available to be used for the cost of loan guarantees for projects receiving financing support or credit enhancements under section 53706(a)(8) of title 46, United States Code, as added by this section. </text></subsection></section> <section id="H3722E996D17841688AB3B588BBF38375"><enum>3537.</enum><header>Accountability for National Maritime Strategy</header> <subsection id="HDF7BF4BE60EA498A92CBCE914EAB9E55"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Biannual briefing</header> <paragraph id="H1E351F6D243F48A18C2F13A8527E3CCC"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Requirement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not less than twice annually, the Administrator of the Maritime Administration, in consultation with the National Security Council, the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Transportation, and the Secretary of Homeland Security, shall provide to the appropriate congressional committees briefings on the status of establishing the type of national maritime strategy required under section 50114 of title 46, United States Code. The Chief of Naval Operations, the Commandant of the Marine Corps, and the Commandant of the Coast Guard shall participate in each briefing required under this paragraph.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H61DB53BBDC9C4EA484FBBB86B2729B8B"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Use</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Administrator shall use the briefings required under paragraph (1) to augment and influence the national maritime strategy discussion with national security focused stakeholders across the administration, until an updated strategy is published and endorsed by the President of the United States.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H0830F5162F2F4E18BD9E92462F75A11E"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>As the national maritime strategy relates to national security, each briefing under subsection (a) shall include the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="HE297C7F8296441139E4F6B0181E57D32"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Recommendations for a whole-of-Government approach to orchestrating national instruments of power to shape all elements of the maritime enterprise of the United States, domestic and international, on the high seas or domestic waterways.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H20474E7DFA8D45AC99BAA668FDDCB8A6"><enum>(2)</enum><text>An assessment of great power competition in the maritime domain, to include opportunities for increased cooperation with allied and partner global maritime industry leaders to improve national shipbuilding and shipping, while promoting the international rules-based maritime order.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H24EA3B9D018B49AEB36E3A4F49C0CCCC"><enum>(3)</enum><text>An analysis of existing shipyards to build and capitalize on the virtuous cycle between commercial and military shipbuilding and repair, including areas of improvement.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA6ADE586713A439EBEE06AC5C565014B"><enum>(4)</enum><text>An analysis of opportunities for private or public financing to increase the capacity, efficiency, and effectiveness of United States shipyards, including infrastructure, labor force, technology, and global competitiveness.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD0A829F0BCC7433689CE6FEB6D131014"><enum>(5)</enum><text>An analysis of potential improvements to national or cooperative arrangements for sealift capacity and shipping, including for contested logistics.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HFBEC4D8D31E249EA86D15DA823EF537D"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Appropriate congressional committees</header><text>In this section, the term <quote>appropriate congressional committees</quote> means—</text> 
<paragraph id="H67E9A335C3A445A1969D814D48A940B2"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the congressional defense committees;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H09D8A19356A840B2B0904C51CEE32167"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H760DC2905ADE408FBF088EAC2912DBAD"><enum>(3)</enum><text>the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate.</text></paragraph></subsection></section></subtitle></title></division> <division id="H18EF6ED48F184288A102891449C2E5C9"><enum>D</enum><header>Funding Tables</header> <section id="HA134C8CF996C4E2CA26D76242217FBCA" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>4001.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Authorization of amounts in funding tables</header> <subsection id="H7D6B89EF228340BAA9E55FB80A59D837" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Whenever a funding table in this division specifies a dollar amount authorized for a project, program, or activity, the obligation and expenditure of the specified dollar amount for the project, program, or activity is hereby authorized, subject to the availability of appropriations.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H118A02CFED254581ACAEC91B64C27A47" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Merit-based decisions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A decision to commit, obligate, or expend funds with or to a specific entity on the basis of a dollar amount authorized pursuant to subsection (a) shall—</text> <paragraph id="H6E1BB775E7CD40FEAB951A06030FB446" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">be based on merit-based selection procedures in accordance with the requirements of sections 3201 and 4024 of title 10, United States Code, or on competitive procedures; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0462688ACD844316A0A60C6B650A99D6" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">comply with other applicable provisions of law.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HBDB1413B10764E35AD73A06AA02D3197" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Relationship to transfer and programming authority</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An amount specified in the funding tables in this division may be transferred or reprogrammed under a transfer or reprogramming authority provided by another provision of this Act or by other law. The transfer or reprogramming of an amount specified in such funding tables shall not count against a ceiling on such transfers or reprogrammings under section 1001 of this Act or any other provision of law, unless such transfer or reprogramming would move funds between appropriation accounts.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA861A6E30CBA4F41A8744BE4082FD662" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(d)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Applicability to classified annex</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">This section applies to any classified annex that accompanies this Act.</text></subsection> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H20D53EC1910E48B7AD1D4AD4BE1C1032"><enum>(e)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Oral or written communications</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">No oral or written communication concerning any amount specified in the funding tables in this division shall supersede the requirements of this section.</text></subsection></section>

<section section-type="subsequent-section" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H646468748D9943DC89AA0245B005421A"><enum>5001.</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Adjustment of threshold amount for minor medical facility projects of Department of Veterans Affairs</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 8104(a) of title 38, United States Code, is amended— </text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HEA2A52DD4E3D45FF97046FDABFA5C420"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">in paragraph (3)(A), by striking <quote>$20,000,000</quote> each place it appears and inserting <quote>the amount specified in paragraph (4)</quote>; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H5D9A73C6EF3C47C39CE2922BA1E18E1D"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by adding at the end the following new paragraph:</text> <quoted-block id="HB3D91A27C87D425EA8EC7BFD33C377D8" display-inline="no-display-inline" style="OLC"> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2B71A59FC0E045108C1B4F6516B077A8" indent="up1"><enum>(4)</enum> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="yes-display-inline" id="HD1E5278F2F274A479A9821FDE8385E8C"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The amount specified in this paragraph is $30,000,000, as adjusted pursuant to this paragraph.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph indent="up1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H78B17874BB2B434E89FA8E2EC609A63D"><enum>(B)</enum> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="yes-display-inline" id="H0273192F483B4559A59CAD309F44E1C6"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary may annually adjust the amount specified in this paragraph to reflect a percentage increase, if any, in construction costs during the prior calendar year, as determined by—</text> <subclause indent="up1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H6E816D24A47647DA890D85A3EE16767C"><enum>(I)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the relevant composite construction and lease cost indices pursuant to section 3307(h) of title 40, or any similar successor index developed by the Administrator of the General Services Administration; or</text></subclause> 
<subclause indent="up1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H8FD60D63017044358211D728A00860CA"><enum>(II)</enum><text>the Producer Price Index for New Health Care Building Construction published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics of the Department of Labor, or any similar successor index developed by the Secretary of Labor.</text></subclause></clause> <clause indent="up1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H6871A796B5824BDD8A444AB21FBE5A60"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>If there is no percentage increase in construction costs determined as described in clause (i) for a calendar year, the Secretary may not adjust the amount specified in subparagraph (A) for that year. </text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph indent="up1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HCE3AA5F3C16D42DB9C4E158FFBC63BD3"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the Secretary adjusts the amount specified in this paragraph, the Secretary shall publish a notice of such adjustment in the Federal Register.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph indent="up1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H8B0D2B6FDBAD43FAA52647325E2A78A1"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 30 days before adjusting the amount specified in this paragraph, the Secretary shall notify the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate and the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph>
