<subtitle id="HEFA6FA649A56456096605E053BDD0EB8" style="OLC"><enum>A</enum><header>Combating Global Corruption</header> 
<section section-type="subsequent-section" id="HC6198C033F054EF29474C8B71FBC05D3" changed="not-changed"><enum>5401.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This subtitle may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Combating Global Corruption Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section> <section id="H2659EA91D5F14AFDB760CD0514F064AC" changed="not-changed"><enum>5402.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In this subtitle:</text> 
<paragraph id="H8FF559CD432549508225E3FE1429F7BA"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The term <term>appropriate congressional committees</term> means—</text> <subparagraph id="H960DCF77F4E24CFCA11F7A773C308F5E"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on Appropriations, the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, and the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H763C2F2297B4499A89BBF7532601B445"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Committee on Foreign Affairs, the Committee on Appropriations, the Committee on Financial Services, and the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2C1E669D491B4EAAA03C03ED74B3EF51" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The term <term>corrupt actor</term> means—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H75A43E4242684112A672909016113412" changed="not-changed"><enum>(A)</enum><text>any foreign person or entity that is a government official or government entity responsible for, or complicit in, an act of corruption; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H97F832CE3FCB47D295668AD56E975B19" changed="not-changed"><enum>(B)</enum><text>any company, in which a person or entity described in subparagraph (A) has a significant stake, which is responsible for, or complicit in, an act of corruption.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5F17918297204982AF78560FBFF48410"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The term <term>corruption</term> means the unlawful exercise of entrusted public power for private gain, including by bribery, nepotism, fraud, or embezzlement.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6A9121094C1D46128D0A5A33161A8550"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The term <term>significant corruption</term> means corruption committed at a high level of government that has some or all of the following characteristics:</text> 
<subparagraph id="HBF8AE49E0C9F4634B16B5F27BC62709D"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Illegitimately distorts major decision-making, such as policy or resource determinations, or other fundamental functions of governance.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2C1A85893CE04D828F125B5275BFA86C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Involves economically or socially large-scale government activities. </text></subparagraph></paragraph></section> 
<section id="H4835BA46B84047F3A8B85DA96D3F7F5D"><enum>5403.</enum><header>Publication and provision of lists regarding progress on anti-corruption efforts</header> 
<subsection id="H08EDF070B0C24ACD8019688B3A20BB33"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Public list</header><text>The Secretary of State shall publish annually, on a publicly accessible website, a list of foreign countries where the government is sustaining or making good progress on anti-corruption efforts in accordance with the minimum standards set forth in section 5404. Such list shall include a brief description of each such country’s progress or justification for being on such list.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H19501F3765A64762BCFF6F6B98E91102"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Classified list</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of State shall provide to the appropriate congressional committees a classified list of countries where the government is making limited or no efforts to comply with minimum standards set forth in section 5404, and are not achieving meaningful progress on combating corruption. Such list shall include a brief description of each country’s lack of progress or justification for being on such list.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA1E2F14FE5AE4EE3AACFA329EDDBCD29"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Annual update</header><text>The Secretary of State shall provide an annual update in a classified setting to the appropriate congressional committees on the United States Government’s efforts to fight against corruption. This update should include an overview of the key obstacles to combating corruption and present near-term and long-term strategies.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HB7BF87B5422441EDB3AB3EBEC4A212D8"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Implementation and timing</header> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HECF18E5004A54ED39B085D54D12408E6"><enum>(1)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Deadline</header><text>The publication and submission of the lists and the annual update required by subsections (a), (b), and (c) shall be completed not later than 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter for seven years.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H60CFE2DC936F4C7FB4C01CA8564D85DE"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Report on methodology</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report detailing the methodology developed to assign countries to either the public list or the classified list and a proposed budget for preparing the first set of lists during the subsequent year.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HE78448A3263C4FD3A1EB0AC1F8DE9B8C"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Exception to publication</header><text>The Secretary may, in specific instances where the Secretary determines the inclusion of specific countries on the public list required by subsection (a) would not be in the national interests of the United States, submit the information required by subsection (a) about such specific countries in a classified manner in writing to the appropriate congressional committees, together with a justification for why publication would not be in the national interest. The justification, if applicable, shall be submitted the same date as the public list required by subsection (a).</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="HCEC17F31BDFE477D85DFA03CB1D2E853" changed="not-changed"><enum>5404.</enum><header>Minimum standards for the elimination of corruption and assessment of efforts to combat corruption</header> 
<subsection id="H45E00AAF915743768C82DF9867C84249" changed="not-changed"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The government of a country is complying with the minimum standards for the elimination of corruption if the government—</text> <paragraph id="H0DEF16FE17A8427FAABC7A6F8D3046F4" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><text>has enacted and implemented laws and established government structures, policies, and practices that prohibit corruption, including significant corruption;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA5D8CFF6086B486BB439946A69BCDFF1" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><text>enforces the laws described in paragraph (1) by punishing any person who is found, through a fair judicial process, to have violated such laws;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H1D1E0C60B9BD46DFBE370ED945FD8192" changed="not-changed"><enum>(3)</enum><text>prescribes punishment for significant corruption that is commensurate with the punishment prescribed for serious crimes; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC7FEE7575582402E8A668EB577B6EEFC" changed="not-changed"><enum>(4)</enum><text>is making serious and sustained efforts to address corruption, including through prevention.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HC2847CD7EFCF4EED8AFA2D952D99025A" changed="not-changed"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Factors for assessing government efforts To combat corruption</header><text>In determining whether a government is making serious and sustained efforts to address corruption, the Secretary of State shall consider, to the extent relevant or appropriate, factors such as—</text> 
<paragraph id="H3EC4BD7403664BB7A062A517099C4D29" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><text>whether the government of the country has criminalized corruption, investigates and prosecutes acts of corruption, and convicts and sentences persons responsible for such acts over which it has jurisdiction, including, as appropriate, incarcerating individuals convicted of such acts; </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC17EC84A3E714D829DFA7AF486E61BE3" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><text>whether the government of the country vigorously investigates, prosecutes, convicts, and sentences public officials who participate in or facilitate corruption, including nationals of the country who are deployed in foreign military assignments, trade delegations abroad, or other similar missions, who engage in or facilitate significant corruption;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H4DFB813CB69E4957841656CCB724E761" changed="not-changed"><enum>(3)</enum><text>whether the government of the country has adopted measures to prevent corruption, such as measures to inform and educate the public, including potential victims, about the causes and consequences of corruption;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5049C901FA004F82A191245A36F45064" changed="not-changed"><enum>(4)</enum><text>what steps the government of the country has taken to prohibit government officials from participating in, facilitating, or condoning corruption, including the investigation, prosecution, and conviction of such officials;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1262AE5880EA4FBEB031C99FC5EF5D34" changed="not-changed"><enum>(5)</enum><text>the extent to which the country provides access, or, as appropriate, makes adequate resources available, to civil society organizations and other institutions to combat corruption, including reporting, investigating, and monitoring;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H98D2DB7F8F224BC8A71775766B76875B" changed="not-changed"><enum>(6)</enum><text>whether an independent judiciary or judicial body in the country is responsible for, and effectively capable of, deciding corruption cases impartially, on the basis of facts and in accordance with the law, without any improper restrictions, influences, inducements, pressures, threats, or interferences (direct or indirect);</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H05741B54384E465994200FEDEA0952E9" changed="not-changed"><enum>(7)</enum><text>whether the government of the country is assisting in international investigations of transnational corruption networks and in other cooperative efforts to combat significant corruption, including, as appropriate, cooperating with the governments of other countries to extradite corrupt actors;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE9345E798A25436182014FAD7AB2B1DC" changed="not-changed"><enum>(8)</enum><text>whether the government of the country recognizes the rights of victims of corruption, ensures their access to justice, and takes steps to prevent victims from being further victimized or persecuted by corrupt actors, government officials, or others;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC1236779482C4FA2AA09336D79CE332E" changed="not-changed"><enum>(9)</enum><text>whether the government of the country protects victims of corruption or whistleblowers from reprisal due to such persons having assisted in exposing corruption, and refrains from other discriminatory treatment of such persons;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF0151AEA3BB64C9DA8BECD7B0079B902" changed="not-changed"><enum>(10)</enum><text>whether the government of the country is willing and able to recover and, as appropriate, return the proceeds of corruption;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2818291A1926451987B0D4266D7091F4" changed="not-changed"><enum>(11)</enum><text>whether the government of the country is taking steps to implement financial transparency measures in line with the Financial Action Task Force recommendations, including due diligence and beneficial ownership transparency requirements; </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFDD1E49A61A04ECE878CAC79391FD9A7" changed="not-changed"><enum>(12)</enum><text>whether the government of the country is facilitating corruption in other countries in connection with state-directed investment, loans or grants for major infrastructure, or other initiatives; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H901B22F7E2BF43AFB911F78E599636FA" changed="not-changed"><enum>(13)</enum><text>such other information relating to corruption as the Secretary of State considers appropriate.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HA0B81522DC4B447D90766350B33F6B63" changed="not-changed"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Assessing government efforts to combat corruption in relation to relevant international commitments</header><text>In determining whether a government is making serious and sustained efforts to address corruption, the Secretary of State shall consider the government of a country’s compliance with the following, as relevant:</text> 
<paragraph id="HC2936EC2C2E147498EEDD6976D3038A0" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The Inter-American Convention against Corruption of the Organization of American States, done at Caracas March 29, 1996.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5FF892AADA154A748ABFD8A68D312E81" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The Convention on Combating Bribery of Foreign Public Officials in International Business Transactions of the Organisation of Economic Co-operation and Development, done at Paris December 21, 1997 (commonly referred to as the <quote>Anti-Bribery Convention</quote>).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H63BA923D585D4361A51A097B6996B33D" changed="not-changed"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime, done at New York November 15, 2000.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H44867C6C8334446DA52EB0362615F815" changed="not-changed"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The United Nations Convention against Corruption, done at New York October 31, 2003.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H953E88A44EE545AEA1EEF479E1AAC74F" changed="not-changed"><enum>(5)</enum><text>Such other treaties or conventions ratified by the United States as the Secretary of State considers appropriate. </text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HED705E33D4C749F69A73E6164E3523A2"><enum>5405.</enum><header>Imposition of sanctions under Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act</header> <subsection id="H637A7B952E494B97AB303ABA0D8D26C8"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, should evaluate whether there are foreign persons engaged in significant corruption for the purposes of potential imposition of sanctions under the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act (subtitle F of title XII of <external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/114/328">Public Law 114–328</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/10101">22 U.S.C. 10101 et seq.</external-xref>)—</text> 
<paragraph id="HA6E8DADB328C41BEAB5EFCB8E8E80303"><enum>(1)</enum><text>in all countries identified pursuant to section 5403(b); and</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HBBC3AB77903647279708A160A620D72B"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">in relation to the planning or construction or any operation of the Nord Stream 2 pipeline.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HB3F4DD0340FB4D8CBD345BA4B7978FA5"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Report required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after providing the list required by section 5403(b), and annually thereafter, the Secretary of State shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report that includes—</text> <paragraph id="H4D733941D450484F92002FD0C0CF50AB"><enum>(1)</enum><text>a list of foreign persons with respect to which the President imposed sanctions pursuant to the evaluation under subsection (a);</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H7EAEFFEAEA514DB1AA35CBED1E669F98"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the dates on which such sanctions were imposed;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H8F438CCB2B674DC0AB77702EFA3D7DBE"><enum>(3)</enum><text>the reasons for imposing such sanctions; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC33CAE57B0BC4E208A7D01D1B1A5BA7C"><enum>(4)</enum><text>a list of all foreign persons that have engaged in significant corruption in relation to the planning, construction, or operation of the Nord Stream 2 pipeline.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HCD3EEFB1EE4348F09E337AB008E37537"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Form of report</header><text>Each report required by subsection (b) shall be submitted in unclassified form but may include a classified annex.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H3B4616183C9A48E39BE017836E0CA857"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Briefing in lieu of report</header><text>The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, may, instead of submitting a written report required under subsection (b) (except with respect to the list required by subsection (b)(4)), provide to the appropriate congressional committees a briefing, together with a written justification, if doing so would better serve the national interests of the United States.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HD42B5041C122496E91416732EEAD674C"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Termination of requirements relating to nord stream 2</header><text>The requirements under subsections (a)(2) and (b)(4) shall terminate on the date that is 5 years after the date of the enactment of this Act.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H134E81E7FCF949C79F3BD5146EDB5471" changed="not-changed"><enum>5406.</enum><header>Designation of embassy anti-corruption points of contact</header> 
<subsection id="H08774336804643E0A14FC4AB471617CC"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of State shall annually designate an anti-corruption point of contact at the United States diplomatic post to each country identified pursuant to section 5403(b), or which the Secretary otherwise determines is in need of such a point of contact. The point of contact shall be the chief of mission or the chief of mission’s designee.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H5AE3866A8A474035A04A5319ED9DE9D8" changed="not-changed"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Responsibilities</header><text>Each anti-corruption point of contact designated under subsection (a) shall be responsible for enhancing coordination and promoting the implementation of a whole-of-government approach among the relevant Federal departments and agencies undertaking efforts to—</text> 
<paragraph id="H31DB2473521B4B9D8EDF5B4E5EC5CE83" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><text>promote good governance in foreign countries; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFE94AA775E8147CC887D5AC3F41D9382" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><text>enhance the ability of such countries—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HB4EFA2EFEF134E5CA76BDED01667A82B" changed="not-changed"><enum>(A)</enum><text>to combat public corruption; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HC1EF6C54F4E74228B26689ECBB54D166" changed="not-changed"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to develop and implement corruption risk assessment tools and mitigation strategies.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HFC08ABEA39D1401FBF1397B5F8712090" changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Training</header><text>The Secretary of State shall implement appropriate training for anti-corruption points of contact designated under subsection (a).</text></subsection></section></subtitle> <subtitle id="H89551B8874664CE887F8634B4B43E38B"><enum>B</enum><header>Other Matters</header> <section id="H7E672BA6A546406DBCE4B24117E20614" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>5411.</enum><header>Global cooperative framework to end human rights abuses in sourcing critical minerals</header> <subsection id="H319684C856C845C6B3C5D1263EF775B5"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of State shall seek to convene a meeting of foreign leaders to establish a multilateral framework to end human rights abuses, including the exploitation of forced labor and child labor, related to the mining and sourcing of critical minerals.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H24352B37942E4F8BA9E0115BDF363D03"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Implementation report</header><text>The Secretary shall lead the development of an annual global report on the implementation of the framework under subsection (a), including progress and recommendations to fully end human rights abuses, including the exploitation of forced labor and child labor, related to the extraction of critical minerals around the world.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HEDD9376D27BB426496659F13D15D87D1"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Consultations</header><text>The Secretary shall consult closely on a timely basis with the following with respect to developing and implementing the framework under subsection (a):</text> 
<paragraph id="H27B2C3E0B361408C932B8A6C4CFF0573"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force established under section 741 of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement Implementation Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/19/4681">19 U.S.C. 4681</external-xref>); and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H38DD507C500945E9AED89923A6FA7BE0"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Congress.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HEC8D628DA2D44983A3445A9459AED346"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Relationship to United States law</header><text>Nothing in the framework under subsection (a) shall be construed—</text> <paragraph id="HEFBE33EC8E7A4986BD55331EB9F2ECA5"><enum>(1)</enum><text>to amend or modify any law of the United States; or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H79977AF1B4944E338AF656FE72A8F475"><enum>(2)</enum><text>to limit any authority conferred under any law of the United States. </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HA562BAC126E74737970C5416EEFBF965"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative and Certain Provisions of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act</header><text>Nothing in this section shall—</text> 
<paragraph id="HE0F9BC2AED684CF19F4F3C0789E527E0"><enum>(1)</enum><text>affect the authority of the President to take any action to join and subsequently comply with the terms and obligations of the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI); or</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H81CCE8C91A9342D9B2D0C0AF2D75B1ED"><enum>(2)</enum><text>affect section 1502 of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/15/78m">15 U.S.C. 78m</external-xref> note), or subsection (q) of section 13 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/15/78m">15 U.S.C. 78m</external-xref>), as added by section 1504 of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/111/203">Public Law 111–203</external-xref>; 124 Stat. 2220), or any rule prescribed under either such section. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H77A50C40A9BA4E848950653A2C681207" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Critical mineral defined</header><text>In this section, the term <term>critical mineral</term> has the meaning given the term in section 7002(a) of the Energy Act of 2020 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/30/1606">30 U.S.C. 1606(a)</external-xref>).</text></subsection></section> <section id="H6E502ACB50984BD6AC1F5222CF1D477B"><enum>5412.</enum><header>Connecting Oceania’s Nations with Vanguard Exercises and National Empowerment</header> <subsection id="H67D1CD51710743BE90C44FCBDEA277A9"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">This section may be cited as the <quote>Connecting Oceania’s Nations with Vanguard Exercises and National Empowerment Act of 2023</quote> or the <quote>CONVENE Act of 2023</quote>.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H03DB312CAA244625BD4A4A37E4D8961F"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="H667D045123F846A59365C666048AEB9B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The term <quote>appropriate committees of Congress</quote> means—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H5C8F549D0F6440B79EC07C2FDDE891BF"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the Committee on Foreign Relations and the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H25407A933DDE4C34BAFF1BD20842BA02"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Committee on Foreign Affairs and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC962FA7790A743ECB1C2506AD64E820E"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the congressional defense committees.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H45633931ED914644A1B9CB931B640D5F"><enum>(2)</enum><header>National security council</header><text>The term <quote>national security council</quote> means, with respect to a specified country, an intergovernmental body under the jurisdiction of the freely elected government of the specified country that acts as the primary coordinating entity for security cooperation, disaster response, and the activities described in subsection (c)(5).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H7D0AC3D8B41E4FEEBECF3A79BE696604"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Specified country</header><text>The term <quote>specified country</quote> means—</text> <subparagraph id="H424B8C2B1573469CA89D331D3A00BA4F"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the Federated States of Micronesia;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HD0EBD378BCC94BE6A3261D5417969F0E"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Republic of the Marshall Islands; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H105B03BA8BCF418AB6B188650ACEAD47"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the Republic of Palau.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H55E66BEE844248EAB3B26802AD55A9DB"><enum>(c)</enum><header>National security councils of specified countries</header> 
<paragraph id="H9D17E45FE07449AE992D4FBE4CF46CC3"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of State, in consultation with other relevant Federal departments and agencies, as appropriate, may consult and engage with each specified country to advise and provide assistance to a national security council (including by developing a national security council, if appropriate), or to identify a similar coordinating body for national security matters, comprised of citizens of the specified country—</text> <subparagraph id="HC2522D5D86E447C0B191666DD62E731D"><enum>(A)</enum><text>that enables the specified country—</text> 
<clause id="HB3117EE3691048A1A0A4E78633D18C4A"><enum>(i)</enum><text>to better coordinate with the United States Government, including the Armed Forces, as appropriate;</text></clause> <clause id="H8DAC09A5EB5B41C6A04F9B42DB846549"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>to increase cohesion on activities, including emergency humanitarian response, law enforcement, and maritime security activities; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H6C8B0CF5C87440A4A5DCB8F455475815"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>to provide trained professionals to serve as members of the committees of the specified country established under the applicable Compact of Free Association; and</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H0F37840550AD4B9CA13AD5A8EF7ED550"><enum>(B)</enum><text>for the purpose of enhancing resilience capabilities and protecting the people, infrastructure, and territory of the specified country from malign actions.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0C9B8C50178A4E91A7F847F692F8C453"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Composition</header><text>The Secretary of State, respecting the unique needs of each specified country, may seek to ensure that the national security council, or other identified coordinating body, of the specified country is composed of sufficient staff and members to enable the activities described in paragraph (5).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H8B3F72A50B3541F58BD837516D912D19"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Standards for equipment and services</header><text>The Secretary of State may work with the national security council, or other identified coordinating body, of each specified country to ensure that—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HAFD175D7162747DFBA53DAE08DDCB336"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the equipment and services used by the national security council or other identified coordinating body are compliant with security standards so as to minimize the risk of cyberattacks or espionage;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H59FFC7D8271A455AAEC5935A960010B8"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the national security council or other identified coordinating body takes all reasonable efforts not to procure or use systems, equipment, or software that originates from any entity identified under section 1260H of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/113">10 U.S.C. 113</external-xref> note); and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H8DAC28A1A59244E6A32E1A9DE6763C6C"><enum>(C)</enum><text>to the extent practicable, the equipment and services used by the national security council or other identified coordinating body are interoperable with the equipment and services used by the national security councils, or other identified coordinating bodies, of the other specified countries.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HCFCD71C9D2434F48BB2A58BCCFD9127E"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Report on implementation</header> <subparagraph id="H5AE56A281AC440D7A3AB8C87DBEFFF0A"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter for 2 years, the Secretary of State shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report that includes—</text> 
<clause id="HA5CC1E04947141788710ED204E45C461"><enum>(i)</enum><text>an assessment as to whether a national security council or a similar formal coordinating body is helping or would help achieve the objectives described in paragraph (1) at acceptable financial and opportunity cost;</text></clause> <clause id="HAA77956E64484EAE8796A97F173AA504"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>a description of all actions taken by the United States Government to assist in the identification or maintenance of a national security council, or other identified coordinating body, in each specified country;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H781CC183832449519826629E5288EBE5"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>with respect to each specified country, an assessment as to whether—</text> <subclause id="HEC3C2B0EE94A41E48BD7E806C15BDECC"><enum>(I)</enum><text>the specified country has appropriately staffed its national security council or other identified coordinating body; and</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="H1259E5F2EC1F411B9D21495176A75401"><enum>(II)</enum><text>the extent to which the national security council, or other identified coordinating body, of the specified country is capable of carrying out the activities described in paragraph (5);</text></subclause></clause> <clause id="H316DF01F40424A4682CAA9C6C699F575"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>an assessment of—</text> 
<subclause id="H365241B63EA145CB8A6BF1364F60FA63"><enum>(I)</enum><text>any challenge to cooperation and coordination with the national security council, or other identified coordinating body, of any specified country;</text></subclause> <subclause id="HFD4279FD9B254D9FB72B001A5F111AEE"><enum>(II)</enum><text>current efforts by the Secretary of State to coordinate with the specified countries on the activities described in paragraph (5); and</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="HC819EC8F25C545D6B19EB6F3A21C8402"><enum>(III)</enum><text>existing governmental entities within each specified country that are capable of supporting such activities;</text></subclause></clause> <clause id="H8BC586EBABEB43D78660FA91AC2A2BC6"><enum>(v)</enum><text>a description of any challenge with respect to—</text> 
<subclause id="H76ED07AA9D7C4663993A0984F471286E"><enum>(I)</enum><text>the implementation of the national security council, or other identified coordinating body, of any specified country; and</text></subclause> <subclause id="H27D37F3F31AA482FB334850391115225"><enum>(II)</enum><text>the implementation of paragraphs (1) through (3);</text></subclause></clause>

<subparagraph id="H4B48E246E704483E9CC1AEFB85204B6F" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Identification and development of an existing governmental entity to support homeland defense and civil support activities.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H3EAC18FB330F48E8A2E2A719ADC2C18C" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>5413.</enum><header>Ending China’s developing nation status</header> <subsection id="H5A34F393D5214C2084CF20530B2A03B7"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Finding; statement of policy</header> <paragraph id="H1B1796B41D324FFDA2D9C137EE19B75F"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Finding</header><text>Congress finds that the People’s Republic of China is still classified as a developing nation under multiple treaties and international organization structures, even though China has grown to be the second largest economy in the world.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCB1DF4CD74D742F69A7584F1D00A1A2B"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Statement of policy</header><text>It is the policy of the United States—</text> <subparagraph id="H100998059968485DA493A270F87D2171"><enum>(A)</enum><text>to oppose the labeling or treatment of the People’s Republic of China as a developing nation in current and future treaty negotiations and in each international organization of which the United States and the People’s Republic of China are both current members;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HB66B255F6BB74E6FBF52DDDC5C6ACF75"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to pursue the labeling or treatment of the People’s Republic of China as a developed nation in each international organization of which the United States and the People’s Republic of China are both current members; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H52AF8481A9864E27BB6E11ED551B1D4A"><enum>(C)</enum><text>to work with allies and partners of the United States to implement the policies described in subparagraphs (A) and (B).</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H463DF740AB034FD1A4E6460C61BAA95E"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="H9E3B58DB7AD3439BB9F08EFB6164D9E0"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The term <quote>appropriate committees of Congress</quote> means—</text>

<paragraph id="HFDF55888108E4E40A8614E8408C4745A"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The term <quote>WTO</quote> means the World Trade Organization.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H3FE9A78DA431406DB865FF09B30808DA"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Duties of the secretary</header> <paragraph id="H054C6413A5BE4E668AEB9E5C15129F1D"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Report on development status in current treaty negotiations</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit a report to the appropriate committees of Congress that—</text>

<paragraph id="HFD244A5FA3C1489E9F8367DEFEAB4CED"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Report on development status in existing organizations and treaties</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit a report to the appropriate committees of Congress that—</text> <subparagraph id="H2851B6F5D69B480AA6015367A1AA5C3A"><enum>(A)</enum><text>identifies all international organizations or treaties of which the United States is a member, that provide different treatment or standards for enforcement based on the respective development status of the member states or states parties;</text></subparagraph>

<clause id="H91E243AD539C40F5AC415012A1B39C2E"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the development of a mechanism described in clause (i) to change the status of the People’s Republic of China in such organization from developing nation to developed nation.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3AAFD1281BC944DFA14F8D9066154958"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Waiver</header><text>The President may waive the application of clause (i) or (ii) of subparagraph (A) with respect to any international organization if the President notifies the appropriate committees of Congress that such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States.</text></subparagraph></paragraph>

<section id="H1B8352B4368A4232B937C6DAD35D477A"><enum>5501.</enum><header>Amendments to the Energy Employees Occupational Illness Compensation Program Act of 2000</header> 
<subsection id="H949EE7E3E2C843BC8B4CDC4C19B34652"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Short title</header><text>This section may be cited as the <quote>Beryllium Testing Fairness Act</quote>.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H01724B6488614028BCB95F5A59E35B52"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Modification of demonstration of beryllium sensitivity</header><text>Section 3621(8)(A) of the Energy Employees Occupational Illness Compensation Program Act of 2000 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/7384l">42 U.S.C. 7384l(8)(A)</external-xref>) is amended—</text> 
<paragraph id="H7252B28ECC6A4CA7B1102EFBA9CA064C"><enum>(1)</enum><text>by striking <quote>established by an abnormal</quote> and inserting the following:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" id="H8599D09D195D4D2797AACB1661DE2880" display-inline="yes-display-inline"><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">established by—</text>

<toc container-level="title-container" quoted-block="no-quoted-block" lowest-level="section" idref="HEAE0F0D37B4B48189DB0FC054E4C9BCB" regeneration="yes-regeneration" lowest-bolded-level="division-lowest-bolded">

<toc-entry idref="H95E13BA4EBCA493B9E0E1AC67B4E3B08" level="section">Sec. 5703. Appointment of Deputy Architect of the Capitol; vacancy in Architect or Deputy Architect.</toc-entry>

<section id="H156D6DE814044A76AACC1BEED7296746"><enum>5701.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This title may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Architect of the Capitol Appointment Act of 2023</short-title></quote>.</text></section> <section id="H4DA595E7E273491BB710E623201171EE"><enum>5702.</enum><header>Appointment and term of service of Architect of the Capitol</header> <subsection id="HF06BFB7A4D2C4C8AB18EA37348B84142"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Appointment</header><text>The Architect of the Capitol shall be appointed, without regard to political affiliation and solely on the basis of fitness to perform the duties of the office, upon a majority vote of a congressional commission (referred to in this section as the <quote>commission</quote>) consisting of the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the majority leader of the Senate, the minority leaders of the House of Representatives and Senate, the chair and ranking minority member of the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives, the chairman and ranking minority member of the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, the chair and ranking minority member of the Committee on House Administration of the House of Representatives, and the chairman and ranking minority member of the Committee on Rules and Administration of the Senate.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HAEBDECE6BA8B43AA9742AD6EAE1399FE"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Term of service</header><text>The Architect of the Capitol shall be appointed for a term of 10 years and, upon a majority vote of the members of the commission, may be reappointed for additional 10-year terms.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H6D3249DFF4D04340998808B2FBBA50B6"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Removal</header><text>The Architect of the Capitol may be removed from office at any time upon a majority vote of the members of the commission.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H3CCF68BDF4744DF3B5653C5A68F4698D"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Conforming amendments</header> 
<paragraph id="H9585C6A2D64D4B7B93A804C63B0BA882"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Section 319 of the Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 1990 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/2/1801">2 U.S.C. 1801</external-xref>) is repealed.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H58299199071743929A35FA27C3859D7E"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The matter under the heading <quote>For the Capitol:</quote> under the heading <quote>DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR.</quote> of the Act of February 14, 1902 (32 Stat. 19, chapter 17; incorporated in <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/2/1811">2 U.S.C. 1811</external-xref>) is amended by striking <quote>, and he shall be appointed by the President</quote>.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H928B1BB0C27C4F4D9DDCD5D717C7FDF3"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Effective date</header><text>This section, and the amendments made by this section, shall apply with respect to appointments made on or after the date of enactment of this Act.</text></subsection></section> <section id="H95E13BA4EBCA493B9E0E1AC67B4E3B08"><enum>5703.</enum><header>Appointment of Deputy Architect of the Capitol; vacancy in Architect or Deputy Architect</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 1203 of title I of division H of the Consolidated Appropriations Resolution, 2003 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/2/1805">2 U.S.C. 1805</external-xref>) is amended—</text> 
<paragraph id="HF9CDCBB3ED124CD7A6FF89A1764ABE71"><enum>(1)</enum><text>in subsection (a)—</text> <subparagraph id="H882065DFEB7046D8B0A727CC9D46B34B"><enum>(A)</enum><text>by inserting <quote>(in this section referred to as the <quote>Architect</quote>)</quote> after <quote>The Architect of the Capitol</quote>; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF92FBF6EB14D492694E3B715D3830532"><enum>(B)</enum><text>by inserting <quote>(in this section referred to as the <quote>Deputy Architect</quote>)</quote> after <quote>Deputy Architect of the Capitol</quote>;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H879CC45C0CF54AC8BF95604933C407D9"><enum>(2)</enum><text>by redesignating subsection (b) as subsection (c);</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H7DED87DD1CCC4DA585B67AE79B3D4028"><enum>(3)</enum><text>by inserting after subsection (a) the following:</text> <quoted-block id="H3EE3B89BD5964EB6B56E0173047CB3A8" style="OLC"> <subsection id="H9C6B74B9035046178EB70C98002D33BC"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Deadline</header><text>The Architect shall appoint a Deputy Architect under subsection (a) not later than 120 days after—</text> 
<paragraph id="H4C845BA0AA754C1EAA202CA7A15392D3"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the date on which the Architect is appointed under section 5702 of the Architect of the Capitol Appointment Act of 2023, if there is no Deputy Architect on the date of the appointment; or</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9579EEE67C574F16B853C6691B9C5E12"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the date on which a vacancy arises in the office of the Deputy Architect.</text></paragraph></subsection><after-quoted-block>;</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H23D31A2B4FBE48FCB3B2EB82E68B5F6A"><enum>(4)</enum><text>in subsection (c), as so redesignated, by striking <quote>of the Capitol</quote> each place it appears; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H266C99B5906E486390B782BD823C6781"><enum>(5)</enum><text>by adding at the end the following:</text> 
<quoted-block id="HCEE89B00A0E84FD1917556F6B957B8BB" style="OLC"> 
<subsection id="H0934EC1A655D43EB90E4A7DAC1AEF1AC" commented="no"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Failure to appoint</header><text>If the Architect does not appoint a Deputy Architect on or before the applicable date specified in subsection (b), the congressional commission described in section 5702(a) of the Architect of the Capitol Appointment Act of 2023 shall appoint the Deputy Architect by a majority vote of the members of the commission.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HC2B8BFE94B1541299791B74DA975BC49"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Notification</header><text>If the position of Deputy Architect becomes vacant, the Architect shall immediately notify the members of the congressional commission described in section 5702(a) of the Architect of the Capitol Appointment Act of 2023.</text></subsection><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph></section> 
<section id="H025BCFFF0A584F7AA6947E4FD92BB8F3"><enum>5704.</enum><header>Deputy Architect of the Capitol to serve as acting in case of absence, disability, or vacancy</header> 
<subsection id="HC46EFB26B21A4175BC95B01AD1633B87"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Deputy Architect of the Capitol (in this section referred to as the <quote>Deputy Architect</quote>) shall act as Architect of the Capitol (in this section referred to as the <quote>Architect</quote>) if the Architect is absent or disabled or there is no Architect.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H95933CE09A8D4FE48E6396A6B668237F"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Absence, disability, or vacancy in office of deputy architect</header><text>For purposes of subsection (a), if the Deputy Architect is also absent or disabled or there is no Deputy Architect, the congressional commission described in section 5702(a) shall designate, by a majority vote of the members of the commission, an individual to serve as acting Architect until—</text> 
<paragraph id="HE9A4B5108BEE4AC3BD645B34C1C6E50E"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the end of the absence or disability of the Architect or the Deputy Architect; or</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H1BB1BE3F319D4023BB759F096EFEBE4B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>in the case of vacancies in both positions, an Architect has been appointed under section 5702(a).</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H5960BF225ABC4015A521A633A6AD497F"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Authority</header><text>An officer serving as acting Architect under subsection (a) or (b) shall perform all the duties and exercise all the authorities of the Architect, including the authority to delegate the duties and authorities of the Architect in accordance with the matter under the heading <quote>Office of the Architect of the Capitol</quote> under the heading <quote>ARCHITECT OF THE CAPITOL</quote> of the Legislative Appropriation Act, 1956 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/2/1803">2 U.S.C. 1803</external-xref>).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H3F1F1DBCFE804920A1B011F3F9778B4A"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Conforming amendment</header><text>The matter under the heading <quote>salaries</quote> under the heading <quote>Office of the Architect of the Capitol</quote> under the heading <quote>ARCHITECT OF THE CAPITOL</quote> of the Legislative Branch Appropriation Act, 1971 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/2/1804">2 U.S.C. 1804</external-xref>) is amended by striking <quote>: Provided,</quote> and all that follows through <quote>no Architect</quote>.</text></subsection></section></title>

<toc-entry idref="H05D33943E25A46C9BD4C6D2FE17A4FAD" level="section">Sec. 5801. Assessment of gifts and grants to United States institutions of higher education from entities on the Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List.</toc-entry></toc> 
<section id="H05D33943E25A46C9BD4C6D2FE17A4FAD" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>5801.</enum><header>Assessment of gifts and grants to United States institutions of higher education from entities on the Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List</header> 
<subsection id="H9A231A6E3C144C01BF240E0338EB5714"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Treasury shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees an assessment of gifts and grants to United States institutions of higher education from entities on the Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List maintained by the Office of Foreign Assets Control. </text></subsection> <subsection id="HC5052F1347AE454B9F66D0A988018F4D"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Education, shall include in the assessment required by subsection (a) an estimate of—</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H80557B5ABA144C01BF57037E7B2DD752"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a list and description of each of the gifts and grants provided to United States institutions of higher education by entities described in subsection (a); and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H836E02EAC7744023A626977FB2C7CF2D"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the monetary value of each of those gifts and grants.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H457033B90D03434F9F9F4200F681C54B"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="H03DB77BA946046B99831534BDA5C6983"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The term <term>appropriate congressional committees</term> means—</text>

<paragraph id="H5024493BC86B44FDAED10595AEF9BEB0"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The term <term>gifts and grants</term> includes financial contributions, material donations, provision of services, scholarships, fellowships, research funding, infrastructure investment, contracts, or any other form of support that provides a benefit to the recipient institution.</text></paragraph></subsection></section></title></division> <division id="HCDD3DF2D25C9484FB8A76E0D3D895513" style="OLC"><enum>F</enum><header>Department of State Authorization Act of 2023</header> <section id="HC2038C55FE6E4CE5ADF7D644EBF7D9E1" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>6001.</enum><header>Short title; table of contents</header> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H5EBCDB99CEB9458090ADEBA58D19DE63"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Short title</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">This division may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Department of State Authorization Act of 2023</short-title></quote>.</text></subsection>

<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H5B31F37AC2274A9C8115AB06A972C350"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Appropriate congressional committees</header><text>The term <term>appropriate congressional committees</term> means the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives.</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB02D0906E1804D0A808F15F2C5F371B2"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Department</header><text>The term <term>Department</term> means the Department of State.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H11362F6D56E84D99BF903D33110C29CA"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Secretary</header><text>The term <term>Secretary</term> means the Secretary of State.</text></paragraph></section> <title style="OLC" commented="no" level-type="subsequent" id="HD627EACE43024767A05DFFC60C4CA076"><enum>LXI</enum><header>Diplomatic security and consular affairs</header> <section id="H893BE0BD726D4A4580C772B728D7A7DF"><enum>6101.</enum><header>Special hiring authority for passport services</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">During the 3-year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this division, the Secretary, without regard to the provisions under sections 3309 through 3318 of title 5, United States Code, may directly appoint up to 80 candidates to positions in the competitive service (as defined in section 2102 of such title) at the Department in the Passport and Visa Examining Series 0967.</text></section> 
<section id="H4C96F7B328FB4871A09A80D9CF6B3C31"><enum>6102.</enum><header>Quarterly report on passport wait times</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Not later than 30 days after the date of the enactment of this division, and quarterly thereafter for the following 3 years, the Secretary shall submit a report to the appropriate congressional committees that describes—</text> <paragraph id="HF8385C93D0A84CAA825E831B53B08C98"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the current estimated wait times for passport processing;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H44EA12850180419AB51214152091CA57"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the steps that have been taken by the Department to reduce wait times to a reasonable time;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDE8C649E8C5242AE976D37B5DE9DDFAF"><enum>(3)</enum><text>efforts to improve the rollout of the online passport renewal processing program, including how much of passport revenues the Department is spending on consular systems modernization; </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HED645CEC24CB4BC896A2B62D4DB53553"><enum>(4)</enum><text>the demand for urgent passport services by major metropolitan area;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2C3794905FFC4B5DA8E29D3BDC9818A7"><enum>(5)</enum><text>the steps that have been taken by the Department to reduce and meet the demand for urgent passport services, particularly in areas that are greater than 5 hours driving time from the nearest passport agency; and </text></paragraph>

<paragraph id="H4FE70E256B994BA1A95F89ABB9B5F940"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Secretary shall develop and implement a standardized, confidential exit survey process that includes anonymous feedback and exit interviews with employees who voluntarily separate from the Department, whether through resignation, retirement, or other means.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H0AC97D66B112412E8BE2DDAF5FCF49C7"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Scope</header><text>The exit surveys conducted pursuant to paragraph (1) shall—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HACC533A6CF1D4E49A37D1D770772214C"><enum>(A)</enum><text>be designed to gather insights and feedback from departing employees regarding—</text> <clause id="HB1FEBF5D1BD5425884A414A18A473662"><enum>(i)</enum><text>their reasons for leaving, including caretaking responsibilities, career limitations for partner or spouse, and discrimination, harassment, or retaliation;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H8157D5D7E31A4B2A83721515A3D56ABA"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>their overall experience with the Department; and</text></clause> <clause id="H30ADD494B40A4DC7A499F932206F9DAD"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>any suggestions for improvement; and</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFAC828E271794F9B8E7CB2795C664FBC"><enum>(B)</enum><text>include questions related to—</text> <clause id="H0E3E32D8EAF34BB7BBAEE22B62D13C8D"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the employee’s reasons for leaving;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H1E2B7F2957A848BCA39E3B6A3197F8DB"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>job satisfaction;</text></clause> <clause id="H4CF3A750515440C1B26E13DFD782BD73"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>work environment;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H8982E77B03324DECBB36BAAEEA9EC0A9"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>professional growth opportunities;</text></clause> <clause id="H0B8508113B0C4675B6E17A486EE045F4"><enum>(v)</enum><text>leadership effectiveness;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H14D08136AE2F4C87BA2930FBD12E0328"><enum>(vi)</enum><text>suggestions for enhancing the Department’s performance; and</text></clause> <clause id="H1A765917DE344AEC9722C8B92812460E"><enum>(vii)</enum><text>if applicable, the name and industry of the employee’s future employer.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H86697A5CF9514F479597D021A22A180F"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Compilation of results</header><text>The Secretary shall compile and analyze the anonymized exit survey data collected pursuant to this paragraph to identify trends, common themes, and areas needing improvement within the Department. </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HFF3F2D6656E74523AF4692C9FEB53988"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Pilot surveys</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Secretary shall conduct a Department-wide survey for Locally Employed Staff regarding retention, training, promotion, and other matters, including harassment, discrimination, and retaliation, that includes workforce perspectives on the accessibility and effectiveness of complaint measures.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H3CA34532D52C4A63A4782A7453050C81"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than 60 days after the conclusion of each survey conducted pursuant to this section, the Secretary shall make the key findings available to the Department workforce and shall submit them to the appropriate congressional committees.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H5AA521943CC84966A4420AE71D0FAFD3"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Retaliation prevention efforts</header> <paragraph id="H56427C95626D4E2092BD1C5CD26BC157"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Employee evaluation</header> <subparagraph id="H285E9CFF04A24132AEF851BD36FF9DF7"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>If there is a pending investigation of discrimination or harassment against a superior who is responsible for rating or reviewing the complainant employee, the complainant shall be reviewed by the superior’s supervisor or other Department employee as appropriate. </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H75DC5AF92D124AD3BFA6D3970CE9EC56"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Effective date</header><text>This paragraph shall take effect 90 days after the date of the enactment of this division.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HAAE0DE8E54B54C21B5DEAB07CCB9F2BB"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Retaliation prevention guidance</header><text>Any Department employee against whom an allegation of discrimination or harassment has been made shall receive written guidance (a <quote>retaliation hold</quote>) on the types of actions that can be considered retaliation against the complainant employee. The employee’s immediate supervisor shall also receive the retaliation hold guidance.</text></paragraph></subsection></section>

<section id="H0522180A964D48C58629127B305F0B87"><enum>6227.</enum><header>Supporting tandem spouses in the Foreign Service</header> 
<subsection id="HDD2F3ED31D8448A98C68889898F578AD"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Sense of Congress</header><text>It is the sense of Congress that—</text> <paragraph id="H9E9380651E394FAC8882D450C23B961A"><enum>(1)</enum><text>challenges finding and maintaining spousal employment and family dissatisfaction are one of the leading reasons employees cite for leaving the Department;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCD0B5A15983B415BBC75A031F5B0142A"><enum>(2)</enum><text>tandem Foreign Service personnel represent important members of the Foreign Service community, who act as force multipliers for our diplomacy;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H87B249D1CACC4BE889C7BC796A469869"><enum>(3)</enum><text>the Department can and should do more to keep tandem spouses posted together and consider family member employment needs when assigning tandem officers; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H35F31445467E431FADC1C50AC24DC7A0"><enum>(4)</enum><text>common sense steps providing more flexibility in the assignments process would improve outcomes for tandem officers without disadvantaging other Foreign Service Officers.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H646ACB9E7FFF4512A4941274A288F2EC"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HE2B670498355487CAC712705A521BA15"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Family togetherness</header><text>The term <term>family togetherness</term> means facilitating the placement of Foreign Service personnel at the same United States diplomatic post when both spouses are members of a tandem couple of Foreign Service personnel.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6A75F9DBE80044F88FDD23692326E690"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Tandem foreign service personnel; tandem</header><text>The terms <term>tandem Foreign Service personnel</term> and <term>tandem</term> mean a member of a couple of which one spouse is a career or career candidate employee of the Foreign Service and the other spouse is a career or career candidate employee of the Foreign Service or an employee of one of the agencies authorized to use the Foreign Service Personnel System under section 202 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/3922">22 U.S.C. 3922</external-xref>).</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H877AC7007381491CB77694723EC5BDE2"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Family togetherness in assignments</header><text>Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this division, the Department shall amend and update its policies to further promote the principle of family togetherness in the Foreign Service, which shall include the following:</text> <paragraph id="H5DA66FB2DDF64D14AAD95143D73D8F57"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Entry-level foreign service personnel</header><text>The Secretary shall adopt policies and procedures to facilitate the assignment of entry-level tandem Foreign Service personnel on directed assignments to the same diplomatic post or country as their tandem spouse if they request to be assigned to the same post or country. The Secretary shall also provide a written justification to the requesting personnel explaining any denial of a request that would result in tandem spouses not serving together at the same post or country.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5B2BC2F66F994535975959BB2A936437"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Tenured foreign service personnel</header><text>The Secretary shall add family togetherness to the criteria when making a needs of the Service determination, as defined by the Foreign Affairs Manual, for the placement of tenured tandem Foreign Service personnel at United States diplomatic posts.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H96D81E7DE2BD4270B47794710764DC1A"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Updates to antinepotism policy</header><text>The Secretary shall update antinepotism policies so that nepotism rules only apply when an employee and a relative are placed into positions wherein they jointly and exclusively control government resources, property, or money or establish government policy.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HAF13CEEE781247ED932CE6381793A2BD"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Temporary supervision of tandem spouse</header><text>The Secretary shall update policies to allow for a tandem spouse to temporarily supervise another tandem spouse for up to 90 days in a calendar year, including at a United States diplomatic mission.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H3ED382FA748F4157A38439CABA2148C4"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this division, and annually thereafter for two years, the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report that includes—</text> 
<paragraph id="H76D352AAECEF4582AAA3F39E48A3093B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the number of Foreign Service tandem spouses currently serving;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H8E0C67D3F09047BF9A98B47F84C33789"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the number of Foreign Service tandems currently serving in separate locations, or, to the extent possible, that are on leave without pay (LWOP); and </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0EF696459FF44A4AB6BDACAE9B8DB994"><enum>(3)</enum><text>an estimate of the cost savings that would result if all Foreign Service tandem spouses were placed at a single post. </text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HBDAB0387800B4875A69ACD8D0804B9FC"><enum>6228.</enum><header>Accessibility at diplomatic missions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Department shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees, the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives a report that includes—</text> 
<paragraph id="H3DA1E2FAA7A24D4E99D311D91D476295"><enum>(1)</enum><text>a list of the overseas United States diplomatic missions that, as of the date of the enactment of this division, are not readily accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC364BEBDC3624327B60B7073EC9FB174"><enum>(2)</enum><text>any efforts in progress to make such missions readily accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2B31921880594C7687F9428E5A7BEBF9"><enum>(3)</enum><text>an estimate of the cost to make all such missions readily accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities. </text></paragraph></section> <section id="H0CCD3DD21F83423CA3FD80AC5B357A00"><enum>6229.</enum><header>Report on breastfeeding accommodations overseas</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report that includes—</text> 
<paragraph id="HA3031FF64CB9476EA8C46E7EEEB5E442"><enum>(1)</enum><text>a detailed report on the Department’s efforts to equip 100 percent of United States embassies and consulates with dedicated lactation spaces, other than bathrooms, that are shielded from view and free from intrusion from coworkers and the public for use by employees, including the expected demand for such spaces as well as the status of such rooms when there is no demand for such space; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA77B22D128414E58878B91C2BB70D2D3"><enum>(2)</enum><text>a description of costs and other resources needed to provide such spaces.</text></paragraph></section> 
<section id="HECBA827F3D8D49B586C3DF58EE03A8B7"><enum>6230.</enum><header>Determining the effectiveness of knowledge transfers between Foreign Service Officers</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">The Secretary shall assess the effectiveness of knowledge transfers between Foreign Service Officers who are departing from overseas positions and Foreign Service Officers who are arriving at such positions, and make recommendations for approving such knowledge transfers, as appropriate, by—</text> <paragraph id="HF7D20943AC4141DBB75D237C163B2C3C"><enum>(1)</enum><text>not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this division, conducting a written survey of a representative sample of Foreign Service Officers working in overseas assignments that analyzes the effectiveness of existing mechanisms to facilitate transitions, including training, mentorship, information technology, knowledge management, relationship building, the role of locally employed staff, and organizational culture; and</text></paragraph>
