<subparagraph id="H842F8DF6A2354E0DB93FC1FC36F70C42"><enum>(D)</enum><text>identifies any steps taken, or intended to be taken, to implement such recommendations, including any additional resources or authorities necessary to implement such recommendations; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H77AD40F21F914350AC0B7D8FBDFD9EF3"><enum>(E)</enum><text>provides recommendations to Congress for legislative action to advance the priority described in subparagraph (C). </text></subparagraph></paragraph></section> 
<section id="HEB1DB014861C4492864E2D4B335AE4FD"><enum>6231.</enum><header>Education allowance for dependents of Department of State employees located in United States territories</header> 
<subsection id="H1579908792DC4F989FC563724C842CF1"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>An individual employed by the Department at a location described in subsection (b) shall be eligible for a cost-of-living allowance for the education of the dependents of such employee in an amount that does not exceed the educational allowance authorized by the Secretary of Defense for such location.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H20DB3B2CD4124AD78724EC72D1A8BCB2"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Location described</header><text>A location is described in this subsection if—</text> 
<paragraph id="H5725C491293C47219B13750C1DFF0542"><enum>(1)</enum><text>such location is in a territory of the United States; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC41EEBCBC214485BBA28C2101AF48B30"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the Secretary of Defense has determined that schools available in such location are unable to adequately provide for the education of—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H30232FE84A9B46C1AE38752510327B14"><enum>(A)</enum><text>dependents of members of the Armed Forces; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H596AE1A5CF2945BAA04E75449F7DA67A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>dependents of employees of the Department of Defense. </text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="HA394B7CCAAAF46F9A81C60D6719E0B91"><enum>6232.</enum><header>Overtime pay exception for protective services</header> 
<subsection id="H61918032C96344A8B2D37F7A58FEF773"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Covered employee defined</header><text>In this section, the term <term>covered employee</term> means any individual employed by, and conducting protective services on behalf of, the Diplomatic Security Service for an individual.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HBC1441E9453C42878F4CCE679FCB070E"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Exception to the limitation on premium pay for protective services</header><text>Notwithstanding the restrictions contained in section 5547 of title 5, United States Code, any covered employee may receive premium pay for overtime officially ordered or approved and performed while conducting protective security functions in excess of the annual equivalent of the limitation on the rate of pay contained in section 5547(a) of such title, except that such premium pay shall not be payable to an employee to the extent that such aggregate amount would exceed the rate of basic pay payable for a position at level II of the Executive Schedule under section 5313 of such title. </text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H210A46CD5AB348C6A832694765ADDB63"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Treatment of additional pay</header><text>If the application of subsection (b) results in the payment of additional premium pay to a covered employee of a type that is normally creditable as basic pay for retirement or any other purpose, that additional pay shall not—</text> <paragraph id="HBAE3954DD237457697055359034FE600"><enum>(1)</enum><text>be considered to be basic pay of the covered employee for any purpose; or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H6A5DC3045A9F4808BB3875835994D608"><enum>(2)</enum><text>be used in computing a lump-sum payment to the covered employee for accumulated and accrued annual leave under section 5551 or section 5552 of title 5, United States Code.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H733ADF311BC947BFA84B9972A7972A83"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Aggregate limit</header><text>With respect to the application of section 5307 of title 5, United States Code, the payment of any additional premium pay to a covered employee as a result of subsection (b) shall not be counted as part of the aggregate compensation of the covered employee.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H54DAE8C59EB74E329FCB39A393790530"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Report</header> 
<paragraph id="H514B2DD7FA8F4B7EA0287FAD26899C15"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report describing the steps the Department is taking to address the increased protective service demands placed upon individuals by the Diplomatic Security Service.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE782C23840EE494BAA282B434FB9B367"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The report required under paragraph (1) shall include the following elements:</text> 
<subparagraph id="HACCEE40812DB49CE9E4AABB43125AE9B"><enum>(A)</enum><text>An analysis of the current operational demands and staffing levels.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE9AFC8AAFD374FE78CF716F0A6EB789B"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Recommended strategies for reducing overtime requirements, including—</text> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HC19590CC17474874B66A958A042CDB82"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">hiring additional personnel; </text></clause> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H44EBAD68A4764BDAA65B77235CA36C5E"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">solutions such that sufficient resources are available throughout each year without the need for waivers of premium pay limitations;</text></clause> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB531725E28B24F0591E809AE7F365909"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">redistribution of workload; and </text></clause> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HC4494E73146B4082AEBBAA57EBB086F1"><enum>(iv)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">other improvements in operational efficiency. </text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H27A6343C470044BFB4A73F6371941428"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Appropriate committees of Congress defined</header><text>In this subsection, the term <term>appropriate committees of Congress</term> means—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H37239D95B2D24F1D9A0E20E471CA1F08"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the appropriate congressional committees;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H6F2A25F0C71549FEAA8EB4573EFD4E3C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3491E71986A641B5A935BAFA56FB421D"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the Committee on Oversight and Accountability and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H7614646E6B6F43D686B34731A171B811"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Effective date</header><text>This section shall take effect as if enacted on Jan 1, 2023.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HBFA993FB670D414BB6F9DF3E8863173D"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text>This section shall terminate on December 31, 2025. </text></subsection></section></subtitle></title> 
<title id="HB8DE71CA44584E36973A76DE08D1A9B3" style="OLC"><enum>LXIII</enum><header>Information security and cyber diplomacy</header> 
<section id="HE2F4F191E27042D1ABDCDD00D45543CA"><enum>6301.</enum><header>Data-informed diplomacy</header> 
<subsection id="HC3B227051FD34C2A873FB7F0E4F71305"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Findings</header><text>Congress makes the following findings:</text> <paragraph id="H471B61E1BA9846868ECFB8934124946B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>In a rapidly evolving and digitally interconnected global landscape, access to and maintenance of reliable, readily available data is key to informed decisionmaking and diplomacy and therefore should be considered a strategic asset.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5368C57CE6A84F70A744D2ECB96382A3"><enum>(2)</enum><text>In order to achieve its mission in the 21st century, the Department must adapt to these trends by maintaining and providing timely access to high-quality data at the time and place needed, while simultaneously cultivating a data-savvy workforce.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2E2E0DF3B76142578963BF5825442AF4"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Leveraging data science and data analytics has the potential to improve the performance of the Department’s workforce by providing otherwise unknown insights into program deficiencies, shortcomings, or other gaps in analysis.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H6460139C0BAA4CE4B9EC3DE80271021E"><enum>(4)</enum><text>While innovative technologies such as artificial intelligence and machine learning have the potential to empower the Department to analyze and act upon data at scale, systematized, sustainable data management and information synthesis remain a core competency necessary for data-driven decisionmaking.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HAE41E0F36F8D408787D43FEA6F5B37A5"><enum>(5)</enum><text>The goals set out by the Department’s Enterprise Data Council (EDC) as the areas of most critical need for the Department, including Cultivating a Data Culture, Accelerating Decisions through Analytics, Establishing Mission-Driven Data Management, and Enhancing Enterprise Data Governance, are laudable and will remain critical as the Department develops into a data-driven agency.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H21C54C0141794F0D9D01D63B9D39A13C"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Sense of Congress</header><text>It is the sense of Congress that—</text> <paragraph id="H2284BAACE751444CACA8896825407196"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the Department should prioritize the recruitment and retainment of top data science talent in support of its data-informed diplomacy efforts as well as its broader modernization agenda; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H75791D05BB754747951D78D8190DC8FD"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the Department should strengthen data fluency among its workforce, promote data collaboration across and within its bureaus, and enhance its enterprise data oversight.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H5A96EB06FCDC44DC80F61B147382FC81" commented="no"><enum>6302.</enum><header>Establishment and expansion of the Bureau Chief Data Officer Program</header> <subsection id="HAAB76A06246A430CBD381B9BBB43A232" commented="no"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Bureau Chief Data Officer Program</header> <paragraph id="HAF261666969A460D998F56D21CB39142" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text>The Secretary shall establish a program, which shall be known as the <quote>Bureau Chief Data Officer Program</quote> (referred to in this section as the <quote>Program</quote>), overseen by the Department’s Chief Data Officer. The Bureau Chief Data Officers hired under this program shall report to their respective Bureau leadership.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H912B727B81A74BA595F57423708A6332" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Goals</header><text>The goals of the Program shall include the following:</text> <subparagraph id="HA75F669D87024D2EA0C65D5AB8ADFE26" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Cultivating a data culture by promoting data fluency and data collaboration across the Department.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H6B69702DA73D43F2926BB58F458550CD" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Promoting increased data analytics use in critical decisionmaking areas.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2EECC587F3DC406EB4AE61F725CC1A48" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Promoting data integration and standardization.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H749FD2DB260F4D98A31FFD3614FD8CC1" commented="no"><enum>(D)</enum><text>Increasing efficiencies across the Department by incentivizing acquisition of enterprise data solutions and subscription data services to be shared across bureaus and offices and within bureaus.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H3C987868E0E64583A0E77BC5E18F9713" commented="no"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Implementation plan</header> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HA2EBB32E9AD549E8B431C34BBE5FA780"><enum>(1)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress an implementation plan that outlines strategies for—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H51BD1CA1D622448593C710AA1F650B1A" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text>advancing the goals described in subsection (a)(2);</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HCC48B8314D1A40C6BA5696AF459F72C3" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>hiring Bureau Chief Data Officers at the GS-14 or GS-15 grade or a similar rank;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H177CCC0EF91B48D686A94CA475EB41C5" commented="no"><enum>(C)</enum><text>assigning at least one Bureau Chief Data Officer to each bureau of the Department; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H5F5C2DCFFB684C5BAC7788767B3EF2B2" commented="no"><enum>(D)</enum><text>allocation of necessary resources to sustain the Program.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H9F458B778E9A4D6585D3DE5933B2BEB4"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Appropriate committees of Congress defined</header><text>In this subsection, the term <term>appropriate committees of Congress</term> means—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HE483FA98EBB74DAC92668EBF6AA01795"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the appropriate congressional committees;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HDCA9586E0E8841F6B6619E3613358485"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H7280F963D1F94DA9AB52AB278A9BD929"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Committee on Oversight and Accountability and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H1E17733554CE4200BE13F7945B50FA4D" commented="no"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Assignment</header><text>In implementing the Bureau Chief Data Officer Program, bureaus may not dual-hat currently employed personnel as Bureau Chief Data Officers.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H464D8020E5854B6E8ACE4228D2C6069D" commented="no"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Annual reporting requirement</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, and annually thereafter for the following 3 years, the Secretary shall submit a report to the appropriate congressional committees regarding the status of the implementation plan required under subsection (b).</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H7170969BF37D43ECBCF49D4310CC7602"><enum>6303.</enum><header>Establishment of the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of State</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 1 of the State Department Basic Authorities Act of 1956 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2651a">22 U.S.C. 2651a</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HE3BF805E3DE54175A5340F2FE61CE26B"> <subsection id="H8B711CA2F01E4CE2AD6CA033AD74235B"><enum>(n)</enum><header>Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer</header> <paragraph id="HF1A6398879F842EFB46D976E415EAB26"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>There shall be within the Department of State a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer, which may be dual-hatted as the Department’s Chief Data Officer, who shall be a member of the Senior Executive Service.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF872D7AD076842B89E2338BFC86846EA"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Duties described</header><text>The principal duties and responsibilities of the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer shall be—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H20ECB5DA856448269C3A9774868E74CA"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to evaluate, oversee, and, if appropriate, facilitate the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning applications to help inform decisions by policymakers and to support programs and management operations of the Department of State; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H9B5A5E110040420381EA8AFA10ABCAAF"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to act as the principal advisor to the Secretary of State on the ethical use of AI and advanced analytics in conducting data-informed diplomacy.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H045034CEC0DE47B9B4DF5935016EF4A1"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Qualifications</header><text>The Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer should be an individual with demonstrated skill and competency in—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HB448BD6F1CCC405B9E4A1623F06B03C5"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the use and application of data analytics, AI, and machine learning; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H1DDE06DA6A944FB4899C41E90C1BF1D8"><enum>(B)</enum><text>transformational leadership and organizational change management, particularly within large, complex organizations.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC58DFF83C9F94761B306B38A1D06CF31"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Partner with the Chief Information Officer on scaling artificial intelligence use cases</header><text>To ensure alignment between the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer and the Chief Information Officer, the Chief Information Officer will consult with the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer on best practices for rolling out and scaling AI capabilities across the Bureau of Information and Resource Management’s broader portfolio of software applications.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H449DBF395F654338A3F6E31AA4F6B172" commented="no"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Artificial intelligence defined</header><text>In this subsection, the term <term>artificial intelligence</term> has the meaning given the term in section 238(g) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/115/232">Public Law 115–232</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/4001">10 U.S.C. 4001</external-xref> note).</text></paragraph></subsection><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section> 
<section id="H45BDD32D4C9C4DF88CB822FF69DCC210"><enum>6304.</enum><header>Strengthening the Chief Information Officer of the Department of State</header> 
<subsection id="H6CFB2E7C44B646118C1C42DCF5340A7C"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Chief Information Officer of the Department shall be consulted on all decisions to approve or disapprove, significant new unclassified information technology expenditures, including software, of the Department, including expenditures related to information technology acquired, managed, and maintained by other bureaus and offices within the Department, in order to—</text> <paragraph id="HC5398DAEAB56426B90CBC4588A8D6C0F"><enum>(1)</enum><text>encourage the use of enterprise software and information technology solutions where such solutions exist or can be developed in a timeframe and manner consistent with maintaining and enhancing the continuity and improvement of Department operations;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCCEE77BCA1A7414DBD0366403EDA8B27"><enum>(2)</enum><text>increase the bargaining power of the Department in acquiring information technology solutions across the Department;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HEBE7B181A71D4EA18950056DB494E598"><enum>(3)</enum><text>reduce the number of redundant Authorities to Operate (ATO), which, instead of using one ATO-approved platform across bureaus, requires multiple ATOs for software use cases across different bureaus;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H854E8779985241F4B917D7B153651A96"><enum>(4)</enum><text>enhance the efficiency, reduce redundancy, and increase interoperability of the use of information technology across the enterprise of the Department;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H81F4CAEEA7CB4F6BA306D6604B45A35D"><enum>(5)</enum><text>enhance training and alignment of information technology personnel with the skills required to maintain systems across the Department;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HDE57BBF074A44A8EB3B991A77EDFDC46"><enum>(6)</enum><text>reduce costs related to the maintenance of, or effectuate the retirement of, legacy systems;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2280B28B698C4732872A06D0C1F7CA07"><enum>(7)</enum><text>ensure the development and maintenance of security protocols regarding the use of information technology solutions and software across the Department; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HAB88ECC8087A4FB5B06E0CC8A61481D7"><enum>(8)</enum><text>improve end-user training on the operation of information technology solutions and to enhance end-user cybersecurity practices.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H019044DF0AFF40C1ABDAC73CC5258F49"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Strategy and implementation plan required</header> <paragraph id="HEA86DD78227B4647A0552567775626F2"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Chief Information Officer of the Department shall develop, in consultation with relevant bureaus and offices as appropriate, a strategy and a 5-year implementation plan to advance the objectives described in subsection (a).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB1610ACB725E47A184F5271BC18427C6"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Consultation</header><text>No later than one year after the date of the enactment of this division, the Chief Information Officer shall submit the strategy required by this subsection to the appropriate congressional committees and shall consult with the appropriate congressional committees, not less than on an annual basis for 5 years, regarding the progress related to the implementation plan required by this subsection.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H97C66E6D3BE54C159735150276AF696C"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Improvement plan for the Bureau for Information Resources Management</header> <paragraph id="H1478217D13914651B9F326A1F7590C76"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Chief Information Officer shall develop policies and protocols to improve the customer service orientation, quality and timely delivery of information technology solutions, and training and support for bureau and office-level information technology officers.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H85DC451D5B6E422BB6C8D723DC3389B9"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Survey</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this division, and annually thereafter for five years, the Chief Information Officer shall undertake a client satisfaction survey of bureau information technology officers to obtain feedback on metrics related to—</text> <subparagraph id="H78DE54A995D24991A73DADB4C4EA4ED4"><enum>(A)</enum><text>customer service orientation of the Bureau of Information Resources Management;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H5BD13DDBA94B41F9BDEED78E352C4D7A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>quality and timelines of capabilities delivered;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H5C91F57E017548BA8F5253088803DC18"><enum>(C)</enum><text>maintenance and upkeep of information technology solutions;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC7D2334D93BB4812BD7C13801B9D0AAD"><enum>(D)</enum><text>training and support for senior bureau and office-level information technology officers; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HC40BE43AB403422BB41D6AC5608F6DE3"><enum>(E)</enum><text>other matters which the Chief Information Officer, in consultation with client bureaus and offices, determines appropriate.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3793B1D999BE48048730D10333C4B820"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Submission of findings</header><text>Not later than 60 days after completing each survey required under paragraph (2), the Chief Information Officer shall submit a summary of the findings to the appropriate congressional committees, the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate, and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability of the House of Representatives. </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HE917D7E90E47442A86BD94A8E4CB9B8F"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Significant expenditure defined</header><text>For purposes of this section, the term <term>significant expenditure</term> means any cumulative expenditure in excess of $250,000 total in a single fiscal year for a new unclassified software or information technology capability.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H84C8AAA2186242A88DB0E62CFA04D83E"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text>Nothing in this section may be construed—</text> <paragraph id="H5BF379D6F2204F5AA1052ACA684CCB10"><enum>(1)</enum><text>to alter the authorities of the United States Office of Management and Budget, Office of the National Cyber Director, the Department of Homeland Security, or the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency with respect to Federal information systems; or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H15601CC4C43A49BBB77146D3EFCCE869"><enum>(2)</enum><text>to alter the responsibilities and authorities of the Chief Information Officer of the Department as described in titles 40 or 44, United States Code, or any other law defining or assigning responsibilities or authorities to Federal Chief Information Officers. </text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HD77B6CF3A18C4CAAA2006905D0425DB3" commented="no"><enum>6305.</enum><header>Sense of Congress on strengthening enterprise governance</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline"> It is the sense of Congress that in order to modernize the Department, enterprise-wide governance regarding budget and finance, information technology, and the creation, analysis, and use of data across the Department is necessary to better align resources to strategy, including evaluating trade-offs, and to enhance efficiency and security in using data and technology as tools to inform and evaluate the conduct of United States foreign policy.</text></section> 
<section id="HB91BDE108DBF47979229F3F060E0C747"><enum>6306.</enum><header>Digital connectivity and cybersecurity partnership</header> 
<subsection id="H7C88D564145149CD91FDA08AD1B16EA0"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Digital connectivity and cybersecurity partnership</header><text>The Secretary is authorized to establish a program, which may be known as the <quote>Digital Connectivity and Cybersecurity Partnership</quote>, to help foreign countries—</text> <paragraph id="H080B52DA9255472B97EA1DEDD95B96D5"><enum>(1)</enum><text>expand and increase secure internet access and digital infrastructure in emerging markets, including demand for and availability of high-quality information and communications technology (ICT) equipment, software, and services;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H15C4D1A9839E434F8777E9FD4493B147"><enum>(2)</enum><text>protect technological assets, including data;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H899210E02E6F4FEE8659702B365C3F35"><enum>(3)</enum><text>adopt policies and regulatory positions that foster and encourage open, interoperable, reliable, and secure internet, the free flow of data, multi-stakeholder models of internet governance, and pro-competitive and secure ICT policies and regulations;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3F14EE85C05C4E9A9CCD617C5729437E"><enum>(4)</enum><text>access United States exports of ICT goods and services;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC622075AA80A4537966C61FC4AE23C26"><enum>(5)</enum><text>expand interoperability and promote the diversification of ICT goods and supply chain services to be less reliant on imports from the People’s Republic of China; </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5C3A6CCA53BE403C9E76B3268A9BC37E"><enum>(6)</enum><text>promote best practices and common standards for a national approach to cybersecurity; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6277E28BDA1C48B69A19B5994F887662"><enum>(7)</enum><text>advance other priorities consistent with paragraphs (1) through (6), as determined by the Secretary.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H46A31F6255434D6FAA58A047866A1C05"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Use of funds</header><text>Funds made available to carry out this section may be used to strengthen civilian cybersecurity and information and communications technology capacity, including participation of foreign law enforcement and military personnel in non-military activities, notwithstanding any other provision of law, provided that such support is essential to enabling civilian and law enforcement of cybersecurity and information and communication technology related activities in their respective countries.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H4781450C2E384CA399FFEF24B67F2EAD"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Implementation plan</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees, the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate, and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability of the House of Representatives an implementation plan for the coming year to advance the goals identified in subsection (a).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H1B2A0D31D32849A49965BCFC65FDF62D"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Consultation</header><text>In developing and operationalizing the implementation plan required under subsection (c), the Secretary shall consult with—</text> <paragraph id="HD9352496DCC74BA6B028FB5CE530A701"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the appropriate congressional committees, the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HBD0D62FEB25A49D0B1CE6CB656BC65F0"><enum>(2)</enum><text>United States industry leaders;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H468B66CAB4384D20B43C1AE12A7C82C0"><enum>(3)</enum><text>other relevant technology experts, including the Open Technology Fund;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2D4FDA9A20414A6E9B0140F6ECE583CB"><enum>(4)</enum><text>representatives from relevant United States Government agencies; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HAD1D8BBD6637431A9C1C138371F0C464"><enum>(5)</enum><text>representatives from like-minded allies and partners.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HC88586B85EBE418D89010023B402BE4A"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Authorization of appropriations</header><text>For the purposes of carrying out this section, funds authorized to be appropriated to carry out chapter 4 of part II of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2346">22 U.S.C. 2346 et seq.</external-xref>) may be made available, notwithstanding any other provision of law to strengthen civilian cybersecurity and information and communications technology capacity, including for participation of foreign law enforcement and military personnel in non-military activities, and for contributions to international organizations and international financial institutions of which the United States is a member. Such funds shall remain available until expended. </text></subsection></section> <section id="H543505D30D7C40B78A1746A2706EBA79" commented="no"><enum>6307.</enum><header>Establishment of a cyberspace, digital connectivity, and related technologies (CDT) fund</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Part II of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2301">22 U.S.C. 2301 et seq.</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following new chapter:</text> 
<quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HE6E046B4788A42CCB8B848C11AE26FEC"> 
<chapter id="HA5003D154C6E4C78B209B0DCCCDB3F95"><enum>10</enum><header>Cyberspace, digital connectivity, and related technologies (CDT) fund</header> 
<section id="HE7311FF7BFE34D6FB4CB8E6C508F4F17"><enum>591.</enum><header>Findings</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Congress makes the following findings:</text> <paragraph id="H46730F9243D248CEA7393080606F06DE"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Increasingly digitized and interconnected social, political, and economic systems have introduced new vulnerabilities for malicious actors to exploit, which threatens economic and national security.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H31B7F12AABB24A65A0AB3DB57D150745"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The rapid development, deployment, and integration of information and communication technologies into all aspects of modern life bring mounting risks of accidents and malicious activity involving such technologies, and their potential consequences.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H51DADBD62F544415A2C70EDED43120A4"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Because information and communication technologies are globally manufactured, traded, and networked, the economic and national security of the United State depends greatly on cybersecurity practices of other actors, including other countries.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1A23E47C9CED4BDC98DBF1BA03869002"><enum>(4)</enum><text>United States assistance to countries and international organizations to bolster civilian capacity to address national cybersecurity and deterrence in cyberspace can help—</text> <subparagraph id="HA72048FE2E724100B5CB418479CE510C"><enum>(A)</enum><text>reduce vulnerability in the information and communication technologies ecosystem; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H03991A41ACBB49D9BD29CF4AE875CC8E"><enum>(B)</enum><text>advance national and economic security objectives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></section> <section id="H055B1C06696E4159BA889EEF2E188CEF"><enum>592.</enum><header>Authorization of assistance and funding for cyberspace, digital connectivity, and related technologies (CDT) capacity building activities</header> <subsection id="HBAEAD39329B949CF81DEEF2F4E69FE14"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Authorization</header><text>The Secretary of State is authorized to provide assistance to foreign governments and organizations, including national, regional, and international institutions, on such terms and conditions as the Secretary may determine, in order to—</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD0A625D5E0F1459C9477D04A168CD920"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">advance a secure and stable cyberspace; </text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H7F4BF7F5B7434A4280B8DD7D00959DB8"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">protect and expand trusted digital ecosystems and connectivity; </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H228285269D6C45498700A58AC81C4202"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">build the cybersecurity capacity of partner countries and organizations; and </text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H9A772DCE01994D4ABD8CC6BA9610288F"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">ensure that the development of standards and the deployment and use of technology supports and reinforces human rights and democratic values, including through the Digital Connectivity and Cybersecurity Partnership.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H1453DBE4CC134265AB268818D77E63F4"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Scope of uses</header><text>Assistance under this section may include programs to—</text> <paragraph id="H1FBB21A4A54B4925A26FE17A3595300F"><enum>(1)</enum><text>advance the adoption and deployment of secure and trustworthy information and communications technology (ICT) infrastructure and services, including efforts to grow global markets for secure ICT goods and services and promote a more diverse and resilient ICT supply chain;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3F0DC0E98D0546258FE6DED6BC786FAB"><enum>(2)</enum><text>provide technical and capacity building assistance to—</text> <subparagraph id="H7A6FA519A4324654BB16E9D81B3188BA"><enum>(A)</enum><text>promote policy and regulatory frameworks that create an enabling environment for digital connectivity and a vibrant digital economy;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HE34364531A504AD78E8E22BDF91CCCA9"><enum>(B)</enum><text>ensure technologies, including related new and emerging technologies, are developed, deployed, and used in ways that support and reinforce democratic values and human rights;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2471F25132E8461C950DCBFA6F06EF0C"><enum>(C)</enum><text>promote innovation and competition; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF21F34E98D8E4F0FAE3063A638AA7CBB"><enum>(D)</enum><text>support digital governance with the development of rights-respecting international norms and standards;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H0AEBA7A7FD7E47CD932E374725835E38"><enum>(3)</enum><text>help countries prepare for, defend against, and respond to malicious cyber activities, including through—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HC937A8E5B4D3487B853ABE5F181568FE"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the adoption of cybersecurity best practices;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF358893659B1484F8D052982041B8372"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the development of national strategies to enhance cybersecurity;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC9C59F7A14A34D4F851D1F74948A2806"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the deployment of cybersecurity tools and services to increase the security, strength, and resilience of networks and infrastructure;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H27275C238CA54BE393F229AFA5958958"><enum>(D)</enum><text>support for the development of cybersecurity watch, warning, response, and recovery capabilities, including through the development of cybersecurity incident response teams;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H79A06D6813A64CB59CAD1863693E90DD"><enum>(E)</enum><text>support for collaboration with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and other relevant Federal agencies to enhance cybersecurity;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HDE4EFB5DBD4142CB8DBC2EBAECB4A893"><enum>(F)</enum><text>programs to strengthen allied and partner governments’ capacity to detect, investigate, deter, and prosecute cybercrimes;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H589FCA4F53A74D7BAD205AFEA0C97C0F"><enum>(G)</enum><text>programs to provide information and resources to diplomats engaging in discussions and negotiations around international law and capacity building measures related to cybersecurity;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HDC827AF803794F639E31801E3007F547"><enum>(H)</enum><text>capacity building for cybersecurity partners, including law enforcement and military entities as described in subsection (f);</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H9C6ADD4E89FA4856A6327CF80A9E8FDA"><enum>(I)</enum><text>programs that enhance the ability of relevant stakeholders to act collectively against shared cybersecurity threats;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE271781B07194DDA887FEAF48872AA9A"><enum>(J)</enum><text>the advancement of programs in support of the Framework of Responsible State Behavior in Cyberspace; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HEB86AAFE06664971A6DE81A6DD575B31"><enum>(K)</enum><text>the fortification of deterrence instruments in cyberspace; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H56F27669A7CB409FBF73618F60F3BEFF"><enum>(4)</enum><text>such other purpose and functions as the Secretary of State may designate.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HEAC22F981AA94339993A261965AA8830"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Responsibility for policy decisions and justification</header><text>The Secretary of State shall be responsible for policy decisions regarding programs under this chapter, with respect to—</text> <paragraph id="H26A4801B60024AF395640BDAB7AB3A7D"><enum>(1)</enum><text>whether there will be cybersecurity and digital capacity building programs for a foreign country or entity operating in that country;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3E60E9CB8A4E438685400B79288E2194"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the amount of funds for each foreign country or entity; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7AB856D3474B42AD929CFD55A63AC5F5"><enum>(3)</enum><text>the scope and nature of such uses of funding.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HCEE71D1ECF3E4A35A19D55B0F7D2505D"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Detailed justification for uses and purposes of funds</header><text>The Secretary of State shall provide, on an annual basis, a detailed justification for the uses and purposes of the amounts provided under this chapter, including information concerning—</text> <paragraph id="HDC8D38D4417040C1810C5FE90A015477"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the amounts and kinds of grants;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD275F5C69B004D0DAE5C9C8435236A5B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the amounts and kinds of budgetary support provided, if any; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC76EC82F723F4F5DB25E2A72AB14005C"><enum>(3)</enum><text>the amounts and kinds of project assistance provided for what purpose and with such amounts.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HECA9912B4EAE4D53B12D1754508B2319"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Assistance and funding under other authorities</header><text>The authority granted under this section to provide assistance or funding for countries and organizations does not preclude the use of funds provided to carry out other authorities also available for such purpose.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HFBFA8712EEF14497A7D9E25379C85AE0"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Availability of funds</header><text>Amounts appropriated to carry out this chapter may be used, notwithstanding any other provision of law, to strengthen civilian cybersecurity and information and communications technology capacity, including participation of foreign law enforcement and military personnel in non-military activities, and for contributions to international organizations and international financial institutions of which the United States is a member, provided that such support is essential to enabling civilian and law enforcement of cybersecurity and information and communication technology related activities in their respective countries. </text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H4C8E4E8803C64BE09E329FB82DB67E25"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Notification requirements</header><text>Funds made available under this section shall be obligated in accordance with the procedures applicable to reprogramming notifications pursuant to section 634A of this Act.</text></subsection></section> <section id="HC9B45C0A445644CD92B359180AE8A5FD"><enum>593.</enum><header>Review of emergency assistance capacity</header> <subsection id="H19434E8C240244438C920FBE4D8E996B"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary of State, in consultation as appropriate with other relevant Federal departments and agencies is authorized to conduct a review that—</text> 
<paragraph id="H882ACBA99F4145989A3F86C39BD90D41"><enum>(1)</enum><text>analyzes the United States Government’s capacity to promptly and effectively deliver emergency support to countries experiencing major cybersecurity and ICT incidents;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HCE3AF227E81A4157A2355E6734A9B1A0"><enum>(2)</enum><text>identifies relevant factors constraining the support referred to in paragraph (1); and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2EAA85CA37C24F92A8CCFC7D8E445183"><enum>(3)</enum><text>develops a strategy to improve coordination among relevant Federal agencies and to resolve such constraints.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H044FFDF932DE4238BB9445C4E4E8B607"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this chapter, the Secretary of State shall submit to the Committee on Foreign Relations and the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability of the House of Representatives a report that contains the results of the review conducted pursuant to subsection (a).</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H29A8CF7A27AE49F1B93688641272E738"><enum>594.</enum><header>Authorization of appropriations</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">There is authorized to be appropriated $150,000,000 during the 5-year period beginning on October 1, 2023, to carry out the purposes of this chapter.</text></section></chapter><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section> <section id="HD9E613B6ED8C429B8D58D39211A3306B"><enum>6308.</enum><header>Cyber protection support for personnel of the Department of State in positions highly vulnerable to cyber attack</header> <subsection id="H8F22E6D24A384588B0BF9637AAA099E2"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> 
<paragraph id="H5C618DB21AF04459BBB0E155A866DDF4"><enum>(1)</enum><header>At-risk personnel</header><text>The term <term>at-risk personnel</term> means personnel of the Department—</text> <subparagraph id="H07D2A5BEC5414329B3D691EE30739844"><enum>(A)</enum><text>whom the Secretary determines to be highly vulnerable to cyber attacks and hostile information collection activities because of their positions in the Department; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HD66975B2C3CC496285230782EA723BBF"><enum>(B)</enum><text>whose personal technology devices or personal accounts are highly vulnerable to cyber attacks and hostile information collection activities.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9C749A5CCCCE4ECB88A78BC9EFC4AD44"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Personal accounts</header><text>The term <term>personal accounts</term> means accounts for online and telecommunications services, including telephone, residential internet access, email, text and multimedia messaging, cloud computing, social media, health care, and financial services, used by Department personnel outside of the scope of their employment with the Department.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8313CF49E835427DAA6ED792E7D3BE99"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Personal technology devices</header><text>The term <term>personal technology devices</term> means technology devices used by personnel of the Department outside of the scope of their employment with the Department, including networks to which such devices connect.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H182F1EE26E3849B695407924679B0171"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Requirement to provide cyber protection support</header><text>The Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Director of National Intelligence, as appropriate—</text> 
<paragraph id="H0E7A84F75FE44DD5AC89A0ED5977BAD8"><enum>(1)</enum><text>shall offer cyber protection support for the personal technology devices and personal accounts of at-risk personnel; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H05B2E683794D438B8EE97564A9B435D0"><enum>(2)</enum><text>may provide the support described in paragraph (1) to any Department personnel who request such support.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H3F2DF0CBABA443B9BCC27145F631F235"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Nature of cyber protection support</header><text>Subject to the availability of resources, the cyber protection support provided to personnel pursuant to subsection (b) may include training, advice, assistance, and other services relating to protection against cyber attacks and hostile information collection activities.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H39C7DC9D97C54055A725A94B80508792"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Privacy protections for personal devices</header><text>The Department is prohibited pursuant to this section from accessing or retrieving any information from any personal technology device or personal account of Department employees unless—</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H1DBAC68DB0614DE9B831D497B6E204B5"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">access or information retrieval is necessary for carrying out the cyber protection support specified in this section; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB9839BCEF34345BAB9C0FC46A45143C7"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the Department has received explicit consent from the employee to access a personal technology device or personal account prior to each time such device or account is accessed.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H72D3F5800FAF457EBD2E01923256B9DD"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text>Nothing in this section may be construed—</text> <paragraph id="H2DDA049B7E87420CA65CB7DB9AAEBC1E"><enum>(1)</enum><text>to encourage Department personnel to use personal technology devices for official business; or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HFC70968F0ACE412B9F67BDEC0E4BC5BD"><enum>(2)</enum><text>to authorize cyber protection support for senior Department personnel using personal devices, networks, and personal accounts in an official capacity.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HC6B0469625C94652BD0BD729DC8D786C"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Report</header> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H435BDCF270AC4282A12024D920418B3F"><enum>(1)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report regarding the provision of cyber protection support pursuant to subsection (b), which shall include—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HB9B3F5C57FE44E8A8C2B7291D3EA2FE6"><enum>(A)</enum><text>a description of the methodology used to make the determination under subsection (a)(1); and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H11FC8F857DE542BD83C8F1FA3B27B456"><enum>(B)</enum><text>guidance for the use of cyber protection support and tracking of support requests for personnel receiving cyber protection support pursuant to subsection (b).</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HBCCFF31982454F8DA7CFBFF1AEE9840A"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Appropriate committees of Congress defined</header><text>In this subsection, the term <term>appropriate committees of Congress</term> means—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H9DA0EF5B352F405EB217F4323325F9F5"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the appropriate congressional committees;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H9B5624BEB14A4094BF8993E7F78BC539"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Select Committee on Intelligence and the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD51F3C80953442DEA39B111AC1C16414"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="H98B79FBB5AA74133B0DB54B2D204737B"><enum>6309.</enum><header>Implementation of GAO High Risk List recommendations</header> 
<subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HF0490909CAC047AA8869FEFD53A55F0F"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary shall implement the Government Accountability Office’s High Risk List recommendations as applicable to the Department for the following activities:</text> <paragraph id="H932A25B3C4774DEF93E271643D140536"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Improving the management of IT acquisitions and operations.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE79EA420295D4A0891567BDAC6A8489E"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Improving strategic human capital management.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HD3F4F51179C245E1A92862C794BEAE81"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Managing Federal real property.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H80693E822529427E90C21DD73BB5F581"><enum>(4)</enum><text>Ensuring the cybersecurity of the nation.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H1568146E4A704F5AB3D3835911595EEE"><enum>(5)</enum><text>Managing government-wide personnel security clearance process.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HE66D0B1C462F45DD90126E6FEAD7408E"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report on the Department’s progress in implementing all of the Government Accountability Office’s High Risk List recommendations as applicable to the Department described in subsection (a).</text></subsection> <subsection id="HEB05E6BA4F90469F96BD964DB34E9CC5"><enum>(c)</enum><header>High Risk List defined</header><text>In this section, the term <term>High Risk List</term> refers to GAO–23–106203, the April 20, 2023, report by the Government Accountability Office titled, <quote>High-Risk Series: Efforts Made to Achieve Progress Need to Be Maintained and Expanded to Fully Address All Areas</quote>. </text></subsection></section></title> 
<title id="H172C40D2F8E94C0CB6B52F42D97E5A1A" style="OLC"><enum>LXIV</enum><header>Organization and operations</header> 
<section id="H245D8141898440798E1959F5D5C31C97"><enum>6401.</enum><header>Personal services contractors</header> 
<subsection id="HF200519FB391491F9003CD4E723665F1"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Sense of Congress</header><text>It is the sense of Congress that the Department should seek to ensure it has sufficient full-time equivalent positions allotted to carry out its current mission, working with the Office of Personnel Management and appropriate congressional committees to that end, and that the use of personal services contractors should not be relied upon to perform core Department functions indefinitely.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H88C785EE4D264CA8BD539C9210742B85"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Exigent circumstances and crisis response</header><text>To assist the Department in addressing and responding to exigent circumstances and urgent crises abroad, the Department is authorized to employ, domestically and abroad, a limited number of personal services contractors in order to meet exigent needs, subject to the requirements of this section.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H41D1E2B942B34F0EB66D5248BF40C562"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Authority</header><text>The authority to employ personal services contractors is in addition to any existing authorities to enter into personal services contracts and authority provided in the Afghanistan Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2022 (division C of <external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/43">Public Law 117–43</external-xref>).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H0E7F1293D867415286F3F644556C429D"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Employing and allocation of personnel</header><text>To meet the needs described in subsection (b) and subject to the requirements in subsection (e), the Department may—</text> 
<paragraph id="HD7ECDE0C34344C88A24005608602977E"><enum>(1)</enum><text> enter into contracts to employ a total of up to 100 personal services contractors at any given time for each of fiscal years 2024, 2025, and 2026; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H590F97CE6A1B4003875E9A3E73163AAF"><enum>(2)</enum><text>allocate up to 20 personal services contractors to a given bureau.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H28E335DFA3A340799AC0026F884AC79B"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Limitation</header><text>Employment authorized by this section shall not exceed two calendar years. </text></subsection> <subsection id="HECF3A9802417466F83C717A88956AC36"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Notification and reporting to Congress</header> <paragraph id="HABEBE9CF91A7424188B364FFC561CAC0"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Notification</header><text>Not later than 15 days after the use of authority under this section, the Secretary shall notify the appropriate congressional committees, the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives of the number of personal services contractors being employed, the expected length of employment, the relevant bureau, the purpose for using personal services contractors, an indication of how many personal services contractors were previously employees of the Department, and the justification, including the exigent circumstances requiring such use.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2398B1E316714F37AF40C6943D7203E7"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Annual reporting</header><text>Not later than December 1, 2024, and annually thereafter for two years, the Department shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees, the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives a report describing the number of personal services contractors employed pursuant to this section for the prior fiscal year, the length of employment, the relevant bureau by which they were employed pursuant to this section, the purpose for using personal services contractors, disaggregated demographic data of such contractors, an indication of how many personal services contractors were previously employees of the Department, and the justification for the employment, including the exigent circumstances. </text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HB285A06B6ECA4D2AB1662553F053347D"><enum>6402.</enum><header>Hard-to-fill posts</header> <subsection id="H96B9047D3B8843B39A81CD35C2572E87"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Sense of Congress</header><text>It is the sense of Congress that—</text> 
<paragraph id="H30BBC4ADA51C42BA8A8C033633F5B8A4"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the number of hard-to-fill vacancies at United States diplomatic missions is far too high, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA4232CD9468F47C7B4B701BA51917E65"><enum>(2)</enum><text>these vacancies—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H538B48C4152040F7ADFD851E1E270363"><enum>(A)</enum><text>adversely impact the Department’s execution of regional strategies;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H61009400FA7E4E1F918786099722E332"><enum>(B)</enum><text>hinder the ability of the United States to effectively compete with strategic competitors, such as the People’s Republic of China and the Russian Federation; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H3724D2A56B92479B8123C032FDF45F7C"><enum>(C)</enum><text>present a clear national security risk to the United States; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H0BB0C80EFD984781A6D2419B8C0DC316"><enum>(3)</enum><text>if the Department is unable to incentivize officers to accept hard-to-fill positions, the Department should consider directed assignments, particularly for posts in Africa, and other means to more effectively advance the national interests of the United States.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H643A83826B314A8B96772682D4FD8A98"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Report on development of incentives for hard-to-fill posts</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Secretary shall submit a report to the appropriate congressional committees on efforts to develop new incentives for hard-to-fill positions at United States diplomatic missions. The report shall include a description of the incentives developed to date and proposals to try to more effectively fill hard-to-fill posts.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H724FB0CBB5474A8DB29A1C49C5CA485F"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Study on feasibility of allowing non-Consular Foreign Service officers given directed Consular posts to volunteer for hard-to-fill posts in understaffed regions</header> <paragraph id="HF921F694C08A40498C75868516B32B94"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Study</header> <subparagraph id="HBD07841B6E8F4D3085A5574D040F965C"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Secretary shall conduct a study on—</text> 
<clause id="HB68EE761208F4305965C0FDCA05E6762"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the number of Foreign Service positions vacant for six months or longer at overseas posts, including for consular, political, and economic positions, over the last five years, broken down by region, and a comparison of the proportion of vacancies between regions; and</text></clause> <clause id="H3090C54F7F7243BAB9DB1524D05C8F63"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the feasibility of allowing first-tour Foreign Service generalists in non-Consular cones, directed for a consular tour, to volunteer for reassignment at hard-to-fill posts in understaffed regions.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H2628B9F6E1324731A336BD21562F2113"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Matters to be considered</header><text>The study conducted under subparagraph (A) shall consider whether allowing first-tour Foreign Service generalists to volunteer as described in such subparagraph would address current vacancies and what impact the new mechanism would have on consular operations. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2E759B2F372E409AB0E65BD49D0B0D3D"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than 60 days after completing the study required under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report containing the findings of the study.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HCEF76A8DA4CC438F8A2ECB5CB0FC36F7"><enum>6403.</enum><header>Enhanced oversight of the Office of Civil Rights</header>

<section id="HCBCEC142F86441AB9D3F3D5320EF1A8B"><enum>6404.</enum><header>Crisis response operations</header> 
<subsection id="HE6045D5C7666440284B008A978795EF4"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this division, the Secretary shall institute the following changes and ensure that the following elements have been integrated into the ongoing crisis response management and response by the Crisis Management and Strategy Office:</text> <paragraph id="HE7A723ADF45F48B49B9D8B14838EAB5D"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The Department’s crisis response planning and operations shall conduct, maintain, and update on a regular basis contingency plans for posts and regions experiencing or vulnerable to conflict or emergency conditions, including armed conflict, natural disasters, significant political or military upheaval, and emergency evacuations.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HBE674426E5294EC491FD67108C101C5A"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The Department’s crisis response efforts shall be led by an individual with significant experience responding to prior crises, who shall be so designated by the Secretary.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H6C76A1D501BA4637BA504C4B722EFCE5"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The Department’s crisis response efforts shall provide at least quarterly updates to the Secretary and other relevant senior officials, including a plan and schedule to develop contingency planning for identified posts and regions consistent with paragraph (1).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8F971DD7466B4389BCD690FA1EC29DE0"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The decision to develop contingency planning for any particular post or region shall be made independent of any regional bureau.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H260D49FCCCBF49439F47E699669307C5"><enum>(5)</enum><text>The crisis response team shall develop and maintain best practices for evacuations, closures, and emergency conditions.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HCD69F5998E3945569386236F1B8E640C" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Updates</header> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3DBFFF4E3C764982AED809EDAE4C8275"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, and every 180 days thereafter for the next five years, the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees, the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives an update outlining the steps taken to implement this section, along with any other recommendations to improve the Department’s crisis management and response operations.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB9DC6945FEE547938C5178D5B0956EE9"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Contents</header><text>Each update submitted pursuant to paragraph (1) should include—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HE04EC268EDD742779E5FF2432745A9AC"><enum>(A)</enum><text>a list of the posts whose contingency plans, including any noncombatant evacuation contingencies, has been reviewed and updated as appropriate during the preceding 180 days; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HEEA44A59660646FABABB857933C0A326"><enum>(B)</enum><text>an assessment of the Secretary’s confidence that each post—</text> 
<clause id="H4CE7AE9631AD4C6F8A6C9EA557B8980C"><enum>(i)</enum><text>has continuously reached out to United States persons in country to maintain and update contact information for as many such persons as practicable; and</text></clause> <clause id="H5D4D49F4E0064654A26D9020CDCE832A"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>is prepared to communicate with such persons in an emergency or crisis situation.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H790204A9C15A41A8B2B7FD7459EF8998"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Form</header><text>Each update submitted pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex. </text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="HE3CC83F73D4E41F19B85F194E1E4B7C3"><enum>6405.</enum><header>Special Envoy to the Pacific Islands Forum</header> <subsection id="H89021301BB184B589F0A6A6DC00C0C66"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Sense of Congress</header><text>It is the sense of Congress that—</text> 
<paragraph id="HC3F35C7C2C0842D7839262BEABA0FE6B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the United States must increase its diplomatic activity and presence in the Pacific, particularly among Pacific Island nations; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB36C377269704E18A959D9F30F15D27B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the Special Envoy to the Pacific Islands Forum—</text>
