<section id="HC2DD32454479456FB4F133E3347A3B7F"><enum>6406.</enum><header>Special Envoy for Belarus</header> 
<subsection id="H8EC1A11715634B42A746F3EF6B677FDD"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Special Envoy</header><text>The President shall appoint a Special Envoy for Belarus within the Department (referred to in this section as the <quote>Special Envoy</quote>). The Special Envoy should be a person of recognized distinction in the field of European security, geopolitics, democracy and human rights, and may be a career Foreign Service Officer.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H6B42F2D82B9E440FADF0FF8C1A864412"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Central objective</header><text>The central objective of the Special Envoy is to coordinate and promote efforts—</text> 
<paragraph id="H67D8C480A6D843059543F440FAB31B98"><enum>(1)</enum><text>to improve respect for the fundamental human rights of the people of Belarus;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HCA60E26091DE4BD79E0118D90A1C3328"><enum>(2)</enum><text>to sustain focus on the national security implications of Belarus’s political and military alignment for the United States; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0297301121444468A0ED60B01A543624"><enum>(3)</enum><text>to respond to the political, economic, and security impacts of events in Belarus upon neighboring countries and the wider region.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H58D79DE24F354DBCAEBB4BD0024ED1F9"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Duties and responsibilities</header><text>The Special Envoy shall—</text> 
<paragraph id="H922B03B2D4AC463284910309FDB30DD3"><enum>(1)</enum><text>engage in discussions with Belarusian officials regarding human rights, political, economic and security issues in Belarus;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9013A27BFB16400AB83BF79C0C75FADD"><enum>(2)</enum><text>support international efforts to promote human rights and political freedoms in Belarus, including coordination and dialogue between the United States and the United Nations, the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe, the European Union, Belarus, and the other countries in Eastern Europe;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCB42ACE4AA7E411B939CBD42157E94F4"><enum>(3)</enum><text>consult with nongovernmental organizations that have attempted to address human rights and political and economic instability in Belarus;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7C959B0B156D47EB9CEC75E55C353856"><enum>(4)</enum><text>make recommendations regarding the funding of activities promoting human rights, democracy, the rule of law, and the development of a market economy in Belarus;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H47E38FF69D7E45DD9C79E12329BC15E8"><enum>(5)</enum><text>review strategies for improving protection of human rights in Belarus, including technical training and exchange programs;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5850CE6F263A4F4C989BE59A3FB329B0"><enum>(6)</enum><text>develop an action plan for holding to account the perpetrators of the human rights violations documented in the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights report on the situation of human rights in Belarus in the run-up to the 2020 presidential election and its aftermath (Human Rights Council Resolution 49/36);</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD0A2195806C545068607875DB5232B97"><enum>(7)</enum><text>engage with member countries of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe and the European Union with respect to the implications of Belarus’s political and security alignment for transatlantic security; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC6EBABAFB62C4B879FCFAAECA967135B"><enum>(8)</enum><text>work within the Department and among partnering countries to sustain focus on the political situation in Belarus.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF9EDE95D7D034C15ADF7091749366AA9"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Role</header><text>The position of Special Envoy—</text> <paragraph id="HDFAAF280A29646F3A98710FE98EC5B0A"><enum>(1)</enum><text>shall be a full-time position;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HAA3D71374008494F8F84A804C077B768"><enum>(2)</enum><text>may not be combined with any other position within the Department;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2661D08668854CC3944EFFDA34063DD4"><enum>(3)</enum><text>shall only exist as long as United States diplomatic operations in Belarus at the United States Embassy in Minsk, Belarus have been suspended; </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE4A62856B6FE4447AAC82A3E38070768"><enum>(4)</enum><text>shall oversee the operations and personnel of the Belarus Affairs Unit; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFA14AE1F637547B08781B333BB641432"><enum>(5)</enum><text>shall have a duty station that is co-located with the Belarus Affairs Unit. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H6F3D63686218425A885F6A4CB4A5784C"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Report on activities</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this division, and annually thereafter for the following 5 years, the Secretary, in consultation with the Special Envoy, shall submit a report to the appropriate congressional committees that describes the activities undertaken pursuant to subsection (c) during the reporting period.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HEE43E10D9FDD486EBEB61E73C4F85B8A"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text>The position of Special Envoy for Belarus and the authorities provided by this section shall terminate 5 years after the date of the enactment of this division.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H32F2B9A695DF49C39D5778F9ADFBD064"><enum>6407.</enum><header>Presidential Envoy for the Abraham Accords, Negev Forum, and Related Integration and Normalization Fora and Agreements</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Title I of the State Department Basic Authorities Act of 1956 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2651a">22 U.S.C. 2651a et seq.</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following new section:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HA5850C5E86394AF5B40C371C80DE3E85"> <section id="HA79EE0A0C1C14CD6AAB8A1E8F3BFAE63"><enum>64.</enum><header>Presidential Envoy for the Abraham Accords, Negev Forum, and Related Integration and Normalization Fora and Agreements</header> <subsection id="H4844624D7D5C4762A95AAC9B83569638"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Office</header><text>There is established within the Department of State the Office of the Special Presidential Envoy for the Abraham Accords, Negev Forum, and Related Integration and Normalization Fora and Agreements (referred to in this section as the <quote>Regional Integration Office</quote>). </text></subsection> 
<subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD124007680394EB09363FE36F47574F2"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Leadership</header> 
<paragraph id="H81968A78FB7542EC85AB52383A1F259A"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Special envoy</header><text>The Regional Integration Office shall be headed by the Special Presidential Envoy for the Abraham Accords, Negev Forum, and Related Normalization Agreements, who shall—</text> <subparagraph id="HD0FCBBFF9BA14D6AB2C04D9D8EA184D2"><enum>(A)</enum><text>be appointed by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H41070EA9B083416098C965333DC7BAC4"><enum>(B)</enum><text>report directly to the Secretary of State.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HA8574BF3F4DF4F32AD0ADF08E175AF7C"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Rank and status of ambassador</header><text>The Special Envoy shall have the rank and status of ambassador.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H9B6B74AF20B140E3AAE1E11FEAA604EF"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Duties</header><text>The Special Envoy shall—</text> <paragraph id="H777D5B88240B47A0BCF6819397EBD99E"><enum>(1)</enum><text>lead diplomatic engagement—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H8338414A45464ED08B5B4D3DF493F16A"><enum>(A)</enum><text>to strengthen and expand the Negev Forum, the Abraham Accords, and related normalization agreements with Israel, including promoting initiatives that benefit the people of key partners in regional integration or other regional actors in order to encourage such expansion; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H8FBBFDD506F14E12949FE990AD01DB5A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to support the work of regional integration;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2B492BABE87C4C1EA2B0413C23D1B2DF"><enum>(2)</enum><text>implement the policy of the United States to expand normalization and support greater regional integration—</text> <subparagraph id="H429D91FFE7E44DAC9FBFF8057F31BCD1"><enum>(A)</enum><text>within the Middle East and North Africa; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H424C6618D76F4544981C96F5833B5B82"><enum>(B)</enum><text>between the Middle East and North Africa and other key regions, including sub-Saharan Africa, the Indo-Pacific region, and beyond;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H74646E12B7D749ABBB21BE15544C0045"><enum>(3)</enum><text>work to deliver tangible economic and security benefits for the citizens of Abraham Accords countries, Negev Forum countries, and countries that are members of other related normalization agreements;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3C4366D0E41C4B108B0BC44D1C6AF84B"><enum>(4)</enum><text>serve as the ministerial liaison for the United States to the Negev Forum and other emerging normalization and integration fora, as necessary, and provide senior representation at events, steering committee meetings, and other relevant diplomatic engagements relating to the Negev Forum or other regional integration bodies;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H16DA93087D924CF9AFBA2A0C7449857D"><enum>(5)</enum><text>coordinate all cross-agency engagements and strategies in support of normalization efforts with other relevant officials and agencies;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HAC113AA1274741D798B046417467C6DC"><enum>(6)</enum><text>ensure that the appropriate congressional committees are regularly informed about the work of the Regional Integration Office;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDD992B01B05B41359E7134E28BAD1696"><enum>(7)</enum><text>initiate and advance negotiations on a framework for an economic and security partnership with the Negev Forum countries, other key partners in regional integration, and other regional actors; </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HBD07C8C3BBE9489FB6041BBA94912380"><enum>(8)</enum><text>oppose efforts to delegitimize Israel and legal barriers to normalization with Israel;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB8246A676D074218A943DDCD1A7D6C62"><enum>(9)</enum><text>initiate negotiations with Abraham Accords countries and Negev Forum countries, observers, and key partners in regional integration on an economic framework that includes—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H38A73BD4BB3F4344B451325EE89971B4"><enum>(A)</enum><text>improving supply chain security and resiliency;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB915D09C5300486AB38C41FD7C04DED2"><enum>(B)</enum><text>aligning common regulatory and financial standards;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFE6504DD14AC435799A673743B281377"><enum>(C)</enum><text>attracting foreign investment;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HC4D4A5BB32DD47B8839009001ABD08FA"><enum>(D)</enum><text>diversification of energy resources, including renewable sources of energy, and the development and deployment of emerging and advanced technologies that promote energy security; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HD86525C561024C9291CF6E85DB25EB13"><enum>(E)</enum><text>digital economy, cybersecurity, and cross-border data flow;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9D558923E8A045A69E040A2DF280E169"><enum>(10)</enum><text>lead interagency efforts to reach an international agreement on the comprehensive economic framework described in paragraph (9); </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H55AA26FA737745F6817B2759C60209B6"><enum>(11)</enum><text>endeavor to embed already established standards on countering money laundering and terrorist financing into the regional economic framework described in paragraph (9); and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H54A92DF166E04608B14585DEAC783404"><enum>(12)</enum><text>promote regional integration and broader interconnectivity among the Abraham Accords countries, Negev Forum countries, observers, key partners in regional integration, and other regional actors by promoting and supporting targeted investment in regional infrastructure and other critical sectors that broaden and deepen interconnectivity, increase economic growth and resilience, create benefits for citizens of Abraham Accords countries and Negev Forum countries, and advance the national security, economic, and development interests of the United States.</text></paragraph></subsection>

<paragraph id="H3D5F71217E124D82969E8722A399146D"><enum>(3)</enum><text>a report on the status of and actions taken to implement section 708 of the Championing American Business through Diplomacy Act of 2019 (title VII of division J of <external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/116/94">Public Law 116–94</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/9904">22 U.S.C. 9904</external-xref>). </text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H7291A3C928E841FE82DCF47A51E04CCF"><enum>6503.</enum><header>Direction to embassy deal teams</header> <subsection id="HF5D1066F2DA14DD5A15191A06407285C"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Purposes</header><text>The purposes of deal teams at United States embassies and consulates are—</text> 
<paragraph id="H7396809DBF9C49F0B8EBA044AE3F2BFA"><enum>(1)</enum><text>to promote a private sector-led approach—</text> <subparagraph id="H6D8E87AD519C43B4A91E0614D34FC373"><enum>(A)</enum><text>to advance economic growth and job creation that is tailored, as appropriate, to specific economic sectors; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H20C7612462D148CB99D5955C53C5344D"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to advance strategic partnerships;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA7B6C98CFE7E4AA49EC23B019359536E"><enum>(2)</enum><text>to prioritize efforts—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H1E97EC561702410BABE0C47671905D6E"><enum>(A)</enum><text>to identify commercial and investment opportunities;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HADC6B12FFA1B4176B2FA12D271A249B8"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to advocate for improvements in the business and investment climate;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H0BE2E68BBD9E4CBAB61237699EE1C765"><enum>(C)</enum><text>to engage and consult with private sector partners; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H94B00B2E8EC14999A49E08E6F6948484"><enum>(D)</enum><text>to report on the activities described in subparagraphs (A) through (C), in accordance with the applicable requirements under sections 706 and 707 of the Championing American Business Through Diplomacy Act of 2019 (22 U.S.C. 9902 and 9903);</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2D11894B03174689A5257D37DF99D274"><enum>(3)</enum> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="yes-display-inline" id="H115B6648AA2A42A6800EDECA3ACDF909"><enum>(A)</enum> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="yes-display-inline" id="H22AD438C48E442C5B862E7FABDC62985"><enum>(i)</enum><text>to identify trade and investment opportunities for United States companies in foreign markets; or</text></clause> <clause id="H1C146CA5CE6A4A9280CCFDFD1DE51CAF" indent="up1"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>to assist with existing trade and investment opportunities already identified by United States companies; and</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H24E8038A920441E1A8BCDA0A863A3392" indent="up1"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to deploy United States Government economic and other tools to help such United States companies to secure their objectives;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HAEB8021AE99E4B54AD131267159C0311"><enum>(4)</enum><text>to identify and facilitate opportunities for entities in a host country to increase exports to, or investment in, the United States in order to grow two-way trade and investment;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H23F8D530C0BE4B68919C8ADF1173557F"><enum>(5)</enum><text>to modernize, streamline, and improve access to resources and services designed to promote increased trade and investment opportunities;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF6E6B04208C6472BA344B8D4F945F992"><enum>(6)</enum><text>to identify and secure United States or allied government support of strategic projects, such as ports, railways, energy production and distribution, critical minerals development, telecommunications networks, and other critical infrastructure projects vulnerable to predatory investment by an authoritarian country or entity in such country where support or investment serves an important United States interest;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H81F10652DC6F49A1AD5C846D0426187A"><enum>(7)</enum><text>to coordinate across the Unites States Government to ensure the appropriate and most effective use of United States Government tools to support United States economic, commercial, and investment objectives; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE3DF4464C43149309CDA5F242842A8B9"><enum>(8)</enum><text>to coordinate with the multi-agency DC Central Deal Team, established in February 2020, on the matters described in paragraphs (1) through (7) and other relevant matters.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HD05519B6BD7949189F61E8BF759EC171" commented="no"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Clarification</header><text>A deal team may be composed of the personnel comprising the mission economic team formed pursuant to section 207 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HD56CBCC6588D48768E90FC61612C3835"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Restrictions</header><text>A deal team may not provide support for, or assist a United States person with a transaction involving, a government, or an entity owned or controlled by a government, if the Secretary determines that such government—</text> 
<paragraph id="H8EED2DD833C54841811C66DD242E140F"><enum>(1)</enum><text>has repeatedly provided support for acts of international terrorism, as described in—</text> <subparagraph id="HB2116392B7F84B7FB8E02719169A3C92"><enum>(A)</enum><text>section 1754(c)(1)(A)(i) of the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 (subtitle B of title XVII of <external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/115/232">Public Law 115–232</external-xref>);</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H52AFB2933AAE49629E622F49682C9029"><enum>(B)</enum><text>section 620A(a) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2371">22 U.S.C. 2371(a)</external-xref>);</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H5739F1B796994E8F84FDBD0128370322"><enum>(C)</enum><text>section 40(d) of the Arms Export Control Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2780">22 U.S.C. 2780(d)</external-xref>); or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H2028296D1F23478FB1D2ED121123F1C2"><enum>(D)</enum><text>any other relevant provision of law; or</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H92B2E1AA22D64ACCB41B39F09F77E70F"><enum>(2)</enum><text>has engaged in an activity that would trigger a restriction under section 116(a) or 502B(a)(2) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2151n">22 U.S.C. 2151n(a)</external-xref> and 2304(a)(2)) or any other relevant provision of law.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H651290EC87714B16A88793C1181EB0C0"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Further restrictions</header> 
<paragraph id="HD19C222010794524A8EF898FABE07EE8"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Prohibition on support of sanctioned persons</header><text>Deal teams may not carry out activities prohibited under United States sanctions laws or regulations, including dealings with persons on the list of specially designated persons and blocked persons maintained by the Office of Foreign Assets Control of the Department of the Treasury, except to the extent otherwise authorized by the Secretary of the Treasury or the Secretary.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDAADDBD5C7C644A4A5AAAA44EF1C6E20"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Prohibition on support of activities subject to sanctions</header><text>Any person receiving support from a deal team must be in compliance with all United States sanctions laws and regulations as a condition for receiving such assistance.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H202B4CF5BF3448D5AF43922445A9D6A9"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Chief of mission authority and accountability</header><text>The chief of mission to a foreign country—</text> <paragraph id="HC4403C4ADC824E21858750DBF0784172"><enum>(1)</enum><text>is the designated leader of a deal team in such country; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0F268EDC4F3648AE9CE028EBDAC49811"><enum>(2)</enum><text>shall be held accountable for the performance and effectiveness of United States deal teams in such country.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H711F0DDE636B402E8160ADC87846F445"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Guidance cable</header><text>The Department shall send out regular guidance on Deal Team efforts by an All Diplomatic and Consular Posts (referred to in this section as <quote>ALDAC</quote>) that—</text> 
<paragraph id="H7C900FD5C4A14EBE933BF30F5B3BA23A"><enum>(1)</enum><text>describes the role of deal teams; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H835448CCF03A4AC09CE4DF795A4D271B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>includes relevant and up-to-date information to enhance the effectiveness of deal teams in a country.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H05F1D2C64DB7463C9931B96E2ADEF65A"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Confidentiality of information</header> 
<paragraph id="HEDAC8CC33DF24E4F9AEA3D67EE7C17E5"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>In preparing the cable required under subsection (f), the Secretary shall protect from disclosure any proprietary information of a United States person marked as business confidential information unless the person submitting such information—</text> <subparagraph id="H5980000530974EF0819DBAC51C722523"><enum>(A)</enum><text>had notice, at the time of submission, that such information would be released by; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HEA390CAFAB784500ADC80A43ED403D37"><enum>(B)</enum><text>subsequently consents to the release of such information.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H4B9814CA7BA84238B2A8708B8D8FCA46"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Treatment as trade secrets</header><text>Proprietary information obtained by the United States Government from a United States person pursuant to the activities of deal teams shall be—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HC1AF7A0B583B4D5BB2D813E5B30E9AA6"><enum>(A)</enum><text>considered to be trade secrets and commercial or financial information (as such terms are used under section 552b(c)(4) of title 5, United States Code); and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H0613EA94DB6D4E6B981AEDF78DF2D51A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>exempt from disclosure without the express approval of the person.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF3F2273ECD7D4276A317CB3D5E72710E"><enum>(h)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text>The requirements under subsections (f) through (h) shall terminate on the date that is 5 years after the date of the enactment of this division.</text></subsection></section> <section id="H64A7878809034022BE23513B42CEED37"><enum>6504.</enum><header>Establishment of a <quote>Deal Team of the Year</quote> award</header> <subsection id="HA563E213E9B84D87B287CA64C2269B28"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text>The Secretary shall establish a new award, to be known as the <quote>Deal Team of the Year Award</quote>, and annually present the award to a deal team at one United States mission in each region to recognize outstanding achievements in supporting a United States company or companies pursuing commercial deals abroad or in identifying new deal prospects for United States companies.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H84624D82F0E048F1AB2B53239998BAB0"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Award content</header>

<subsection id="HC1B1E44482DD49C0BD6D1B79D13E4448"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Eligibility</header><text>Any interagency economics team at a United States overseas mission under chief of mission authority that assists United States companies with identifying, navigating, and securing trade and investment opportunities in a foreign country or that facilitates beneficial foreign investment into the United States is eligible for an award under this section.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H15DFE94ACAE24F57B779EBCF151BD128"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than the last day of the fiscal year in which awards are presented pursuant to subsection (a), the Secretary shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees, the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate, and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability of the House of Representatives a report that includes—</text>

<section id="HBCC9412F82444466B49B3725D992017D"><enum>6604.</enum><header>John Lewis Civil Rights Fellowship program</header> 
<subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H22BFBEEF92D041F79088B02399260DE5"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Mutual Educational and Cultural Exchange Act of 1961 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2451">22 U.S.C. 2451 et seq.</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H0E436E89B9F347769EB8948F65D8B76D"> <section id="H6E4F73C7660B47589F1A32E0755D2C1D"><enum>115.</enum><header>John Lewis civil rights fellowship program</header> <subsection id="HD90E7777EAE34F8882F980C7E3761064"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text>There is established the John Lewis Civil Rights Fellowship Program (referred to in this section as the <quote>Fellowship Program</quote>) within the J. William Fulbright Educational Exchange Program.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H891E5B703A9340ACAEA013D80A0AA146"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Purposes</header><text>The purposes of the Fellowship Program are—</text> <paragraph id="H53CA8AAF16A341F6A22D58848DB2BBAE"><enum>(1)</enum><text>to honor the legacy of Representative John Lewis by promoting a greater understanding of the history and tenets of nonviolent civil rights movements; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H7A13B9EB402D407FAF8C927117430D0C"><enum>(2)</enum><text>to advance foreign policy priorities of the United States by promoting studies, research, and international exchange in the subject of nonviolent movements that established and protected civil rights around the world.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H575E60A6B13A4CCF8AD76DE62722E9B5"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Administration</header><text>The Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs (referred to in this section as the <quote>Bureau</quote>) shall administer the Fellowship Program in accordance with policy guidelines established by the Board, in consultation with the binational Fulbright Commissions and United States Embassies.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HE88E8018D55849E3A3DD96DA5CEFB9D6"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Selection of fellows</header> 
<paragraph id="HA76B6847EDB4443F8F8C0DDB82C6DE91"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Board shall annually select qualified individuals to participate in the Fellowship Program. The Bureau may determine the number of fellows selected each year, which, whenever feasible, shall be not fewer than 25.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFC3D003F8BE9470690775F9893E646DE"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Outreach</header> <subparagraph id="HDDBA0EDF328E4700B7ED52DC13AE6C12"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>To the extent practicable, the Bureau shall conduct outreach at institutions, including—</text> 
<clause id="H305563E6A78D4627A52D1C8B13FB5C80"><enum>(i)</enum><text>minority serving institutions, including historically Black colleges and universities; and</text></clause> <clause id="HAC0105F095194EA09E35152FF86341E9"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>other appropriate institutions that are likely to produce a range of qualified applicants, as determined by the Bureau.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H47E589CBCCAA42B9A7346573CD60B321"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this paragraph:</text> <clause id="H75AFE1E92D0C48FD92F0126D20820D2E"><enum>(i)</enum><header>Historically black college and university</header><text>The term <term>historically Black college and university</term> has the meaning given the term <term>part B institution</term> in section 322 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/1061">20 U.S.C. 1061</external-xref>).</text></clause> 
<clause id="H32B318CE8A944B3781CAE393D0EB64B6"><enum>(ii)</enum><header>Minority serving institution</header><text>The term <term>minority-serving institution</term> means an eligible institution under section 371(a) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/1067q">20 U.S.C. 1067q(a)</external-xref>).</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H9C90399FA3374459BEEE9BE2C4DFD0A9"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Fellowship orientation</header><text>Annually, the Bureau shall organize and administer a fellowship orientation, which shall—</text> 
<paragraph id="HE2FB355B247042DEAA1C42A8CBCBF44F"><enum>(1)</enum><text>be held in Washington, D.C., or at another location selected by the Bureau; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HAD719C1134A34236BD0E29C324124E35"><enum>(2)</enum><text>include programming to honor the legacy of Representative John Lewis.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H5A835DEC2998421886702DECC2A137BC"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Structure</header> 
<paragraph id="H0371B9737C4C43AAADB4D8E98B28C154"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Work plan</header><text>To carry out the purposes described in subsection (b)—</text> <subparagraph id="H3931CFFDDF674278A143B4AE4D2E2AD4"><enum>(A)</enum><text>each fellow selected pursuant to subsection (d) shall arrange an internship or research placement—</text> 
<clause id="HC6E03611176D46C09063D4B8D8D34EC0"><enum>(i)</enum><text>with a nongovernmental organization, academic institution, or other organization approved by the Bureau; and</text></clause> <clause id="H6ADFCD36A7F34AF096FFA45B5CD36D67"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>in a country with an operational Fulbright U.S. Student Program; and</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H39B78105924A4B2ABD0F582955E4708C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Bureau shall, for each fellow, approve a work plan that identifies the target objectives for the fellow, including specific duties and responsibilities relating to those objectives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H18E78D3E11BF44FA9B8AD7BA63835A29"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Conferences; presentations</header><text>Each fellow shall—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HA1A9CF928C88479D884575A2786D554A"><enum>(A)</enum><text>attend a fellowship orientation organized and administered by the Bureau under subsection (e);</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HC00B5D4989C44E76BF479F5203A35A4D"><enum>(B)</enum><text>not later than the date that is 1 year after the end of the fellowship period, attend a fellowship summit organized and administered by the Bureau, which—</text> 
<clause id="H33FF496C872141D79BD234020FFD0ED2"><enum>(i)</enum><text>whenever feasible, shall be held in a location of importance to the civil rights movement in the United States; and</text></clause> <clause id="HC5453B151FB14934AE4BBA2263BBE9FE"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>may coincide with other events facilitated by the Bureau; and</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H6763BC6A461549C290ED89C8EEECEAB3"><enum>(C)</enum><text>at such summit, give a presentation on lessons learned during the period of the fellowship.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9217CE3670C64E7C80CB11E9A85B2BEA"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Fellowship period</header><text>Each fellowship under this section shall continue for a period determined by the Bureau, which, whenever feasible, shall be not fewer than 10 months.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HBC2525CF01424A20B9C4D7B9E9033AEB"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Fellowship award</header><text>The Bureau shall provide each fellow under this section with an allowance that is equal to the amount needed for—</text> <paragraph id="HC1EBE9009C7648A98959D8B49503A28D"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the reasonable costs of the fellow during the fellowship period; and</text></paragraph>

<section id="H37C0E476CDE1469FBFE93B2BE0E6F746" commented="no"><enum>6708.</enum><header>Art in embassies</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 5112(c) of the Department of State Authorization Act of 2021 (division E of <external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/81">Public Law 117–81</external-xref>; 135 Stat, 2350) is amended by striking <quote>2 years after</quote> and inserting <quote>4 years after</quote>.</text></section> <section id="H00C658444F11420DB296FB02B413B03B"><enum>6709.</enum><header>Institute for Transatlantic Engagement</header> <subsection id="H0C854B919A4542B1B150619B9E179ADB"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text>The Secretary of State is authorized to establish the Institute for Transatlantic Engagement (referred to in this section as the <quote>Institute</quote>).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H9B37B6FD5BD040FE851559674C9B083A"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Purpose</header><text>The purpose of any Institute established pursuant to subsection (a) shall be to strengthen national security by highlighting, to a geographically diverse set of populations from the United States, Canada, and European nations, the importance of the transatlantic relationship and the threats posed by adversarial countries, such as the Russian Federation and the People’s Republic of China, to democracy, free-market economic principles, and human rights.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H251A0150AD2749E19F1F31B6645F3205"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Director</header><text>Any Institute established pursuant to subsection (a) shall be headed by a Director, to be appointed by the Secretary, who shall have expertise in transatlantic relations and diverse populations in the United States and Europe.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H8A8E63C60DC34D87A0F10DCBEDA039C8"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Scope and activities</header><text>Any Institute established pursuant to subsection (a) shall—</text> <paragraph id="HDAB02E2D54F8471E9C578D28D80C048B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>strengthen knowledge among participants of the formation and implementation of transatlantic policies critical to national security, including the threats posed by the Russian Federation and the People’s Republic of China;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H380EDF8BF0AE41BAB6C07E1A1A1DC46A"><enum>(2)</enum><text>increase awareness among participants of the roles of government and nongovernmental actors, such as multilateral organizations, businesses, civil society actors, academia, think tanks, and philanthropic institutions, in transatlantic policy development and execution;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5565312C52A64CBD862C9E9E984A6F1D"><enum>(3)</enum><text>increase understanding among participants of the manner in which diverse backgrounds and perspectives affect the development of transatlantic policies;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H75ACD89065F84ED189CB11EA2B4333E4"><enum>(4)</enum><text>enhance the skills, abilities, and effectiveness of participating government officials;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H95608A4C4A3040A888726669DCF2ADDA"><enum>(5)</enum><text>increase awareness among participants of the importance of, and interest in, international public service careers;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2DB4D59C87624B25876916170451FA29"><enum>(6)</enum><text>not less than 3 times annually, convene representatives of the United States Government, the Government of Canada, and of governments of European nations for a program offered by the Institute; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF33F419DE2944406B7A162C7BAECA711"><enum>(7)</enum><text>develop metrics to track the success and efficacy of the program which shall be reported to the appropriate congressional committees and prior to the convening of the first program described in paragraph (6).</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H89FC43AF7EF5477285ADF34FF00E4D82"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Eligibility to participate</header><text>Participants in the programs of the Institute shall include elected government officials—</text> <paragraph id="H7644AC3936B746B9A1F0D9643CEC7F9E"><enum>(1)</enum><text>serving at national, regional, or local levels in the United States, Canada, and European nations; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HED0074D696D642FE8ACC720A17EBE39D"><enum>(2)</enum><text>who represent geographically diverse backgrounds or constituencies in the United States, Canada, and Europe.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HF263D44E3339456FAF9440B31EEF5FBB"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Selection of participants</header> <paragraph id="HCBE0CE91F10E437CA58DD09081BEFB85"><enum>(1)</enum><header>United States participants</header><text>Participants from the United States shall be appointed in an equally divided manner by—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H493C61DAFFAB41E9BBEE62CE1FBB2B1A"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the chairpersons and ranking members of the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H043171BCC10D4153B94D8FBB828BB443"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the majority leader of the Senate and the minority leader of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFDACC2E3CB98415E9DEFBF0485C24524"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the minority leader of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HBC2F5C0732FE423D978BF0637001C8AA"><enum>(2)</enum><header>European and Canadian participants</header><text>Participants from Europe and Canada shall be appointed by the Secretary of State, in consultation with—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H1D75F57812AD47149A53A741CB23D332"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the chairpersons and ranking members of the appropriate congressional committees;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE7EDB2356C624DC28F4A88008E5E627A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the majority leader of the Senate and the minority leader of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF87CB97D719B4B65B22B847AE14B29D9"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the minority leader of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H4FAE87A8E1294479B1A0122A2EAA902A"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Restrictions</header> <paragraph id="HDDFDE92432C7414A946CD11612AFACF4"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Unpaid participation</header><text>Participants in the Institute may not be paid a salary for such participation.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8B54FE9C6EEA4727AF3B48D3A8C4E2D9"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Reimbursement</header><text>The Institute may pay or reimburse participants for reasonable travel, lodging, and food in connection with participation in the program.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H1BE0C2D32FED41599DDDFFA170F9357A"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Travel</header><text>No funds authorized to be appropriated under subsection (h) may be used for travel for members of Congress to participate in Institute activities.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H9BC2B48416454B12B1CF403C4CBE28FE"><enum>(h)</enum><header>Authorization of appropriations</header><text>There is authorized to be appropriated up to $750,000 for fiscal years 2024 and 2025 to carry out this section.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H61605207EF9948B384B4FA9D21FED440"><enum>(i)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text>The authority provided by this section terminates on December 31, 2025.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="HCB2D5CCDB7AD44669C1523D76CDAEDBB" commented="no"><enum>6710.</enum><header>Notification of revocation of clearances</header> 
<subsection id="HA4D4E2C2BFE74D948483A092D6472625"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>With respect to any covered official whose security clearance is suspended or revoked, the Secretary shall—</text> <paragraph id="HE310FB9FDAAF49E5A5C47D7962D9DCF7"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">submit to the Chair and Ranking Member of the appropriate congressional committees, the Majority Leader of the Senate, the Minority Leader of the Senate, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, and the Minority Leader of the House of Representatives a notification not later than 15 days after the suspension or revocation of such clearance; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H4BC10D5AB1314ED19C05AC59E6FFA4FD"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">brief the Chair and Ranking Member of the appropriate congressional committees, the Majority Leader of the Senate, the Minority Leader of the Senate, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, and the Minority Leader of the House of Representatives not later than 30 days after such suspension or revocation on the present employment status of such individual and whether the job duties of such individual have changed since such suspension or revocation.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H0B03100762E1490A8289A9EDD55216D8"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The notification and briefing required by subsection (a) may be provided in classified form, if necessary.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HB03771B8E1DA46BFAED2536DABACBBD9"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Covered official defined</header><text>For purposes of this section, the term <term>covered official</term> means any of the following:</text> <paragraph id="H8357774C5F8D4679AD8B025E9B32CF3F"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Any individual holding a position at or higher than the level of Assistant Secretary or its equivalent in the Department of State.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC494F2DC893F4613911D195B92F1837E"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Any individual holding the position of chief of mission or principal officer at any diplomatic or consular post.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HED2D76BC05D040EB9A50730398B3C17C"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Any individual holding the rank and status of an ambassador or otherwise holding a position that reports directly to the Secretary, such as a special envoy.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H4F6B504C5B974E37A0C8B51ADD122AF8"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text>This section shall terminate not later than three years after the date of the enactment of this division.</text></subsection></section></title></division> <division id="H223F5151FBE34FF9AD202F3495FE1327" style="OLC"><enum>G</enum><header>Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024</header> <section section-type="subsequent-section" id="H62E0B3FC5B234C078382E3811169BACA"><enum>7001.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This division may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024</short-title></quote>.</text></section> 
<section id="H5B4953FC35AE4F71B11B67C00349E700"><enum>7002.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In this division:</text> <paragraph id="H7587376FD0E04ACA846FF3299D2DAA6A"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Congressional intelligence committees</header><text>The term <term>congressional intelligence committees</term> has the meaning given such term in section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3003">50 U.S.C. 3003</external-xref>).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H18B87E06986E48CBAD5FDD7A603335A1"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Intelligence community</header><text>The term <term>intelligence community</term> has the meaning given such term in such section 3.</text></paragraph></section> <section id="H903466D9506F4920873EF919A3CE5718"><enum>7003.</enum><header>Explanatory statement</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">The explanatory statement regarding this division, printed in the House section of the Congressional Record by the Chairman of the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives and in the Senate section of the Congressional Record by the Chairman of the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate, shall have the same effect with respect to the implementation of this division as if it were a joint explanatory statement of a committee of conference. </text></section>

<section id="HBD95B3BB36FB412BA5B859B06BA8A138" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>1105A.</enum><header>Notice and damage assessment with respect to significant unauthorized disclosure or compromise of classified national intelligence</header> 
<subsection id="H274FF3894DB047D5B63129083B735C81" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Notification and damage assessment requirements</header> 
<paragraph id="H9D50855579134B2290FF84AD67E40FCF" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Requirements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the Director of National Intelligence becomes aware of an actual or potential significant unauthorized disclosure or compromise of classified national intelligence—</text> <subparagraph id="HC8DC026C26884736B55C779E382B0980" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">as soon as practicable, but not later than 7 days after the date on which the Director becomes so aware, the Director shall notify the congressional intelligence committees of such actual or potential disclosure or compromise; and</text></subparagraph>

<subparagraph id="H432F3405B1B54F84837269BAD5EBADCA" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a summary of the facts and circumstances of such disclosure or compromise;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9B8E2EC7A94B45EF896016E88A5CB67A" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a summary of the contents of the national intelligence revealed or potentially revealed, as the case may be, by such disclosure or compromise;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H26835FDDD9F94F6BB09C4EA6AF63F9C8" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">an initial appraisal of the level of actual or potential damage, as the case may be, to the national security of the United States as a result of such disclosure or compromise; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H347A1E7D8C7848CDB5CD179439DE7A02" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(D)</enum><text>in the case of an actual disclosure or compromise, which elements of the intelligence community will be involved in the damage assessment conducted with respect to such disclosure or compromise pursuant to paragraph (1)(B).</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>

<clause id="H6951A3533B704822B1DE31872031823D"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>Ensuring that counterintelligence threat information and, as appropriate, finished intelligence on topics related to the functions of the Department, are provided to appropriate personnel of the department or agency without delay.</text></clause> <clause id="H90351F9392BD44ABB57D16E0AC03E1BB"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>Ensuring critical intelligence relevant to the Secretary is requested and disseminated in a timely manner.</text></clause> 
<clause id="H9DA4287E68C746F6B3066A2D600F9F28"><enum>(v)</enum><text>Establishing, as appropriate, mechanisms for collaboration through which Department subject matter experts, including those without security clearances, can share information and expertise with the intelligence community.</text></clause> <clause id="H137771CEA6CD47A7B0987EDCC07AD1BB"><enum>(vi)</enum><text>Correlating and evaluating counterintelligence threats identified within intelligence community reporting, in coordination with the National Counterintelligence and Security Center, and providing appropriate dissemination of such intelligence to officials of the Department with a need-to-know.</text></clause>

<clause id="HCDAEBFA92C0E4DC8BBC5D96F20E09758"><enum>(ix)</enum><text>In coordination with the National Counterintelligence and Security Center, establishing counterintelligence partnerships to improve the counterintelligence defense of the Department.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF67F8DA54A734B2FB7D0E42BFA1E2492"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Deputy Director</header><text>There shall be within the Intelligence Community Counterintelligence Office a Deputy Director who is appointed by the Secretary, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence. <paragraph id="H7EE53E37D3014962853492578EA87D9E"><enum>(5)</enum><header>United States person</header><text>The term <term>United States person</term> means—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HCC0203B0999D45DAA1FB0DAD0DD9E699"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a United States citizen;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H82070144117E4EA49A94D393D20C642D"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">an alien known by the Office of Intelligence and Analysis to be a permanent resident alien;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H008B784AACBF45F9B5213AD034FB36E4"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">an unincorporated association substantially composed of United States citizens or permanent resident aliens; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD8BC7A27E100418D87B334DE37690CFE"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a corporation incorporated in the United States, except for a corporation directed and controlled by a foreign government or governments.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H0F976C62EA3349E0A7057DD304956F0E"><enum>(6)</enum><header>United States person information (USPI)</header><text>The term <term>United States person information</term>—</text> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HCE0D8CDA47A840E980A1E678510D5618"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">means information that is reasonably likely to identify 1 or more specific United States persons; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3D43618017A549AB923B8A4F9F01D2C3"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">may be either a single item of information or information that, when combined with other available information, is reasonably likely to identify one or more specific United States persons.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H74E0A0F4EDBF4080BD1E8A6E10B9D1DA"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Prohibition on availability of funds for covered activities of Overt Human Intelligence Collection Program and Open Source Intelligence Collection Program</header><text>None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this division may be made available to the Office of Intelligence and Analysis of the Department of Homeland Security to conduct a covered activity.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HBAC80E2BF4A746BDA46A8DF764ADB078"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Limitation on personnel</header><text>None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this division may be used by the Office of Intelligence and Analysis of the Department of Homeland Security to increase, above the staffing level in effect on the day before the date of the enactment of this Act, the number of personnel assigned to the Open Source Intelligence Division who work exclusively or predominantly on domestic terrorism issues.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H0494689F3ADE454D8FC06F5932070DB5"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Inspector General of the Intelligence Community assessment of Overt Human Intelligence Collection Program and Open Source Intelligence Collection Program</header> 
<paragraph id="HD99C30D605AC46B9835BF64CED1070A8"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Requirement</header><text>The Inspector General of the Intelligence Community shall conduct an assessment of the Overt Human Intelligence Collection Program and the Open Source Intelligence Collection Program.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2703A103846848F58DBEED8FABB3F041"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The assessment under paragraph (1) shall include findings and, as the Inspector General considers appropriate, recommendations on the following:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H898A193832254C3B84660F31D4142DCD"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Whether the Overt Human Intelligence Collection Program and the Open Source Intelligence Collection Program are legally authorized, and if so, an identification of the legal authorities.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H72423D761B4047D78FE8F871F0A6FCD1"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Whether, and to what extent, such programs have provided valuable insights on national intelligence priorities and intelligence priorities of the Department of Homeland Security, citing specific examples of such insights at the appropriate classification level.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H764F43A5DB7842F2827A7A23F236FB29"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Whether there is sufficient training provided to, and sufficient oversight provided of, personnel of the Office of Intelligence and Analysis of the Department of Homeland Security who conduct intelligence collection under such programs.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HDD13801CC14A40FDAD8C8993AEDE1417"><enum>(D)</enum><text>Whether the responsibilities and requirements for such programs set forth in the relevant policy instructions, intelligence oversight guidelines, and other governing documents or standard operating procedures of the Office of Intelligence and Analysis, particularly as they relate to the obligation to safeguard the privacy, civil liberties, and civil rights of United States persons, are adequate, appropriate, and consistently adhered to by such personnel.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H10C9D862288A4311B28967A01C175DBF"><enum>(E)</enum><text>Whether such programs raise or have raised legal, ethical, or operational concerns, including concerns relating to the actual or potential violation of any applicable policies or procedures for protecting the constitutional or statutory rights of United States persons.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HD1AEE73EAE424343A40C71A56881F9DE"><enum>(F)</enum><text>Whether other Federal agencies, such as the Federal Bureau of Investigation, conduct similar programs and, if so, a comparison of any similarities and differences between the respective programs.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H444B4A300F7A48178BD1474D2501E24D"><enum>(G)</enum><text>With respect to non-analytic intelligence reports produced by the Office of Intelligence and Analysis derived in whole or in part from such programs, whether such reports appropriately minimize United States person information and use press reporting in an appropriate manner.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF4F35CCA1EAE453781EDA563CE6D1428"><enum>(H)</enum><text>With respect to the Open Source Intelligence Collection Program, whether such program is effective at identifying threats directed against the United States, including true threats, incitement to violence, and malign cyber activity.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H6094FEE1FC3F48169C62EE9DBBD2432B"><enum>(I)</enum><text>Whether there have been any identified instances in which State, local, territorial, or Tribal government agencies have used, or sought to use, the Office of Intelligence and Analysis as an instrument to introduce political or politicized information into the national intelligence collection and reporting stream.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H520A7A7FE0404D68BFF45BE9E08EC3A1"><enum>(J)</enum><text>Any other matter the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community determines appropriate.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2DE2EB53E08548BCA780C76D27B2592C"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Briefing</header><text>Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community shall provide to the appropriate congressional committees a briefing on the preliminary findings and recommendations of the Inspector General with respect to the assessment under paragraph (1).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB7922FD992D14B2780A17FD87A53BC06"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Report</header> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H8E17625A4AF141E88652F9C5FEEB39B1"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report containing the findings and recommendations of the Inspector General with respect to the assessment under paragraph (1).</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H28AEF1FE78AE4F00BD9A5EB0C67F3BE3"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Form</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The report submitted pursuant to subparagraph (A) shall be submitted under that subparagraph in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H87B132D62D6A40CA9B71026854005B74"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Quarterly briefings</header><text>The Under Secretary of Homeland Security for Intelligence and Analysis shall, not less than once per quarter, provide to the appropriate congressional committees a briefing on the intelligence collection activities of the Office of Intelligence and Analysis. <paragraph id="H17533BAAA27E42BE90AB5A7E24877D2C" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The manner in which the transnational criminal organization is tailoring the fentanyl products of such organization to attract a wider variety of United States consumers, including unwitting users.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H148325D936B54968998A0E4CF0712AA2" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The degree to which the transnational criminal organization is using human and technical operations to undermine counternarcotics efforts by United States and Mexican security services.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB756E6F8BE8D48DF8B4A66498CEA7A0C" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(6)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An estimate of the annual revenue received by the transnational criminal organization from the sale of illicit drugs, disaggregated by drug type.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE0A67A7BC249474EAC6B9777F2FAE26D" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(7)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any other information the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency determines relevant.</text></paragraph></subsection>

<section id="HEDB755015CC54BF69A39E7703E020ACE" section-type="subsequent-section" display-inline="no-display-inline" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>7337.</enum><header>Assessment of availability of mental health and chaplain services to Agency employees</header> 
<subsection id="H9362B050835A4E95A9BEE35DAE23AA35" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Assessment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Director of the Central Intelligence Agency shall conduct an assessment on the availability of the services of mental health professionals and chaplains with appropriate security clearances to employees of the Agency. Such assessment shall include—</text> <paragraph id="HAA67DE3B080B42508743D1AB38A6FE12" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><text>an evaluation of the current availability of and demand for such services globally;</text></paragraph>
