<section id="HD83FE4794C0E466EAF9E87784235F472" section-type="subsequent-section" display-inline="no-display-inline" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>7338.</enum><header>Assessment by Director of Central Intelligence Agency on certain effects of Abraham Accords</header> 
<subsection id="H3AD33FBFBB784FFCBFF7073BE68B2735" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Assessment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency, in consultation with the heads of the other elements of the intelligence community that the Director determines appropriate, shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress an assessment of the current effects on the intelligence community of the agreements between Israel and 4 other foreign countries, collectively known as the Abraham Accords, and of the potential effects on the intelligence community if the Abraham Accords were to be expanded to additional foreign countries. </text></subsection> <subsection id="H780F3D5D51F44D29A9AC71ECB13E4F2C" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The assessment under subsection (a) shall include, with respect to the agreements referred to in such subsection, the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H2D1FC0306E754E379AF5D9D432541B6F" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of whether, and in what respects, the agreement between Israel and Bahrain has resulted in the intelligence community obtaining new and valuable insights regarding national intelligence priorities.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFEA910914D1E49F7976A8210F5EBE056" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><text>A description of whether, and in what respects, the agreement between Israel and Morocco has resulted in the intelligence community obtaining new and valuable insights regarding national intelligence priorities.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0547CB9148124EB181015660D9637B2F" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(3)</enum><text>A description of whether, and in what respects, the agreement between Israel and the United Arab Emirates has resulted in the intelligence community obtaining new and valuable insights regarding national intelligence priorities.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H09DF993688B64FAA99C75A0E64555338" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(4)</enum><text>A description of whether, and in what respects, the agreement between Israel and Sudan has resulted in the intelligence community obtaining new and valuable insights regarding national intelligence priorities.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCB97F7D69B2844B2B4547F0AB7A7B034" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(5)</enum><text>An assessment of whether, and in what respects, additional agreements between Israel and other foreign countries to normalize or otherwise enhance relations would result in the intelligence community obtaining new and valuable insights regarding national intelligence priorities.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HB1721CE5AB214A81875C32F5EE399C91" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The assessment under subsection (a) may be submitted in classified form.</text></subsection> 
<subsection changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H5C84528C6E11459698F6282249867A7F"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Definition of appropriate committees of Congress</header><text>In this section, the term <term>appropriate committees of Congress</term> means—</text> <paragraph changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H8D6A8222D9F54D43B3D31F998E28D2C5"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the congressional intelligence committees; </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H958E89D9183E4CF888FB4A52D07CA63B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and </text></paragraph> <paragraph changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H617E60276E51452B80366A8464EDA210"><enum>(3)</enum><text>the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="H73B57DCB4A3A44F4BFBB136D0869B366"><enum>7339.</enum><header>Reporting and investigating allegations of sexual assault and sexual harassment within the Central Intelligence Agency</header> 
<subsection id="HFD99BED2EC7C49FC9104B63286DDDF75"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Sense of Congress</header><text>It is the sense of Congress that—</text> <paragraph id="H7986ECE79E5B4E68B9CD16C4B47279F7"><enum>(1)</enum><text>sexual assault and sexual harassment arise from, and are often indicative of, an environment where toxic, provocative, and sometimes significantly inappropriate behavior is tolerated;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1647691DF8F64421981DE48EAF683CEB"><enum>(2)</enum><text>when supervisors and senior leaders at headquarters and in the field are among the offenders and facilitate a work climate in which toxic and disrespectful behavior is tolerated, harassment and even assault will often go unaddressed and unpunished;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H30336326B3BB4FACB17900222E23EC7D"><enum>(3)</enum><text>while establishing clear policies and procedures and enhancing training are necessary first steps toward protecting victims and establishing stronger internal mechanisms for preventing and responding to future sexual assault and sexual harassment within the Central Intelligence Agency, comprehensive culture change driven by Agency leadership will be necessary to accomplish impactful and enduring improvement; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H60DBB6FA9A4A436DA168D024C2EE5003"><enum>(4)</enum><text>it is vital for the Central Intelligence Agency to maintain an independent and neutral person with whom all employees at all levels, supervisors and non-supervisors, may speak confidentially, informally, and off-the-record about work-related concerns or questions.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HCD0CBD07C8E045E49DBEC42AD1562513"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Sexual assault and sexual harassment within the Agency</header><text>The Central Intelligence Agency Act of 1949 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3501">50 U.S.C. 3501 et seq.</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following new section:</text> 
<quoted-block id="H709D9B64479B4F6FB7EFE942BCD8B55F" style="OLC"> 
<section id="H0E4A1899E2D24BCBA7249376E021191E"><enum>30.</enum><header>Sexual assault and sexual harassment within the Agency</header> 
<subsection id="H2B52A891EA59432496DA7D93177EEFF8"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Responsibilities of Director</header><text>The Director shall carry out the following responsibilities:</text> <paragraph id="HAAA0B061BC9A4907BA1DAD2453DC178B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Establishing professional and uniform training for employees assigned to working with all aspects of the response of the Agency to allegations of sexual assault and sexual harassment.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H92578600BCC646F495537CCD9C707AED"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Developing and implementing policies and procedures to protect the confidentiality of employees who report sexual assault or sexual harassment and to mitigate negative effects on the reputation or career of such an employee as a result of such a report.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC64D243A85F04E18B9AA57062D65DDD6"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Developing and implementing documented standards for—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HE17DF306E7344BD49D29D448026A496A"><enum>(A)</enum><text>appropriate mitigation and protection measures for individuals who make allegations of a sexual assault or sexual harassment to be put in place while an investigation proceeds;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H8D994A5E353E4A8E8D53EE9F79C30901"><enum>(B)</enum><text>appropriate employee consequences to be imposed based on the findings of an inquiry or investigation into a substantiated allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H1B6B92F74A1747C38FB3F6465CF7F4C7"><enum>(C)</enum><text>appropriate career path protection for all employees involved in an incident resulting in a reported allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment while an administrative or criminal investigation or review of the allegation is pending; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H25943B51FC4B42A485ECA394B6A07C2B"><enum>(D)</enum><text>mitigation measures to protect employees and mission execution while such allegations are being addressed.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H15231B2C98E64AE186579908C04D0F89"><enum>(4)</enum><text>Articulating and enforcing norms, expectations, practices, and policies, including with respect to employee promotions and assignments, that are published for the workforce and designed to promote a healthy workplace culture that is inhospitable to sexual assault and sexual harassment.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HAAA41609F5F24ACE9F2033CC7343AA5B"><enum>(5)</enum><text>Developing and issuing workforce messaging to inform Agency employees of policies, procedures, resources, and points of contact to obtain information related to, or to report, sexual assault or sexual harassment globally.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HC492DAD5DA274702BE0B7B3FB20B36A2"><enum>(6)</enum><text>Developing and implementing sexual assault and sexual harassment training for all Agency employees that—</text> <subparagraph id="H2FA58C468C774757933DE9E43CDBC79F"><enum>(A)</enum><text>is designed to strengthen individual knowledge, skills, and capacity to prevent and respond to sexual assault and sexual harassment;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H2B755A9508E94B7083204231A4D6DE91"><enum>(B)</enum><text>includes onboarding programs, annual refresher training, and specialized leadership training; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H135D50A469AF41CD8B8FB0D179EFFCB8"><enum>(C)</enum><text>includes details of the definitions of sexual assault and sexual harassment, the distinction between such terms, and what does or does not constitute each.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE47AA72A541D424BBF96CA2B11653A4D"><enum>(7)</enum><text>Developing and implementing processes and procedures applicable to personnel involved in providing the training referred to in paragraph (6) that—</text> <subparagraph id="H41D69F5012E747BB9253509F5A5A05B1"><enum>(A)</enum><text>are designed to ensure seamless policy consistency and mechanisms for submitting reports of sexual assault and sexual harassment in all training environments; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H7EE66D9EE3874DBFBA2E6E445035E9E9"><enum>(B)</enum><text>include requirements for in-person training that—</text> <clause id="H00259D7D9C354B7BA4DAC4D2D8307456"><enum>(i)</enum><text>covers the reporting processes for sexual assault and sexual harassment that are specific to training environments for students and trainers; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H7B37D5A2B6064BD483A1F404A3440F45"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>shall be provided at an appropriate time during the first 5 days of any extended or residential training course.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE918683BEDC64C18BB463EC6FE5BAF69"><enum>(8)</enum><text>Developing and implementing, in consultation with the Victim Advocacy Specialists of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, appropriate training requirements, policies, and procedures applicable to all employees whose professional responsibilities include interaction with people making reports alleging sexual assault or sexual harassment.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD17C18E2EE864766A2B63419E2190CF6"><enum>(9)</enum><text>Developing and implementing procedures under which current and former employees of the Agency who have reported an allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment may obtain documents and records related to such a report, as appropriate and upon request.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5D1072677C6349E59E283608FDCD8BE4"><enum>(10)</enum><text>Developing and implementing procedures under which an employee who makes a restricted or unrestricted report containing an allegation of a sexual assault or sexual harassment may transfer out of the current assignment or location of the employee, upon the request of the employee making the report. Such procedures shall be consistent with the privilege established in section 31.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H6E459968270645E580E28186A21F9EC1"><enum>(11)</enum><text>Developing policies and procedures for the Special Victim Investigator, as applicable, to facilitate outside engagement requests of employees reporting allegations of sexual assault or sexual harassment as described in sections 31 and 32.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H66C1FB737D7A4EA598474DC27082749F"><enum>(12)</enum><text>Coordinating the response of the Agency to allegations of sexual assault and sexual harassment.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H21996C58B7BF4F9ABEE03CB67F666070"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Semiannual report</header><text>Not less frequently than once every 180 days, the Director shall submit to the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives a report on the activities of all Agency offices responsible for preventing, investigating, adjudicating, and addressing claims of sexual assault or sexual harassment. The Director shall personally review, approve, and submit each report under this subsection on a nondelegable basis. Each such report shall include—</text> <paragraph id="H5342C3D7EF8F4B11A99A5DA9A69E78FF"><enum>(1)</enum><text>for the period covered by the report—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H0E0CC0BE154C4FB084D23CB48B2BE303"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the number of new allegations of sexual assault and sexual harassment reported to any Agency office, disaggregated by restricted and unrestricted reports;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H46DFF9BF05DF42268DC0375E15BB87A1"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the number of new or ongoing cases in which the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office has provided victim advocacy services;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H29394A765B864B22BF1B96E9D257B912"><enum>(C)</enum><text>a description of all training activities related to sexual assault and sexual harassment carried out Agency-wide, and the number of such trainings conducted; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5088A07B8058486E828132AF290AD32A"><enum>(2)</enum><text>for the period beginning on the date of the enactment of the <short-title>Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024</short-title> and ending on the last day of the period covered by the report—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HF2D722ADFBFC44DC9C31B9792ED0FF73"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the total number of allegations of sexual assault and sexual harassment;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H414B1C6C81CE429DA83198E79425E92A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the disposition of each report of such an allegation;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H267F2C00CFAD407696D589DAA3F47ADF"><enum>(C)</enum><text>any corrective action taken in response to each such report;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HAE2CAF965F3C4CD0AB9A6C1187991E2F"><enum>(D)</enum><text>the number of such allegations that were not substantiated; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H82CCC2E055994DB891638EA06F26AE47"><enum>(E)</enum><text>the number of employee reassignment and relocation requests, including—</text> <clause id="H0163C3A1D0DF439B9CCAF705E3F55858"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the number of such requests that were granted;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HEF5D75A480DF4BED9E35F26909D2A412"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the number of such requests that were denied; and</text></clause> <clause id="H76D717CFE01A4402BE75628CEB1AE874"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>for any such request that was denied, the position of the individual who denied the request and the reason for denial.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HEE764A907A9A47C9A13346C112345AC1"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Applicability</header> 
<paragraph id="H449F6F0F23564BE98B7AE8384BD40CDD"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The policies developed pursuant to this section shall apply to each of the following:</text> <subparagraph id="H2428584741B6442F975E93696DF56164"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Any employee of the Agency.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H19FF1089981D47259D0ABA1E50672703"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Any person other than an Agency employee who alleges they were sexually assaulted or harassed at a facility associated with the Agency or during the performance of a function associated with the Agency. If such person is an employee of an industrial contractor, the contracting officer for the relevant contract shall coordinate with the contractually identified representative for the prime contractor in a manner consistent with section 31.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC223897B072F4E7299F18949A8E13DB3"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Relation to existing regulations</header><text>The policies developed pursuant to this section for handling allegations of sexual harassment shall be in addition to the requirements of part 1614 of title 29, Code of Federal Regulations, or successor regulations.</text></paragraph></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subsection> 
<subsection id="HE053D4AA95E14FE5B137D6E4DF7238D4"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Reporting and investigation of allegations of sexual assault and sexual harassment</header><text>Such Act is further amended by adding at the end the following new section:</text> <quoted-block id="H7665567C4EB04516873FFAE1BD2247FF" style="OLC"> <section id="H84590C7C08DE4E19875049F7E474CDA2"><enum>31.</enum><header>Reporting and investigation of allegations of sexual assault and sexual harassment</header> <subsection id="H876A6C0C27FB4ECB957C149E27C1DFE4"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Policies relating to restricted and unrestricted reporting of sexual assault and sexual harassment</header> <paragraph id="H9246235813F54AA48D6479FF37A953DC"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Director shall develop and implement policies, regulations, personnel training, and workforce education to establish and provide information about restricted reports and unrestricted reports of allegations of sexual assault and sexual harassment within the Agency in accordance with this subsection.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HFCD9E5FE56624B6F9A2DEAB7AD287E3C"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Workforce education</header><text>Workforce education developed under paragraph (1) shall be designed to clearly inform Agency employees of the differences between restricted and unrestricted reporting of allegations of sexual assault and sexual harassment, and which individual or office within the Agency is responsible for receiving each type of report.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HB1F5C18EC4CF4928949F5A1C6CC778DE"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Relationship to the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office</header><text>To the extent consistent with preserving a victim’s complete autonomy, the policies, regulations, training, and messaging described in this subsection shall—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HBBC425A90F2042B0847D72642B553063"><enum>(A)</enum><text>encourage Agency employees to make restricted or unrestricted reports of sexual assault and sexual harassment to the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H3FA7EC3EC4404DCDB33820F2C75BE968"><enum>(B)</enum><text>encourage Agency employees to use the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office as the primary point of contact and entry point for Agency employees to make restricted or unrestricted reports of sexual assault and sexual harassment;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H3953153DD7DE4B4581A481561F8B792C"><enum>(C)</enum><text>encourage Agency employees to seek the victim advocacy services of the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office after reporting an allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment, to the extent consistent with the victim’s election; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HD8CF279BC2134C3D9C935161CB2A2003"><enum>(D)</enum><text>encourage Agency employees and individuals who receive disclosures of sexual assault and sexual harassment to provide the report to, and receive guidance from, the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF1958CD169F8439285994617E6115E48"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Election</header><text>Any person making a report containing an allegation of a sexual assault or sexual harassment shall elect whether to make a restricted report or an unrestricted report. Once an election is made to make an unrestricted report, such election may not be changed.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HD1A5A4682D354DE88F6E3654700979AE"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Unrestricted reports</header> <paragraph id="H70803CBBA7EB40EE8A7C25E9066A5B63"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Assistance</header><text>A person who elects to make an unrestricted report containing an allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment may seek the assistance of another employee of the Agency with taking the action required under paragraph (2).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCE18B19CD5E748E2A7BE7EC0A7705068"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Action required</header><text>A person electing to make an unrestricted report containing an allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment shall submit the report to the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office. To the extent consistent with the person’s election after consultation with the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office, the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office may facilitate the person’s contact with any other appropriate Agency official or office, and make available to Agency employees the following:</text> <subparagraph id="H9072525B7CCA423D85823EB5D852B966"><enum>(A)</enum><text>A list of physicians and mental health care providers (including from the private sector, as applicable) who have experience with the physical and mental health care needs of the Agency workforce.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H7190F204A21E4F219CB9D5591256C8C2"><enum>(B)</enum><text>A list of chaplains and religious counselors who have experience with the needs of the Agency workforce, including information regarding access to the Chaplain Corps established under section 26.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H03A9BC9905A74415872595A64B18F03E"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Information regarding how to select and retain private attorneys who have experience with the legal needs of the Agency workforce, including detailed information on the process for the appropriate sharing of information with retained private attorneys.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H9058A0713CB14A7D9163ECAFA9224353"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text>The inclusion of any person on a list maintained or made available pursuant to subsection (c)(2) shall not be construed as an endorsement of such person (or any service furnished by such person), and neither the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office nor the Agency shall be liable, as a result of such inclusion, for any portion of compensable injury, loss, or damage attributable to such person or service.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HAAB843F216C441238EFFA026A1EA427B"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Restricted reports</header> <paragraph id="HBA26C612CE63412B8FB9404F71F5A348"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Process for making reports</header><text>A person who elects to make a restricted report containing an allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment shall submit the report to the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H709D74E89D3D449EB6C704B01ED4F4A0"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Action required</header><text>A restricted report containing an allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment—</text> <subparagraph id="HF7B848BA33A34C2EAE2624117F786DCE"><enum>(A)</enum><text>shall be treated by the person who receives the report in the same manner as a communication covered by the privilege set forth in this section;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HA6D12AFE8A124B53B804D7D3B54D7ACB"><enum>(B)</enum><text>shall not result in a referral to law enforcement or commencement of a formal administrative investigation, unless the victim elects to change the report from a restricted report to an unrestricted report;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H22861207CA6144DD8677CD6AAE0DD326"><enum>(C)</enum><text>in a case requiring an employee reassignment, relocation, or other mitigation or protective measures, shall result only in actions that are managed in a manner to limit, to the extent possible, the disclosure of any information contained in the report;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H32BAE3C7395E4AF1A979FBBDF78F5C10"><enum>(D)</enum><text>shall be exempt from any Federal or, to the maximum extent permitted by the Constitution, State reporting requirements, including the requirements under section 535(b) of title 28, United States Code, section 17(b)(5) of this Act, relevant provisions of Executive Order 12333 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3001">50 U.S.C. 3001</external-xref> note; relating to United States intelligence activities), or successor order, Executive Order 13462 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3001">50 U.S.C. 3001</external-xref> note; relating to President's intelligence advisory board and intelligence oversight board), or successor order, title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/2000e">42 U.S.C. 2000e et seq.</external-xref>), the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/29/621">29 U.S.C. 621 et seq.</external-xref>), title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/12111">42 U.S.C. 12111 et seq.</external-xref>), and sections 501 and 505 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. 791 and 794a), except when reporting is necessary to prevent or mitigate an imminent threat of serious bodily harm.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HEF30B3778CF0463682F328E060521103"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text>The receipt of a restricted report submitted under subsection (d) shall not be construed as imputing actual or constructive knowledge of an alleged incident of sexual assault or sexual harassment to the Agency for the purpose of the Agency’s responsibility to exercise reasonable care to take immediate and appropriate corrective action to prevent and correct harassing behavior.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA31AD261B8784CE5BC25E6BD8DD0B531"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Privileged communications with Agency employees</header> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2E7B76F23D994F17BC543509C06A7134"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A victim shall be entitled to maintain and assert a privilege against disclosure of, and be able to prevent any other person from disclosing, any confidential communication made between the victim and any employee of the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office, if such communication was made for the purpose of facilitating advice or assistance to the victim in accordance with this section. A victim may consent to additional disclosures.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H14549AE5253B4F69A962BF6460BCAE64"><enum>(2)</enum><header>When a communication is confidential</header><text>A communication is confidential for the purposes of this section if made in the course of the relationship between the victim and any employee of the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office and not intended to be disclosed to third persons, other than those to whom disclosure is made in furtherance of the provision of advice or assistance to the victim or those reasonably necessary for such transmission of the communication.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H11A33B4FE9BF44C1A5173FD82D13495E"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Maintenance of privilege</header><text>The privilege is maintained by the victim. A victim may authorize the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office employee who received the communication to assert the privilege on his or her behalf, with confidentiality. The Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office employee who received the communication may assert the privilege on behalf of the victim. The authority of such Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office employee to so assert the privilege is presumed in the absence of evidence to the contrary.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE81E0031402B4BC0AFF802B8A49DA53B"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Exceptions</header><text>The privilege shall not apply to prevent limited disclosures necessary under the following circumstances:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H49D84AAB0A304A91AE1B186B90126A82"><enum>(A)</enum><text>When the victim is deceased.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H244042F0559F4231B4B5509740836A60"><enum>(B)</enum><text>When the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office employee who received the communication has a reasonable belief that a victim’s mental or emotional condition makes the victim a danger to any person, including the victim.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4364EBBC296E47E6ADB153EDACE788C6"><enum>(C)</enum><text>When the otherwise privileged communication clearly contemplates the future commission of a crime or breach of national security, or aiding any individual to commit or plan to commit what the victim knew or reasonable should have known to be a crime or breach of national security.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HFD210D306A054A389BCC9D42109DC992"><enum>(D)</enum><text>When disclosure of a communication is constitutionally required.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HFBEBD46FDC654D4C8260C9E16558CCEF"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Handling of exceptions</header><text>When the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office employee determines that information requires an exception to the privilege, the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office employee who received the communication will protect information pertaining to the facts and circumstances surrounding the underlying sexual assault or sexual harassment allegations to the greatest extent possible.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HDD0A2BCA115D4FC08E51F79C5505E3BE"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Incident reports when victim or alleged perpetrator is an Agency employee</header> <paragraph id="H42742724235E429FA58754FEB7AFE5FA"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Incident reporting policy</header><text>The Director shall establish and maintain a policy under which—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H14D5B4E4081C47B48AC624210818CD92"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the head of the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office is required to submit a written incident report not later than 8 days after receiving an unrestricted report containing an allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H5B9C65107D3D455F827F99C0892B9C74"><enum>(B)</enum><text>each such incident report required under subparagraph (A) shall be provided to—</text> 
<clause id="HB57CCCAAEF864F9CAD20598CC2E8D457"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the Director of the Agency;</text></clause> <clause id="H8D53A3F0C73A4B79871EF792525BBAF7"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the Chief Operating Officer of the Agency;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H61377868593F4AA79C9227E2A47586B4"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the Special Victim Investigator; and</text></clause> <clause id="HA2D8EAF420C14FB2B8A1702011980DDF"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>such other individuals as the Director determines appropriate.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0D786698E9E74D6DAB81E9427ABFE3B2"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Purpose</header><text>The purpose of an incident report required under paragraph (1) is—</text> <subparagraph id="HDC512A0C0D79402B892BAD78B7986792"><enum>(A)</enum><text>to record the details about actions taken or in progress to provide the necessary care and support to the victim of the alleged incident;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H30A9E0E73D73473DBD5C224CDB74DA0C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>to document the referral of the allegations to the appropriate investigatory or law enforcement agency; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HA28A7B0E228A4E748DC02C68513302C9"><enum>(C)</enum><text>to provide initial formal notification of the alleged incident.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2DE5BE43F6304CC795044B09BAD33A5C"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>Each incident report required under paragraph (1) shall include each of the following:</text> <subparagraph id="H8307590BA47645C090D73E6B94C1FD2E"><enum>(A)</enum><text>The time, date, and location of the alleged sexual assault or sexual harassment.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H0DDFB3301D4C4C47B53457EBBD98D995"><enum>(B)</enum><text>An identification of the type of offense or harassment alleged.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H285D36EC6E9F4063A5501FB960CC0825"><enum>(C)</enum><text>An identification of the assigned office and location of the victim.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H1D60009B86E24B199093AC939E39D53D"><enum>(D)</enum><text>An identification of the assigned office and location of the alleged perpetrator, including information regarding whether the alleged perpetrator has been temporarily transferred or removed from an assignment or otherwise restricted, if applicable.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF31545BA1E6C467C8222DF52402DA24B"><enum>(E)</enum><text>A description of any post-incident actions taken in connection with the incident, including—</text> 
<clause id="H95F212C3745C47619A3BF8EE51843D00"><enum>(i)</enum><text>referral to any services available to victims, including the date of each referral;</text></clause> <clause id="HEA4D8FCE97EA47FF8CFEAEAF98A5920A"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>notification of the incident to appropriate investigatory organizations, including the organizations notified and dates of notifications; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HCE9C0C378CAB45B1958A65304DF3F325"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>issuance of any personal protection orders or steps taken to separate the victim and the alleged perpetrator within their place of employment.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9AB47DE225824EA5BF6ED1A477F01A12"><enum>(F)</enum><text>Such other elements as the Director determines appropriate.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H45200D1EB561489E924C392FBDBB1B9B"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Common perpetrator notice requirement</header> 
<paragraph id="H37D665F51F344350BCE0FF6C312CF987"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Unrestricted reports</header><text>Upon receipt of an incident report under subsection (f)(1) containing an allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment against an individual known to be the subject of at least one allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment by another reporter, the Special Victim Investigator shall notify each of the following of all existing allegations against the individual:</text> <subparagraph id="H3E0FF714967547C0B46E7C4586891FEB"><enum>(A)</enum><text>The Director of the Agency.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4E0EAA19F2D54A72ABBFBB175262E8BC"><enum>(B)</enum><text>The Chief Operating Officer of the Agency.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB30D609015964FEBB776E4D2F6F26925"><enum>(C)</enum><text>The Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HCFF98348357141E5A0AA6A3D12D73DD8"><enum>(D)</enum><text>If the individual is an Agency employee, the head of the directorate employing the individual and the first-level supervisor of the individual.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H8CB5114BF2564F24B1DE43EE20A72ABB"><enum>(E)</enum><text>If the individual is an Agency contractor, the Acquisition Group Chief and the contracting officer for the relevant contract. For industrial contractor personnel, the contracting officer shall notify the contractually identified representative for the prime contractor.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H54652EFD93544916AB20B14277653349"><enum>(F)</enum><text>The Inspector General of the Agency.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HBE44C969C312470DA22668EEC8E32206"><enum>(G)</enum><text>Such other individuals as the Director determines appropriate.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H86499344DC964E6FBFF6F3364108F147"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Restricted reports</header><text>In the case of restricted reports under subsection (d), the Sexual Harassment/Assault Response and Prevention Office shall notify any victims known to have filed a restricted report against an individual known to be the subject of at least one unrestricted allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment by another reporter that another allegation has been made against the same individual who is the alleged subject of the victim’s report at the time of the victim’s initial report or any time thereafter upon receipt of any subsequent unrestricted report under subsection (c) or a common perpetrator notice under paragraph (1) of this subsection.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H3A18D3FAE31348238EBD73C97D0BB3BB"><enum>(h)</enum><header>Applicability</header><text>The policies developed pursuant to this section shall apply to each of the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H6521E06D7BB84A15BE43835251BE7B87"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Any employee of the Agency.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H10849F638F2744C2AD261F762CF0A179"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Any person other than an Agency employee who alleges they were sexually assaulted or harassed at a facility associated with the Agency or during the performance of a function associated with the Agency.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HC7EA40182DFF44138522624CB56A725C"><enum>(i)</enum><header>Records</header> 
<paragraph id="HC7C3442ABCB54EAB962A1AC15111CAAF"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Director shall establish a system for the tracking and, in accordance with <external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/44/31">chapter 31</external-xref> of title 44, United States Code (commonly known as the <quote>Federal Records Act of 1950</quote>), long-term temporary retention of all Agency records related to any investigation into an allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment made in an unrestricted report, including any related medical documentation.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H468C921D251D441EA4FB2DA62B7FFEFF"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Relation to privilege</header><text>Any Agency records created under the authority of this section are subject to the privileges described in this section. Routine records management activities conducted by authorized Agency personnel with respect to such records, including maintaining, searching, or dispositioning of records, shall not result in a waiver of those privileges.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD60EDFA4CE5F41ABBBAD2092872852BE"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Applicability to FOIA</header><text>This section shall constitute a withholding statute pursuant to section 552(b)(3) of title 5, United States Code, with respect to any information that may reveal the identity of a victim of sexual assault or sexual harassment, or any information subject to the privileges described in this section.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H3861BA79005B4D0C90D0CDC5D34F4864"><enum>(j)</enum><header>Relationship to the Office of Equal Employment Opportunity</header><text>In the case of a restricted report of sexual harassment, such report shall not result in a referral to the Office of Equal Employment Opportunity, unless the victim elects to change the report from a restricted report to an unrestricted report. In the case of an unrestricted report, the Special Victim Investigator, the Office of Equal Employment Opportunity, law enforcement, or any other appropriate investigative body, or any appropriate combination thereof, may investigate the unrestricted report, as appropriate. Policies and procedures developed pursuant to this section are intended to offer victims options in addition to the process described in part 1614 of title 29, Code of Federal Regulations, or successor regulations.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H8C6F7EB840E6471B9B7D05CC84ADBE57"><enum>(k)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="HCA38BB2237FF4F0D80636E77D6B7EE53"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Report</header><text>The term <term>report</term> means a communication—</text> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB697878A6BF14231BB61F98DE495AFB1"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by a victim;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2A02EDC5FA03433AB0367A7791E17A40"><enum>(B)</enum><text>that describes information relating to an allegation of sexual assault or sexual harassment;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HA43E336BA85C416CA74DD34576B72E6B"><enum>(C)</enum><text>to an individual eligible to document an unrestricted or restricted report; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H779997DADEA3405BB93C2375BC34BDF3"><enum>(D)</enum><text>that the victim intends to result in formal documentation of an unrestricted or restricted report.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF72BB1952FD34D9CBFF7EBEE73A1EF9B"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Victim</header><text>The term <term>victim</term> means a person who alleges they have suffered direct physical or emotional harm because they were subjected to sexual assault or sexual harassment.</text></paragraph></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subsection> <subsection id="H723425248647409A83AA6A232535BE7F"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Special Victim Investigator</header><text>Such Act is further amended by adding at the end the following new section:</text>

<section id="H57AAB23F5E78401AAE5B2A4CF4295682"><enum>32.</enum><header>Special Victim Investigator</header> 
<subsection id="HB5196B2D2A814AAFA69BEABB4F6F8DE7"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text>The Director shall establish in the Office of Security a Special Victim Investigator, who shall be authorized to investigate or facilitate the investigation of unrestricted reports containing allegations of sexual assault and sexual harassment. The person appointed as the Special Victim Investigator shall be an appropriately credentialed Federal law enforcement officer and may be detailed or assigned from a Federal law enforcement entity.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H76090EFE4E154612B95D9F8771C6BEDE"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Responsibilities</header><text>The Investigator shall—</text> 
<paragraph id="H3AD8EB0449224041B14C00E326280B0A"><enum>(1)</enum><text>at the election of a victim (as defined in section 31(k)), be authorized to conduct internal Agency inquiries, investigations, and other fact-finding activities related to allegations of sexual harassment, which may be separate and in addition to any inquiry or investigation conducted by the Office of Equal Employment Opportunity;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2B5C92FD58894ADBB90BAF59EA3CF2AF"><enum>(2)</enum><text>conduct and manage internal Agency inquiries, investigations, and other fact-finding activities related to specific allegations of sexual assault;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA500809CED6349DAA6A3A20FCB0E4E88"><enum>(3)</enum><text>testify in a criminal prosecution in any venue, where appropriate;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HCBC9832B04A24850838CC1FEB815C5E9"><enum>(4)</enum><text>serve as the case agent for a criminal investigation in any venue, where appropriate;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD0E4D92B1E4E429A926BA84ADC4C6E72"><enum>(5)</enum><text>facilitate engagement with other law enforcement relating to such allegations, where appropriate, including coordinating on the matter and any related matters with other Federal, State, local, and Tribal law enforcement agencies, as necessary and appropriate, pursuant to regulations, requirements, and procedures developed in consultation with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service, or other Federal, State, local, or Tribal law enforcement authorities, for any such inquiries, investigations, or other fact-finding activities;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HBC350C28FF3D4193A29728F9004812A2"><enum>(6)</enum><text>develop and implement policies and procedures necessary for the Special Victim Investigator or any law enforcement partner to conduct effective investigations and also protect sensitive information;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE1247E72665649A9A2117250ED1D4764"><enum>(7)</enum><text>serve as the primary internal investigative body in the Agency for allegations of sexual assault, except that, in the case of an allegation of a sexual assault involving an employee of the Office of Security, the Special Victim Investigator shall coordinate with the Inspector General or appropriate criminal investigators employed by a Federal, State, local, or Tribal law enforcement entity, as necessary, to maintain the integrity of the investigation and mitigate potential conflicts of interest;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE8BBFBA6896B4FBE9896CDB841BC9F0D"><enum>(8)</enum><text>establish and coordinate clear policies regarding which agency should take the lead on conducting, or be the lead in coordinating with local law enforcement when applicable, investigations of sexual assault and sexual harassment overseas; and</text></paragraph>

<section id="HDBDE8A70C58A4D6CAA6EF4A64186F8A8" section-type="subsequent-section" display-inline="no-display-inline" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>7342.</enum><header>Defense Intelligence Agency assessment of strategic competition in Latin America and the Caribbean</header> 
<subsection id="H209016FC8A4C450F93C5C7A7542A24DC" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Assessment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency, in consultation with the heads of the other elements of the intelligence community that the Director determines appropriate, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees an intelligence assessment on the level of intelligence and defense cooperation between covered countries and—</text> <paragraph id="HB326FEA0A8FA417E99F69B259B1C04D6" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the People’s Republic of China; and</text></paragraph>

<paragraph id="HB7417F6BEAE449829A9C13B12ED3FDA2" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(5)</enum><text>Arms transfers.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC660EEDE1FFC4BD49E8E268D4A08C191" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(6)</enum><text>Defense equipment transfers.</text></paragraph>

<subsection id="H462EA9FAE03146B8B19F1A4AB7E14801" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Format</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To the extent practicable, the Director shall present the information contained in the assessment under subsection (a) in the format of a chart or other graphic.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HD32638D701474807A95D1632A2AF44A4" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text>

<section id="HD14A5F7C1D4F4CB1A7818495F405D9A0" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>22.</enum><header>Congressional notification of intelligence collection adjustments</header>

<section id="H139DDC0B6AE54C218985DDBA2B43F6CD" section-type="subsequent-section" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>7353.</enum><header>Support by intelligence community for certain cross-functional team of Department of Defense</header> 
<subsection id="H91F585DD18BD42FF8F39895506FA18E3" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Access to information</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Upon request by the cross-functional team of the Department of Defense established under section 910 of the National Defense Authorization Act of Fiscal Year 2022 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/81">Public Law 117–81</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/111">10 U.S.C. 111</external-xref> note) (in this section referred to as the <quote>cross-functional team</quote>), and consistent with the protection of intelligence sources and methods, the head of any element of the intelligence community shall provide such team with access to any information (including any intelligence reporting, analysis, or finished intelligence product) of the element potentially relevant to the duties of such team required under subsection (b)(1) of such section.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H4536F06AFC4D4BBAB5DDD761B9F3DE41" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in subsection (a) shall be construed as waiving the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/104/191">Public Law 104–191</external-xref>) or any other applicable law regarding privacy or the protection of health information.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HFA236AD8E9924AECBA3609906CB947B8" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Staffing of cross-functional team by certain elements</header> 
<paragraph id="H1FDA5261D013499E848F1AA2A35C36F0" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Staffing</header> 
<subparagraph commented="no" changed="not-changed" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H7C3961FAED044A0483465658F9192CCD"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Covered elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The head of each covered element shall detail or assign to the cross-functional team, including through a joint duty assignment (as applicable), intelligence or counterintelligence personnel of that covered element in such numbers as the head, in consultation with such team, determines necessary to support such team in fulfilling the duties required under section 910(b)(1) of the National Defense Authorization Act of Fiscal Year 2022 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/81">Public Law 117–81</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/10/111">10 U.S.C. 111</external-xref> note).</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H10328F1556F94DFDAABDF5F7A61FB368"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Other elements</header><text>The head any element that is not a covered element may only detail or assign to the cross-functional team, including through a joint duty assignment (as applicable), intelligence or counterintelligence personnel of such element if the head of such element—</text> 
<clause changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H6D26FF443CF3495895DF89BE62E61426"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">receives written concurrence from the Director of National Intelligence and the Secretary of Defense regarding the specific personnel to be detailed or assigned; and </text></clause> <clause changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H17469579DD4248F3AB0E29767EC22268"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">submits to the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Armed Services of the Senate, and the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives a notification describing the personnel to be detailed or assigned and the rationale for participation in the cross functional team.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5F638B53D48543E88311DDD6D49C9D8A" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><header>National Security Agency</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In carrying out paragraph (1) with respect to the National Security Agency, the Director of the National Security Agency shall ensure there is detailed or assigned to the cross-functional team at least 1 individual determined appropriate by the Director, who, while so detailed or assigned, shall provide such team with technical expertise of the National Security Agency relevant to the fulfilment of the duties referred to in paragraph (1).</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HDC39DF115D78499A9559BD9F7AAF2D3C" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Additional detail authority</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Upon request by the cross-functional team, the head of any element of the intelligence community may detail to such team personnel of the element to provide intelligence, counterintelligence, or related support. </text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA3A9C5A3563345A1B2C3F9D645473C20" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Covered element defined</header><text>In this section, the term <term>covered element</term> means the following:</text> <paragraph id="HFD9A2F56FD924C199F8AE5BD498E31EF" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The National Security Agency.</text></paragraph>

<section id="H0CDAFFDACB734F9FA5F03DAFE6501244" section-type="subsequent-section" display-inline="no-display-inline" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>7356.</enum><header>Analysis of commercial cloud initiatives of intelligence community</header> 
<subsection id="H5905660F29814BF19BEDB75D3A87F772" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of National Intelligence shall, in coordination with such heads of elements of the intelligence community as the Director considers appropriate—</text> <paragraph id="H7556A354AF854151AD3D9AA83248D7F1" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">complete a comprehensive analysis of the commercial cloud initiatives of the intelligence community relating to the Commercial Cloud Enterprise contract entered into by the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency in November 2020; and </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE05B14746ADE4860A649AE974781BE70" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><text>provide to the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on the Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives a briefing on the findings of the Director with respect to the analysis conducted pursuant to paragraph (1).</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H4CAF5D13A2BB4A4D826816CFC823AB5B" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The analysis conducted under <internal-xref idref="H5905660F29814BF19BEDB75D3A87F772" legis-path="__(a)">subsection (a)</internal-xref> shall include—</text>

<paragraph id="HE88E49E13E204867834C5255AAA4895D" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">efforts underway by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence and elements of the intelligence community to utilize multiple commercial cloud service providers;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H0EA40CEC6F6C41C78F56EF56EEE4DF32" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(4)</enum><text>the operational value that elements of the intelligence community are achieving through utilization of commercial cloud analytic tools and services; and</text></paragraph>

Monitoring Iranian enrichment of uranium-235.</toc-entry></toc> <subtitle id="H93403BD639BB44FDBB18F9B27B72E2DB" style="OLC"><enum>A</enum><header>People’s Republic of China</header> <section id="HBE12D4B386C64A33AC45480D9FA6D1E6"><enum>7401.</enum><header>Intelligence community coordinator for accountability of atrocities of the People's Republic of China</header> <subsection id="H681D08A64B25437BBDB1C323C00F5CE2"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H29EF54CD27A1432DA2691F6D29F7A18E"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Appropriate committees of Congress</header><text>The term <term>appropriate committees of Congress</term> means—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H225B8754316B4E6FA024B96D72A31F2F"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the congressional intelligence committees; </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H14955B38429C42E0B64E66BB97BBABD5"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on the Judiciary, the Committee on Armed Services, and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2628A3BAA6744EED8F9EE68C841EA6FB"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the Committee on Foreign Affairs, the Committee on the Judiciary, the Committee on Armed Services, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H5B860B7621D440C4BC09B137AC7CB711"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Atrocity of the People's Republic of China</header><text>The term <term>atrocity of the People's Republic of China</term> means a crime against humanity, genocide, or a war crime committed by a foreign person who is—</text> <subparagraph id="H24B4DB2C619B4E7DB46D11F25FF26053"><enum>(A)</enum><text>a member, official, or employee of the government of the People’s Republic of China;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H83108F103D5D422CAB82FA3584079A18"><enum>(B)</enum><text>a member, official, or employee of the Chinese Communist Party;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HDCBB714A9B344C17862441E347A27EFE"><enum>(C)</enum><text>a member of the armed forces, security, or other defense services of the People’s Republic of China; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF3B60D8596294178B0B77381869FA144"><enum>(D)</enum><text>an agent or contractor of a person specified in subparagraph (A), (B), or (C). </text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC63B2BD3E76744B489A044CAD9B4BAF1"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Commit</header><text>The term <term>commit</term>, with respect to an atrocity of the People's Republic of China, includes the planning, committing, aiding, and abetting of such atrocity of the People's Republic of China. </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF5029212E25245A4B5AB3C6828196749"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Foreign person</header><text>The term <term>foreign person</term> means—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H1484210C500A42969BCDCFFDB89D4F60"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">any person or entity that is not a United States person; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H154FAD87F6BF45599D2CFABBEC951BBA"><enum>(B)</enum><text>any entity not organized under the laws of the United States or of any jurisdiction within the United States.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H4533659CC7574FC5B95216E035849AE5"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Government of the People’s Republic of China</header><text>The term <term>government of the People’s Republic of China</term> includes the regional governments of Xinjiang, Tibet, and Hong Kong. </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2AAC859E1C5E469BA441C5A35376D110"><enum>(6)</enum><header>United States person</header><text>The term <term>United States person</term> has the meaning given that term in section 105A(c) of the National Security Act of 1947 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3039">50 U.S.C. 3039(c)</external-xref>).</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H16C17523E2B44BC6A1A9D5144273D58A"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Intelligence community coordinator for accountability of atrocities of the People's Republic of China</header> <paragraph id="HDB6B77FF73F041B488B3205F09F58CE6"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Designation</header><text>Not later than 30 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of National Intelligence shall designate a senior official of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence to serve as the intelligence community coordinator for accountability of atrocities of the People's Republic of China (in this section referred to as the <quote>Coordinator</quote>).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H08BD351B79594A549B61688D19BB43E8"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Duties</header><text>The Coordinator shall oversee the efforts of the intelligence community relating to the following:</text> <subparagraph id="HC95814AC44B14560864FAA8C0E0B57C1"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Identifying and, as appropriate, disseminating within the United States Government, intelligence relating to atrocities of the People’s Republic of China.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF577C3A354664442B6D783148791B82C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Identifying analytic and other intelligence needs and priorities of the United States Government with respect to the commitment of atrocities of the People’s Republic of China.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB9FC4FD25CDD412099CCEFB129CA940F"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Collaborating with appropriate counterparts across the intelligence community to ensure appropriate coordination on, and integration of the analysis of, the commitment of atrocities of the People’s Republic of China.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H41343BEE7ECC40A8891CA883180CAF7A"><enum>(D)</enum><text>Ensuring that relevant departments and agencies of the United States Government receive appropriate support from the intelligence community with respect to the collection, analysis, preservation, and, as appropriate, downgrade and dissemination of intelligence products relating to the commitment of atrocities of the People’s Republic of China. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H14BEDB57CF36408A971A08022F4ED26D"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Plan required</header><text>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of National Intelligence shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H265E51E0EA35445E93C6B01CA0A6C24C"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the name of the official designated as the Coordinator pursuant to paragraph (1); </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HFFFB058061C24B83AC0918A4BED72D73"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the strategy of the intelligence community for the prioritization and integration of intelligence relating to atrocities of the People's Republic of China, including a detailed description of how the Coordinator shall support the implementation of such strategy; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HA0B8EDEFC04F4CCAABC38A43AFB73378"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the plan of the intelligence community to conduct a review of classified and unclassified intelligence reporting regarding atrocities of the People’s Republic of China for downgrading, dissemination, and, as appropriate, public release.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC13A2569453A468692A0BFC6D34844C7"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Briefings to Congress</header><text>Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act, and not less frequently than quarterly thereafter, the Director of National Intelligence, acting through the Coordinator, shall brief the appropriate committees of Congress on—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H3EB488C850C842ADA69C54FAC4E94EC2"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the analytical findings, changes in collection, and other activities of the intelligence community with respect to atrocities of the People's Republic of China; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HFDAA19BEFE8F46C4934C09C63D337528"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the recipients of intelligence reporting shared pursuant to this section in the prior quarter, including for the purposes of ensuring that the public is informed about atrocities of the People’s Republic of China and to support efforts by the United States Government to seek accountability for the atrocities of the People's Republic of China, and the date of any such sharing.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H4F29D815122547D4B65B8CF45440284E"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text>This section shall cease to have effect on September 30, 2027.</text></subsection></section> <section id="H31B83FFC93724A0F9BE0B8BE14F90A41"><enum>7402.</enum><header>Interagency working group and report on the malign efforts of the People's Republic of China in Africa</header> <subsection id="H1A0C976C10F04DD4A09753C53E5ECCA2"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment</header> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H7F1D806B0DDA4A3B8A6A2C6CEE43A457"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Director of National Intelligence, in consultation with such heads of elements of the intelligence community as the Director considers appropriate, shall establish an interagency working group within the intelligence community to analyze the tactics and capabilities of the People’s Republic of China in Africa.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H9F8275C906684EDC98244977603B709A"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Establishment flexibility</header><text>The working group established under paragraph (1) may be—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HE729210ECE4B40EAA4707A7F5C201926"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">independently established; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H04A6B6C9ACA940E6A1A19E64708F9FCB"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to avoid redundancy, incorporated into existing working groups or cross-intelligence efforts within the intelligence community.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HCA5A3B0C043848C7B84B84BD0D2334B8"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Report</header> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HA26DAE735F964081B279366983888413"><enum>(1)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Definition of appropriate committees of Congress</header><text>In this subsection, the term <term>appropriate committees of Congress</term> means—</text> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD3D1C90ECA904C2E87ABC17FC586392A"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the congressional intelligence committees;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HF7C597112D7342CA8AB47E0C02C3AE3B"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources, and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H28AEC43D24B442619860D397021B5C09"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the Committee on Foreign Affairs, the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HF685A0033DBB46A8A5ED1D932119BE30"><enum>(2)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the working group established under subsection (a) shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report on the specific tactics and capabilities of the People’s Republic of China in Africa.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3869EF8EA9E94FCFB6ADA91E7523CFE3"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>Each report required by paragraph (2) shall include the following elements:</text> <subparagraph id="H2E57D42F544C4B4ABD18D2D02539A376"><enum>(A)</enum><text>An assessment and description of efforts by the Government of the People's Republic of China to exploit mining and reprocessing operations in Africa.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H8E7E5F132F3F4FB8AD1078C977F9C03E"><enum>(B)</enum><text>An assessment and description of efforts by the Government of the People's Republic of China to provide or fund technologies in Africa, including—</text> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB4C7A7D7B754493F8270E53B06E0278B"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">telecommunications and energy technologies, such as advanced reactors, transportation, and other commercial products; and</text></clause> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H855D4CB2856A4ACBBB9A29579E1282C5"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by requiring that the People's Republic of China be the sole provider of such technologies.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF30816F5F7B844A6985AF1F4A0650144"><enum>(C)</enum><text>An assessment of opportunities for mitigation.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H86BDB14AB43148D3A65D44DA21BB5BE5"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Form</header><text>The report required by paragraph (2) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may include a classified annex if necessary.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD59626E6AD89439A8F2C6844ED5D3330"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text>The requirements of this section shall terminate on the date that is 5 years after the date of the enactment of this Act.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="HC7A8DA796BEE4BE9B650A2963BE36676"><enum>7403.</enum><header>Amendment to requirement for annual assessment by intelligence community working group for monitoring the economic and technological capabilities of the People's Republic of China</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 6503(c)(3)(D) of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (division F of <external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/263">Public Law 117–263</external-xref>) is amended by striking <quote>the top 200</quote> and inserting <quote>all the known</quote>.</text></section> <section id="H89F4BF84BF9A4FB783D00C58CA31FD17"><enum>7404.</enum><header>Assessments of reciprocity in the relationship between the United States and the People’s Republic of China</header> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H48C8E82660EF4F83BA25BBE69936460A"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research, in consultation with the Director of National Intelligence and such other heads of elements of the intelligence community as the Assistant Secretary considers relevant, shall submit to Congress the following: </text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H7BF7D0AAC3BA4BD5B2C9CF62C116F498"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A comprehensive assessment that identifies critical areas in the security, diplomatic, economic, financial, technological, scientific, commercial, academic, and cultural spheres in which the United States does not enjoy a reciprocal relationship with the People's Republic of China.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H79C73410A8A84EA88C57B4D542C51F7D"><enum>(2)</enum><text>A comprehensive assessment that describes how the lack of reciprocity between the People's Republic of China and the United States in the areas identified in the assessment required by paragraph (1) provides advantages to the People's Republic of China. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HC9E1A797605F4FD997010920F809DA75"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Form of assessments</header>
