<subsection id="H87CBA85323124C06B9F1DC3747BC60FA"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Detail</header><text>Detailees on a joint duty assignment (JDA) assigned pursuant to subsection (a) shall be drawn from such elements of the intelligence community as the Director considers appropriate, in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce.</text></subsection> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HBF6A187714E44C3FA455707347BBAD71"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Expertise</header><text>The Director shall ensure that detailees referred to in subsection (a) have subject matter expertise on countries of concern, including China, Iran, North Korea, and Russia, as well as functional areas such as illicit procurement, counterproliferation, emerging and foundational technology, economic and financial intelligence, information and communications technology systems, supply chain vulnerability, and counterintelligence.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HE485B1E38C294D13B006C8AF1086C93E" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Duty credit</header><text>The detail of an employee of the intelligence community to the Department of Commerce under subsection (a) shall be without interruption or loss of civil service status or privilege. </text></subsection></section> <section id="H2AEFDE37641C4295A50DD14A86C86073"><enum>7502.</enum><header>Intelligence Community Innovation Unit</header> <subsection id="HC1A3B393805B43DA8BD5DE4E76DE8A85"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text>Title I of the National Security Act of 1947 ( <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3021">50 U.S.C. 3021 et seq.</external-xref>) is amended by inserting after section 103K the following new section (and conforming the table of contents at the beginning of such Act accordingly):</text> 
<quoted-block style="USC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB991DB5800D8491C8169AEDA7BB5613F"> 
<section id="HCC0127B7B9DA45519B34C36EF839D011"><enum>103L.</enum><header>Intelligence Community Innovation Unit</header> 
<subsection id="H219ADEF99A2D4943A25EA3FA7821B6C4"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2851208A22C24A3F812DEC942541958D"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Emerging technology</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the term <term>emerging technology</term> has the meaning given that term in section 6701 of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/263">Public Law 117–263</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3024">50 U.S.C. 3024</external-xref> note).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H4AB02F11138340BA8C8CB5AAAA0097D3"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Unit</header><text>The term <term>Unit</term> means the Intelligence Community Innovation Unit.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H088AF065AB614F22923FD6AC53AAEB3B"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Plan for implementation of Intelligence Community Innovation Unit</header> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H23984B63B123493FBECFB1E1DE25D330"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Plan required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of the <short-title>Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024</short-title>, the Director of National Intelligence shall develop a plan for how to implement the Intelligence Community Innovation Unit within the intelligence community.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HFB6EA7652DA348DD861DE23CFE5E15C2"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Matters covered</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The plan developed pursuant to paragraph (1) shall cover how the Unit will—</text> <subparagraph id="H6FEB8B18066149EEBDE207FD6C5D03FD"><enum>(A)</enum><text>benefit heads of the elements of the intelligence community in identifying commercial emerging technologies and associated capabilities to address critical mission needs of elements of the intelligence community;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H63E28DE9262B414F9DFCEDB99A3815B7"><enum>(B)</enum><text>provide to the heads of the elements of the intelligence community seeking to field commercial emerging technologies technical expertise with respect to such technologies.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF5E7E6834B4D4FADAA37BE962BF4A60C"><enum>(C)</enum><text>facilitate the transition of potential prototypes and solutions to critical mission needs of the intelligence community from research and prototype projects to production; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H2AE1706D7D664155A177BA8AC7ED51D5"><enum>(D)</enum><text>serve as a liaison between the intelligence community and the private sector, in which capacity such liaison shall focus on small- and medium-sized companies and other organizations that do not have significant experience engaging with the intelligence community.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5D1FDA0F19644AF8917234EBE3F678B9"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Requirements</header><text>The plan developed pursuant to paragraph (1) shall—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HDAC5D57218784612ABCC8C7CF8CE10D0"><enum>(A)</enum><text>plan for not more than 50 full-time equivalent personnel; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H14A10FC70121434C9EAA98E4C7DFC381"><enum>(B)</enum><text>include an assessment as to how the establishment of the Unit would benefit the identification and evaluation of commercial emerging technologies for prototyping and potential adoption by the intelligence community to fulfill critical mission needs.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3E30D0FDA8724429B5CCE4999EDCE88D"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Submission to Congress</header><text>Upon completing development of the plan pursuant to paragraph (1), the Director shall—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H76C9A12B7B4E4AFA8725126769F97DA6"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">submit to the congressional intelligence committees, the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives a copy of the plan; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H8630451D9F7B4597A2863A4E05435A38"><enum>(B)</enum><text>provide such committees and subcommittees a briefing on the plan.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H215E590CB1B046B0A544143F406A0362"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text>To the extent and in such amounts as specifically provided in advance in appropriations Acts for the purposes detailed in this section, not later than 180 days after the date on which the Director of National Intelligence submits the plan pursuant to subsection (b)(4)(A), the Director of National Intelligence shall establish the Unit within the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H3E3CC289724046B8BA9FEB4C7AEA15F2"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Limitation</header><text>The Unit shall not abrogate or otherwise constrain any element of the intelligence community from conducting authorized activities.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H4A271DD9207F43BAB82340602B1C574B"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Director of the Intelligence Community Innovation Unit</header> <paragraph id="HB49C32A198BC470CAC6528F61D649625"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Appointment; reporting</header><text>The head of the Unit is the Director of the Intelligence Community Innovation Unit, who shall be appointed by the Director of National Intelligence and shall report directly to the Director of National Intelligence.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HE3E8C7AC0BEF48F5BD9684ED56895456"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Qualifications</header><text>In selecting an individual for appointment as the Director of the Intelligence Community Innovation Unit, the Director of National Intelligence shall give preference to individuals who the Director of National Intelligence determines have—</text> <subparagraph id="H9D98E57C028945FABCC4CF8DF6D645A6"><enum>(A)</enum><text>significant relevant experience involving commercial emerging technology within the private sector; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF0BE703DCC1C46CF9665A14BD9A86B00"><enum>(B)</enum><text>a demonstrated history of fostering the adoption of commercial emerging technologies by the United States Government or the private sector.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HEF09D0F3B2B244D7A34755ECD78B42CC"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Staff</header> <paragraph id="H0D668C0F5B894A84ABEDA2836C49A49B"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>In addition to the Director of the Intelligence Community Innovation Unit, the Unit shall be composed of not more than 50 full- time equivalent positions.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H4A948D4CD6A049DD8790F0FB957538B4"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Staff with certain expertise</header><text>The Director of National Intelligence shall ensure that there is a sufficient number of staff of the Unit, as determined by the Director, with expertise in—</text> <subparagraph id="H33CE601BBFA74441BCE6A6FC4112B147"><enum>(A)</enum><text>other transaction authorities and nontraditional and rapid acquisition pathways for emerging technology;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HD380029787DB42479C2416500674B193"><enum>(B)</enum><text>engaging and evaluating small- and medium-sized emerging technology companies; </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H15FB461136DB4B3784A585C65FAC19EA"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the mission needs of the intelligence community; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HDBE633D185294D4C97A23828F56E7B89"><enum>(D)</enum><text>such other skills or experiences as the Director determines necessary.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H78C043D5E25D4A7490EF74E5BD995EE8"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Authority relating to detailees</header><text>Upon request of the Unit, each head of an element of the intelligence community may detail to the Unit any of the personnel of that element to assist in carrying out the duties under subsection (b) on a reimbursable or a nonreimbursable basis.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H636D65FE7F5542F494FE3FFF45FE8886"><enum>(h)</enum><header>Ensuring transition from prototyping to production</header><text>The Director of the Intelligence Community Innovation Unit shall transition research and prototype projects to products in a production stage upon identifying a demonstrated critical mission need of one or more elements of the intelligence community and a potential mission partner likely to field and further fund upon maturation, including by designating projects as Emerging Technology Transition Projects under the pilot program required by section 6713 of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (<external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/117/263">Public Law 117–263</external-xref>; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3024">50 U.S.C. 3024</external-xref> note).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H3843A40D786E41DEADAFBEF708D9CA54"><enum>(i)</enum><header>Encouragement of use by elements</header><text>The Director of National Intelligence shall take such steps as may be necessary to encourage the use of the Unit by the heads of the other elements of the intelligence community. </text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H5F89205908D14784A006E033EF60FD53"><enum>(j)</enum><header>Rules of construction</header> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD143A040796C4677A37417E9CE59A6DF"><enum>(1)</enum><header>No preferential treatment for private sector</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in this section shall be construed to require any element of the intelligence community to provide preferential treatment for any private sector entity with regard to procurement of technology construed as restricting or preempting any activities of the intelligence community.</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3092FF0C5084494C9FB04DEF4958D67C"><enum>(2)</enum><header>No additional authority</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Unit established pursuant to subsection (c) will be limited to the existing authorities possessed by the Director of National Intelligence. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H08547812B8464F72BB52332770D95C1E"><enum>(k)</enum><header>Sunset</header><text>The authorities and requirements of this section shall terminate on the date that is 5 years after the date of the establishment of the Unit.</text></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subsection> <subsection id="H980DEB397B5B482E93B0EBCD904F7885"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Clarification of emerging technology definition</header><text>Section 6701(8)(A) of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117– 263; <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3024">50 U.S.C. 3024</external-xref> note) is amended by striking <quote>during the 10-year period beginning on January 1, 2022</quote> and inserting <quote>during the subsequent 10-year period</quote>.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H886048B534D2441B905A6C94AD0DF0C5"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Briefings</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the establishment of the Intelligence Community Innovation Unit pursuant to section 103L of the National Security Act of 1947, as added by subsection (a), and on a semiannual basis thereafter for 5 years, the Director of National Intelligence shall provide to the appropriate congressional committees<italic></italic> a briefing on the status of the Intelligence Community Innovation Unit, the staffing levels of such Unit, and the progress of such Unit in identifying and facilitating the adoption of commercial emerging technologies capable of advancing the mission needs of the intelligence community.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H898B3D737ADB45868D29DBF61EA1EF5D"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H9EEDCFBF57A943E7B78EBB04D3A8478D"><enum>(1)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Appropriate congressional committees</header><text>The term <term>appropriate congressional committees</term> means the congressional intelligence committees, the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives.</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HF523C687E77B47639AB730BA676B1F28"><enum>(2)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Emerging technology</header><text>The term <term>emerging technology</term> has the meaning given such term in section 103L of the National Security Act of 1947, as added by subsection (a). </text></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="H9021C205CF854D70B347E547C7AEC6FF" section-type="subsequent-section" display-inline="no-display-inline" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>7503.</enum><header>Establishment of Office of Engagement</header> 
<subsection id="H1437707FC92C42C8BA46BFDDA9789E98" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Title I of the National Security Act of 1947 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3021">50 U.S.C. 3021 et seq.</external-xref>), as amended by <internal-xref legis-path="901." idref="H3C7DE1F68F164C6CBD6E50433B63C8B5">section 901</internal-xref>, is further amended by adding at the end the following new section (and conforming the table of contents at the beginning of such Act accordingly):</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" id="H907D440A80564E8F901733DC195B8EEA" display-inline="no-display-inline" changed="not-changed"> <section id="HD01E0EE829FA46F08BF933CA32B5EFCD" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>122.</enum><header>Office of Engagement</header> <subsection id="HEF6BAD93C80142889C0F7F9134AD8CAD" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">There is within the Office of the Director of National Intelligence an Office of Engagement (in this section referred to as the <quote>Office</quote>).</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H7819F2F4BC18495FA56CAE9B4A818FFF" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Head; staff</header> 
<paragraph id="H54EA63AA9B5D4205884ADD2D9AE8114E" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Head</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Director of National Intelligence shall appoint as head of the Office an individual with requisite experience in matters relating to the duties of the Office, as determined by the Director of National Intelligence. Such head of the Office shall report directly to the Director of National Intelligence.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE1DCA702F50043C7A37FD678C4BDFF41" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Staff</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To assist the head of the Office in fulfilling the duties of the Office, the head shall employ full-time equivalent staff in such number, and with such requisite expertise in matters relating to such duties, as may be determined by the head.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HCAAA16A462244A6697AD55F0BFE06EA2" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Duties</header><text>The duties of the Office shall be as follows:</text> <paragraph id="H33398EA8336844FDBD3E561D18A23FF0" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><text>To ensure coordination across the elements of the intelligence community efforts regarding outreach, relationship development, and associated knowledge and relationship management, with covered entities, consistent with the protection of intelligence sources and methods.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H728FE6F8E66B48559E0F519F42834F76" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To assist in sharing best practices regarding such efforts among the elements of the intelligence community.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H397606339DA3473D97E4127922C6E823" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(3)</enum><text>To establish and implement metrics to assess the effectiveness of such efforts.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H492148548A52414EB1F5B9D7185B7A56" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Covered entity defined</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section, the term <term>covered entity</term> means an entity that is not an entity of the United States Government, including private sector companies, institutions of higher education, trade associations, think tanks, laboratories, international organizations, and foreign partners and allies.</text></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subsection> <subsection id="H183ABC656FE644A5B120581F31B9148B" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Deadline</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To the extent and in such amounts as specifically provided in advance in appropriations Acts for the purposes detailed in section 122 of the National Security Act of 1947, as added by subsection (a), the Director of National Intelligence shall establish the Office of Engagement by not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act.</text></subsection> 
<subsection changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HDE19D84DEF8244349BA479905BD7A1F6"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Transfer</header><text>The Director shall transfer to the Office of Engagement all functions within the Office of the Director of National Intelligence that, on the day before the date of the enactment of this Act, performed duties set forth in section 122 of the National Security Act of 1947, as added by subsection (a).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H1287FA7A3812469885050A8B07AA5972" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Plan and briefings</header> <paragraph id="H97F4C9AD0630456F88168FC429A6774F" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of National Intelligence shall submit to the congressional intelligence committees a plan for the establishment of the Office of Engagement.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H442CC13ED28544BB8E65AE90770B2E30" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Quarterly briefings</header><text>Not later than 1 year after the date of the establishment of the Office of Engagement, and on a quarterly basis for 5 years thereafter, the Director of National Intelligence shall submit to the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives a briefing on the status of the Office, including with respect to the staffing levels, activities, and fulfilment of duties of the Office.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HF9E9DE1A23E4405881DC0834146F4B57"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Rule of Construction</header><text>Nothing in this section, or an amendment made by this section, shall be construed as restricting or preempting engagement or outreach activities of elements of the intelligence community. </text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H38DB12E1F02B487F9E75C284A5A16D41" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section, the term <term>Office of Engagement</term> means the Office of Engagement established under section 122 of the National Security Act of 1947, as added by subsection (a).</text></subsection></section> <section id="HBC91467EF8DB433E93122245B8713754" section-type="subsequent-section" display-inline="no-display-inline" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>7504.</enum><header>Designation of a chief technology officer within certain elements of the intelligence community</header> <subsection id="HCAA1BD4E66D44733A37C0E91D26CC6D0"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Designation authority</header><text>The head of each covered element of the intelligence community shall designate a senior official to serve as the chief technology officer of such element.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA17ADB4E86C14A12A972669920226825"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Covered elements</header><text>For purposes of this section, the covered elements of the intelligence community are the following:</text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H342791D5CA744B3EA5FA4E9A1300027C"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Central Intelligence Agency.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H1054F44FD1B84C2BA7824C2398089BF3"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Defense Intelligence Agency.</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HFCAE514BECB14E469162B8FCBDAB6EC0"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Federal Bureau of Investigation.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HA4657DEF05914763AEB50B52BC073B04"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency.</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD640BB51BD724E22A24119634E956AA2"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The National Security Agency.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HCCB6B8CD47EE40AF9A47D89493CD5C0B"><enum>(6)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The National Reconnaissance Office. </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H4041C01099B74961A05D278B19F8D428"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Responsibility</header><text>The chief technology officer of each covered element of the intelligence community shall be responsible for assisting the head of such element in the identification and adoption of technology to advance mission needs.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HA8E09CF6C7BA4204BF75F962B293DA85"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Prohibition of dual appointment</header><text>Any chief technology officer designated pursuant to subsection (a) may not concurrently serve as the chief information officer, the chief data officer, or the principal science officer of any element of the intelligence community.</text></subsection></section> <section id="H1B3479D8B7A447D0AF3B0256BCBCC1B5" section-type="subsequent-section" display-inline="no-display-inline" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>7505.</enum><header>Requirement to authorize additional security clearances for certain contractors</header> <subsection id="HF75A82767A2B47DF83F9A9C16EFB4D1C" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section:</text> 
<paragraph changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H308F0D90398247B4A9DC9FE8CA084AC5"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Appropriate committees of Congress</header><text>The term <term>appropriate committees of Congress</term> means—</text> <subparagraph changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3ADB0012FB5C45598450C3A68A9BCB92"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the congressional intelligence committees;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H7719EE699427449E950C6E23E68695C0"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H803BF6CCBF7A480CB9992BD41A94C2C9"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H02542FD8F23A47A4AB2F0802F1B61691" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Covered contract or agreement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>covered contract or agreement</term>, with respect to an entity, means a contract or other agreement between that entity and an element of the intelligence community the performance of which requires a specified number of covered persons to hold a security clearance.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H57F3EE0A97E04E0A98C1002A3EEAD18F" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Covered person</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>covered person</term>, with respect to an entity, means a contractor or employee of that entity.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HBEEF52FE6A454B65A75099576C08E700"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Plan and study</header> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H25BFDB7EDE224B72B6C4A0D29C057E67"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">No later than April 1, 2024, the Director of National Intelligence shall—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H481CBD0652404FA49AD0A09F139C3E1F"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">complete a study on the feasibility and advisability of implementing a program to authorize additional security clearances for certain contractors as described in subsection (c);</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3AA41FC6CCEC4DEE86EADE49C069633A"><enum>(B)</enum><text>develop a plan to implement the program described in subparagraph (A); and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H8640486C32944A5AB19C4BB9D325261E"><enum>(C)</enum><text>submit to the appropriate committees of Congress—</text> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H76240D0BA6A64A78B9A3124CA65D4B4F"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a report on the findings of the Director with respect to the study completed pursuant to subparagraph (A); and</text></clause> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2756EDEA6B024B9C89D33072420B3F0E"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the plan developed pursuant to subparagraph (B).</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H6BCE562B328947B28E176ECFE21E296A"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Study elements</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The study completed pursuant to paragraph (1)(A) shall address the following:</text> <subparagraph id="H348039295F0744F98D8B4561D6D485F9"><enum>(A)</enum><text>For contracts agreed to after the date of the enactment of this Act, how private entities that contract with the intelligence community would make payments for additional clearances for their employees and how the intelligence community would receive payments.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HF72D8FAA47BE44B18CCF1796E19A1346"><enum>(B)</enum><text>A list of and changes to provisions of law required in order to fully implement the program required by subsection (c) and achieve the intent indicated in subparagraph (A) of this paragraph.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HD55D0330800E49179F2677CA80A8B61C"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Such considerations as the Director may have for carrying out the program required by subsection (c) and achieving the intent indicated in subparagraph (A) of this paragraph.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H9FEF1896FCBF41AAB856D475BBB55554"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Program to authorize additional security clearances for certain contractors</header><text> Subject to the limitations described in subsection (d), the Director shall establish a program under which— </text> <paragraph id="HE916E07DB7E447AB92A184C031C05C52" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">any entity that enters into a covered contract or agreement with an element of the intelligence community may designate an additional number of covered persons who may submit an application for a security clearance;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HE6B4CD88DFBA452C9D0892BD8F788DDB" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the appropriate authorized investigative agency and authorized adjudicative agency, as such terms are defined in section 3001(a) of the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3341">50 U.S.C. 3341(a)</external-xref>), shall—</text> <subparagraph id="HA8E76448C2934E96B1678CB21CD52340" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">upon receiving such an application—</text> 
<clause id="HC7C62697A16E4B7A9EFAD7A9C7452FDF" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(i)</enum><text>conduct an appropriate investigation of the background of the additional covered person; and</text></clause> <clause id="HF13FF3B8FFE543209DEC6204EA3E2F1F" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>make a determination as to whether the additional covered person is eligible for access to classified information; and</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H1112A4152D3843D69A92F47D58123B8C" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">if the determination under subparagraph (A)(ii) is favorable, upon any of the specified number of covered persons required to hold a security clearance for the performance of work under that covered contract or agreement becoming unable to perform such work, make a determination as to whether the additional covered person has a demonstrated need-to-know under Executive Order 12968 (60 Fed. Reg. 40245; relating to access to classified information), or any successor thereto, or Executive Order 10865 (25 Fed. Reg. 1583; relating to safeguarding classified information within industry), or any successor thereto (without requiring an additional investigation to be conducted under subparagraph (A)(i)); and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H4515256D663E43FF90FB830ADB2901AC" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">if the additional covered person receives a favorable determination regarding the need-to-know under paragraph (2)(B) and signs an approved nondisclosure agreement, the additional covered person may perform such work in lieu of such covered person.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H6076165A5F2E46D8A3D0CF64A531813A" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Limitations</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The limitations described in this subsection are as follows:</text> <paragraph id="H77EED75ED7CC4BF2A6108CFDE71925D5" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Limitation on number designated per contract</header><text>The additional number designated by an entity under the program established pursuant to subsection (c) for each covered contract or agreement may not exceed the greater of the following:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H768F8210C33E4DF99E88286D138E5760" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">10 percent of the number of security clearances required to be held by covered persons to perform work under the covered contract or agreement.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HEAB13327701549559720285F3A1597B6" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(B)</enum><text>1 person.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H79F57194EC2B4EBEB2228DFBBA1466AD" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Limitation on number designated per entity</header><text>The total additional number designated by an entity under the program established pursuant to subsection (c) may not exceed the greater of the following:</text> <subparagraph id="H29CE2D42004D4B89BE17C7121AD422E9" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">10 percent of the sum total number of security clearances required to be held by covered persons to perform work under all covered contracts or agreements of the entity.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H7C01B134B79D4D8690D93E4C62E7A32D" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(B)</enum><text>1 person.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HA79B340043ED492787E11D4EBDEAB59E" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Prohibitions</header> <paragraph commented="no" changed="not-changed" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H0DB8FC7D22DE4479A1CF28E34C27F4A5"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">No application for a security clearance may be submitted by a covered person of an entity or granted pursuant to the program established under subsection (c) in excess of the limitations under subsection (d) applicable to such entity.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H446F68DEC0294630BA08CC1A03A48B7D"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Prohibition on bearing costs</header><text>No head of an element of the intelligence community may bear any cost associated with granting or maintaining a security clearance the application for which is submitted pursuant to subsection (c)(1). </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H7C398785A7404F7CA4FAF29CE9405BEA" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text>Nothing in this section may be construed as requiring the head of an element of the intelligence community to grant any covered person access to classified information if a favorable determination of eligibility to access such classified information is not made with respect to such person.</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H0D07D1FF425B4355B3244D6F21BC7112" section-type="subsequent-section" display-inline="no-display-inline" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>7506.</enum><header>Intelligence Innovation Board</header> 
<subsection id="HBF96C47013B641378299A1727C45AB07" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Establishment of Intelligence Innovation Board</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">There is established in the executive branch of the Federal Government a board to be known as the Intelligence Innovation Board (in this section referred to as the <quote>Board</quote>).</text></subsection> <subsection id="H166AEDAD9EA24C5687419764CFF42B51" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Purpose</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The purpose of the Board is to provide to the Director of National Intelligence and the heads of the other elements of the intelligence community advice and recommendations on changes to the culture, organizational structures, processes, and functions of the intelligence community necessary to address the adoption of emerging technologies by the intelligence community and to accelerate such adoption. </text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HAB7350BABFE84F7BA8007AA0493402A8" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Membership</header> 
<paragraph id="HB65412C6DD6C4BF3B20054596A0E74A2" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Appointment of members</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Board shall be composed of 9 members appointed by the Director of National Intelligence, after consultation with the Chair and Ranking Member of the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives and the Chair and Vice Chair of the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate, from among citizens of the United States—</text> <subparagraph id="H849A97DA29794EEAAA339FD50A2635CC" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(A)</enum><text>who are not officers or employees of an element of the intelligence community;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HCE331E1ECB4D4FD187A8A8D81EC22050" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">who are eligible to hold an appropriate security clearance;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H706595F336464717BC2BC2D6F6C7115B" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(C)</enum><text>who have demonstrated academic, government, business, or other expertise relevant to the mission and functions of the intelligence community; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HC1263917475B480C97F6BA175DC7A1AD" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">who the Director of National Intelligence determines—</text> <clause id="HA4C937DA7DB7485AA2069DA4D50C73C8" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(i)</enum><text>meet at least 1 of the qualifications described in paragraph (2); and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H4F875BE9250B4A108F1940E2AF15D2CC" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>do not present any active or potential conflict of interest.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC0EE959C9A86479E9CB36FAB6DA9D630" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Qualifications</header> <subparagraph commented="no" changed="not-changed" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD602CF30EF584EE6B71AF1462A3866D1"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The qualifications described in this paragraph are the following:</text> 
<clause id="H97A2AAC14FA046C8A780319963A66318" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A proven track record of sound judgment in leading or governing a large and complex private sector corporation or organization.</text></clause> <clause id="HA952F42971DA4F16826B6198A4E7B925" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>A proven track record as a distinguished academic or researcher at an accredited institution of higher education (as defined in section 101 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/1001">20 U.S.C. 1001</external-xref>)).</text></clause> 
<clause id="HA3568EE18EB948D0A313CAA869DC0979" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>Demonstrated experience in identifying emerging technologies and facilitating the adoption of such technologies into the operations of large organizations in either the public or private sector.</text></clause> <clause id="HE75D588ED9BF49479C26C365FD02DC8A" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>Demonstrated experience in developing new technology.</text></clause> 
<clause id="H0270BBAB69A5432EA8D25B4DB52AE6F8"><enum>(v)</enum><text>Demonstrated experience in technical evaluations of commercial products.</text></clause> <clause id="H2ECDF5C252DA4B639BCA67927D487BE3"><enum>(vi)</enum><text>Demonstrated expertise in privacy and civil liberties implications associated with emerging technologies.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H34DC279BBE7A4C0CA6065B792C77D105"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Membership structure</header><text>The Director shall ensure that no more than 4 concurrently serving members of the Board qualify for membership on the Board based predominately on a single qualification set forth under subparagraph (A). </text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H23D4484D6828476FBAC8AFAAFA5D3DDB" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Chair</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Board shall have a Chair, who shall be appointed by the Director of National Intelligence from among the members of the Board, after consultation with the Chair and Ranking Member of the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives and the Chair and Vice Chair of the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H54670648672945669DF8B55AFBCA0FF8" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Notifications</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 30 days after the date on which the Director of National Intelligence appoints a member to the Board under paragraph (1), or appoints a member of the Board as Chair under paragraph (3), the Director shall notify the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives of such appointment in writing. </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H43714BD50244417B800533CF9A49DC51" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Terms</header> <subparagraph id="H8951000F7A6A433DAE233559D5A2569A" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Except as provided in subparagraph (B), each member of the Board shall be appointed for a term of 2 years.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H83DEC4FBEB3E4E31AFDF5D61B91AC9B1" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Vacancies</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A member of the Board appointed to fill a vacancy occurring before the expiration of the term for which the predecessor of the member was appointed shall be appointed only for the remainder of that term. A vacancy in the Board shall not affect the powers of the Board and shall be filled in the manner in which the original appointment was made.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HE44381F4FDFD4F41BED27F3142069F44" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Reappointments</header><text>A member of the Board may not be reappointed for an additional term, unless the Director of National Intelligence certifies to the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives that reappointment for a single additional term is vital to the completion of an ongoing project or initiative of the Board.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H110B324DFB354360A83C1E4D5DE5FC21" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(6)</enum><header>Prohibition on compensation</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Members of the Board shall serve without pay. </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H96368A45E27D412BB9701562A0A1962A" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(7)</enum><header>Travel expenses</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Each member of the Board may reimbursement of reasonable travel expenses, subject to a process established by the Director and in accordance with applicable provisions under subchapter I of <external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/5/57">chapter 57</external-xref> of title 5, United States Code.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H23AE4971055F4991AA8E1469ED088880" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(8)</enum><header>Meetings</header> 
<subparagraph commented="no" changed="not-changed" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HA14D4F5C0E59440D918447CB9A18A5C1"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Board shall meet as necessary to carry out its purpose and duties under this section, but shall meet in person not less frequently than on a quarterly basis. A majority of the members of the Board shall constitute a quorum.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" changed="not-changed" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3C79E70F8CB944698D8C9A013E678573"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Closed meetings</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Meetings of the Board may be closed to the public only to protect national security.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H0C38DF2AE3EE45D5BC7BF580387CAB3B" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Staff</header> 
<paragraph id="H29A3A61F425C4AE1A721F396CF8149CA" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Composition</header><text>To the extent and in such amounts as specifically provided in advance in appropriations Act for the purposes detailed in this section, the Board shall be supported by full-time staff with requisite experience to assist the Board in carrying out its purpose and duties under this section in such number as the Director of National Intelligence determines appropriate. Such staff may be appointed by the Director of National Intelligence or detailed or otherwise assigned from another element of the intelligence community.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDEECF0DB70744B149965AF3855B82A8E" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Security clearances</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Staff of the Board, shall, as a condition of appointment, detail, or assignment to the Board, as the case may be, hold appropriate security clearances for access to the classified records and materials to be reviewed by the staff, and shall follow the guidance and practices on security under applicable Executive orders and Presidential or agency directives. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H735D092AB6F24402806ABD6FF91917C0" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Reports</header> 
<paragraph id="H8ABCBF9CD4BE448796E5AA8417618EFD" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Submission</header><text>Beginning on the date that is 2 years after the date on which the Board is established, and once every 2 years thereafter until the date on which the Board terminates under subsection (i), the Board shall submit to the Director of National Intelligence and the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives a report on the activities of the Board, which shall include, with respect to the period covered by the report, the following:</text> <subparagraph id="HD09F1D471BBE487FBA55ED37AC6BA339" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An assessment of the efforts of the intelligence community taken during such period to accelerate the adoption of competitive emerging technologies by the intelligence community, including such efforts taken with respect to the culture, organizational structures, processes, or functions of the intelligence community.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HA7D239F171EA4818AA63DE54039C9E2C" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Recommendations on how the intelligence community may make further progress to accelerate such adoption, including recommendations on changes to the culture, organizational structures, processes, and functions of the intelligence community necessary for such accelerated adoption.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HA4707FB7EF86402388BDABA61D72ACB1" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Any other matters the Board or the Director of National Intelligence determines appropriate.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCC74EEB2219C4917A83FAA55526C9BBC" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Form</header><text>Each report under paragraph (1) may be submitted in classified form, but if so submitted shall include an unclassified executive summary.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H89EE37C577D84AFBB846958CBEC527BE" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Termination</header> <paragraph id="H30C9F1971C154D33B3B108D59F1CC660" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Except as provided in paragraph (2), the Board shall terminate on September 30, 2026.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H1E8106B94F684B979176DEF8829CDB25" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Renewal</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Director of National Intelligence may renew the Board for an additional 2-year period following the date of termination specified in paragraph (1) if the Director notifies the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives of such renewal.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H5C604F919A224AFAB9E9E5998A58B791" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Charter</header> <paragraph commented="no" changed="not-changed" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H912D07302CBB4183870929798E863BD7"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of National Intelligence shall establish a charter for the Board, consistent with this section.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H0DF6B7FF90C147BB9A96ECF75E0E5DFC"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Elements</header><text>The charter established pursuant to paragraph (1) shall include the following:</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HF6313FE495CF4E92B13C49857B18C4F2"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Mandatory processes for identifying potential conflicts of interest, including the submission of initial and periodic financial disclosures by Board members.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H0C8B9E15E8FE4F32BC4EC75129FF9328"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The vetting of potential conflicts of interest by the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H796A617592CB4A66A2E542CCC2FCAD09"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The establishment of a process and associated protections for any whistleblower alleging a violation of applicable conflict of interest, Federal contracting, or other provision of law. </text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> 
<section id="H49182956C6414CA98BB6F3C7E8D541B6" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>7507.</enum><header>Programs for next-generation microelectronics in support of artificial intelligence</header> 
<subsection id="H9AC2B32A213C409FA291A59EC4FF2987" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Program establishment</header><text>Subject to the availability of appropriations, the Director of National Intelligence, acting through the Director of the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity, shall establish or otherwise oversee a program to advance microelectronics research.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H226666FE78774948A300BB1AFC5D532F" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Research Focus</header><text>The Director of National Intelligence shall ensure that the research carried out under the program established under subsection (a) is focused on the following:</text> 
<paragraph id="H16E2C4E690384257BFA8B3181110B4AE" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Advanced engineering and applied research into next-generation computing models, materials, devices, architectures, and algorithms to enable the advancement of artificial intelligence and machine learning.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H9F5D7BA118454C21AC72219F1382C4A7" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Efforts to—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HDE2874DB84374D4685E91E509CBB841F" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(A)</enum><text>overcome challenges with engineering and applied research of microelectronics, including with respect to the physical limits on transistors, electrical interconnects, and memory elements; </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HB65E1CA2BE834425BE659A059363C772" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(B)</enum><text>promote long-term advancements in computing technologies, including by fostering a unified and multidisciplinary approach encompassing research and development into—</text> 
<clause id="H02912B8503174A128302EAA73FE8FD6C" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(i)</enum><text>next-generation algorithm design;</text></clause> <clause id="H5DDA029AC0D349A681DAC4E7C1766029" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>next-generation compute capability;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HC39C14C43F3D454CB1720D04C121314E" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">generative and adaptive artificial intelligence for design applications;</text></clause> <clause id="H8C01C3833E48406DB826D01DBCB849F3" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(iv)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">photonics-based microprocessors, including electrophotonics;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H33CCD015FFDE4BF8A4FD96D88F120FA8" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(v)</enum><text>the chemistry and physics of new materials;</text></clause> <clause id="H3E1FBF0DD12C455FB581EAF06A87DF48" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(vi)</enum><text>optical communication networks, including electrophotonics; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HBD7BDA684217445BBC4F8787354C29E7" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(vii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">safety and controls for generative artificial intelligence applications for the intelligence community.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC669285BFC4941699A4898E35B481742" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any other activity the Director determines would promote the development of microelectronics research for future technologies, including optical communications or quantum technologies.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H3195697570F04CFE898C117D868749EA" commented="no" changed="not-changed"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Consideration, consultation, and collaboration</header><text>In carrying out the program established under subsection (a), the Director of National Intelligence shall—</text> <paragraph changed="not-changed" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H665BAF9EC89E4B2CA167239CEB4EE1CF"><enum>(1)</enum><text>consider the national strategy developed pursuant to subsection (a)(3)(A)(i) of section 9906 of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/15/4656">15 U.S.C. 4656</external-xref>); </text></paragraph>

<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H6913E99A569F46FEBEF4A5F8DAEA7A52"><enum>(2)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Policies described</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The policies described in this paragraph are policies for the acquisition, adoption, development, use, coordination, and maintenance of artificial intelligence capabilities that—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2ED4B9A412114ADD8E2D24462CFE5DD8"><enum>(A)</enum><text>establish a lexicon relating to the use of machine learning and artificial intelligence developed or acquired by elements of the intelligence community; </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HDB6EBE1B159B4BE0BC93F12A1B0BE0FB"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">establish minimum guidelines for evaluating the performance of models developed or acquired by elements of the intelligence community, such as by—</text> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3BD58E8020754033A23CBA13382D537B"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">specifying conditions for the continuous monitoring of artificial intelligence capabilities for performance, including the conditions for retraining or retiring models based on performance; </text></clause> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HE809DE111F04438FACC60DE6CBFAC0CC"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">documenting performance objectives, including specifying how performance objectives shall be developed and contractually enforced for capabilities procured from third parties; </text></clause> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3C12DDEC1F3B4D6FB19231DCE7812BB8"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">specifying the manner in which models should be audited, as necessary, including the types of documentation that should be provided to any auditor; and</text></clause> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB70FC8864C434413AACF81085B682028"><enum>(iv)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">specifying conditions under which models used by elements of the intelligence community should be subject to testing and evaluation for vulnerabilities to techniques meant to undermine the availability, integrity, or privacy of an artificial intelligence capability; </text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF9CBFD843FEB49F7AED4E1F893535ABA"><enum>(C)</enum><text>establish minimum guidelines for tracking dependencies in adjacent systems, capabilities, or processes impacted by the retraining or sunsetting of any model described in subparagraph (B); </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HF681BF33FDC543D8B61D1539B53DAC20"><enum>(D)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">establish minimum documentation requirements for capabilities procured from third parties, aligning such requirements, as necessary, with existing documentation requirements applicable to capabilities developed by elements of the intelligence community; </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H05BB459135A147BCBFB76B86EF2D2D41"><enum>(E)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">establish minimum standards for the documentation of imputed, augmented, or synthetic data used to train any model developed, procured, or used by an element of the intelligence community; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H928A9A278CA045A6B82D96884284FBEE"><enum>(F)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">provide guidance on the acquisition and usage of models that have previously been trained by a third party for subsequent modification and usage by such an element. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HFEF2C61A026E41B8856E27AAB412F689"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Policy review and revision</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Director of National Intelligence shall annually review or revise each policy established under paragraph (1).</text></paragraph></subsection><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HD526501C03F5407F8BA6C4613E141D85" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Conforming amendment</header><text>Section 6712(b)(1) of such Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3024">50 U.S.C. 3024</external-xref> note) is amended by striking <quote>section 6702(b)</quote> and inserting <quote>section 6702(c)</quote>. </text></subsection></section></subtitle></title> <title style="OLC" commented="no" level-type="subsequent" id="HD0F1508040C94E15892AA22CC8092A56"><enum>VI</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Classification reform</header> <toc container-level="title-container" quoted-block="no-quoted-block" lowest-level="section" idref="HD0F1508040C94E15892AA22CC8092A56" regeneration="yes-regeneration" lowest-bolded-level="division-lowest-bolded"> <toc-entry idref="H1DDF2D8706A840BBB00154466291C836" level="section">Sec. 7601. Short title.</toc-entry> <toc-entry idref="H98BCDB4654FF46FF90951C6FC8B0CCF3" level="section">Sec. 7602. <section id="H98BCDB4654FF46FF90951C6FC8B0CCF3"><enum>7602.</enum><header>Promoting efficient declassification review</header> 
<subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD842C0E0CDA94418ABE36605A07CB9BD"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Whenever an agency is processing a request pursuant to section 552 of title 5, United States Code (commonly known as the <quote>Freedom of Information Act</quote>) or the mandatory declassification review provisions of Executive Order 13526 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3161">50 U.S.C. 3161</external-xref> note; relating to classified national security information), or successor order, and identifies responsive classified records that are more than 25 years of age as of December 31 of the year in which the request is received, the head of the agency shall, in accordance with existing processes to protect national security under the Freedom of Information Act and the mandatory review provisions of Executive Order 12526, review the record and process the record for declassification and release by the National Declassification Center of the National Archives and Records Administration, unless the head of agency—</text> <paragraph id="H098650A718BC47679DC0E27092009FD9"><enum>(1)</enum><text>makes a certification to Congress, including the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate, and the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Oversight and Accountability, the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives, that the declassification of certain components within the record would be harmful to the protection of sources and methods or national security, pursuant to existing processes; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA5433CEF40A04DEF98B0B1900717EB05"><enum>(2)</enum><text>provides an explanation to Congress, including the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate, and the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Oversight and Accountability, the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives, for such certification. </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB7EE0CF93E9E4457985F6803ECB73EAA"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Application</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Subsection (a) shall apply regardless of whether or not the record described in such subsection is in the legal custody of the National Archives and Records Administration. </text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H94F9C3D8D3EA4E85BAAC940458AC857F"><enum>7603.</enum><header>Training to promote sensible classification</header> 
<subsection id="HD1158CD80A154BBD9720AF533C6B0DB5"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> <paragraph id="H6DAFFFA579024C3E93513E0695C32387"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Over-classification</header><text>The term <term>over-classification</term> means classification at a level that exceeds the minimum level of classification that is sufficient to protect the national security of the United States.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H4268122F5B7949688B21403584DA4AB0"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Sensible classification</header><text>The term <term>sensible classification</term> means classification at a level that is the minimum level of classification that is sufficient to protect the national security of the United States.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H711FC960E22E41AB972C7DC5074C990F"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Training required</header><text>Each head of an agency with classification authority shall conduct training for employees of the agency with classification authority to hold employees accountable for over-classification and to promote sensible classification.</text></subsection></section>

<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H9085801345FF4F7F8B29C749840E7E16"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the date that is 1 year after the date of the expiration of the term.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph indent="up1" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H1AF8049130F644AE81561142777EBDDD"><enum>(6)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 30 days after the date on which the term of a member of the Board ends, the appointing authority of the member shall submit to Congress a plan to appoint a successor.</text></paragraph><after-quoted-block>; and</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HACE79EB435664CBC99F43376CF596553"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">in subsection (f)—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HBE344F2512634D03B01C965284ACB3CF"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by inserting <quote>(1)</quote> before <quote>Any employee</quote>; and </text></subparagraph>

<section id="H540419D3DE324361A616201716E7A640"><enum>7605.</enum><header>Implementation of technology for classification and declassification</header> 
<subsection id="HA704CE8099EB4B9599312D529800DBDF"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Administrator of the Office of Electronic Government (in this section referred to as the <quote>Administrator</quote>) shall, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency, the Director of National Intelligence, the Public Interest Declassification Board, the Director of the Information Security Oversight Office, and the head of the National Declassification Center of the National Archives and Records Administration—</text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H16251EE4681E41889303CCFCDE2D3034"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">research a technology-based solutions—</text> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H255DC80655B04D02A010BF90E3D85D53"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to support efficient and effective systems for classification and declassification; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HCF25FCE2BCDC40E79B749F729D785372"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to be implemented on an interoperable and federated basis across the Federal Government; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3E2ABFEC39E54A4490066A8C32D22C2D"><enum>(2)</enum><text>submit to the President and Congress, including the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate, and the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Oversight and Accountability, the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives, recommendations regarding a technology-based solutions described in paragraph (1). </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H5DEB8FAE94764DC68DD2C61AD43043BA"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Report</header><text>Not later than 540 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the President shall submit to Congress a classified report describing actions taken to implement the recommendations under subsection (a)(2).</text></subsection></section> 
<section id="H828D76AAE039423B9A1CB43A57B5C9BD"><enum>7606.</enum><header>Studies and recommendations on necessity of security clearances</header> 
<subsection id="H67DF35825E634C469EF1128C269E21C3"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Agency studies on necessity of security clearances</header> 
<paragraph id="HEF47020A1EB5403D834039A12425D45E"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Studies required</header><text>The head of each agency that grants security clearances to personnel of such agency shall conduct a study on the necessity of such clearances.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H3FF7174EB66942628C06414B45357989"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Reports required</header> <subparagraph id="HE03E5B8195914FF684D16CDA76BFC8D1"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, each head of an agency that conducts a study under paragraph (1) shall submit to Congress, including the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate, and the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Oversight and Accountability, the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives, a report on the findings of the agency head with respect to such study, which the agency head may classify as appropriate.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H8398BB4DCAE746E1ACF9C7A5CB32C076"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Required elements</header><text>Each report submitted by the head of an agency under subparagraph (A) shall include, for such agency, the following:</text> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H82037561384542379A221358C1E21F02"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The number of personnel eligible for access to information up to the <quote>Top Secret</quote> level.</text></clause> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H718B669FD06F4829B040A84B8BEE44BF"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The number of personnel eligible for access to information up to the <quote>Secret</quote> level.</text></clause> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H18EE239F91024A6EA1C8C7B0B65CB4E6"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Information on any reduction in the number of personnel eligible for access to classified information based on the study conducted under paragraph (1). </text></clause> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HA2E7704B4D9E43E19D6317B52723FC31"><enum>(iv)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A description of how the agency head will ensure that the number of security clearances granted by such agency will be kept to the minimum required for the conduct of agency functions, commensurate with the size, needs, and mission of the agency.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HED13E22F1EB9418F8E80631F5E50E76D"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Industry</header><text>This subsection shall apply to the Secretary of Defense in the Secretary's capacity as the Executive Agent for the National Industrial Security Program, and the Secretary shall treat contractors, licensees, and grantees as personnel of the Department of Defense for purposes of the studies and reports required by this subsection.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HF4D4B07C816E45EFB4168541850097E0"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Director of National Intelligence review of sensitive compartmented information</header><text>Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of National Intelligence shall—</text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HF37D451669EF4F90896796818FAE9375"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">review the number of personnel eligible for access to sensitive compartmented information; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H00672DC46E364114AC5698BB379961F7"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">submit to Congress, including the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate, and the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Oversight and Accountability, the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives, a report on how the Director will ensure that the number of such personnel is limited to the minimum required.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H70D620ED9DE542FAB029ED76DBBDFEA7"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Agency review of special access programs</header><text>Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, each head of an agency who is authorized to establish a special access program by Executive Order 13526 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3161">50 U.S.C. 3161</external-xref> note; relating to classified national security information), or successor order, shall—</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HDEFD479279584C8C8677330FBAB2985C"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">review the number of personnel of the agency eligible for access to such special access programs; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H020BFDD5729F46B198A43B881CD3F98E"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">submit to Congress, including the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate, and the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Oversight and Accountability, the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives, a report on how the agency head will ensure that the number of such personnel is limited to the minimum required.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H1173E14D3C7F4134BE9ABD02EB80F1C4"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Secretary of Energy review of Q and L clearances</header><text>Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Energy shall—</text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H0B626C645E8E4E5DBF5803B9B3A1A51C"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">review the number of personnel of the Department of Energy granted Q and L access; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H6C0E82458B8C44AE8CD4AEA5A51B7C3C"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">submit to Congress, including the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate, and the Committee on Armed Services, the Committee on Oversight and Accountability, the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives, a report on how the Secretary will ensure that the number of such personnel is limited to the minimum required</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H379BFD53ADF749929FA78E1CACD49EB6" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Independent reviews</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date on which a study is completed under subsection (a) or a review is completed under subsections (b) through (d), the Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall each review the study or review, as the case may be. </text></subsection></section></title>
