<section id="H1D858485348D481AAFF988F643A00AD8"><enum>7701.</enum><header>Review of shared information technology services for personnel vetting</header> 
<subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H1D877CE08EBC4B54BCFBA95A31866480"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Definition of appropriate committees of Congress</header><text>In this section, the term <term>appropriate committees of Congress</term> means—</text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H497CB280BE3542C68599D2CB7F3EB7C1"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the congressional intelligence committees;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H81C45692A64B4079B9E88D1D2DE33B56"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Committee on Armed Services and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H755B25B387A047828D6050B260ACA620"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Committee on Armed Services and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H5F9391BE005F4B7D9D9FA5FB450D92D5"><enum>(b)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of National Intelligence shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a review of the extent to which the intelligence community can use information technology services shared among the intelligence community for purposes of personnel vetting, including with respect to human resources, suitability, and security. </text></subsection></section> <section id="H64F73D8782C34B11AAF29628725D6EA1"><enum>7702.</enum><header>Timeliness standard for rendering determinations of trust for personnel vetting</header> <subsection id="H0950275E82774A32883090DC3DB8E7F3"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Timeliness standard</header> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD176F7DABA11479491CD0A90B57E4CE2"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The President shall, acting through the Security Executive Agent and the Suitability and Credentialing Executive Agent, establish and publish in such public venue as the President considers appropriate, new timeliness performance standards for processing personnel vetting trust determinations in accordance with the Federal personnel vetting performance management standards.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF6EA7628C4164D959631A122B3760C02"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Quinquennial reviews</header><text>Not less frequently than once every 5 years, the President shall, acting through the Security Executive Agent and the Suitability and Credentialing Executive Agent—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H384AA6393DEB4AE6B4194A8DC5D70A40"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">review the standards established pursuant to paragraph (1); and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HF9E2CC3DA5204442804BE3A9E1DCD097"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">pursuant to such review—</text> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H330BE18037CD46299C0DD3A4C3AB1024"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">update such standards as the President considers appropriate; and</text></clause> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H8BAC9BA409EF4B8F9097370E585A9165"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">publish in the Federal Register such updates as may be made pursuant to clause (i).</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2EEF855D8BDF4CFE9DE4F8F1178EB4DB"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Conforming amendment</header><text>Section 3001 of the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3341">50 U.S.C. 3341</external-xref>) is amended by striking subsection (g).</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H7EFF150D5EF84AA89E3BD763C5F0274C"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Quarterly reports on implementation</header> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H4C0C44672AAB4B8F85A7C67890E1ACE6"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not less frequently than quarterly, the Security Executive Agent and the Suitability and Credentialing Executive Agent shall jointly make available to the public a quarterly report on the compliance of Executive agencies (as defined in section 105 of title 5, United States Code) with the standards established pursuant to subsection (a).</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H25D7FA8B11854E7ABFDC5C17827DECC7"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Disaggregation</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Each report made available pursuant to paragraph (1) shall disaggregate, to the greatest extent practicable, data by appropriate category of personnel risk and between Government and contractor personnel.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H17FF771BFF174A5FA4A3598A9D7CAA32" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Complementary standards for intelligence community</header><text>The Director of National Intelligence may, in consultation with the Security, Suitability, and Credentialing Performance Accountability Council established pursuant to Executive Order 13467 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3161">50 U.S.C. 3161</external-xref> note; relating to reforming processes related to suitability for Government employment, fitness for contractor employees, and eligibility for access to classified national security information) establish for the intelligence community standards complementary to those established pursuant to subsection (a). </text></subsection></section> <section id="H275F059E46A94E3FBCCE35E54AC42D9F"><enum>7703.</enum><header>Annual report on personnel vetting trust determinations</header> <subsection id="H8B6393C7ABF241D9A184652FF3C4F716"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Definition of personnel vetting trust determination</header><text>In this section, the term <term>personnel vetting trust determination</term> means any determination made by an executive branch agency as to whether an individual can be trusted to perform job functions or to be granted access necessary for a position. </text></subsection> 
<subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HEDE89AFC33734A0A938299A3E8F1FD6B"><enum>(b)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Annual report</header><text>Not later than March 30, 2024, and annually thereafter for 5 years, the Director of National Intelligence, acting as the Security Executive Agent, and the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, acting as the Suitability and Credentialing Executive Agent, in coordination with the Security, Suitability, and Credentialing Performance Accountability Council, shall jointly make available to the public a report on specific types of personnel vetting trust determinations made during the fiscal year preceding the fiscal year in which the report is made available, disaggregated, to the greatest extent possible, by the following:</text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H52FF162B6E804BF1916BDE0FF8908925"><enum>(1)</enum><text>Determinations of eligibility for national security-sensitive positions, separately noting—</text> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HFBAEA19AE46F49B8B72C86FFDF2F2937"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the number of individuals granted access to classified national security information; and </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H931A06DC374B499C92FE6F737D3EF636"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the number of individuals determined to be eligible for but not granted access to classified national security information. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD079197237104BB6B519EBE30556B516"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Determinations of suitability or fitness for a public trust position. </text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HBD3A6DDA016748A5B21E1A96BDE67DB7"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Status as a Government employee, a contractor employee, or other category. </text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H48E990266EC44B4FB857A9ABCE30F14F" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Elimination of report requirement</header><text>Section 3001 of the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3341">50 U.S.C. 3341</external-xref>) is amended by striking subsection (h).</text></subsection></section> <section id="H5647500552A44BA382B2D55386FEF43F"><enum>7704.</enum><header>Survey to assess strengths and weaknesses of Trusted Workforce 2.0</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, and once every 2 years thereafter until 2029, the Comptroller General of the United States shall administer a survey to such sample of Federal agencies, Federal contractors, and other persons that require security clearances to access classified information as the Comptroller General considers appropriate to assess—</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H80664FF5172C4A67B52CCC7E62643A69"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the strengths and weaknesses of the implementation of the Trusted Workforce 2.0 initiative; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7082586BC44947F39F08EB2DB4CB66A7" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the effectiveness of vetting Federal personnel while managing risk during the onboarding of such personnel.</text></paragraph></section></title>

<section id="HFD206B4563E245A0BBC56AFCBFE0EAE4"><enum>7801.</enum><header>Improved funding flexibility for payments made by the Central Intelligence Agency for qualifying injuries to the brain</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 19A(d) of the Central Intelligence Agency Act of 1949 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3519b">50 U.S.C. 3519b(d)</external-xref>) is amended by striking paragraph (3) and inserting the following new paragraph:</text> <quoted-block id="H56288A6910C8472194F19FAA9C3C2DCA" style="OLC"> <paragraph id="HB4C4502084A54084B1CF90E5A72009A5"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Funding</header> <subparagraph id="H80B3AC20E4974B67AC2DAAB2FF931D71"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Payment under paragraph (2) in a fiscal year may be made using any funds—</text> 
<clause id="HD20FADE652244D96A1440E0E9BBE5367"><enum>(i)</enum><text>appropriated specifically for payments under such paragraph; or</text></clause> <clause id="H3BCBDE9F9F5A4AF2904DA58819D3ED47"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>reprogrammed in accordance with section 504 of the National Security Act of 1947 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3094">50 U.S.C. 3094</external-xref>).</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H69C58B8104D64B9FB10316994989C009"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Budget</header><text>For each fiscal year, the Director shall include with the budget justification materials submitted to Congress in support of the budget of the President for that fiscal year pursuant to section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code, an estimate of the funds required in that fiscal year to make payments under paragraph (2).</text></subparagraph></paragraph><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section> <section id="HDA72FABC68B947A6862F0F4540B724E9"><enum>7802.</enum><header>Clarification of requirements to seek certain benefits relating to injuries to the brain</header> <subsection id="HFD3B38D392D641FB84FA683F3A526270"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Section 19A(d)(5) of the Central Intelligence Agency Act of 1949 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3519b">50 U.S.C. 3519b(d)(5)</external-xref>) is amended—</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H4AD2F2936DC0472F97D5C41B77F45FE8"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by striking <quote>Payments made</quote> and inserting the following:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HF5D59B5A2C0B463C940C65AEF71CBAAD"> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HE352803A6E9B4AA0A835E4BB86B0C92D"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Payments made</text></subparagraph><after-quoted-block>; and</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HED28308A7BC441D5901AF20107EE8F4D"><enum>(2)</enum><text>by adding at the end the following:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H00B119FF487D492EB6CCEA09FAE19A75"> <subparagraph id="H65E4DDB6C29446D3AC8E713266C52C21"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Relation to certain Federal workers compensation laws</header><text>Without regard to the requirements in sections (b) and (c), covered employees need not first seek benefits provided under <external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/5/81">chapter 81</external-xref> of title 5, United States Code, to be eligible solely for payment authorized under paragraph (2) of this subsection.</text></subparagraph><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H98501BB2FDBA42079332C8E43DC515F2"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Regulations</header><text>Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency shall—</text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2A8D1DEC40984DB6AA9CC630D26C5941"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">revise applicable regulations to conform with the amendment made by subsection (a); and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H2488969C3603405693EE057D51377042" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(2)</enum><text>submit to the congressional intelligence committees, the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives copies of such regulations, as revised pursuant to paragraph (1). </text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H8AB2441CF1EE4378B86D1ECDAFD02AD1"><enum>7803.</enum><header>Intelligence community implementation of HAVANA Act of 2021 authorities</header> <subsection id="HB2ABDB39D31544C18256945DE5290FF1"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Regulations</header><text>Except as provided in subsection (c), not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, each head of an element of the intelligence community that has not already done so shall—</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H612B453F06A249A38B7F97B926D89E9B"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">issue regulations and procedures to implement the authorities provided by section 19A(d) of the Central Intelligence Agency Act of 1949 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3519b">50 U.S.C. 3519b(d)</external-xref>) and section 901(i) of title IX of division J of the Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2020 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/22/2680b">22 U.S.C. 2680b(i)</external-xref>) to provide payments under such sections, to the degree that such authorities are applicable to the head of the element; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H33A75FBA1A2E4626B722755C02EA3CF7"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">submit to the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Armed Services and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Armed Services and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives copies of such regulations.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="HAA7C1A250BFA4DE181D62C4C367F2B61"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Reporting</header><text>Not later than 210 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, each head of an element of the intelligence community shall submit to the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Armed Services and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Armed Services and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives a report on—</text> <paragraph id="H0015F2ACB42346358739C6DF780F59BD"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the estimated number of individuals associated with their element that may be eligible for payment under the authorities described in subsection (a)(1);</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8C95FCA44C4C494EAA51539B255DB236"><enum>(2)</enum><text>an estimate of the obligation that the head of the intelligence community element expects to incur in fiscal year 2025 as a result of establishing the regulations pursuant to subsection (a)(1); and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HD3F8094958044A99ACBB4D88829281A1"><enum>(3)</enum><text>any perceived barriers or concerns in implementing such authorities.</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H17C24D185E4E446CB4843200B48063F1"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Alternative reporting</header><text>Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, each head of an element of the intelligence community (other than the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency) who believes that the authorities described in subsection (a)(1) are not currently relevant for individuals associated with their element, or who are not otherwise in position to issue the regulations and procedures required by subsection (a)(1) shall provide written and detailed justification to the congressional intelligence committees, the Committee on Armed Services and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate, and the Committee on Armed Services and the Subcommittee on Defense of the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives to explain this position.</text></subsection></section> <section id="HC8214E225D53428989465332185E1BCD"><enum>7804.</enum><header>Report and briefings on Central Intelligence Agency handling of anomalous health incidents</header> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H20D5F271691C4FDD9191BDD6D884C08A"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H5586B67986C44816953B29486899B3C5"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Agency</header><text>The term <term>Agency</term> means the Central Intelligence Agency.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H0C66A2BEB2A34F1FB167DE74EF1E6B41"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Appropriate committees of Congress</header><text>The term <term>appropriate committees of Congress</term> means—</text> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H71E22B53349A4D15977830A2EA4DA7C3"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the congressional intelligence committees; </text></subparagraph> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HC74EA601EC964BC29095FE2E90FAB1A1"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate; and </text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB9B7A5E1AFA44FEF8C8888645B327F04"><enum>(C)</enum><text>the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives. </text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H11E4D74329F249BDBD671A5F4351E9C5"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Qualifying injury</header><text>The term <term>qualifying injury</term> has the meaning given such term in section 19A(d)(1) of the Central Intelligence Agency Act of 1949 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/50/3519b">50 U.S.C. 3519b(d)(1)</external-xref>).</text></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB77ECB42F5774CDEB20D0EB5844483C2"><enum>(b)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 60 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress a report on the handling of anomalous health incidents by the Agency.</text></subsection> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H4B6E7F51B7924815A65BCBF8F55EB8AF"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Contents</header><text>The report required by subsection (b) shall include the following:</text> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H51B8EE13680641ABBB5D57003DB991B2"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Priority cases</header> 
<subparagraph id="H0B17FB1AC0DB4C9E976D7D96705D1F20"><enum>(A)</enum><text>A detailed list of priority cases of anomalous health incidents, including any cases that the Agency has assessed as potentially resulting from an external stimulus or the actions of a foreign actor, including, for each case, locations, dates, times, and circumstances of the anomalous health incidents.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9E8370B806C9455F8CB681E336FE6334"><enum>(B)</enum><text>For each priority case listed in accordance with subparagraph (A)—</text> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB23E7BA4CD094CA9A099FC1E71326867"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">an explanation as to why such case was determined to be a priority case;</text></clause> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HF08406BABDAB49C7A1B08FC1BCF4DB99"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>a description of each entity assigned to investigate the case;</text></clause> 
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H89341B3D48D64C908CA7344A842079B8"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">a detailed explanation of each credible alternative explanation that the Agency assigned to the incident, including whether each individual affected by the incident was informed about and provided with an opportunity to appeal such credible alternative explanation; and</text></clause> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB86FF05ED157404C8F8BEF471D1F5073"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>a detailed account of the input, data, evidence, or opinions the Agency has received from other agencies or components of the Federal Government that the Agency may have used to reach a conclusion on such case.</text></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H45E56CE4CFA5459DBDBBA3DF6EAE9CC2"><enum>(C)</enum><text>For each priority case of an anomalous health incident determined to largely display the core characteristics of an anomalous health incident established by the Intelligence Community Experts Panel, including each case for which the Agency does not have a credible alternative explanation, a detailed description of such case.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H649DDC506E2E40F78E762AE3D4E769A6"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Anomalous health incident sensors</header> <subparagraph id="H9A6B761C51C54292A849A0428108A200"><enum>(A)</enum><text>A list of all types of sensors that the Agency has developed or deployed with respect to reports of anomalous health incidents, including, for each type of sensor, the deployment location, the date and the duration of the employment of such type of sensor, and, if applicable, the reason for removal.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HFE420AE54A5C4B3A8C31676AC24D14EE"><enum>(B)</enum><text>A list of entities to which the Agency has provided unrestricted access to data from sensors associated with anomalous health incidents.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2BBA1ACC6A4A434B83A4EDF3951F634C"><enum>(C)</enum><text>A list of requests for support the Agency has received from elements of the Federal Government regarding sensor development, testing, or deployment, and a description of the support provided in each case.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HEE9D9B3945D849FFBD7D742B6A320C94"><enum>(D)</enum><text>A description of each emitter signature that the Agency prioritizes as a threat obtained by sensors associated with anomalous health incidents in Agency holdings since 2016, and an explanation of such prioritization.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3C12179E8CCF431096E6448A3EC580F1"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Additional submissions</header><text>Concurrent with the submission of the report required by subsection (b), the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency shall submit to the appropriate committees of Congress—</text> 
<paragraph id="HC0F9B1C67AA74EC99153C2B26256E83C"><enum>(1)</enum><text>a report on the length of time, from the time of initial application, for an applicant for payment under the Expanded Care Program of the Central Intelligence Agency to receive a determination from the Agency, disaggregated by qualifying injuries and qualifying injuries to the brain; </text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H28A8ED8F6C754811A21E6D3E33CBD04B"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">copies of all informational and instructional materials provided to employees of and other individuals affiliated with the Agency, with respect to applying for the Expanded Care Program; and </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HBC90A1D394B847B4B961B637B603EC4A"><enum>(3)</enum><text>copies of Agency guidance provided to employees of and other individuals affiliated with the Agency, with respect to reporting and responding to a suspected anomalous health incident, and the roles and responsibilities of each element of the Agency tasked with responding to a report of an anomalous health incident. </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H0CB172BC563746A8936479778C152835"><enum>(e)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Briefing requirement</header> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HC1F96CC274BC42D8A0A88B6F4CDF72DD"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency shall brief the appropriate committees of Congress on the report required by subsection (b).</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H1C16E00375314BB580CDB9B2C47A0CBC"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Additional briefings</header><text>Upon request of the appropriate committees of Congress, the Director shall brief such committees on anomalous health incidents.</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H1F9529304AD14B5BA0EE7C0373F6AB63"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Availability</header><text>The Director shall ensure that employees and other personnel of the Agency are made available for briefings under this subsection. </text></paragraph></subsection></section></title>
